values.name: Forward
values.tooltip: Align the +X (forward) axis. In a look-at, +X ends up pointing at the target.

values.name: Backward
values.tooltip: Align the -X (backward) axis. In a look-at, +X ends up pointing away from the target.

values.name: Right
values.tooltip: Align the +Y (right) axis. In a look-at, +Y ends up pointing at the target.

values.name: Left
values.tooltip: Align the -Y (left) axis. In a look-at, +Y ends up pointing away from the target.

values.name: Up
values.tooltip: Align the +Z (up) axis. In a look-at, +Z points at the target and the up vector drives +Y instead of +Z.

values.name: Down
values.tooltip: Align the -Z (down) axis. In a look-at, +Z points away from the target and the up vector drives +Y instead of +Z.

values.name: SizeMatters
values.tooltip: Apply the direction constraint first and the size constraint second, so size has the final say.

values.name: DirectionMatters
values.tooltip: Apply the size constraint first and the direction constraint second, so direction has the final say.

values.name: None
values.tooltip: Apply no direction shift to the picked axis.

values.name: Avoid
values.tooltip: When the picked axis is the one most aligned with Direction, fall back to the median-length axis.

values.name: Favor
values.tooltip: When the picked axis is not the one most aligned with Direction, step one rank toward the longer axes.

values.name: None
values.tooltip: Apply no size shift to the picked axis.

values.name: Greater
values.tooltip: Step one rank toward the longer axes for every remaining axis whose extent is under Threshold.

values.name: Smaller
values.tooltip: Shares its value with Greater, so picking it selects Greater and reads back as Greater. The step-toward-shorter branch is unreachable.

values.name: Sum
values.tooltip: Errors accumulate across axes. Averaging behavior.

values.name: Max
values.tooltip: Largest single-axis error dominates. Any axis blowout disqualifies.

values.name: ClosestVolume
values.tooltip: Score by absolute volume difference (normalized). Scale-sensitive; ignores axis mask.

values.name: ClosestPerAxis
values.tooltip: Score by per-axis extent differences on selected axes. Scale-sensitive.

values.name: ClosestAspectRatio
values.tooltip: Score by shape similarity on selected axes (max-normalized extents). Scale-agnostic, with optional volume influence.

values.name: TopK
values.tooltip: Pool = the K best-scoring entries. Pool size is constant (per point).

values.name: Tolerance
values.tooltip: Pool = entries within PoolSize ratio of the best score. Pool size varies with data.

values.name: Uniform
values.tooltip: Keep the profile ratio uniform

values.name: Scale
values.tooltip: Use a scale factor relative to the bevel distance

values.name: Distance
values.tooltip: Use a fixed distance relative to the bevelled point

values.name: None
values.tooltip: Bevel is not limited

values.name: ClosestNeighbor
values.tooltip: Closest neighbor position is used as upper limit

values.name: Balanced
values.tooltip: Weighted balance against opposite bevel position, falling back to closest neighbor

values.name: Radius
values.tooltip: Width is used as a radius value to compute distance along each point neighboring segments

values.name: Distance
values.tooltip: Width is used as a distance along each point neighboring segments

values.name: Line
values.tooltip: Line profile

values.name: Arc

values.name: Custom
values.tooltip: Custom profile

values.name: Global
values.tooltip: depth / MaxDepth. Uniform gradient from seed (0) to deepest node (1).

values.name: Cascade
values.tooltip: Hierarchical falloff. 1.0 at seed, 0.0 at leaf endpoints. Branches inherit from the trunk and smoothly decay toward their own leaves.

values.name: UVWConstant

values.name: UVWAttribute

values.name: PositionConstant
values.tooltip: A constant world position

values.tooltip: Use an array to mutate the bits of the incoming bitmask (will modify the constant value on output)

values.name: OR

values.name: NOT
values.tooltip: NOT (Flags &= ~Mask) Like AND, but inverts the masks.

values.name: XOR
values.tooltip: XOR (Flags ^= Mask) Invert the flag bit where the mask == 1.

values.name: Individual
values.tooltip: Uses individual blend operation subnodes to get full control. Best if you're looking to pick only a few specific things.

values.name: Monolithic
values.tooltip: Blend attributes & properties using monolithic settings. Best if you want to grab everything, or only select things to leave out.

values.name: None
values.tooltip: No blending is applied, keep the original value.

values.name: Average
values.tooltip: Average all sampled values.

values.name: Weight

values.name: Min

values.name: Max

values.tooltip: Copy target data (second value)

values.name: Sum
values.tooltip: Sum

values.name: WeightedSum

values.name: Lerp

values.name: Subtract
values.tooltip: Subtract.

values.name: Longest

values.name: Median

values.name: ClosestBounds

values.tooltip: Picks & process the farthest bounds only

values.tooltip: Picks & process the largest bounds only (extents length)

values.tooltip: Picks & process the smallest bounds only (extents length)

values.name: MinimumPenetration

values.name: EdgeDirection

values.name: Centroid

values.tooltip: Operate on edge chains which form paths with no crossings.  e.g, nodes with only two neighbors.

values.name: Delaunay3D
values.tooltip: Uses Delaunay 3D graph to find connections.

values.name: Delaunay2D
values.tooltip: Uses Delaunay 2D graph to find connections.

values.name: LeastEdges
values.tooltip: Ensure all clusters are connected using the least possible number of bridges.

values.name: MostEdges
values.tooltip: Each cluster will have a bridge to every other cluster

values.name: None
values.tooltip: No inheritance. Each entry keeps its own category as authored.

values.name: FillEmpty
values.tooltip: When an entry's category is None, inherit the closest non-None category from the ancestor chain of sub-collection entries.

values.name: Replace
values.tooltip: The closest non-None category from the ancestor chain of sub-collection entries always wins. The entry's own category survives only when no ancestor provides one.

values.name: Balanced
values.tooltip: Pick centroid if circumcenter is out of bounds, otherwise uses circumcenter.

values.name: Circumcenter
values.tooltip: Uses Delaunay cells' circumcenter.

values.name: Centroid
values.tooltip: Uses Delaunay cells' averaged vertice positions.

values.tooltip: Seed position is unchanged

values.name: Centroid
values.tooltip: Place the seed at the centroid of the path

values.name: PathBoundsCenter
values.tooltip: Place the seed at the center of the path' bounds

values.name: FirstNode
values.tooltip: Place the seed on the position of the node that started the cell.

values.name: LastNode
values.tooltip: Place the seed on the position of the node that ends the cell.

values.name: SeedOrder
values.tooltip: First seed (by index order) wins ownership of a cell

values.name: Closest
values.tooltip: Closest seed to cell centroid (3D world distance) wins ownership

values.name: ClosestProjected
values.tooltip: Closest seed to cell centroid (2D projected distance) wins ownership

values.name: BestCandidate
values.tooltip: Use sorting rules to determine which seed wins ownership

values.name: Both

values.name: ConvexOnly
values.tooltip: Output only convex cells

values.name: ConcaveOnly
values.tooltip: Output only concave cells

values.name: None
values.tooltip: Do not emit any centroid-to-corner spokes.

values.name: AllCorners
values.tooltip: Emit a spoke from each cell centroid to every one of its corners.

values.name: LongestSpoke
values.tooltip: Emit only the single longest centroid-to-corner spoke per cell.

values.name: ShortestSpoke
values.tooltip: Emit only the single shortest centroid-to-corner spoke per cell.

values.name: Separate
values.tooltip: Output Inside/Touching/Outside to separate pins

values.name: Combined
values.tooltip: Output matching cells to a single pin with triage tags

values.name: None
values.tooltip: All connected filters must pass.

values.name: Ratio
values.tooltip: Sample using a random subset of the nodes.

values.name: Filters
values.tooltip: Use filters to drive which nodes are added to the subset

values.name: Betweenness
values.tooltip: Brandes' algorithm. Measures how often a node lies on shortest paths between other nodes.

values.name: Closeness
values.tooltip: 1 / sum(distances). Measures how close a node is to all other nodes.

values.name: HarmonicCloseness
values.tooltip: sum(1/distance). Like closeness but handles disconnected graphs gracefully.

values.name: Degree
values.tooltip: Link count. Trivial O(N) measure of local connectivity.

values.name: Eigenvector
values.tooltip: Power iteration on adjacency matrix. High score = connected to other high-score nodes.

values.name: Katz
values.tooltip: Attenuated walk count. Considers all paths with exponential decay.

values.name: ForceKeep
values.tooltip: Chains hit by the edge filters are kept, regardless of the gating criteria.

values.name: ForceRemove
values.tooltip: Chains hit by the edge filters are removed, regardless of the gating criteria.

values.name: All
values.tooltip: A chain matches only if every enabled criterion is satisfied.

values.name: Any
values.tooltip: A chain matches if at least one enabled criterion is satisfied.

values.name: Intersection
values.tooltip: Keep only the regions covered by both subjects and operands.

values.name: Union
values.tooltip: Merge subjects (and operands, if any) into their combined regions.

values.name: Difference
values.tooltip: Subtract the operand regions from the subjects.

values.name: Xor
values.tooltip: Keep the regions covered by either subjects or operands, but not both.

values.name: Joined

values.tooltip: Round ends

values.tooltip: Only odd-numbered sub-regions are filled.

values.tooltip: Only sub-regions with winding counts greater than zero are filled.

values.name: Negative
values.tooltip: Only sub-regions with winding counts less than zero are filled.

values.name: Round
values.tooltip: Round joins

values.name: Bevel

values.tooltip: Do not output open paths

values.name: Primitive
values.tooltip: Spawn a simple static-mesh collider (convex simple collision) per footprint and output UPCGPrimitiveData -- for contexts where an AVolume isn't suitable.

values.name: OnlyBest
values.tooltip: Allows duplicate picks for multiple targets

values.name: NextBest
values.tooltip: If a cluster was already the closest pick of another target, pick the next best candidate.

values.name: Vtx
values.tooltip: Proximity to node position

values.name: Edge
values.tooltip: Proximity to edge, then endpoint

values.name: Vtx
values.tooltip: Only match vtx (most efficient check)

values.name: Edges
values.tooltip: Only match edges

values.name: Any
values.tooltip: Match either vtx or edges

values.name: Both
values.tooltip: Match both vtx and edges

values.name: Separated
values.tooltip: Uses two separate set of match handlers -- the default pin will be used on Vtx, the extra one for Edges.

values.name: Count
values.tooltip: Every contributor weighs equally; the vtx becomes the mean of the seeds that reached it.

values.name: Distance
values.tooltip: Closer seeds (by distance to the vtx) weigh more, farther seeds less.

values.name: Depth
values.tooltip: Weight by diffusion depth (graph steps from the seed).

values.name: CountAndDepth
values.tooltip: A blend of equal weighting and depth weighting.

values.name: Relative
values.tooltip: Each vtx is normalized so its strongest contributor reaches full intensity -- a territorial / Voronoi-style blend. Distance/Depth only bias overlaps; a vtx reached by a single seed always gets that seed at full strength.

values.name: Falloff
values.tooltip: Absolute intensity: each seed is full at its origin and fades to 0 at that diffusion's furthest reach. Distance/Depth become real gradients out from each seed, and Seed Factor is an absolute multiplier. Where intensity is low the vtx fades to its original value (if it participates) or to 0.

values.name: Vtx
values.tooltip: Value is fetched from the point being evaluated.

values.name: Edge
values.tooltip: Value is fetched from the edge connecting to the point being evaluated.

values.tooltip: Uses the first entry in the matching collection

values.name: LastIndex
values.tooltip: Uses the last entry in the matching collection

values.tooltip: Uses a random entry in the matching collection

values.tooltip: Uses pickers to select indices that will be turned into tags

values.tooltip: All input clusters are merged into a single vtx dataset; new edges may connect anything to anything.

values.tooltip: Attempt function S-curve - symmetrical, subtle

values.tooltip: Check for overlap with both nodes and edges

values.tooltip: Export a level to an embedded PCGDataAsset

values.tooltip: Combines all the values

values.tooltip: Attribute is treated as a Normal.

values.tooltip: Attribute is treated as a lookup index in the same data block.

values.name: Uniform
values.tooltip: Equal-width bins across the value range.

values.name: Quantile
values.tooltip: Equal-count bins (each bin has roughly the same number of nodes).

values.name: Nearest
values.tooltip: Merge each under-populated cell into the globally nearest other cell by centroid. Established behaviour; cost grows with the square of the cell count, so it is best for moderate cell counts.

values.name: Adjacent
values.tooltip: Merge each under-populated cell into the largest grid-adjacent cell only. O(N) -- scales to very fine grids -- and keeps cells grid-contiguous; a spatially isolated under-populated cell is left as its own cell.

values.name: Natural
values.tooltip: Cut at the Fiedler sign -- the graph's natural bottleneck. Preserves the most meaningful boundaries, but may produce fewer than NumPartitions when a cut is degenerate (unused budget is still recovered onto the sibling branch).

values.name: Balanced
values.tooltip: Cut at the Fiedler median so the two halves are even. Always yields a non-empty split, so it tracks NumPartitions closely; trades the natural bottleneck for balanced halves.

values.name: Exact
values.tooltip: Reach exactly NumPartitions whenever the cluster has at least that many valid nodes: after balanced bisection, keep splitting the largest partition until the count is met. Extra cuts may be arbitrary when the graph has no further natural boundary.

values.name: Raw
values.tooltip: Use world axes. Assumes the cluster grid is already axis-aligned.

values.name: BestFit
values.tooltip: Auto-detect principal axes via PCA (FBestFitPlane).

values.name: Custom
values.tooltip: User-supplied transform defines the grid basis.

values.name: EdgeInferred
values.tooltip: Auto-detect voxel size from average cluster edge length.

values.name: Manual
values.tooltip: Use a user-specified voxel size.

values.name: Multiplier
values.tooltip: High-weight boxes score higher during extraction. The algorithm naturally prefers bigger boxes around important nodes.

values.name: Priority
values.tooltip: Two-pass extraction. Pass 1: only extract boxes whose average weight exceeds the threshold. Pass 2: standard extraction for the rest.

values.name: Clamp
values.tooltip: Clamp the density value to [0, 1] before picking.

values.name: SkipPoint
values.tooltip: Return an invalid pick result so the consuming node skips the point.

values.name: WeightModulation
values.tooltip: Per-point effective weight = entry.Weight * f(density). Higher density prefers higher-weight entries.

values.name: RandomnessModulation
values.tooltip: density=1 picks purely weighted-random; density=0 picks uniform-random; blends linearly between.

values.name: Dot
values.tooltip: Extensive comparison using Dot product

values.name: Hash
values.tooltip: Simplified check using hash comparison with a destructive tolerance

values.name: None
values.tooltip: Do not use attributes to check sameness

values.name: Single
values.tooltip: Use a single, overridable attribute.

values.name: List
values.tooltip: Use a list of attributes. Arrays are not overridable

values.name: FIFO
values.tooltip: First in, first out

values.name: LIFO

values.tooltip: Discard all collections that have found duplicates (does not keep any)

values.name: Center
values.tooltip: Center

values.name: BoxBounds
values.tooltip: Point extents

values.tooltip: Euclidian distance

values.name: Max

values.name: GreatestToSmallest

values.name: EndpointsIndices
values.tooltip: Uses the edge' Start & End indices

values.name: EndpointsSort

values.tooltip: Scale the offset by 1 + Scale * cos(corner angle). The corner angle is PI on a straight run and 0 at a hairpin, so a negative Scale widens tight corners.

values.tooltip: Widen the offset on turns sharper than 90 degrees and leave gentler corners untouched. Peaks near 4.1x the offset at a full hairpin.

values.tooltip: Extend the offset to Offset / sin(half the corner angle) so the two offset walls meet at a point, capped at Mitre Limit times the offset.

values.tooltip: Move each point along its own offset direction by the offset distance. Corners need the Adjustment setting to land at the requested distance.

values.name: LinePlane
values.tooltip: Place each point where its outgoing segment, offset by the distance, crosses the plane of the previous offset segment. Corners hold the distance with no adjustment, and near-parallel segments fall back to a plain slide.

values.tooltip: Mean of the incoming and outgoing segment normals. Smoother than Normal at corners, but the effective distance shrinks as the corner tightens.

values.tooltip: Torsion-minimizing normal carried along the path from the first edge. Stable through vertical segments where Up-based normals degenerate; on closed loops the residual seam twist is distributed along the path.

APCGExSocketActor.name: Socket Actor
APCGExSocketActor.purpose: A marker you place to give a level entry or an actor entry a named socket. Mesh entries bake their sockets from the mesh itself, and a level or an actor class has nothing equivalent to read, so those sockets are authored instead: drop a Socket Actor where the attachment point belongs, and the entry built from that level gains a socket there. Socket Component is the same marker for actor entries, added to the actor rather than placed in a level. What the entry ends up with is an ordinary baked socket, so everything downstream that reads sockets applies unchanged.
APCGExSocketActor.situation: A level or actor kit piece needs known attachment points, so whatever places it can hang props, joins or decals off them.

mechanism.text: A socket actor carries a name, a tag and its own transform, and contributes exactly one socket to the entry built from the level it stands in. The transform recorded is its placement measured from the level origin, and that is the offset the socket keeps once the entry is staged onto a point. A socket component works one level down: each one on an actor contributes one socket to that actor class's entry, measured from the actor's origin. Both produce managed sockets, so every staging rebuild discards them and re-reads the source, while sockets typed onto the entry by hand sit beside them and survive.

off_label.claim: The socket is taken before the marker is rejected, so a socket actor can sit well outside the level's dressed footprint, an approach lane or a connector reach, without inflating the bounds that fitting and size-aware selectors solve against.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExLevelCollectionEntry::UpdateStaging emplaces the socket ahead of UPCGExActorContentFilter::StaticPassesFilter, which rejects strip-from-export providers before the bounds evaluator ever runs

SocketName.semantics: The name is what downstream selection runs on: Staging : Load Sockets narrows by it and can write it onto the points it emits. Nothing enforces uniqueness within an entry, so two markers sharing a name give two socket points that only their tag or their transform separates.

SocketTag.semantics: The second axis Staging : Load Sockets narrows on, tested independently of the name, so one shared name across a kit plus a per-marker tag lets a consumer take every socket of a kind or one exact marker.

bStripFromExport.semantics: This decides only what the marker contributes besides its socket, because the socket is harvested first and lands on the entry either way. Left on, the marker is rejected before bounds accumulate and before a level export runs, so it adds nothing to the entry's footprint and never reaches an exported PCG data asset. Turned off, it becomes ordinary level content: its tripod mesh counts toward the bounds and ships with the export. The same toggle sits on a socket component, where it has nothing to act on: the component contributes no bounds, and the export paths test actors.
bStripFromExport.trap: Staging : Spawn Level honours this on the loose-actor and streamed paths, which skip stripped markers. With Spawn As Level Instance on, the level is instanced whole and the socket actors come with it into the spawned scene.

hints.text: The marker's scale rides along in the socket transform. Scaling a socket actor up in the viewport to make the tripod easier to see scales the socket point Staging : Load Sockets emits there.

FPCGExApplySamplingDetails.name: Apply Sampling Details
FPCGExApplySamplingDetails.purpose: A sampler normally writes what it found to attributes and leaves the point where it is. This block is the other option: move the point itself onto what it sampled, one component at a time. It rides along on the samplers that resolve a target transform, and everything it does is off until you tick one of its two switches.
FPCGExApplySamplingDetails.situation: Points that should snap onto whatever they sampled, in some axes but not others, without a separate transform node downstream.

mechanism.text: Two sources feed one point. The sampled transform supplies position, rotation and scale, and the look-at transform supplies rotation alone. For each of those, a bitmask names which of the X, Y and Z components are taken; a component nobody names keeps the point's own value. Rotation is matched in Euler components rather than as a whole orientation, so picking one axis replaces that angle and leaves the other two as they were. The look-at pass runs after the transform pass, so where both name the same rotation component the look-at value is the one that lands.
steps: The sampled transform's named position, rotation and scale components replace the point's.
The look-at rotation's named components replace whatever is there by then, including anything the step above just wrote.

off_label.claim: Naming rotation components one at a time is a way to keep a point upright while still aiming it. Take Z from the look-at rotation and leave X and Y alone, and the point yaws toward its target without ever pitching or rolling off the ground plane.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExApplySamplingDetails::Apply reads the look-at as Euler and assigns only the components registered in LkRotComponents, leaving the rest of OutRotation at the point's own values.

bApplyTransform.semantics: Opens the position, rotation and scale masks below it. On its own it changes nothing: the masks ship empty, so a point moves only once you have named at least one component. The transform this reads is whatever the host sampler resolved as its target, so what a component means follows from that node rather than from here.
bApplyTransform.trap: Ticking this and leaving the masks empty is indistinguishable from leaving it off. Nothing warns, because a block with no components registered is treated as not wanting to apply anything at all.

TransformPosition.tooltip: Which position components from the sampled transform should be applied to the point.

TransformRotation.tooltip: Which rotation components from the sampled transform should be applied to the point.
TransformRotation.semantics: Components are matched as Euler angles, and the result is rebuilt into an orientation once every component has been decided. Taking a single axis is a partial rotation rather than a partial blend, so the point ends up with the sampled angle on that axis and its own on the others.

TransformScale.tooltip: Which scale components from the sampled transform should be applied to the point.

bApplyLookAt.semantics: The second source, and the one that wins. It carries rotation only: position and scale are declared on the struct but the panel never shows them and the apply path never reads them, so a look-at can aim a point and nothing else. Which direction it looks along is the host sampler's decision.
bApplyLookAt.trap: It runs after the transform pass rather than blending with it, so naming the same rotation component in both masks is not a conflict the panel reports. The transform value is written and then overwritten.

LookAtRotation.tooltip: Which rotation components from the sampled look at should be applied to the point.

hints.text: This moves the points that did the sampling. A sampler is usually read for its attributes, so a graph that turns this on and keeps sampling downstream is measuring from positions that have already been changed.

FPCGExAttachmentRules.name: Attachment Rules
FPCGExAttachmentRules.purpose: How a spawned component sits under the actor that owns it. Each of location, rotation and scale can either keep the value it was given or take its parent's, and the three are independent, which is what lets a component inherit an actor's rotation while keeping its own world position.
FPCGExAttachmentRules.situation: Components being spawned onto an actor whose own transform should partly apply and partly not.

mechanism.text: Each of the three rules is resolved on attachment: keeping relative preserves the transform as authored, keeping world preserves where the component actually is, and snapping takes the parent's value outright. Because they are independent, the combination is what matters rather than any one of them, and a mismatched set is the usual reason spawned components appear in the wrong place.

LocationRule.tooltip: The rule to apply to location when attaching

RotationRule.tooltip: The rule to apply to rotation when attaching

ScaleRule.tooltip: The rule to apply to scale when attaching

bWeldSimulatedBodies.tooltip: Whether to weld simulated bodies together when attaching
bWeldSimulatedBodies.semantics: Only reaches components taking part in physics simulation, where it joins them into one simulated body rather than leaving them separately simulated. On components that never simulate it does nothing.

hints.text: The three rules are resolved independently, so keeping world location while snapping rotation puts a component where it was and turns it to match its parent. That combination is often what is wanted and is not what either rule alone produces.

FPCGExAttributeGatherDetails.name: Attribute Gather Details
FPCGExAttributeGatherDetails.purpose: Which attributes a node should pick up, named by pattern rather than one at a time. Graphs routinely carry attributes nobody enumerated, so a node that has to act on a subset needs a way to say which without listing them, and this is that way.
FPCGExAttributeGatherDetails.situation: A node acting on a set of attributes that is not known when the graph is authored.

mechanism.text: Names are matched against the authored list under whichever mode is set, and what passes is what the node acts on. The matching is on names alone, so it knows nothing about types: a pattern that admits an attribute the node cannot handle is a matching success followed by a separate failure.

hints.text: Matching is by name and not by type. A pattern wide enough to catch attributes of several types will catch them, and what happens next depends on what the consuming node does with a type it did not expect.

FPCGExAttributeToTagDetails.name: Attribute To Tag Details
FPCGExAttributeToTagDetails.purpose: Turns attribute values into tags on the data. A tag travels with a dataset rather than with its points, so this is how a per-element value becomes something the graph can route on: filters and matching read tags, and a value buried in an attribute is invisible to them.
FPCGExAttributeToTagDetails.situation: A value that has to survive as something the graph can branch on, rather than as data a later node has to read.

mechanism.text: The named attributes are read and their values written into the dataset's tags, one tag per mapping. Prefixing with the attribute name is what keeps several mappings distinguishable, since a tag is a flat string with no structure of its own. The index tag is separate and records position rather than any attribute.

IndexTagPrefix.tooltip: Prefix added to the reference point index
IndexTagPrefix.semantics: The index tag records the dataset's position rather than any attribute value, which is how a set of datasets keeps its ordering through nodes that do not preserve one. This prefix is what stops that tag colliding with an attribute-derived one.

bPrefixWithAttributeName.tooltip: If enabled, prefix the attribute value with the attribute name
bPrefixWithAttributeName.semantics: Puts the attribute's name in front of its value, which is what makes a tag readable as a key and value rather than as a bare string. Without it two mappings whose values coincide produce indistinguishable tags.

AttributeMappings.tooltip: Attributes whose value is promoted to tags, each with an optional source->target output-name remap. Leave the target empty to keep the source's resolved name (the pre-remapping behavior).

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Attribute to read on input

fields.name: Target
fields.tooltip: Attribute to write on output, if different from input

AttributeMappings.semantics: Which attributes become tags and what those tags are called. The values are read at the point the block runs, so a tag is a snapshot rather than a link: changing the attribute afterwards leaves the tag as it was.

CommaSeparatedAttributeSelectors.tooltip: A list of selectors separated by a comma, for easy overrides. Will be appended to the existing array.

FPCGExBlendingDetails.name: Blending Details
FPCGExBlendingDetails.purpose: How several values become one. Wherever a node merges points, samples a neighbourhood or fuses a group, something has to say what happens to each attribute, and this is that statement. It is one default plus a list of exceptions rather than a per-attribute table, which is what keeps it workable on data carrying attributes the graph author has never enumerated.
FPCGExBlendingDetails.situation: A node that combines several elements into one, on data whose attributes should not all be treated the same way.

mechanism.text: `Default Blending` applies to every attribute that reaches the node, and `Attributes Overrides` names the ones that need something else. A filter decides which attributes are admitted at all, so an attribute the filter excludes keeps whatever it had rather than being blended by the default. Point properties are handled separately from attributes, through their own overrides, because averaging a position and averaging a colour are rarely wanted together.

BlendingFilter.semantics: Decides which attributes are admitted to blending at all, read together with the list beside it. An excluded attribute is not blended by the default: it keeps the value it arrived with, which is what makes this the way to protect identifiers and references from being averaged into nonsense.

DefaultBlending.semantics: The rule for everything not named elsewhere, which on real data is most attributes. Choosing it well matters more than any single override, since it is what silently governs the attributes nobody thought about.

PropertiesOverrides.semantics: Point properties, handled apart from attributes because they usually want different treatment. Averaging positions collapses a group to its centre, which is right for a fuse and wrong for most samplers, so the two surfaces are kept separate rather than sharing one default.

AttributesOverrides.semantics: Per-attribute exceptions to the default, and the place where attributes that are not quantities get their treatment. An attribute holding an index or an asset path wants copying rather than averaging, and nothing else in the block will notice that on its own.

hints.text: An attribute the filter excludes is not left untouched in the sense of being ignored: it keeps whichever source element's value the node happened to build its result from. On a blend of many that is one arbitrary member's value, which reads as a correct copy and is not a reproducible one.

FPCGExCellArtifactsDetails.name: Cell Artifacts Details
FPCGExCellArtifactsDetails.purpose: The **Artifacts** block, carried by every cell node, deciding what a cell that survived the constraints turns into on the way out. **Pathfinding : Find Cells**, **Pathfinding : Find All Cells**, both **(Bounded)** variants and **Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull** all carry it. It offers two shapes for the output, switched independently: a closed path per cell, and one point per cell carrying that cell's oriented box. Everything under the two switches writes a measurement onto whichever of them is on.
FPCGExCellArtifactsDetails.situation: A cell node has found the regions you wanted and the remaining question is what shape they should arrive in, and which of each cell's own measurements should travel with them.

mechanism.text: Every surviving cell passes through this block once. `Output Paths` gives each cell its own dataset, a closed path whose points are that cell's Vtx in loop order, carrying the tags of the Vtx and Edges data it came from. `Output Cell Bounds` gives each cluster one dataset instead, holding one point per cell whose transform and extents are that cell's oriented box. Both can be on together, and the three measurements every cell has, its hash, its area and its compactness, are written to whichever is on. Where they land differs: on a path they are `@Data` attributes describing that one cell, and on the box points they are per-point attributes.

off_label.claim: Cell Hash is derived from the cell's own Vtx loop rather than from where it sits in the output, so the same region found again after the cluster was rebuilt carries the same value. Writing it on both outputs is what lets a box point be matched back to its path.
off_label.grounded_in: FCell::GetCellHash is written through MakeDataIdentifier in FPCGExCellArtifactsDetails::Process and through MakeElementIdentifier in ProcessCellsAsOBBPoints, from the same value.

bOutputPaths.tooltip: Output cells as closed paths (one path per cell)
bOutputPaths.semantics: The two output switches are independent rather than a choice between modes, and a cell node with both of them off finds its cells and emits nothing. Every path is marked as a closed loop, so the path nodes downstream read it as one without being told.

bOutputCellBounds.tooltip: Output cells as OBB points (one point per cell)
bOutputCellBounds.semantics: One dataset per cluster, one point per cell, in the order the cells were kept. The transform comes from a plane fitted to the cell's Vtx, so the box follows the cell's own orientation rather than the world axes, and the extents are symmetric about that transform's origin.

OBBAttributes.semantics: `Min Extent` is a floor applied per axis after the fit, which is what stops a cell that is flat in one direction from producing a box with no thickness. `Axis Order` decides which of the fitted plane's axes becomes X, Y and Z, reordering the extents and the rotation together. `Use Min Box Fit` costs more per cell and changes the result on cells whose Vtx are unevenly spread, where the plain fit follows where the points are dense rather than the outline they trace.

CellHashAttributeName.tooltip: Write cell unique hash to an attribute

AreaAttributeName.tooltip: Write cell area to an attribute
AreaAttributeName.semantics: The value is the projected polygon's area divided by 100, which is the same scaling the `Min Area` and `Max Area` constraints compare against. The two agree with each other and neither is in square centimetres, so a threshold taken from a real measurement has to be scaled to match.
AreaAttributeName.trap: Area is measured on the projection, not in 3D. A cell tilted away from the projection plane reports less area than its points span.

CompactnessAttributeName.tooltip: Write cell compactness to an attribute
CompactnessAttributeName.semantics: Measured on the same projected polygon as the area, and it is a ratio, so it survives the scaling that area does not.

NumNodesAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the num nodes attribute (Points mode only)
NumNodesAttributeName.semantics: Counts positions in the traced loop rather than distinct Vtx, so it matches the point count of the same cell's path exactly, spikes into leaves included.

VtxIdAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the attribute to write the vtx index of its point to. This is useful if you want to find contours, mutate the cluster it comes from and remap the updated cluster positions onto the original cell. (Paths mode only)

TerminalFlagAttributeName.semantics: Flags the leaf Vtx themselves, the ends the loop turns around at, and not the pair of points either side of the turn. With `Keep Cells With Leaves` off, no cell reaching a leaf survives and every value written is false.

NumRepeatAttributeName.tooltip: Number of time a point is repeated in the cell (Paths mode only)
NumRepeatAttributeName.semantics: The value is how many extra times a point appears, so a point the loop visits once carries 0 and the turnaround Vtx of a leaf spike carries 1. Filtering on non-zero is what isolates the doubled-back stretches.

ConcaveTag.semantics: Every cell is one or the other, so with both toggles on each path carries exactly one of the two tags and the pair splits the output cleanly downstream.

TagForwarding.tooltip: Tags to be forwarded from clusters (Paths mode only)

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

TagForwarding.semantics: Tags come from both halves of the cluster, the Vtx data and the Edges data, and the ones PCGEx uses to pair them are stripped before this filter is consulted, so a cell path never arrives still claiming to be cluster data. `Include` keeps only what matches and `Exclude` drops what matches; the default passes everything that survived that first strip.

hints.text: The same three names, `Cell Hash`, `Cell Area` and `Cell Compactness`, describe one cell either way, so with both outputs on they exist twice in different domains: as `@Data` attributes on each path, and as per-point attributes on the box points. A downstream node reading one of them has to be pointed at the domain matching the output it is holding.

FPCGExCellConstraintsDetails.name: Cell Constraints Details
FPCGExCellConstraintsDetails.purpose: The **Constraints** block, and where most cell settings live. A cluster's edges enclose many closed loops, and this block is the test each one passes to become a cell: a shape filter, a rule for loops that reach a dead end, a rule for the cluster's outer boundary, and paired limits on how large a loop may be. It runs before anything downstream sees a cell, so a loop that fails here is never claimed by a seed, never sorted against a bound and never counted. The cell nodes carry it, along with **Cluster : Cell Diagram** and **Topology : Cluster Surface**.
FPCGExCellConstraintsDetails.situation: A cell node is handing back loops that were never wanted, and the ones that were can be told apart by something they measure.

mechanism.text: Every closed loop the cluster's edges enclose is measured once and tested against the whole block, and a loop that fails any test is discarded there and never becomes a cell. Six pairs of limits sit behind their own checkboxes and start switched off, so the block as it ships admits everything except the cluster's outer boundary. Half of what it measures comes from the cluster's own positions in world units, the bounds size, the perimeter and the segment lengths; half comes from the flattened polygon, the area and the compactness. `Aspect Filter` and `Keep Cells With Leaves` test shape instead of size. `Output Winding` decides nothing about survival, only the direction a surviving loop is written in.

off_label.claim: `Min Segment Length` discards the cell rather than the segment, so walking the value up until a region disappears reports the shortest edge inside that region. It is a quick way to find where a generator left a near-duplicate pair of Vtx.
off_label.grounded_in: BuildCellFromFace returns OutsideSegmentsLimit from inside the per-node walk, on the first segment outside the range, so one short segment ends the whole loop.

OutputWinding.tooltip: Output winding order for cell paths.
OutputWinding.semantics: A loop traced the other way round is reversed before it becomes a path, so a whole cluster's cells come back wound alike instead of following whichever way each trace happened to run. The row is hidden on the consumers that emit no paths, and the default still normalises their loops.

AspectFilter.semantics: Convexity is decided from the cell's Vtx positions in space, with each turn measured against the world up vector and not against the projection plane the cell was found in. Aim `Projection` anywhere other than up and this filter starts sorting cells by a shape that is not the one you see flattened.
AspectFilter.trap: A loop that reaches a dead end is always concave. The turnaround visits the same Vtx on both sides of the leaf, which the convexity test reads as a reversal, so `Convex Only` discards every cell with a spike in it whatever `Keep Cells With Leaves` is set to.

bKeepCellsWithLeaves.tooltip: Whether to keep cells that include dead ends wrapping
bKeepCellsWithLeaves.semantics: The test reads the Vtx's degree in the cluster, not the shape of the loop, so a single dead end anywhere on a cell discards it however short the spike is. Turning it off removes the region entirely; the cell does not come back trimmed of its spike.

bDuplicateLeafPoints.tooltip: Whether to duplicate dead end points
bDuplicateLeafPoints.semantics: The duplicate is added while the cell is built, after the point-count limits have already been checked, so an emitted path can be longer than `Max Point Count` allows by one position per dead end it turns around at. This is also the one field of the block that **Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull** reads.

bOmitWrappingBounds.tooltip: Omit cells that represent the outer boundary of the graph.
bOmitWrappingBounds.semantics: The outer boundary is picked out by area and winding once every loop has been built, so it is measured against every limit in this block first. A limit the boundary fails removes it before this switch is consulted, and `Keep If Sole` then has nothing to put back. What keeping it means differs by consumer: on the exhaustive nodes the boundary joins the output as one more cell, while on the seeded ones it is offered only to a seed that fell inside no cell at all.

bKeepWrapperIfSolePath.tooltip: Keep the wrapper cell if it's the only cell found.
bKeepWrapperIfSolePath.semantics: The escape for a cluster with no interior faces, a tree or a single open chain among them, where the node otherwise finds nothing and emits nothing. It is consulted only when the count of surviving cells reaches zero, so a cluster holding one interior cell and a boundary comes back with the interior cell alone.

MinBoundsSize.tooltip: Omit cells whose bounds size.length is smaller than the specified amount
MinBoundsSize.semantics: The measurement is the diagonal of the cell's axis-aligned box in world units, not the length of a side, so a square cell lying flat measures about 1.4 times its own side. The box is built from the Vtx positions as they sit in space, so a cell tilted out of the projection plane measures larger here than its flattened footprint suggests.

MaxBoundsSize.tooltip: Omit cells whose bounds size.length is larger than the specified amount

MinPointCount.tooltip: Omit cells whose point count is smaller than the specified amount
MinPointCount.semantics: Counts positions in the traced loop, so a cell that runs out along a dead end and back counts the Vtx either side of that spike twice. Values below 3 change nothing, because a loop of fewer than three positions is discarded before the limit is read.
MinPointCount.trap: The count is taken before `Duplicate Leaf points` adds its copies, so it disagrees with the `Num Nodes` attribute the artifacts block writes by one per dead end.

MaxPointCount.tooltip: Omit cells whose point count is larger than the specified amount

MinArea.tooltip: Omit cells whose area is smaller than the specified amount
MinArea.semantics: Area is measured on the flattened polygon and divided by 100, the same value the artifacts block writes as `Cell Area`. A threshold taken from a real measurement in centimetres has to be scaled to match it, and a cell tilted away from the projection plane measures smaller here than the ground it actually spans.

MaxArea.tooltip: Omit cells whose area is larger than the specified amount

MinPerimeter.tooltip: Omit cells whose perimeter is smaller than the specified amount
MinPerimeter.semantics: Summed in world units over the loop's segments in space, including the one closing back to the first Vtx, and a dead end contributes its edge twice because the loop walks out along it and back. The perimeter inside `Compactness` is a different number, measured on the flattened polygon.

MaxPerimeter.tooltip: Omit cells whose perimeter is larger than the specified amount

MinSegmentLength.tooltip: Omit cells that contains any segment which length is smaller than the specified amount
MinSegmentLength.semantics: Tested per segment in world units, and one segment outside the range discards the whole cell. That makes the pair a shape test: `Min Segment Length` removes cells holding a near-duplicate pair of Vtx, `Max Segment Length` removes cells with one long span across them.

MaxSegmentLength.tooltip: Omit cells that contains any segment which length is larger than the specified amount

MinCompactness.tooltip: Omit cells whose compactness is smaller than the specified amount (0-1 range).
MinCompactness.semantics: The ratio of the flattened polygon's area to the square of its perimeter, scaled so a circle reads 1 and a long thin sliver approaches 0. Being a ratio it survives the projection unscaled, which makes it the limit to reach for when the cluster's absolute size is not fixed.
MinCompactness.trap: A cell that runs out along a dead end pays for that stretch twice in the perimeter and gains no area for it, so its compactness collapses. A `Min Compactness` above roughly 0.2 removes leafy cells as a side effect.

MaxCompactness.tooltip: Omit cells whose compactness is larger than the specified amount (0-1 range).

hints.text: **Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull** carries this block and reads one field of it. Its boundary is traced with everything else replaced by defaults, so no limit runs, `Aspect Filter` is ignored, `Keep Cells With Leaves` is held on and `Output Winding` has no effect there. `Duplicate Leaf points` is the exception, and it applies.

FPCGExCellGrowthDetails.name: Cell Growth Details
FPCGExCellGrowthDetails.purpose: The **Growth** block: how far a claim spreads out from the cell a seed or a hole point landed in, counted in cells. **Pathfinding : Find Cells** and **Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)** carry it as `Seed Growth`, where spreading adds cells to what a seed takes; **Pathfinding : Find All Cells** and **Pathfinding : Find All Cells (Bounded)** carry it as `Hole Growth`, where spreading removes them. `Merge Adjacent Cells` sits alongside and fuses everything one claim covers into a single closed path. Nothing here moves a cell's boundary or changes its shape.
FPCGExCellGrowthDetails.situation: A seed should come away with a territory rather than a single region, or a hole should clear the ring of regions around it.

mechanism.text: The cell the point landed in is depth 0, the cells around it are depth 1, theirs are depth 2, and the spread stops at whatever depth that point asked for. Two cells count as neighbours when they share an edge, so cells meeting at a single Vtx are not neighbours, and the cluster's outer boundary is a neighbour of nothing, which is what keeps a claim inside the cluster. The spread crosses cells the constraints discarded without taking them, so a claim at depth 2 can land on the far side of a rejected cell. A cell that two seeds both reached goes to one of them, settled by `Seed Ownership`.

off_label.claim: Set `Growth` high enough to reach every cell in the cluster and turn `Merge Adjacent Cells` on, and a single seed hands back the whole connected decomposition as one outline. That is the cluster's boundary with the constraint block still applying to the cells underneath it, which **Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull** cannot give you.
off_label.grounded_in: ExpandSeedToAdjacentCells walks the face adjacency map breadth-first with no cap but the depth, and the per-seed MergeAdjacentCells call in OnRangeProcessingComplete traces one boundary per connected run of the claim.

Growth.tooltip: Growth depth for expansion. 0 = no expansion, 1 = immediate neighbors, 2 = neighbors of neighbors, etc.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Growth.semantics: The value is read per point from whichever dataset drives the block, the **Seeds** on the seeded nodes and the **Holes** on the exhaustive ones, so `Attribute` mode looks for its attribute there and not on the cluster. Depth counts cells, so how far a claim actually reaches follows how finely the cluster is divided and not any length. When the largest value across the whole dataset works out to 0 the spread is skipped outright, which is why the default costs nothing.
Growth.trap: An attribute that cannot be found is a warning rather than an error. The block falls back to a constant 0, the node finishes normally, and every claim comes back ungrown.

bMergeAdjacentCells.tooltip: When enabled, all cells assigned to the same seed are merged into a single closed path by dissolving shared interior edges. Only effective when Growth > 0. Constraint filtering may still produce multiple output cells if the grown region is non-contiguous.
bMergeAdjacentCells.semantics: Merging dissolves the borders shared inside one claim and traces what is left, so a claim that came apart into separate islands comes back as one path per island. The fused outline is a new cell that no constraint is re-applied to: it can exceed `Max Area`, carry more points than `Max Point Count` allows, and it is always reported concave, which is what the artifacts block's convex and concave tags read.
bMergeAdjacentCells.trap: On **Pathfinding : Find All Cells** and **Pathfinding : Find All Cells (Bounded)** this does not do what its own description says. There are no seeds there and it is not gated on `Growth`, so it fuses every surviving cell into one path per connected run of them and an ordinary decomposition collapses into a single outline.

hints.text: On the exhaustive nodes the **Holes** input is what switches this block on. With nothing wired there, `Growth` is never read at all and `Merge Adjacent Cells` is the only live setting on the block.

FPCGExCellSeedMutationDetails.name: Cell Seed Mutation Details
FPCGExCellSeedMutationDetails.purpose: The **Seed Mutations** block, carried by **Pathfinding : Find Cells** and **Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)**. It rewrites the seed point that won a cell so the point stands for the region instead of for the spot it was dropped on: moved onto the cell, sized to it, and carrying the cell's own measurements on point properties. The rewritten points leave on **SeedGenSuccess**, which is the only place they exist, and the seeds that won nothing are untouched.
FPCGExCellSeedMutationDetails.situation: The found regions are wanted as one point each rather than as paths, or something downstream needs a point per region carrying that region's size.

mechanism.text: Each seed that won a cell is rewritten once, while that cell's path is being built. Order is what makes the block predictable: the point is placed before its bounds are matched, so the bounds are expressed against wherever it ended up, and the transform is cleared in between.
steps: The point moves to whatever `Location` names, or stays where it was.
`Reset Scale` and `Reset Rotation` clear the transform it will carry.
`Match Cell Bounds` sets the extents, measured out from the point's new position.
`Area To`, `Perimeter To` and `Compactness To` write onto point properties, unclamped.

off_label.claim: Leave `Location` on `Original` with the two resets and `Match Cell Bounds` off, and the block stops moving anything: the seeds come back exactly where they were put, each carrying the area of the region it landed in. That turns the node into a containment query with a measurement attached.
off_label.grounded_in: ApplyToPoint applies each half independently, and the three SetPointProperty calls run whatever Location and the reset flags were set to.

AspectFilter.tooltip: Filter cells by convex/concave shape for seed mutation.
AspectFilter.semantics: Read by nothing. Every seed that won a cell is mutated, whatever shape that cell came out, and no seed is held back from **SeedGenSuccess** on account of convexity. Sorting cells by shape is the constraints block's `Aspect Filter`, which does it by discarding cells rather than by choosing which seeds get touched.

Location.semantics: `Centroid` averages the loop's positions rather than finding the polygon's centre of area, so an edge crowded with Vtx pulls it that way and a dead end pulls it twice. `First Node` and `Last Node` read the first and last point of the finished path, which is wherever the loop was cut and, under `Output Winding`, possibly reversed.

bMatchCellBounds.tooltip: Match seed bounds to cell bounds.
bMatchCellBounds.semantics: The extents are written out from the point's own position, so with `Location` left on `Original` the seed keeps its place and gets a lopsided box reaching out to the cell around it. The box comes from the cell's Vtx in space, not from its flattened shape.
bMatchCellBounds.trap: The extents are local to the point, so with `Reset Rotation` or `Reset Scale` turned off they are rotated and scaled by whatever the seed was already carrying and stop matching the cell.

AreaTo.tooltip: Output cell area to a point property.
AreaTo.semantics: The value is the same scaled figure the artifacts block writes as `Cell Area`: the flattened polygon's area divided by 100. `Perimeter To` is unscaled and measured in world units, so the two land on the target property at different orders of magnitude.

PerimeterTo.tooltip: Output cell perimeter to a point property.

CompactnessTo.tooltip: Output cell compactness to a point property.
CompactnessTo.semantics: The only one of the three already inside 0 to 1, which makes it the one that survives being written to `Density` or a colour channel without further scaling.

hints.text: Two switches on the node gate this block, and neither of them lives here. `Output Filtered Seeds` has to be on, because the rewritten points are the **SeedGenSuccess** pin and nothing else. `Output Paths` has to be on too, because the rewrite happens while a cell's path is being built. With either off the block runs on no seed at all, silently.

A seed that owns several cells is rewritten once per cell onto the same point, so only one of them survives on it and nothing you can set decides which. `Seed Growth` above 0 is where a seed comes to own several; turning `Merge Adjacent Cells` on collapses the claim back to one cell per seed and the ambiguity with it.

FPCGExCollisionDetails.name: Collision Details
FPCGExCollisionDetails.purpose: What counts as geometry, for the nodes that query the physics world. Everything about which surfaces can be hit lives here: the shape of the query, which channel or profile it uses, and which actors are excluded. The nodes that embed it decide where to query; this decides what answers.
FPCGExCollisionDetails.situation: A node reading the level's collision, where the wrong surfaces are being found or none are.

mechanism.text: The query is built from three independent choices. `Trace Mode` sets its shape, a ray or a swept sphere or box, which changes how much can be hit rather than what may be. `Collision Type` sets how eligibility is decided, by channel, by object type, or by named profile, and only the matching setting beneath it is read. The ignore settings then remove actors from the result whatever the rest admitted.

TraceMode.tooltip: Trace mode - line, sphere sweep, or box sweep
TraceMode.semantics: A ray hits what lies exactly along its line; a swept shape hits anything its volume passes through, which finds surfaces a ray between them would miss. The swept modes cost more and read their size from the setting beneath them, so the shape is as much a tuning parameter as the mode is.

SphereRadius.tooltip: Sphere radius for sphere sweep traces

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

BoxHalfExtents.tooltip: Box half extents for box sweep traces

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

bTraceComplex.tooltip: Trace against complex collision geometry instead of simple bounds.
bTraceComplex.semantics: Queries the real triangles rather than the simplified collision shape. It is materially slower, and it is also the only way to get a hit position that follows the visible surface, since simple collision can be a long way from the mesh it stands for.

CollisionType.semantics: Decides which of the three settings under it is consulted, and the other two are inert. That is the usual reason a configured channel appears to do nothing: the type is set to profile or object type, and the channel beside it is never read.

CollisionObjectType.tooltip: Collision object type to check against

bIgnoreSelf.tooltip: Ignore the actor that owns the PCG component -- everything on that actor, not just its PCG content.
bIgnoreSelf.semantics: Excludes everything on the actor owning the PCG component, not merely the component's own output. On a graph generating onto an actor that already holds geometry, that is a broader exclusion than the name suggests.

IgnoredActorSelector.tooltip: Actor selection criteria for actors to ignore in collision checks.
IgnoredActorSelector.semantics: Removes actors from the result after the query has already found them, so an exclusion costs the query rather than saving it. It is a correctness tool rather than a performance one.

FPCGExDotComparisonDetails.name: Dot Comparison Details
FPCGExDotComparisonDetails.purpose: The block that decides how closely two directions have to agree. Whatever hosts it reduces a pair of directions to one dot product per element, and this block holds the operator, the threshold, and the units the threshold is written in. It appears on **Filter : Angle**, **Filter : Dot**, **Filter : Tensor Dot**, **Vtx Filter : Edge Angle**, **Vtx Filter : Edge Direction**, **Edge Filter : Edge Direction** and **Vtx : Edge Match**, each supplying its own pair of vectors and reading back one verdict; on the Edge Direction filters it is live only while `Comparison Quality` is Dot (Precise). **Path : Stitch** carries a constant-only variant under `Requires Alignment`, with the same domain, operator and sign settings and no attribute row.
FPCGExDotComparisonDetails.situation: A node has a direction to weigh against a reference, and the only thing left to say is how far apart the two are allowed to be.

mechanism.text: One dot product in, one verdict out, per element. The host reduces two directions to a single number, the threshold is converted into the same units, and `Comparison` runs on the pair. Because the operator runs on dots and a dot falls as the angle opens, `>=` keeps the directions nearest the reference and `<=` keeps the ones furthest from it, whichever domain the threshold is written in. Both domains name the same angle: Scalar 0.5 and Degrees 60 are one test. The threshold is either a single number for the run or one per element read from whichever dataset the host bound, and the details panel draws the outcome as a circle around a reference arrow with every direction shaded pass or fail.

off_label.claim: **Filter : Angle** and **Filter : Dot** print the resolved threshold in their node subtitle, always in degrees whichever domain it was typed in, so setting Domain to Scalar and reading the subtitle converts a dot into an angle without leaving the graph.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExDotComparisonDetails::GetDisplayComparison runs the Scalar constant through Acos before printing; UPCGExAngleFilterProviderSettings::GetDisplayName and UPCGExDotFilterProviderSettings::GetDisplayName are its only two callers.

Domain.tooltip: How threshold values are interpreted. Scalar = raw dot product (-1 to 1), Degrees = angular (0-180).
Domain.semantics: The threshold is converted with cosine before anything is compared, so a Degrees value and its cosine are the same test: Degrees 0 is Scalar 1, Degrees 60 is Scalar 0.5, Degrees 90 is Scalar 0, Degrees 180 is Scalar -1. The measured value is a dot product either way. Scalar and Degrees are separate fields, so switching Domain leaves the test at whatever the other field was last set to.
Domain.trap: The operator applies to the dot, not to the angle. `>=` against a Degrees threshold means the angle is no wider than that, and raising the number widens the cone it keeps. A Degrees threshold of 180 with `>=` passes every direction there is.

Comparison.semantics: `~=` and `!~=` are the only two operators that consult Tolerance. The other six ignore it, which is why the Tolerance row leaves the panel the moment one of them is picked.
Comparison.trap: `==` and `!=` are exact double equality on a number the host computed from vector maths. Axis-aligned inputs can land on a threshold bit for bit, but anything that passed through a normalize or a rotation almost never does, so `==` fails and `!=` passes across the whole dataset. `~=` and `!~=` are the equality pair to reach for.

bUnsignedComparison.tooltip: Use absolute value of dot product before comparing. Treats opposite directions as equivalent.
bUnsignedComparison.semantics: The measured dot and the threshold are both replaced by their magnitudes, which folds every direction onto its axis. A threshold of 30 degrees and one of 150 degrees become the same setting, and no configuration can separate a direction pointing toward the reference from one pointing away. What it buys is the axis test: `<=` against a small Scalar threshold asks for perpendicular, either way round.
bUnsignedComparison.trap: Degrees 90 with `>=` becomes a magnitude threshold of 0, which every direction clears, so the block passes everything. A negative Scalar threshold loses its sign the same way.

ThresholdInput.tooltip: Whether threshold comes from a constant or per-point attribute.
ThresholdInput.semantics: Attribute mode reads one value per element from the data the host bound to this block, which is not always the data the node is named after. **Filter : Angle**, **Filter : Dot** and **Filter : Tensor Dot** bind the points being filtered; **Vtx Filter : Edge Angle**, **Vtx Filter : Edge Direction** and **Vtx : Edge Match** bind the Vtx; **Edge Filter : Edge Direction** binds the Edges. A selector in the `@Data` domain reads once for the whole dataset instead, which is one of the conditions **Filter : Dot** checks before it will judge a dataset in a single test.
ThresholdInput.trap: **Edge Filter : Edge Direction** binds its threshold to the Edges dataset, so an attribute authored on the Vtx is invisible to it. An attribute that cannot bind fails the host's initialization, not just this block's.

ThresholdAttribute.tooltip: Attribute to read threshold from. Value interpretation depends on Domain setting.
ThresholdAttribute.semantics: The clamps shown on the constant rows are editor clamps and do not reach an attribute.
ThresholdAttribute.trap: A Scalar value outside -1 to 1 makes the comparison unconditionally true or false, and a Degrees value past 180 folds back through cosine, so 200 and 160 give the same threshold.

DotConstant.tooltip: Threshold for comparison in scalar domain. -1 = opposite, 0 = perpendicular, 1 = same direction.
DotConstant.semantics: Clamped to the full dot range, so 1 and -1 are both reachable and either end of the scale can be named exactly. A host feeding a plain dot product never exceeds them, which makes `>` against 1 a block that rejects everything. The shipped 0 is perpendicular, the same cutoff the Degrees side ships.

DotTolerance.tooltip: Tolerance for ~= and !~= comparisons in scalar domain.
DotTolerance.semantics: A band around the threshold, measured in dot: the test passes when the measured dot sits within this much of the threshold dot, either side. The band is the same width with the sign kept or discarded, so Unsigned Comparison can be flipped without retuning it. The shipped 0.1 spans just under six degrees either side of perpendicular, and the same 0.1 of dot covers far more angle nearer the reference direction, where a threshold of 0.9 admits everything from 0 to about 37 degrees.

DegreesConstant.tooltip: Threshold for comparison in degrees. 0 = same direction, 90 = perpendicular, 180 = opposite.
DegreesConstant.semantics: The shipped 90 with `>=` admits the whole half-space around the reference direction. Drop it to 30 and only directions within 30 degrees of the reference survive.
DegreesConstant.trap: The constant-only variant on **Path : Stitch** ships `Scalar` at 0.5 and `Degrees` at 90, which are 60 degrees and 90 degrees, so flipping Domain on an otherwise untouched node changes the test. Both defaults are frozen on purpose: a field the user never touched serializes nothing, so moving a default moves the test inside graphs that were saved long ago.

DegreesTolerance.tooltip: Tolerance for ~= and !~= comparisons in degrees.
DegreesTolerance.semantics: An angular tolerance becomes the dot span between the reference direction and that angle, so T degrees is a band of `1 - cos(T)` in dot, zero at 0 and growing from there. It reaches exactly T degrees of angle where the threshold sits on the reference direction, and covers less angle as the threshold opens out toward perpendicular.
DegreesTolerance.trap: Both tolerance fields ship at 0.1 on scales that have nothing in common: 0.1 in Scalar is a band of 0.1 of dot, 0.1 in Degrees is a band of about 0.0000015. At the Degrees default `~=` is barely looser than `==`, and carrying a configured block across to the other domain changes what it admits by roughly five orders of magnitude.

FPCGExEdgeDirectionSettings.name: Edge Direction Settings
FPCGExEdgeDirectionSettings.purpose: An edge joins two Vtx and has no direction of its own, so any node that needs one has to pick an endpoint to call first. This block is that decision, and it appears wherever the answer becomes visible: **Cluster : Edge Properties** writing a direction vector, **Cluster : Break to Paths** deciding which way each extracted path runs, **Cluster : Edge Order** rewriting the stored endpoint pair, **Edge Filter : Edge Direction** testing an edge against a reference vector, and the fallback half of the flood-fill direction block on **Cluster : BFS Depth** and **Cluster : Flood Fill**. Two more live in the companion plugins, on **Valency : Write Junctions** and **Cluster to Zone Graph**.
FPCGExEdgeDirectionSettings.situation: Edge directions came out pointing the opposite way from what the graph downstream expects, or half of them point one way and half the other.

mechanism.text: The block orders an edge's two endpoints, and that ordering is everything it produces. A consumer that writes a direction vector builds it the same way every time, from the second endpoint towards the first and normalised, so the vector points **at** whichever endpoint sorted first, which is the part most often read backwards. `Direction Method` is what does the ordering, and the four methods read four different things: the order already stored on the edge, the two endpoints' row indices, sort rules over the Vtx dataset, or a vector attribute on the edge point itself. `Direction Choice` then applies to whichever one ran, and applies the same way in all four.

off_label.claim: In `Edge Dot Attribute` the comparison is per edge, so an attribute varying across the Edges dataset gives a per-edge answer: write a field into the edge points first, and the block orients each edge to its own local flow rather than to one global rule.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExEdgeDirectionSettings::InitFromParent binds the selector on the edge data facade, and SortEndpoints reads it at the edge's own index before comparing dot products.

DirectionMethod.tooltip: Method to pick the edge direction amongst various possibilities.
DirectionMethod.semantics: `Endpoints Order` compares nothing: it takes the pair as the Edges data already stores it, which is whatever the last node to write that pair left behind. `Endpoints Indices` compares the two endpoints' row numbers in the Vtx dataset, so it is stable as long as nothing reorders the Vtx. `Endpoints Sort` grows a **Direction Sorting** input pin on the host node, required once it appears, and runs those rules over the **Vtx** dataset. `Edge Dot Attribute` reads its vector from the **Edges** dataset instead, and keeps whichever of the two orientations points more nearly the same way as that vector.
DirectionMethod.trap: The two methods with a dependency fail in different places. `Endpoints Sort` makes the **Direction Sorting** pin appear and required, so nothing valid on it stops the node at boot with a missing-input error, before a cluster is read at all. `Edge Dot Attribute` binds once per Edges dataset instead, so a `Dir Source Attribute` that does not resolve there raises an attribute error and skips that one cluster while the others carry on.

DirSourceAttribute.tooltip: Attribute picker for the selected Direction Method.
DirSourceAttribute.semantics: This one reads from the **Edges** dataset, one vector per edge point, which is the opposite side from the sort rules `Endpoints Sort` uses. An attribute that exists only on the Vtx will not be found here.

DirectionChoice.tooltip: Which way the edge direction points relative to the method's endpoint ordering.
DirectionChoice.semantics: What counts as the smallest value changes with the method: the lower row index under `Endpoints Indices`, the endpoint the rules put first under `Endpoints Sort`, the orientation nearer the reference vector under `Edge Dot Attribute`. `Endpoints Order` has no per-endpoint value at all, so there `Greatest to Smallest` reverses every edge in the dataset.

hints.text: The vector points **at** the endpoint that sorted first, not away from it. Under the defaults, `Endpoints Order` with `Smallest to Greatest`, that is the endpoint the Edges data already stored first.

FPCGExEdgeEdgeIntersectionDetails.name: Edge/Edge Intersections
FPCGExEdgeEdgeIntersectionDetails.purpose: Where two edges cross, and whether that crossing should become a point. Edges that pass through each other are a fact of any generated cluster; this decides which of those crossings are real enough to act on, and the angle limits are what separates a genuine intersection from two edges that merely graze.
FPCGExEdgeEdgeIntersectionDetails.situation: A cluster whose edges cross each other, where the crossings should become junctions rather than being ignored.

mechanism.text: Every pair of edges is tested and the ones that cross within `Tolerance` are candidates. The angle limits then reject crossings that are too shallow or too square, which is the block's real work: a near-parallel crossing is usually two edges following the same route rather than a junction, and turning it into one produces a degenerate result. What survives can be recorded on the points it creates.

bEnableSelfIntersection.tooltip: If disabled, edges will only be checked against other datasets.
bEnableSelfIntersection.semantics: Whether an edge set is tested against itself as well as against others. Off, only crossings between separate inputs are found, which is what to use when a cluster's own edges are known to be well-formed and the cost of testing them is not wanted.

Tolerance.tooltip: Distance at which two edges are considered intersecting.
Tolerance.semantics: How near two edges must come to count as crossing. Edges rarely intersect exactly in generated data, so this is what makes the test usable at all, and it is a world-space distance rather than a relative one.

MinAngle.tooltip: Minimum angle between edges to count as intersection.
MinAngle.semantics: Rejects crossings shallower than this, which are the ones most likely to be two edges running alongside each other rather than meeting. Read together with the maximum, the pair defines a band of angles that count as a genuine junction.

MaxAngle.tooltip: Maximum angle between edges to count as intersection.

CrossingAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the attribute to flag point as crossing (result of an Edge/Edge intersection)
CrossingAttributeName.semantics: Marks the points created at crossings, which is otherwise impossible to recover: a point born at an intersection looks like any other Vtx once the cluster is rebuilt.

FPCGExFilterResultDetails.name: Filter Result Details
FPCGExFilterResultDetails.purpose: The block a filter consumer shows when it records verdicts onto elements instead of acting on them. Every element keeps its place in the data and carries the answer as an attribute, so the verdict travels downstream with everything else. Three shapes are on offer: a plain boolean, a running count, or bit flags. It appears on **Uber Filter** in Write mode and on **Cluster : Filter Vtx** and **Cluster : Refine** in Attribute mode, each of which decides for itself what counts as a pass.
FPCGExFilterResultDetails.situation: A downstream node needs to know which elements passed, and splitting the data in two would break the pairing or the ordering the rest of the graph depends on.

mechanism.text: One attribute per block, named by `Result Attribute Name`, holding one value for every element its host evaluated: points for **Uber Filter**, Vtx for **Cluster : Filter Vtx**, Vtx and Edges under separate blocks for **Cluster : Refine**. Feed **Uber Filter** an attribute set and the same values land on its rows. The data is otherwise untouched: no element added, removed or reordered, and a cluster keeps its Vtx and Edges paired. `Action` is the only thing that varies, and what it varies is the attribute's type and whether the write replaces the stored value or builds on it.

off_label.claim: Point several blocks at one attribute name in Counter mode, with `Pass Increment` at 1 and `Fail Increment` at -1, and the attribute becomes a running score of how many of those filter stacks each element satisfied.
off_label.grounded_in: The counter buffer opens with EBufferInit::Inherit in FPCGExFilterResultDetails::Init, and Write adds the increment to the value already at that index.

off_label.claim: Clear one side's bitmask toggle and each block can own a different bit of the same 64-bit attribute, which lets a downstream bitflag filter ask about combinations of them.
off_label.grounded_in: The single-sided branches of FPCGExFilterResultDetails::Write, where the untouched verdict never reaches BitmaskBuffer, over a buffer opened with EBufferInit::Inherit.

bEnabled.semantics: The toggle is shown only when the host node declares the block optional, and none of the three hosts do, so it stays hidden and result writing stays on. What governs writing in practice is the host's own output mode, which hides the whole block when it is set to anything else.

Action.tooltip: How should the result be used.
Action.semantics: Boolean starts the attribute over on every run, so whatever was stored under that name before this node ran is gone. Counter and Bitmask open on the values already there and build on them, which is what makes their results accumulate across nodes and across runs.

ResultAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the attribute to write the result to.
ResultAttributeName.semantics: The name is the join between blocks. Two blocks writing the same name land on one attribute, which is how results from several nodes are gathered into a single number or a single set of flags.
ResultAttributeName.trap: Every block starts at `Result`, so two of them left untouched over the same data share an attribute by accident: under Boolean the second overwrites the first, under Counter and Bitmask the two silently add up.

PassIncrement.tooltip: Value added to the counter when filters pass (use minus sign to decrement)

FailIncrement.tooltip: Value added to the counter when filters fail (use minus sign to decrement)

PassBitmask.tooltip: Operations executed on the flag when filters pass

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: How the bitmask value is constructed. Direct uses raw value, Mutations applies per-bit operations.

fields.name: Bitmask
fields.tooltip: Base 64-bit mask value. In Direct mode, used as-is. In Mutations mode, modified by operations.

fields.name: Op
fields.tooltip: How the final mask is combined with existing flags when applied.

fields.name: Mutations
fields.tooltip: Per-bit operations applied to the base bitmask. Only used in Mutations mode.

fields.name: Compositions
fields.tooltip: Additional bitmask references combined with the result.
