CoordinateSpace.semantics: What the mesh's vertex positions are relative to. The shipped original-component space keeps the mesh where the source data was, so moving the component moves the mesh; a world space instead bakes the positions and leaves them where they were generated.

FPCGExUVW.name: UVW
FPCGExUVW.purpose: A position inside a point's bounds, named as a fraction rather than a distance. Zero is one face, one is the opposite, and half is the middle, on each axis independently. That is what lets one setting mean the same corner across points of wildly different sizes.
FPCGExUVW.situation: Naming a spot on or inside a point's bounds that should mean the same thing whatever the point's size.

mechanism.text: The three components are resolved per point and multiplied through the referenced bounds to give a world position. Values outside zero to one are legal and land outside the bounds, which is how the block expresses an offset beyond a face rather than a position within. Which bounds are referenced is its own setting, since a point has several.

BoundsReference.tooltip: Which bounds to use for UVW coordinate calculations.
BoundsReference.semantics: Which of a point's bounds the fraction is measured across. Scaled and unscaled bounds differ wherever a point carries a scale, so the same coordinate names a different world position under each, which is the usual reason a coordinate that worked on one dataset misses on another.

U.tooltip: U coordinate within bounds (0 = min X, 1 = max X).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

U.semantics: Read per point, so the coordinate can vary across a set from an attribute. The three components are independent, which is what lets a coordinate name a face on one axis and the middle on the others.

V.tooltip: V coordinate within bounds (0 = min Y, 1 = max Y).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

W.tooltip: W coordinate within bounds (0 = min Z, 1 = max Z).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

hints.text: Nothing clamps the components, so values beyond zero and one place the result outside the bounds. That is useful for expressing an offset away from a face and is also the reason an accidentally large value produces a position nowhere near the point.

UK2Node_GetPCGExCollectionMember.name: Get Collection Member
UK2Node_GetPCGExCollectionMember.purpose: Reads any authorable field of the collection asset itself into a Blueprint graph, addressed by name. Right-click the node and use Pick Member to choose a field; the pick writes the path and stamps the Value pin with the field's exact type. This is the collection-scoped read of the member family, so it takes no entry index and never reaches into the entries array.
UK2Node_GetPCGExCollectionMember.situation: A staging pipeline or editor utility needs a value that lives on the collection rather than on one of its rows.

mechanism.text: The member path is resolved against the collection object and the field's value is copied onto the Value pin. The copy is exact-type: the pin has to carry the field's reflected type, which is what Pick Member stamps, so a field renamed or retyped since the pick returns false instead of converting. Success reports whether the path resolved and the copy happened, and a miss also writes a Blueprint log warning naming the path and the collection. Pick Member lists the fields of the collection class wired to the Collection pin, or of the type forced through the same menu; a collection class the registry does not know still lists its own fields, so a Blueprint subclass of a collection stays readable. The node is pure, so it re-reads every time the graph evaluates it.

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection to read from. The class wired here decides which fields Pick Member offers.

inputs.label: Member
inputs.note: Dot-separated path to the field. Pick Member fills it in; wire it only for a data-driven path.

outputs.label: Value
outputs.note: The field's value, on a pin typed to the picked field.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: False when the path did not resolve or the types did not match, in which case Value is left untouched.

pins.dynamic: The Value output is a wildcard until a member is picked. The pick stamps it with the field's reflected type including container type, so a whole array or a whole struct is a legitimate target, and links that no longer match are broken when the type changes. The type survives save and reopen. Compiling with no member picked is an error, as is a member that resolves to a hard object or class reference; soft references are supported.

hints.text: Wiring the Member pin for a data-driven path leaves the Value pin on whatever type was picked last. A path that resolves to a different type returns false and logs rather than converting, so a graph that ignores Success reads the pin's default and not the field.

UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryMember.name: Get Entry Member
UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryMember.purpose: Reads any authorable field of one collection entry into a Blueprint graph, addressed by raw index and field name. Right-click the node and use Pick Member to choose a field; the pick writes the path and stamps the Value pin with the field's exact type. Weight, category, tags, the baked staging data, per-entry fitting and grammar are all reachable this way, which covers most of what a staging pipeline reads while it walks entries.
UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryMember.situation: A pipeline hook has an entry index in hand and needs that row's authored value before deciding what to write back.

mechanism.text: The entry at the given raw index is located, the path is resolved against it, and the field's value is copied onto the Value pin. The copy is exact-type: a path that does not resolve, or resolves to a field of a different type than the pin carries, returns false and writes a Blueprint log warning instead of converting. Pick Member lists the entry struct registered for the collection's type, falling back to the base entry struct when the registry has nothing, while at run time the path is resolved against the row's own entry struct. The index is the raw position in the entries array, so it counts rows the pick pool ignores and does not move when weights change. The node is pure, so it re-reads every time the graph evaluates it.

off_label.claim: The Member pin accepts a wired name, so a loop over a list of same-typed field names reads many fields through one node, and Success per iteration doubles as a report of which paths a given collection actually has.
off_label.grounded_in: MemberPath is a plain FName input pin; an unresolved path returns false and logs rather than failing the graph

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection that owns the entry. The class wired here decides which fields Pick Member offers.

inputs.label: Entry Index
inputs.note: Raw position in the entries array, defaulting to 0.

inputs.label: Member
inputs.note: Dot-separated path to the field. Pick Member fills it in; wire it only for a data-driven path.

outputs.label: Value
outputs.note: The field's value, on a pin typed to the picked field.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: False when the index, the path or the type did not match, in which case Value is left untouched.

pins.dynamic: The Value output is a wildcard until a member is picked. The pick stamps it with the field's reflected type including container type, so a whole array or a whole struct is a legitimate target, and links that no longer match are broken when the type changes. The type survives save and reopen. Compiling with no member picked is an error, as is a member that resolves to a hard object or class reference; soft references are supported.

hints.text: An Omni Collection holds rows of different entry types, and at run time each row is resolved against its own entry struct. A path picked against one type returns false on rows of another, so walking a mixed collection by index has to branch on the row's type before reading.

An entry's property overrides are absent from the member list on purpose. Reading a declared property goes through Get Entry Property, which resolves it across the entry, category and collection tiers.

UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryProperty.name: Get Entry Property
UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryProperty.purpose: Reads a declared property of one entry, resolved the way the rest of the collection system resolves it. The entry's own enabled override comes first, then its category's row, then the collection's declared default. The Value output is a wildcard you type yourself, by connecting it or by picking a type from its right-click menu, and the stored value is converted to that type. This is the property half of the Blueprint surface, so it reads the custom data a collection declares instead of the fields of the entry struct.
UK2Node_GetPCGExEntryProperty.situation: A pipeline or editor utility needs the value a given entry resolves for a declared property, without caring which tier supplies it.

mechanism.text: The entry at the given raw index resolves the named property across its three tiers, and the stored value is converted to whatever type the Value pin carries. Conversion goes by metadata type, so a value stored as one numeric type reads out as another wherever a conversion exists; Success reports whether the property resolved and the conversion ran. A name that is not part of the collection's schema resolves nothing and returns false. The index is the raw position in the entries array, so it counts rows the pick pool ignores. The node is pure, so it re-reads every time the graph evaluates it.

off_label.claim: Wiring the Prop pin from a name variable and reading Success alone turns the node into a schema probe: it reports which entries resolve a usable value for a name, with the graph never touching the value.
off_label.grounded_in: PropertyName is a plain FName input pin, and the read returns false when no tier supplies a slot for that name

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection that owns the entry and declares the property.

inputs.label: Entry Index
inputs.note: Raw position in the entries array, defaulting to 0.

inputs.label: Prop
inputs.note: Name of the declared property to resolve.

outputs.label: Value
outputs.note: The resolved value, converted to the pin's type.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: False when the name resolved to nothing or the conversion did not run, in which case Value is left untouched.

pins.dynamic: The Value output starts as a wildcard. Connecting it adopts the connected pin's type and drops any container type, so an array is never the target; breaking the last connection returns the pin to wildcard. The pin's right-click menu picks a concrete type outright, from the metadata types the collection property system stores, and that choice survives save and reopen even with nothing wired. Compiling on a bare wildcard is an error.

hints.text: Success reports the conversion, and a conversion that does not run leaves the Value pin at its default rather than at the stored value. A graph that guessed the declared type wrong reads a zero, not an error.

UK2Node_SetPCGExCollectionMember.name: Set Collection Member
UK2Node_SetPCGExCollectionMember.purpose: Writes one reflected member of the collection asset itself from Blueprint. Right-click the node and pick a member: the pick fills the Member pin and stamps New Value to that member's exact reflected type, containers included. What it reaches is the collection object's own editable members, a different surface from the entry rows Set Entry Member addresses and from the declared properties Set Entry Property overrides.
UK2Node_SetPCGExCollectionMember.situation: A staging pipeline or editor utility needs to set a collection-wide value, the same edit an author would make in the collection's details panel, without opening every collection by hand.

mechanism.text: The picked member is written on the collection the Collection pin points at, and Success reports whether it landed. A write that lands snapshots the collection for undo, marks its package dirty, and forces its picking data to be rebuilt on next use; no staging rebuild follows, so baked staging data stays as the last rebuild left it. A write that fails changes nothing and logs a Blueprint runtime warning: either the member path did not resolve, or New Value is not the member's exact reflected type. Which members the picker offers comes from the collection type wired into the Collection pin, or from the type forced through the node's Collection Type menu, falling back to the base collection class when neither resolves.

inputs.label: Exec
inputs.note: Runs the write. The node is impure.

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection asset to write to. Its connected class also decides which members the picker lists.

inputs.label: Member
inputs.note: Dot-separated path to the member. Picking a member fills it; wiring it makes the path data-driven.

inputs.label: New Value
inputs.note: The value to write, typed to the picked member.

outputs.label: Then
outputs.note: Continues after the attempt, whether or not the write succeeded.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: True when the member resolved and the value was written.

pins.dynamic: New Value starts as a wildcard and takes the picked member's exact reflected type, container types included. The type is persisted, so it survives save and reopen even with nothing connected, and picking a different member breaks any connection whose type no longer matches. A node left on wildcard fails the Blueprint compile rather than doing nothing at runtime.

hints.text: Collection Properties and Category Overrides never appear in the member picker, and Entries is absent on the write direction: they carry sync invariants the collection's own editors maintain.

Wiring the Member pin makes the path data-driven, but New Value keeps whatever type the last pick stamped. A path that resolves to a differently typed member writes nothing and returns false, so a graph that ignores Success reads as a silent no-op.

UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryMember.name: Set Entry Member
UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryMember.purpose: Writes one reflected member of a single collection entry, addressed by its raw index. Right-click the node and pick a member: the pick fills the Member pin and stamps New Value to that member's exact reflected type. The roster is the entry struct the collection's type declares, its top-level fields plus one level into struct members, which is a different surface from the declared properties Set Entry Property overrides on the same entry.
UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryMember.situation: A staging pipeline hook holds an entry index and needs to write a field of that entry, the same edit an author would make in the collection's grid.

mechanism.text: The picked member is written on the entry at Entry Index, and Success reports whether it landed. A write that lands snapshots the collection for undo, marks its package dirty, and forces its picking data to be rebuilt on next use, so a weight or category edit takes effect on the next pick. No staging rebuild follows: editing a member that staging bakes from, such as an entry's static mesh, leaves the baked staging data as the last rebuild left it. A write fails without changing anything, logging a Blueprint runtime warning, when the member path does not resolve or New Value is not the member's exact reflected type.

inputs.label: Exec
inputs.note: Runs the write. The node is impure.

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection that owns the entry. Its connected class also decides which members the picker lists.

inputs.label: Entry Index
inputs.note: Raw index of the entry to write. Defaults to 0.

inputs.label: Member
inputs.note: Dot-separated path to the member. Picking a member fills it; wiring it makes the path data-driven.

inputs.label: New Value
inputs.note: The value to write, typed to the picked member.

outputs.label: Then
outputs.note: Continues after the attempt, whether or not the write succeeded.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: True when the entry and member resolved and the value was written.

pins.dynamic: New Value starts as a wildcard and takes the picked member's exact reflected type, container types included, so whole-array members are legitimate picks. The type is persisted, so it survives save and reopen even with nothing connected, and picking a different member breaks any connection whose type no longer matches. A node left on wildcard fails the Blueprint compile rather than doing nothing at runtime.

hints.text: Writing a member that staging bakes from does not re-bake it. Call Restage Entry afterwards, or make the edit in On Pre Rebuild, where the rebuild session stages the entry naturally.

Property Overrides never appears in the member picker, and Is Sub Collection and Staging are absent on the write direction: they carry invariants the collection's own editors and the rebuild maintain.

Wiring the Member pin makes the path data-driven, but New Value keeps whatever type the last pick stamped. A path that resolves to a differently typed member writes nothing and returns false, so a graph that ignores Success reads as a silent no-op.

UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryProperty.name: Set Entry Property
UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryProperty.purpose: Writes one of the collection's declared properties onto a single entry, addressed by its raw index, and enables that entry's own override for it. The effect is the edit an author makes in the grid: ticking the entry override and typing a value, so that entry stops answering with its category row or the collection default. New Value and Readback are a locked wildcard pair, which is how the node reports what the property actually stored after conversion.
UK2Node_SetPCGExEntryProperty.situation: A staging pipeline computes a per-entry value and needs it stored as that entry's own override rather than left to the collection default.

mechanism.text: The named property's override slot on the entry at Entry Index takes New Value, and the slot is enabled, so that entry now answers with its own value. Readback re-reads the property as it now resolves, after conversion into the property's stored type, which is what makes a coerced write visible. A write that lands snapshots the collection for undo and marks its package dirty, and no staging rebuild follows. The write fails without changing anything, logging a Blueprint runtime warning, when the name is not part of the collection's declared properties; an out-of-range index or a value that will not convert fails quietly with Success false.

inputs.label: Exec
inputs.note: Runs the write. The node is impure.

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection that owns the entry and declares the property.

inputs.label: Entry Index
inputs.note: Raw index of the entry to write. Defaults to 0.

inputs.label: Prop
inputs.note: Name of the declared property whose entry override is written.

inputs.label: New Value
inputs.note: The value to store. Shares its type with Readback.

outputs.label: Then
outputs.note: Continues after the attempt, whether or not the write succeeded.

outputs.label: Readback
outputs.note: The property as it resolves for that entry after the write, converted into the property's stored type.

outputs.label: Success
outputs.note: True when the override was written.

pins.dynamic: New Value and Readback always carry one concrete type. Connecting either to a typed pin types both; either pin's right-click Change Value Type menu picks a type explicitly from the property system's types; the choice is persisted and survives save and reopen with nothing connected. Disconnecting both returns the pair to wildcard, and a node left on wildcard fails the Blueprint compile.

hints.text: Readback is an independent read, not an echo of the write. A failed write still reports the value the entry resolved to before, so a graph that consumes Readback without checking Success cannot tell a stored value from an untouched one.

UK2Node_SwitchOnCollectionType.name: Switch on Collection Type
UK2Node_SwitchOnCollectionType.purpose: Branches Blueprint execution on which kind of collection it was handed, and hands that collection back already cast. Every registered collection type contributes an exec output paired with a typed collection output, and a Default branch catches everything else. Logic written once against a generic collection can then do type-specific work without a chain of cast nodes.
UK2Node_SwitchOnCollectionType.situation: One staging pipeline is assigned to collections of several types and needs a different branch per type.

mechanism.text: The collection's registered type id decides the branch, matched exactly: a collection whose type is registered leaves on that type's exec output, anything else, including an unset Collection pin, leaves on Default. Each branch's paired output carries the same collection already cast to that type's class, valid on that branch by construction. Blueprint subclasses of a shipped collection report the type id they inherit, so they leave on their parent's branch rather than one of their own. The pin set is generated from the collection type registry when the node is built, one pair per registered type whose class is loaded, ordered lexically by type id rather than by display name.

off_label.claim: Dropping the node into a graph is a quick read of which collection types the running editor has registered, including types contributed by other plugins.
off_label.grounded_in: AllocateDefaultPins builds one pin pair per entry of FTypeRegistry::GetAllTypeIds that still has a live collection class

inputs.label: Exec
inputs.note: Entry flow.

inputs.label: Collection
inputs.note: The collection whose registered type decides the branch. Left unset, execution leaves on Default.

outputs.label: One exec output per registered type
outputs.note: Labelled with the type's display name, for example Mesh Collection. Execution leaves here when the collection's type id matches exactly.

outputs.label: One typed collection output per registered type
outputs.note: The same collection pre-cast to that branch's class, labelled As followed by the type's display name, for example As Mesh Collection. Valid on its own branch by construction.

outputs.label: Default
outputs.note: Execution leaves here when the type id matches no registered type, including when Collection is unset.

pins.dynamic: The output pin set is not fixed: it is regenerated from the collection type registry each time the node is constructed. Types registered by other plugins appear as their own branches with no work on this node's part, and a type that stops being registered stops contributing pins.

hints.text: A custom collection type registered under the id Selection or Default collides with the switch's own internal pins. Register any other id.
A type whose module is no longer loaded contributes no pins, and pins generated for it earlier become orphaned the next time the node is reconstructed, with the usual broken-link warnings.

UPCGExActionProviderSettings.name: Action : Abstract
UPCGExActionProviderSettings.purpose: The shape every action shares, and the page to read once rather than on each of them. An action is a sub-node that pairs a filter test with a pair of consequences: one for the points that pass, one for the points that fail. It emits a factory on the Action pin, which is fed to Batch Actions, and the abstract base itself carries no consequence, so it never appears in the palette on its own.
UPCGExActionProviderSettings.situation: Reading the settings any action node shares before going to the specific one that does the work.

mechanism.text: When Batch Actions runs the produced factory, the factory's own filter stack is bound to the dataset being processed and then tested once per point. A point that passes takes the action's success branch, a point that fails takes its fail branch, and both branches are the action type's own business. Every point in the dataset is visited, so an action always has an opinion about every point, even when that opinion is to do nothing. Actions in one stack run in Priority order, ascending, and later actions see what earlier ones wrote.

inputs.label: Conditions
inputs.note: The filters that decide, per point, whether this action takes its success branch or its fail branch. Every action requires it, so an action with nothing wired here does not build.

outputs.label: Action
outputs.note: The factory, for the Actions pin of Batch Actions. Single connection out.

Priority.tooltip: Priority for transmutation order. Higher values are processed last.
Priority.semantics: Sorts the whole stack on the consumer's Actions pin, lowest first, so a higher value runs later and sees what the earlier actions wrote. Actions sharing a value keep the order they were wired in.

hints.text: The filters on Conditions are point filters and are asked about every point, so an action is never limited to a subset of the data: the fail branch is what happens to the rest.

UPCGExActionWriteValuesProviderSettings.name: Action : Write Attributes
UPCGExActionWriteValuesProviderSettings.purpose: Stamps one set of attribute values onto the points that pass its conditions and a different set onto the points that fail. Both sets are described by wiring attribute sets into the two pins: the attributes those sets declare become the attributes written, and the value written is each attribute's own default. It is the action for turning a filter verdict into data the rest of the graph can read.
UPCGExActionWriteValuesProviderSettings.situation: Marking points with a small block of typed values according to a test, where the values are authored once as an attribute set rather than repeated per node.

mechanism.text: When Batch Actions runs this action, the attributes declared on the Match Success and Match Fail data are created on the output as writable attributes, keeping any value the points already carried. Each point is then tested against the action's Conditions, and the branch it lands on writes its own attribute list. The value written is the source attribute's default value, so the rows of the attribute set are never read and one row is enough; what the attribute set supplies is names, types and defaults. A point never touched by either branch keeps whatever it already had.

off_label.claim: Naming the same attribute on both pins with different defaults turns the pair into a two-valued switch, which is the shortest way to write a per-point boolean or enum from a filter verdict.
off_label.grounded_in: both branches write to buffers obtained by attribute identity, so the same name on both pins resolves to one output attribute written from two different defaults

inputs.label: Conditions
inputs.note: The filters deciding, per point, which of the two branches applies.

inputs.label: MatchSuccess
inputs.note: An attribute set whose attributes are written to points that pass. Its rows are not read; only its attribute declarations and their defaults are.

inputs.label: MatchFail
inputs.note: The same, for points that fail.

outputs.label: Action
outputs.note: The factory, for the Actions pin of Batch Actions.

SuccessAttributesFilter.semantics: Narrows which of the attributes present on the Match Success data are actually written, by name. Leaving it open takes all of them, PCGEx-prefixed ones included.

FailAttributesFilter.semantics: The same narrowing for the Match Fail data. The two lists are gathered separately, so an attribute can be written on one branch and left alone on the other.

Priority.tooltip: Priority for transmutation order. Higher values are processed last.
Priority.semantics: Where this action sits in the stack. A later action writing the same attribute overwrites what this one wrote, which is how a stack of actions builds a value in layers.

hints.text: An attribute named on both pins must carry the same type on both, or Batch Actions refuses the whole stack with a type-mismatch error rather than skipping the offending pair.
Leaving a pin unwired is a valid configuration: that branch then writes nothing and the points it covers pass through untouched.

UPCGExActorCollection.name: Collection | Actor
UPCGExActorCollection.purpose: A weighted list of actor classes for staging to pick from. An entry can go past the class reference and record a placed actor: give it a level and an actor name, and the rebuild captures that actor's property delta, which Staging : Spawn Actors re-applies so the spawned actor comes out configured the way the placed one was. Source actors carrying a PCGEx property collection component hand their declared properties to the collection in the same pass, so one capture supplies both how an entry spawns and what data it carries. The capture is driven from the collection editor: Add Selected Actors turns a viewport selection into entries bound back to the actors they came from, and the toolbar's cleanup actions prune the entries whose source has since gone.
UPCGExActorCollection.situation: A handful of actors were dressed by hand in a level, and they now have to become a pickable library that spawns them configured the same way.

mechanism.text: The asset holds one flat list of entries, each referencing an actor class or another collection as a sub-collection. A staging rebuild bakes every class-referencing entry: it spawns a throwaway actor in the editor to measure bounds, turns any socket components that actor carries into managed sockets, and notes whether the class defaults hold a PCG component. An entry that also names a delta source records the placed actor's difference from its class defaults, plus the asset paths that difference references, which is what keeps those assets reachable through a cook. All of that is editor work: a rebuild outside the editor bakes empty bounds and logs an error. Downstream, a pick resolves to the entry and the spawn node loads the class and re-applies the delta.

BoundsEvaluator.tooltip: Bounds evaluator for bounds computation. If null, basic GetActorBounds fallback is used.
BoundsEvaluator.default:
Cast<UPCGExBoundsEvaluator>(
		ObjectInitializer.CreateDefaultSubobject(this, TEXT("BoundsEvaluator"),
		                                         UPCGExBoundsEvaluator::StaticClass(), EvalClass, false, false))
BoundsEvaluator.semantics: The evaluator reads a throwaway actor spawned at the identity transform, so the box it returns is the actor's own, and that box is what every size-aware consumer downstream sees: fitting solves against it, and selectors that reason about entry size read it. A new collection is created holding an instance of whichever class the Collections project settings name as the default bounds evaluator, so a project-wide answer to what counts in an actor's bounds is set once there instead of per asset.

fields.name: Weight
fields.tooltip: Core Properties

fields.name: PropertyOverrides
fields.tooltip: Property overrides for this entry. Values here take precedence over collection-level defaults. Only include properties you want to override.

fields.name: AssetGrammar
fields.tooltip: Per-entry grammar configuration. Shared between leaf and subcollection entries; for subcollections this slot is populated only when SubGrammarMode == Override (it then replaces the subcollection's own SubCollectionGrammar wholesale). Customization gates EPCGExGrammarAxisSize values based on bIsSubCollection.

fields.name: ScaleToFitSource
fields.tooltip: Where this entry's Scale to Fit comes from when a staging node considers entry overrides.

fields.name: JustificationSource
fields.tooltip: Where this entry's Justification comes from when a staging node considers entry overrides.

fields.name: SubCollection
fields.tooltip: Subcollection to draw picks from when bIsSubCollection is enabled. Accepts any collection type; consuming nodes type-check resolved entries, so mixed-type nesting must be routed through type filters downstream. Kept populated when bIsSubCollection is toggled off so the ref survives iteration. Do not rename: legacy per-type entry members were also named "SubCollection", so their on-disk tags deserialize straight into this property.

fields.name: Actor
fields.tooltip: Actor-Specific Properties

fields.name: DeltaSourceLevel
fields.tooltip: Optional: reference a specific level to capture property deltas from a placed actor. The actor's class must match the Actor class ref. During UpdateStaging, the property delta is computed from that instance vs its CDO.

fields.name: DeltaSourceActorName
fields.tooltip: Name of the actor within the level to capture delta from.

Entries.semantics: The collection editor's own actions author this list rather than the array widget. Add Selected Actors and the actor-name search mint entries keyed on their delta source, so re-running either over the same actors updates the existing rows instead of appending duplicates. Remove Missing drops entries whose source actor is gone from the level currently open and leaves entries pointing at other levels alone; Cleanup drops entries whose source level no longer exists, whose delta reference is half-filled, and that name neither an actor class nor a sub-collection.
Entries.trap: An entry with a weight but no actor class and no sub-collection stays in the pick pool and produces nothing at spawn. Do Not Ignore Invalid Entries is the toggle that refuses it instead.

SchemaMergePolicy.tooltip: Policy used when merging actor-component schemas into CollectionProperties on staging rebuild. Applies to the editor auto-rebuild path (EDITOR_OnPostStagingRebuild). For embedded collections built by UPCGExDefaultLevelDataExporter, this field is overwritten on each export to mirror the exporter's SchemaMergePolicy so manual rebuilds of the embedded asset stay consistent with how it was generated.
SchemaMergePolicy.semantics: Priority follows the source order, and the collection's own hand-authored properties are last in it: the donor actors' inherited class defaults come first, then each donor's resolved values, then whatever was declared on the collection by hand. Under the default, a name declared both by an actor and by hand dedupes silently when the two types agree, and drops the hand-authored one with a logged conflict when they do not.

hints.text: An entry's staleness fingerprint covers the actor class package only. Editing and saving the placed actor a delta came from does not mark the entry stale, so the automatic rebuild never fires for it and the capture is only refreshed by rebuilding the collection explicitly.

The bounds pass runs before the delta capture. An entry that names a delta source but no actor class has its class filled in from the found actor during the rebuild, by which point the bounds pass has already been skipped, so its staging bounds stay empty until a second rebuild.

Reject treats any repeated property name across the merged sources as a hard failure and yields an empty schema, which is then written over Collection Properties wholesale. A rebuild in that mode wipes the collection's declared properties and the per-entry overrides that were synced to them.

UPCGExAdjacencyStateFactoryProviderSetti.name: State : Bitmask Adjacency
UPCGExAdjacencyStateFactoryProviderSetti.purpose: A state whose bits are keyed to directions. Rather than one condition setting one bitmask, it carries a list of direction-and-bitmask pairs and walks every edge at the Vtx: an edge leaving within `Angle` of a listed direction applies that entry's operation to the Vtx's mask. What comes out describes the shape of the junction, one bit per direction the Vtx actually connects along. The directions and the bits they carry are authored on a **Bitmask Collection** asset, so one vocabulary serves every node that references it.
UPCGExAdjacencyStateFactoryProviderSetti.situation: A cluster on a layout with a known set of directions, where what matters about a Vtx is which of them it has an edge in.

mechanism.text: When **Cluster : Write States** reaches a Vtx, this state tests every one of its edges against every entry in its list. An entry is a direction carrying a bitmask and a bit operation; the test passes when the edge leaves within `Angle` of that direction, and every entry that passes applies its operation to that Vtx's mask. Nothing is exclusive, so one edge can trip several entries and several edges can trip the same one. The direction each edge is judged by runs from the Vtx out toward its neighbour.

off_label.claim: Because every entry that matches fires, giving several entries the same bit turns the list into an any-of test: the bit lands when the Vtx has an edge along any of those directions, without a filter or a group node anywhere.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExBitmask::FBitmaskData::MutateMatch walks every entry per direction and applies each matching one, rather than stopping at the first

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Point, Vtx, Filter Group or Data filters deciding whether this state holds at a Vtx. With nothing wired here every Vtx passes. Edge filters are not accepted.

outputs.label: State
outputs.note: The state this node defines, for the **States** pin on **Cluster : Write States**.

hints.text:
## Three rows come from the shared state base

`Name` labels the node in the graph and reaches no data. `Priority` orders this state against the others on the consumer's **States** pin, lowest first, with equal priorities keeping the order they were wired in. `Output Bitmasks` does nothing here: the two bitmask output pins it governs belong to the states that decide a single mask, and this node emits neither.

The **Filters** pin declares the broad filter type and narrows when the factory is built, so an **Edge Filter :** connects, logs an invalid-input warning and is dropped. The pin is optional, so what follows is the state running unfiltered, with every Vtx passing, rather than an error.

UPCGExAngleFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Angle
UPCGExAngleFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Tests the corner an ordered element makes with the element before it and the element after it. Both directions are derived from positions the data already carries, so there is nothing to author first and no operand to name: index order is the entire input. That is the line between this node and Filter : Dot, which compares two vectors you supply and never looks at a neighbour. The verdict comes out of Dot Comparison Details, handed the dot of those two directions and holding the cutoff they are judged against.
UPCGExAngleFilterProviderSettings.situation: An ordered point set where what survives depends on how sharply the run turns at each element.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element, and the only thing measured is position: the element's own, and those of the elements one index before and one index after it. Mode decides which pair of directions those three positions produce, the dot product of that pair is compared against the threshold, and that single comparison is the verdict. The dataset the element belongs to is the whole world, and index order is taken as it stands. An element with no neighbour on one side, which on an open dataset means the first and the last, returns its fallback with no measurement taken at all; on a dataset carrying `@Data.IsClosed` those two wrap onto each other and are tested like everything between them.

off_label.claim: Set both point fallbacks to Pass and give the dot comparison a threshold no corner can reach, Scalar domain with `>` against 1. Every interior element then fails and the only survivors are the two ends of an open dataset, which turns the filter into an endpoint marker that reports nothing at all on a closed one.
off_label.grounded_in: FAngleFilter::Test returning the First and Last Point Fallback verdict at index 0 and the last index before any dot product is computed, and the closed-loop branch wrapping those indices instead

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

hints.text: Nothing here checks that the data is a path. Index order is taken as given, so on points that were never ordered the filter still answers, and it answers about whichever elements happen to sit either side of each index.

UPCGExAssetCollection.name: Asset Collection
UPCGExAssetCollection.purpose: The abstract base every collection type inherits, and the page for the settings that are identical on every one of them. It never appears in the new-asset menu; what it carries is the shared surface: collection tags, the declared properties and category override rows entries resolve against, the collection-wide rules that can overrule per-entry fitting and grammar, how a sub-collection entry reports its size, and the staging pipelines that run on rebuild. Each type's own page describes the asset its entries point at and what a rebuild bakes out of it; what these shared settings mean is stated here and holds across the family.
UPCGExAssetCollection.situation: Reading any collection type's page and needing to know what its Collection Properties, Category Overrides, Global rules or Subcollection Bounds Mode do, since those are the same on all of them.

mechanism.text: A collection is a data asset holding a list of weighted entries, and this base owns the half of that asset that is not about any particular kind of content. Nothing on it loads an asset: a staging rebuild bakes each entry's asset path, bounds and sockets into the entry, and every stage before spawning reads those baked values. An entry whose weight is 0 is dropped from the pool outright, and a pick landing on a sub-collection entry descends into the child and rolls again on the child's own weights, however the top-level pick was decided. The asset carries a persistent identity, minted when it is created and re-minted on duplicate or on paste, which is what lets a recorded pick name this collection and no other. Each entry carries one of its own, so an outside reference to a single row keeps resolving as the list is reordered and rows come and go around it.

Notes.tooltip: Freeform authoring notes. Editor-only, never cooked.

StagingPipelines.tooltip: Optional post-process pipelines invoked around editor staging rebuilds (once before the session, once per re-staged entry, once after the native post-rebuild work). Composable: pipelines run in array order at every hook point, so later pipelines see earlier ones' mutations; null entries are skipped. Use them to drive per-entry property overrides, tags, weights etc. from Blueprint or C++. Editor-only: never serialized into or executed by cooked targets.
StagingPipelines.semantics: What a pipeline writes is baked into the asset and is not re-derived when a graph executes. A rebuild triggered from inside a hook still runs, but without re-firing hooks, so a pipeline that edits the collection cannot loop.
StagingPipelines.trap: Assigning any pipeline changes how a rebuild decides it changed something: the asset is compared whole, before and after, so a hook that only touches collection-level values still marks the package dirty even when no entry moved.

CollectionTags.tooltip: Tags carried by this collection: appended to spawned components' ComponentTags, and merged into entry tags wherever this collection is consumed as a subcollection or flattened.
CollectionTags.semantics: Nesting is the route that reaches a point: a pick descending into a sub-collection entry picks up that child collection's Collection Tags only while the consuming staging node's Grab Tags includes Collection. Flatten Collection is the other route onto entries, baking the source collection's own tags into every flattened row.
CollectionTags.trap: A collection's own Collection Tags never join the tags of a point staged directly from it. On the Component Tags route they reach mesh and skinned mesh entries only when the descriptor resolves from the collection globals, so an entry spawning on its own local descriptor carries none of them.

GlobalVariationMode.tooltip: Collection-level rule for entry variation overrides: let entries choose (PerEntry) or force GlobalVariations on all of them (Overrule).
GlobalVariationMode.semantics: Overrule is resolved before an entry's own Variation Mode is read, so it also replaces the values of entries set to None. Under Per Entry, an entry set to None resolves to identity ranges rather than skipping the roll, so moving an entry between None and a defaulted Local leaves every downstream seed-driven result unchanged.

GlobalVariations.tooltip: Collection-level fitting variations, consumed by entries whose Variation Mode is Global (or by all entries when Overrule).

fields.name: OffsetMin
fields.tooltip: Minimum random offset per axis.

fields.name: OffsetMax
fields.tooltip: Maximum random offset per axis.

fields.name: SnapPosition
fields.tooltip: How to snap the random offset.

fields.name: OffsetSnap
fields.tooltip: Grid size for offset snapping.

fields.name: bAbsoluteOffset
fields.tooltip: Apply offset in world space instead of local space.

fields.name: RotationMin
fields.tooltip: Minimum random rotation per axis.

fields.name: RotationMax
fields.tooltip: Maximum random rotation per axis.

fields.name: SnapRotation
fields.tooltip: How to snap the random rotation.

fields.name: RotationSnap
fields.tooltip: Angular increment for rotation snapping (degrees).

fields.name: AbsoluteRotation
fields.tooltip: Replace rotation instead of adding to it on the selected axes.

fields.name: ScaleMin
fields.tooltip: Minimum random scale per axis.

fields.name: ScaleMax
fields.tooltip: Maximum random scale per axis.

fields.name: SnapScale
fields.tooltip: How to snap the random scale.

fields.name: ScaleSnap
fields.tooltip: Increment for scale snapping.

fields.name: bUniformScale
fields.tooltip: Use same scale on all axes (X component only).

GlobalGrammarMode.tooltip: Collection-level rule for entry grammar overrides: let entries choose (PerEntry) or force GlobalAssetGrammar on all of them (Overrule).
GlobalGrammarMode.semantics: This rule reaches leaf entries only. A sub-collection entry answers through its own Grammar Mode, Inherit, Override or Flatten, and never consults the collection rule, so overruling grammar on a collection full of nested entries changes nothing.

GlobalAssetGrammar.tooltip: Collection-level grammar, consumed by entries whose grammar source is Global (or by all entries when Overrule).

fields.name: Symbol
fields.tooltip: Symbol for the grammar. Shared across all enabled axes.

fields.name: DebugColor
fields.tooltip: For easier debugging, using Point color in conjunction with PCG Debug Color Material. Shared across axes.

fields.name: Axes
fields.tooltip: Subdivision axes this module participates in. None = not a valid module (skipped during export). Defaults to X for new entries, matching the most common single-axis use case. PostLoad migration overrides this explicitly for legacy entries (empty Symbol -> None; legacy Size axis -> matching bit).

GlobalAssetGrammar.semantics: This one applies downward, to the collection's own leaf entries. What the collection reports upward, when an entry elsewhere nests it, is Sub Collection Grammar.

GlobalScaleToFitMode.tooltip: Collection-level rule for entry Scale to Fit overrides: let entries choose (PerEntry) or force GlobalScaleToFit on all of them (Overrule).
GlobalScaleToFitMode.semantics: Overrule is resolved before the entry's Scale to Fit Source is read, so an entry set to Local is overruled just as one set to None is, and the consuming staging node's own Scale to Fit stops applying to every entry at once. Under Per Entry, an entry whose source is None hands the decision back to the node.

GlobalScaleToFit.tooltip: Collection-level Scale to Fit, consumed by entries whose ScaleToFitSource is Global (or by all entries when Overrule).

fields.name: ScaleToFitMode
fields.tooltip: How scaling is applied to fit within target bounds. None = no scaling, Uniform = same scale all axes, Individual = per-axis control.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: Uniform scaling strategy. Fill = stretch to fill, Min = fit smallest axis, Max = fit largest axis, Avg = average.

fields.name: ScaleToFitX
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for X axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitY
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Y axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitZ
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Z axis when using Individual mode.

GlobalJustificationMode.tooltip: Collection-level rule for entry Justification overrides: let entries choose (PerEntry) or force GlobalJustification on all of them (Overrule).
GlobalJustificationMode.semantics: Resolved independently of the scale rule and on the same terms, so a collection can force one justification on every entry while still letting entries and the consuming node decide scale to fit.

GlobalJustification.tooltip: Collection-level Justification, consumed by entries whose JustificationSource is Global (or by all entries when Overrule).

fields.name: JustifyX
fields.tooltip: X axis justification settings.

fields.name: JustifyY
fields.tooltip: Y axis justification settings.

fields.name: JustifyZ
fields.tooltip: Z axis justification settings.

SubCollectionGrammar.tooltip: This collection's identity as a grammar module when it is used as a subcollection entry elsewhere (resolved when the parent entry has SubGrammarMode == Inherit). Per-axis like any other grammar struct; customization gates EPCGExGrammarAxisSize values for the subcollection-aggregation set (Min/Max/Average + Fixed).

fields.name: Symbol
fields.tooltip: Symbol for the grammar. Shared across all enabled axes.

fields.name: DebugColor
fields.tooltip: For easier debugging, using Point color in conjunction with PCG Debug Color Material. Shared across axes.

fields.name: Axes
fields.tooltip: Subdivision axes this module participates in. None = not a valid module (skipped during export). Defaults to X for new entries, matching the most common single-axis use case. PostLoad migration overrides this explicitly for legacy entries (empty Symbol -> None; legacy Size axis -> matching bit).

SubCollectionGrammar.semantics: Read by the parent, not by this collection: it is the module this collection reports when an entry elsewhere nests it with Grammar Mode set to Inherit. A parent entry set to Override replaces it with its own grammar block, and one set to Flatten emits no module for this collection at all, letting its leaves contribute directly.

bDoNotIgnoreInvalidEntries.tooltip: Exclude entries whose asset slot is EMPTY from the pickable set. Off (default): empty entries stay valid picks that stage nothing -- weighted "spawn nothing" slots. Governs only empty asset slots, nothing else.
bDoNotIgnoreInvalidEntries.semantics: Weight is gated separately and this setting has no bearing on it. An entry at weight 0 is dropped from the pool whatever this is set to, and nothing on the collection brings it back.

SubcollectionBoundsMode.tooltip: How an entry that is itself a subcollection computes its aggregate Staging.Bounds (extents, centered at origin). Consumed by selectors that reason about entry size.
SubcollectionBoundsMode.semantics: Aggregation runs over every entry of the child collection, not over its pickable ones, so an entry at weight 0 or with a missing asset still contributes its size. Children whose staged bounds are invalid or near-zero are skipped, and Weight-Weighted Mean counts a weight-0 child as if it were weight 1. The result is extents around the origin, so a mode changes how large a nested entry reports itself and never where it sits.
SubcollectionBoundsMode.trap: Aggregation reads whatever the children last baked. A plain Rebuild leaves a nested tree's lower levels alone, so a parent re-aggregates stale child bounds; the recursive Rebuild is what stages the children first.

CollectionProperties.tooltip: Collection-level properties with default values. Entries inherit these unless they provide overrides.

fields.name: Schemas
fields.tooltip: Schema array (locals -- always take precedence over imported entries with matching names)

fields.name: ImportedSchemas
fields.tooltip: Imported schema assets, resolved in array order after locals. Hard refs -- assets stay loaded as long as the owning collection exists. Recursion through imported assets' own ImportedSchemas is supported with cycle detection.

fields.name: ImportOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-entry value overrides for imported entries. EditAnywhere is required so the detail panel's GetChildHandle can reach this property's children -- the registered FPCGExPropertySchemaCollectionCustomization takes over rendering entirely (CustomizeChildren controls every visible row), so this never appears as a top-level array editor in the inspector. The array is kept parallel with the imports-only schema via ReconcileImportOverrides (which delegates to FPCGExPropertyOverrides::SyncToSchema). UE per-instance UPROPERTY delta serialization handles three-layer composition: asset default -> template (collection on CDO) -> instance (collection on actor instance). Each layer overrides the previous via bEnabled toggles on individual entries. Locals do not appear here -- they are edited in-place on Schemas.

CollectionProperties.semantics: Declarations, not values: what an entry ends up with is resolved in three tiers, the entry's own enabled override first, then the row its category has under Category Overrides, then the default declared here. Imported Schemas resolve after the local list and dedupe by name with the first occurrence winning, so a local declaration always beats an imported one of the same name, and an earlier import beats a later one. Imports recurse through the imported assets' own imports, with cycles skipped.
CollectionProperties.trap: Imported schemas are hard references, so every schema asset a collection imports stays loaded for as long as the collection does.

CategoryOverrides.tooltip: Middle resolution tier: an entry whose Category names a row here reads that row's enabled slots before falling back to CollectionProperties. Cooked -- runtime resolution reads it. Rows only refine names CollectionProperties already declares; they never declare their own. EditFixedSize is load-bearing: it suppresses the details panel's add/insert/delete AND reset-to-default, the latter of which would otherwise wipe every row in one click (the CDO default is empty). Rows are minted and re-keyed through the EDITOR_* helpers below.

fields.name: PropertyOverrides
fields.tooltip: Schema-parallel, exactly like an entry's -- same SyncToSchema / ApplyHeaderIdRemap contract.

CategoryOverrides.semantics: Rows are minted from the collection editor's grid, at the gear on a category group header, rather than by adding array elements here.
CategoryOverrides.trap: A blank category never matches a row. Uncategorized entries skip the middle tier entirely and fall from their own overrides straight to the collection defaults, whatever rows exist.

hints.text: The settings on this page are the collection-level half of the asset. The per-entry half, weight, category, tags, the sub-collection flag, the fitting and grammar sources, property overrides and the baked staging slot, lives on the entry and is shared by every type just as widely; each type adds its own payload fields beside it.

Pointing a sub-collection entry at a collection that would close a cycle is refused by clearing the reference. The slot goes back to empty on the same edit that introduced the cycle, with an error in the log, so a nesting that quietly does not stick is a cycle rather than a failed edit. Dragging such a collection onto the grid is skipped instead.

Editing any setting on a collection re-stages every entry in it, which on a long list is not free and can pick up asset changes made since the last rebuild. Dragging a slider does not trigger it; releasing the drag does.

Entry identities are minted rather than authored, so a collection whose rows have none yet gets them the first time something asks: on any staging rebuild, when the editor opens it, or when an entry picker is pointed at it, which announces the mint in a toast. Each of those marks the asset dirty, and until it is saved a reference from another asset to one of its rows does not survive a restart.

UPCGExAssetStagingSettings.name: Staging : Distribute
UPCGExAssetStagingSettings.purpose: This is where a point gets its entry. Distribute takes points and a collection, asks the selector wired to its Selector pin which entry each point gets, fits the entry's staged bounds into the point's bounds, and records the decision. Staging decides and records the pick; spawning happens later, in vanilla mesh spawners driven by PCGEx Mesh Selector Staged, or in the dedicated Staging : spawn nodes for actors, levels and PCG data. The same node also reopens a decision it already made: the palette entry Staging : Redistribute preconfigures it to read an upstream Collection Map and re-pick the points staged on a sub-collection entry, and Staging : Randomize Materials preconfigures the same map-reading path to re-roll material variants and nothing else.
UPCGExAssetStagingSettings.situation: Points exist and something has to decide what each of them becomes, or an earlier decision has to be partly rolled again without disturbing the rest.

mechanism.text: One pass over the points, one entry decided per point. The Out pin carries the input points minus anything pruning removed, the Map carries one row per collection the picks reached, and Sockets carries one point per socket of each staged entry. Which pipeline runs is decided by Source Mode, and inside Collection Map source mode by Redistribution Mode.

off_label.claim: Flatten Sub Collections is the setting that gives Redistribute Collections anything to do. Every ordinary pick descends to a leaf, so no point ever carries a sub-collection pick unless flattening left one behind on purpose. Staging flat now and redistributing later splits one decision into two graph stages that re-roll independently.
off_label.grounded_in: FSelectorHelper::GetEntry descends through GetEntryWeightedRandom whenever the picked entry has a valid sub-collection and flattening is off; Boot in Collection Map source mode builds its routing table only from entries where HasValidSubCollection is true.

off_label.claim: Flatten Sub Collections stays available in Collection Map source mode and is applied to the re-pick, so a chain of Redistribute nodes walks a nested collection one level per node instead of resolving the whole subtree at once.
off_label.grounded_in: the bFlattenSubCollections edit condition excludes only Redistribute Micro Cache, and the point loop passes it into the same GetEntry call in map mode.

off_label.claim: Redistribute Micro Cache runs with nothing on the Selector pin, driven by the inline Distribution (Micro-cache) settings, and folds the node's own Seed into the roll. That makes the node a one-property material re-roll on already-staged data.
off_label.grounded_in: the Selector pin drops to Advanced when IsMicroRedistribution is true, Boot skips the missing-factory error, and FMicroSelectorHelper is constructed from EntryDistributionSettings when SelectorFactory is null.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to stage. One entry is decided per point.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The upstream Collection Map the staged picks resolve against. It accepts several datasets, so branches merged upstream resolve together. A map that rebuilds no valid collection is an execution error.
inputs.condition: when Source Mode is Collection Map, where the pin only exists

inputs.label: Selector
inputs.note: The sub-node deciding which entry each point gets. Exactly one factory is accepted, and more than one is an execution error. In Legacy selector mode the pin is ignored entirely; in Redistribute Micro Cache it is optional and drives the variant re-pick when connected.
inputs.condition: when Selector Mode is External and the mode is not Redistribute Micro Cache

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which points participate. A point the filters reject takes the same route as a failed pick, so it is pruned or sentinel-marked, never passed along untouched.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The staged points, one per input point minus anything pruning removed.

outputs.label: Map
outputs.note: The Collection Map that keeps the written hashes resolvable, one row per collection the picks reached. In Collection Map source mode it is a superset of the incoming map, so pass-through picks stay resolvable downstream.
outputs.condition: when Output Mode is Collection Map

outputs.label: Sockets
outputs.note: One point per socket of each staged entry.
outputs.condition: when Output Sockets is on, and never in Redistribute Micro Cache

SourceMode.tooltip: Where the collection(s) to distribute from come from. Default reads SourceCollection (asset reference or per-point path attribute). Collection Map reads already-staged picks from an upstream Collection Map and redistributes them according to Redistribution Mode; unresolvable points always pass through untouched.
SourceMode.semantics: This chooses which pipeline runs, and the pin set follows it: Collection Map adds the required Map input and takes Source Collection away. The node subtitle reports the choice, reading Staging [ Collection Map ] or Staging [ Micro Cache ] where Default mode shows the collection name.
SourceMode.trap: Collection Map source mode never fails a point. Anything that does not resolve to something redistributable leaves with every attribute intact, which is why Prune Empty Points is greyed out and ignored there.

RedistributionMode.tooltip: What gets redistributed when consuming a Collection Map. Collections re-picks entries for points whose staged entry is a sub-collection. Micro Cache keeps every staged entry pick and only re-randomizes the entry's micro cache selection (secondary index, e.g. mesh material variants) -- lets you refresh material assignments without changing the asset distribution.
RedistributionMode.semantics: Redistribute Collections needs points staged on a sub-collection entry, which exist only when the upstream Distribute had Flatten Sub Collections on. With none in the map the node warns and passes everything through. Redistribute Micro Cache reduces the node to re-rolling material variants: fitting, weight, entry type, translation and socket output are skipped, and leaving any of them enabled produces a warning naming the setting being ignored.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SourceCollection.semantics: The Constant form stages the whole input from one collection. The Attribute form reads an asset path per point, and every collection it names is discovered and loaded before processing, so a single dataset can stage from many collections at once. A Build Asset Collection node's transient output wires into the Constant override, which is how a collection assembled inside the graph gets staged from.
SourceCollection.trap: Nodes migrated from the removed Attribute Set source arrive with an empty Constant and error on execution. The message names Build Asset Collection as the replacement path.

OutputMode.semantics: Collection Map writes the int64 pick hash and emits the Map, which is what every downstream staging node consumes. Point Attributes writes the resolved asset path and emits no Map, ending the point's participation in the staging ecosystem; what survives is readable by anything that understands a soft-path attribute.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node writes to. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>), letting multiple staging layers stack on the same data.
StagingLayer.semantics: Layers are how one point carries several picks at once: each staging pass writes to its own layer, and every staging consumer carries a matching Staging Layer setting deciding which one it reads. Producers and consumers pair on the layer name; the default layer is where every node reads and writes until told otherwise.

AssetPathAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write asset path to.

bFlattenSubCollections.tooltip: If enabled, doesn't go through collections recursively and assign top-level collections "as assets"
bFlattenSubCollections.semantics: Off, a pick that lands on a sub-collection entry keeps descending by weighted random until it reaches a leaf, so the recorded pick names the leaf and the nesting is gone. On, the sub-collection entry itself is the pick, staged against its aggregate bounds. That is the only way a point ends up carrying a sub-collection pick, and it is what Redistribute Collections later reopens.

SelectorMode.tooltip: How distribution is configured for this node. Legacy uses the inline settings below -- only set for legacy nodes. External uses a factory on the Selector input pin.
SelectorMode.semantics: Nodes saved before the selector system arrive on Legacy, where the inline Distribution settings drive the pick, the Selector pin is ignored, and every execution warns that the mode is scheduled for removal. Nodes created since take External. Migration is switching the mode and wiring a Selector : Classic configured the way the inline settings were.

DistributionSettings.tooltip: Distribution details Note : LEGACY Nodes only.

fields.name: Category
fields.tooltip: Category name source (constant or per-point attribute).

fields.name: MissingCategoryBehavior
fields.tooltip: What to do when a point asks for a category the collection cannot serve. A blank key selects the uncategorized entries, and only counts as missing when there are none.

fields.name: Distribution
fields.tooltip: Distribution type

fields.name: IndexSettings
fields.tooltip: Index settings

fields.name: LocalSeed
fields.tooltip: Only accounted for if selected in the seed component.

EntryDistributionSettings.tooltip: Distribution details that are specific to the picked entry -- what it picks depends on the type of collection being staged. For Mesh Collections, this let you control how materials are picked. Drives Micro Cache redistribution when no Selector is connected; otherwise LEGACY Nodes only.

fields.name: Distribution
fields.tooltip: Distribution type

fields.name: IndexSettings
fields.tooltip: Index settings

bApplyFitting.semantics: On by default, and the defaults are not neutral: uniform Min scale-to-fit with justification active on all three axes, so staged points differ visibly from what the same points would produce through a bare spawner. Off leaves the transform and bounds exactly as they arrived, and the Sockets output still works because sockets come from the entry rather than from the fit. Fitting runs entirely against baked staging bounds; nothing the entries reference is loaded to solve it.

fields.name: ScaleToFitMode
fields.tooltip: How scaling is applied to fit within target bounds. None = no scaling, Uniform = same scale all axes, Individual = per-axis control.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: Uniform scaling strategy. Fill = stretch to fill, Min = fit smallest axis, Max = fit largest axis, Avg = average.

fields.name: ScaleToFitX
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for X axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitY
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Y axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitZ
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Z axis when using Individual mode.

bConsiderEntryScaleToFit.tooltip: When enabled, entries that define a Scale to Fit override (entry-local or collection-global) replace this node's Scale to Fit for their points.

bConsiderEntryJustification.tooltip: When enabled, entries that define a Justification override (entry-local or collection-global) replace this node's Justification for their points.

fields.name: Offset
fields.tooltip: When to apply random offset variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.tooltip: When to apply random rotation variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

fields.name: Scale
fields.tooltip: When to apply random scale variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

bPruneEmptyPoints.tooltip: If enabled, filter output based on whether a staging has been applied or not (empty entry).  Current implementation is slow. Not applicable in Collection Map source mode, where unresolvable points always pass through untouched.
bPruneEmptyPoints.semantics: This decides whether a failure is visible. On, failed points are gathered out at the end of the pass and the output is shorter than the input. Off, they stay in place carrying a sentinel, a hash of -1 or an empty asset path, and every downstream staging node skips them.
bPruneEmptyPoints.trap: It does nothing when the input points already carry the pick attribute from an earlier staging pass. Those points keep their earlier values instead, so nothing is pruned and nothing is sentinel-marked, and a second staging pass over already-staged points always returns the same count it received.

EntryTypeFilter.tooltip: Lets you filter which collection type gets staged. This is most useful when using per-point collections and you want to stage only certain types of assets.

fields.name: TypeFilter
fields.tooltip: Type inclusion map - keys are read-only, populated from registry

fields.name: bIncludeInvalid
fields.tooltip: Include/exclude invalid/unresolved entries

EntryTypeFilter.semantics: A point whose pick resolves to an excluded type takes the failure path, so it is pruned or sentinel-marked. Staging : Type Filter routes the points it does not keep; this discards them. In Redistribute Micro Cache the same filter decides which entries get their variant refreshed, and the entries it excludes pass through with their pick intact.

EntryTypeAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the FName entry type will be written to

WeightToAttribute.tooltip: Update point scale so staged asset fits within its bounds
WeightToAttribute.semantics: Raw and Normalized write to the weight attribute; the two Density options bypass that attribute and write into the point's Density property. Normalization is against the pool the pick actually came out of, so a category-restricted pick normalizes against that category and a pick that descended into a sub-collection normalizes against the sub-collection, never against the root collection's total.

WeightAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write asset weight to.
WeightAttributeName.edit_condition: WeightToAttribute != EPCGExWeightOutputMode::NoOutput && WeightToAttribute != EPCGExWeightOutputMode::NormalizedToDensity && WeightToAttribute != EPCGExWeightOutputMode::NormalizedInvertedToDensity && (SourceMode != EPCGExDistributeSourceMode::CollectionMap || RedistributionMode != EPCGExRedistributionMode::MicroCache)

bOutputMaterialPicks.tooltip: If enabled, will output mesh material picks.
bOutputMaterialPicks.semantics: Writes one soft-path attribute per material slot, named from the prefix and the slot index, carrying the variant each point picked. Only mesh entries have variants, and a Constant collection of another type disables the option with a warning.
bOutputMaterialPicks.trap: In Collection Map output mode the toggle is greyed out but not reset, and the element still honours it, so a graph switched over from Point Attributes keeps writing the slot attributes alongside the hash.

MaxMaterialPicks.tooltip: If > 0 will create dummy attributes for missing material indices up to a maximum; in order to create a full, fixed-length list of valid (yet null) attributes for the static mesh spawner material overrides. Otherwise, will only create attribute for valid indices.
MaxMaterialPicks.semantics: At zero the attribute set is sized from the highest slot index any picked entry actually used, so the same graph can emit a different number of attributes from run to run as picks change. A fixed value produces the same set every time, which is what a Static Mesh Spawner's material override list needs to bind against.

MaterialAttributePrefix.tooltip: Prefix to be used for material slot picks.

TranslationAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the FVector attribute to write fitting offset to. This is the translation added to the point transform according to staging/justification rules. Mostly useful for offsetting spline meshes.

bQuietEmptyCollectionError.tooltip: Suppress warnings when the asset collection is empty or has no valid entries.
bQuietEmptyCollectionError.semantics: It also silences the two Collection Map pass-through warnings: a map holding no sub-collection entries, and a map holding no entries with refreshable variants. Both mean the node will pass its whole input through unchanged, so silencing them removes the only signal that a Redistribute did nothing.

hints.text: A selector is required. A Distribute with an empty **Selector** pin errors on execution, which makes it the most common first-contact failure: wire a **Selector : Classic** in weighted-random mode.

Picking loads the collections, never the content they reference. Bounds, sockets and material variants all come from the entries' staged data, which is why a hundred thousand points can be staged against assets the graph never touches.
Pruning is on by default, so a Distribute that cannot serve some of its points quietly returns fewer points than it received. Count the output before assuming a downstream node dropped them.

UPCGExAttributeCheckFilterProviderSettin.name: Data Filter : Attribute Exists
UPCGExAttributeCheckFilterProviderSettin.purpose: Asks whether a dataset declares an attribute of a given name, and answers for the dataset as a whole. It reads the roster of attribute names the data carries, across both the element domain and the `@Data` domain, and reads no values at all; testing what an attribute holds at dataset level is a `@Data` selector on a point filter instead. `Match` widens the question from one spelled-out name to a pattern, `Domain` restricts which side of the data is searched, and `Type` adds a second condition on what the attribute stores.
UPCGExAttributeCheckFilterProviderSettin.situation: Datasets arriving from several branches, where the work downstream needs an attribute only some of them were built with.

mechanism.text: The filter walks the names of every attribute the dataset's metadata holds and passes at the first one that matches. `Domain` decides which declared names are eligible, `Match` decides how each name is measured against the text you typed, and `Type` adds a second condition the same attribute has to satisfy. Nothing is read from the values, so the verdict depends only on what the dataset declares.

off_label.claim: With `Match` set to `Matches` and a query of a single asterisk, the test passes any dataset carrying at least one attribute of any name, which turns the node into a check for whether the data carries metadata at all.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExStringMatchMode::Matches routes to FString::MatchesWildcard, and the loop only ever visits attributes that exist

outputs.label: Data Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. The Data Filter family qualifies for dataset-level evaluation by construction, with no condition on how the node is configured, so every filter pin in the plugin takes it, **Uber Branch** and **Break** included.

UPCGExAttributeHashSettings.name: Attribute Hash
UPCGExAttributeHashSettings.purpose: Reduces one attribute's values, across a whole dataset, to a single integer that identifies them. Two datasets carrying the same values under that attribute produce the same number, and by default the order they are in and how often each value repeats are both ignored, so the number identifies the set rather than the sequence. That is what makes it useful as a fingerprint: a key to group datasets by, a value to compare against a later run, or a stable per-dataset seed that only changes when the data does.
UPCGExAttributeHashSettings.situation: Several datasets have to be told apart, or matched up, by what one of their attributes holds.

mechanism.text: The points pass through and one value per dataset is produced, written into the `@Data` domain as an `int32` and, when asked, as a tag alongside it. Each point's value is hashed on its own, the resulting numbers are collected, optionally reduced to distinct ones and optionally sorted, and the whole sequence is hashed once more into the answer. Which points contribute is `Scope`, and its two end-point modes read only the first and last rows rather than walking the data. Nothing on the points is written and no attribute is consumed.

off_label.claim: Hash a constant-per-dataset attribute with `Scope` on First only and the node becomes a cheap grouping key: every dataset sharing that value gets the same number, without reading past the first row.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExDataHashScope::First skips compilation entirely and takes the value hash of row 0 in FAttributeHasher::Init

off_label.claim: Two hashes of the same attribute, one with sorting on and one off, differ exactly when the order changed, so running both and comparing detects a reordering that a single hash is designed not to see.
off_label.grounded_in: bSortInputValues is what makes the collected value hashes order-independent before CityHash32 runs over them

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points whose attribute is hashed. Each dataset is hashed on its own.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, carrying the hash where the output settings put it.

HashConfig.tooltip: Configuration for which attributes to hash and how.

fields.name: SourceAttribute
fields.tooltip: Which attribute should be used to generate the hash

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Which values will be combined to a hash

fields.name: Sorting
