fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Height.semantics: Read per point, so a footprint can vary in height along its length. Each convex piece takes the tallest value among its own points, so the stepping follows the decomposition rather than the point spacing.
Height.trap: Vertices the triangulation created, at ring intersections for instance, have no source point and contribute a height of zero, so a piece made only of such vertices falls back to Min Thickness.

MinThickness.tooltip: Minimum extrusion height. Pieces thinner than this are clamped up so the prism never collapses.
MinThickness.semantics: The floor under the resolved height, applied per piece. It exists so a prism can never collapse to zero thickness and produce degenerate collision.

BaseMode.tooltip: How each convex piece's floor Z is chosen from its points, so the volume steps to follow uneven input (Flat keeps one shared floor).
BaseMode.semantics: Flat puts every piece on one plane at the whole footprint's lowest point, which is the only mode that gives a single flat-bottomed volume. Min, Max and Average instead give each piece its own floor from its own points, so the underside steps to follow uneven input. The prism is always flat-bottomed either way; what changes is where that bottom sits.

bMergeConvexPieces.tooltip: If enabled, greedily merge triangles into larger convex pieces (Hertel-Mehlhorn). Disable for raw per-triangle prisms.
bMergeConvexPieces.semantics: Merging gives fewer, larger pieces, which is cheaper for physics. It also coarsens both the height and the floor, since each is resolved per piece: turning it off gives one prism per triangle and the closest following of uneven input.

MaxConvexPieces.tooltip: Safety cap on convex pieces per volume. Volumes exceeding this are skipped with a warning (protects physics broadphase).
MaxConvexPieces.semantics: A ceiling on physics cost. A footprint that decomposes into more pieces than this is not simplified, it is abandoned: no actor is spawned for it and the run warns.

bOverrideCollisionProfile.tooltip: If enabled, override the spawned volume's collision profile with the one below (Volume mode). Otherwise the class default is kept.
bOverrideCollisionProfile.semantics: Volume mode keeps the class's own collision unless this is set, so a custom volume class that already collides correctly needs nothing here.

CollisionProfileName.tooltip: Collision profile applied to the spawned volume's brush component when the override is enabled (Volume mode).

CollisionBody.tooltip: Full collision setup (preset/object type/responses) applied to the spawned static-mesh collider (Primitive mode). Defaults to a blocking profile.
CollisionBody.semantics: Primitive mode's full collision setup rather than a profile name, since a bare collider has no class defaults worth keeping. It ships blocking. Physics simulation is forced off whatever this carries.

AttachOptions.tooltip: Controls where each spawned volume/primitive actor lands in the Outliner: in a folder named after the target actor (default), attached to it, or loose at the root. The anchor is the PCG component's target actor.
AttachOptions.semantics: Anchored on the PCG component's target actor. In Folder keeps the Outliner tidy without changing any transform; Attached parents the volumes so they move with the target.

ActorReferenceAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the soft-object-path attribute written into each output volume's @Data domain (points at the spawned actor).
ActorReferenceAttributeName.semantics: Written into the emitted data's @Data domain, not onto any point, which is how a later node reaches the actor that was spawned.

bQuietTriangulationWarnings.tooltip: Suppress per-group warnings about degenerate footprints / failed triangulation.

PostProcessFunctionNames.tooltip: Specify a list of functions to be called on the target actor after actor creation. Functions need to be parameter-less and with "CallInEditor" flag enabled.
PostProcessFunctionNames.semantics: Parameterless functions marked callable in editor, run on the spawned actors after creation. The route for anything the settings above cannot configure.

MainDataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, matches main inputs into pre-groups (by tags / @Data) before the grouping policy below is applied within each. If disabled, the grouping policy alone partitions the inputs.
MainDataMatching.semantics: Runs before the grouping policy and partitions the inputs into pre-groups, so the policy is then applied within each. Wire it when several unrelated sets of paths arrive on one pin and should not be allowed to nest into one another.

MainInputGroupingPolicy.tooltip: How main inputs are grouped. With data matching enabled this applies *within* each matched pre-group; otherwise it applies across all main inputs.
MainInputGroupingPolicy.semantics: Decides how many volumes a set of paths becomes. Auto reads the nesting: an outer path and the rings inside it become one volume with the rings as holes, while unrelated footprints stay apart. Separate gives one volume per path and Merged folds every path in the group into one. Auto is the default this node ships with, whatever the settings table says.

hints.text: Spawned actors are owned by a managed resource and re-created on every generation; the node is never cached. Treat the actors as regenerating output rather than as something to hand-edit in the level.
Under Primitive, the static mesh is a collision carrier: the component is set invisible and its only render geometry is a placeholder box the cook needs. Nothing about it is meant to be seen.

UPCGExClusterCentralitySettings.name: Cluster : Centrality
UPCGExClusterCentralitySettings.purpose: Scores every Vtx by how central it is to its cluster and writes the score as one double attribute. Six measures are on offer and they disagree with each other by design: three walk the cluster from every Vtx (Betweenness, Closeness, Harmonic Closeness), one counts edges (Degree), and two settle by repeated passes over the connections (Eigenvector, Katz). The three walking measures carry no length of their own, so what counts as the cheapest route between two Vtx is decided entirely by the heuristics wired to the Heuristics pin, which is why that pin is required for them and ignored by the other three.
UPCGExClusterCentralitySettings.situation: A cluster where the next operation has to treat junctions differently from dead ends, and the difference has to arrive as a number sitting on each Vtx.

mechanism.text: Vtx in, the same Vtx out with one double attribute added, and the Edges pass through untouched. Every Vtx of a cluster gets a raw score from the chosen measure, then Normalize, OneMinus and Contrast reshape it against that cluster's own range. A Vtx dataset shared by several Edges datasets is scored once per Edges dataset, so each connected component is normalized against its own highest score. Centrality Type is the only thing that changes what is computed, and the rows below it change with it.
steps: The chosen measure produces a raw score for every Vtx of the cluster.
Normalize divides those scores by the cluster's highest one, so the most central Vtx lands on exactly 1, and OneMinus then flips the result.
Contrast reshapes whatever came out of that, remapped across the range those values actually span and back into it, so it never pushes a value outside the range it started in.

off_label.claim: Degree with Normalize off writes the plain edge count on every Vtx, which is the same figure Cluster : Vtx Properties writes, reachable here without wiring a sub-node.
off_label.grounded_in: The Degree branch of FProcessor::Process fills CentralityScores from Nodes[i].Links.Num() and goes straight to WriteResults with no further pass

off_label.claim: Betweenness with Downsampling Mode set to Filters and a filter that passes a handful of Vtx stops being a global measure and becomes a traffic map: every Vtx is credited with the routes leaving those chosen origins alone.
off_label.grounded_in: TryStartCompute rebuilds the sample from IsNodePassingFilters, and ProcessSingleNode_Betweenness credits every Vtx along the sampled origin's own shortest-path tree rather than only the origin

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster to score, and where the result is written.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Every Edges dataset that finds its Vtx is one cluster and one score pass.

inputs.label: Heuristics
inputs.note: What an edge costs, which is the only notion of length the three walking measures have. Several heuristics combine through Heuristics Score Mode. The other three measures never read the pin.
inputs.condition: required when Centrality Type is Betweenness, Closeness or Harmonic Closeness

inputs.label: VtxFilters
inputs.note: Which Vtx the walks start from. Read only in the one configuration that uses it, and left alone otherwise.
inputs.condition: required when Centrality Type is one of the three walking measures and Downsampling Mode is Filters

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, carrying the centrality attribute.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged.

CentralityType.semantics: Betweenness walks out of every Vtx along cheapest routes and credits each Vtx in between with its share of the routes crossing it, halving the total at the end because an undirected cluster meets every pair twice; the result counts routes, so its raw scale grows with the cluster and carries no division by the pair count. Closeness scores a Vtx by how many Vtx it reached divided by what reaching them cost, which is one over the mean cost. Harmonic Closeness adds one over each individual cost instead, so a Vtx it cannot reach contributes nothing rather than spoiling the figure. Degree is the count of edges meeting at the Vtx, never zero because being an edge endpoint is what puts a Vtx in the cluster, and a duplicate edge between the same pair counts twice. Eigenvector repeats a pass where each Vtx takes the sum of its neighbours' current values and the whole set is rescaled to unit length. Katz repeats a pass where each Vtx takes Katz Alpha times that same sum plus one, so every Vtx keeps a floor of one however isolated it is.
CentralityType.trap: Only the first three read the Heuristics pin. Degree, Eigenvector and Katz work from the connections alone, so edge length, geometry and anything wired to that pin change nothing about their result.

HeuristicScoreMode.tooltip: Scoring mode for combining multiple heuristics
HeuristicScoreMode.edit_condition: CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::Betweenness || CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::Closeness || CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::HarmonicCloseness
HeuristicScoreMode.semantics: How several heuristics collapse into the one number that stands in for an edge's length. With a single heuristic wired the mode changes nothing. Because that number is the only cost the three walking measures know, the shape of the result follows the heuristics rather than the cluster's geometry: a stack that scores flat ground cheap and steep ground dear yields a centrality of walkable routes, not of straight lines.

CentralityValueAttributeName.semantics: The value is a double, written on the Vtx. A Vtx in the incoming dataset that belongs to none of the clusters the node processed is never visited, and keeps the attribute's starting value, which is 1 when OneMinus is on and 0 otherwise.

bNormalize.tooltip: Discrete mode write the number as-is, relative will normalize against the highest number of overlaps found.
bNormalize.semantics: Divides every score by the highest one found in the same cluster, so the most central Vtx lands on exactly 1. Raw scales differ wildly between the six measures, from an integer edge count through a route tally to a Katz value floored at one, and this is what makes any of them usable as a 0 to 1 weight downstream. When every score in a cluster is zero the whole cluster is written flat instead.
bNormalize.trap: The maximum is per cluster, so a Vtx dataset carrying several Edges datasets ends up with one Vtx scoring 1 in each connected component, and values from different components cannot be compared with each other.

bOutputOneMinus.tooltip: Whether to do a OneMinus on the normalized overlap count value
bOutputOneMinus.semantics: Flips the normalized value, so the most central Vtx becomes 0 and the least central becomes 1. It also sets what an untouched Vtx carries, because the attribute starts at 1 under this setting instead of 0.

bApplyContrast.tooltip: Apply a contrast curve to reshape the value distribution.
bApplyContrast.semantics: Runs after Normalize and OneMinus, over whatever range the values then span, and maps the result back into that same range. With Normalize off it works on the raw range instead of on 0 to 1, and a cluster whose values are all the same is left alone.

ContrastAmount.tooltip: Contrast amount. 1.0 = no change, >1 = more contrast, <1 = less contrast
ContrastAmount.semantics: Exactly 1 is a no-op and the curve is skipped outright. Above 1 pushes values away from the middle of the range, below 1 pulls them toward it.

MaxIterations.tooltip: Maximum iterations for iterative centrality types (Eigenvector, Katz)
MaxIterations.semantics: The hard stop for Eigenvector and Katz. Reaching it is not reported, so a run that ran out of iterations before settling looks like any other run; the value written is whatever the last pass produced.

Tolerance.tooltip: Convergence tolerance for iterative centrality types (Eigenvector, Katz)
Tolerance.semantics: Eigenvector stops when the total change across all Vtx in one pass falls below this. Katz stops on the largest single change instead, which is the stricter of the two tests on a large cluster.

KatzAlpha.tooltip: Attenuation factor for Katz centrality. Must be less than 1/lambda_max (largest eigenvalue).
KatzAlpha.semantics: Each pass multiplies a Vtx's neighbour sum by this before adding the baseline of one, so it decides how far influence carries. It has to stay below one over the cluster's largest eigenvalue, and one over the highest edge count found on any Vtx is a safe stand-in for that bound: the shipped 0.1 holds while no Vtx has more than ten edges.
KatzAlpha.trap: Past that bound the values grow with every pass instead of settling, and the run stops only when Max Iterations runs out. Normalize then divides by a number that ran away, crushing everything outside the densest neighbourhood to near zero.

DownsamplingMode.tooltip: Downsampling strategy to reduce processing time on large clusters. Only applies to path-based centrality types.
DownsamplingMode.edit_condition: CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::Betweenness || CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::Closeness || CentralityType == EPCGExCentralityType::HarmonicCloseness
DownsamplingMode.semantics: Which Vtx the walks start from. None starts one from every Vtx. Random ratio draws a subset. Filters takes the Vtx that pass the wired filters, which is the one mode where the selection is yours to choose rather than random. Either sampling mode then scales the accumulated scores by the ratio of Vtx to samples.
DownsamplingMode.trap: A sample that comes out empty, which a filter passing nothing will do, falls back to a single Vtx and scales its result by the whole Vtx count.

RandomDownsampling.tooltip: If enabled, only compute centrality on a subset of the nodes to get a rough approximation. This is useful for large clusters, or if you want to tradeoff precision for speed.

fields.name: BaseSeed
fields.tooltip: Seed for random number generation.

fields.name: Units
fields.tooltip: How amount is interpreted: Relative = 0-1 percentage, Discrete = fixed count.

fields.name: RelativeAmount
fields.tooltip: Percentage of items to pick (0 = none, 1 = all).

fields.name: DiscreteAmount
fields.tooltip: Exact number of items to pick.

fields.name: ClampMin
fields.tooltip: Minimum number of items to pick regardless of relative amount.

fields.name: ClampMax
fields.tooltip: Maximum number of items to pick regardless of relative amount.

RandomDownsampling.semantics: The draw is over the cluster's Vtx, so a relative amount is a share of that cluster rather than of the incoming Vtx dataset, and a cluster split across several Edges datasets draws separately in each.

hints.text: Downsampling is an approximation for Betweenness alone. A Betweenness walk credits every Vtx it passes through, so a sample still touches most of the cluster. Closeness and Harmonic Closeness credit only the Vtx the walk started from, so under either sampling mode every Vtx outside the sample is left at zero and then the sampled ones are scaled up. The result reads as a sparse scattering of high values over a field of zeroes.

Closeness and Harmonic Closeness are computed over what each walk actually reached, so a cluster arriving as one Edges dataset with several disconnected islands in it scores each island against itself rather than producing an undefined result.

UPCGExClusterDecompositionSettings.name: Cluster : Decomposition
UPCGExClusterDecompositionSettings.purpose: Splits a cluster's Vtx into groups and writes each Vtx's group as an integer `CellID`. The cluster comes out unchanged, connections and all; the grouping arrives as an attribute on the Vtx, and whatever acts on it downstream is a partition, a filter or a colouring that reads that attribute. The grouping rule is the `Decomposition` sub-node, and the seven that ship divide either by quantising space into boxes or by grouping the Vtx themselves, on connectivity or on a numeric attribute. Two more attributes are available on request: how many Vtx share a group, and the size of the box that group occupies.
UPCGExClusterDecompositionSettings.situation: One large cluster that has to be worked on in pieces, where the pieces are decided by a rule and carried as an attribute instead of by cutting the cluster apart.

mechanism.text: One execution takes a cluster and returns the same cluster with one integer attribute added to every Vtx. The Edges dataset is passed straight through, and the Vtx keep their positions, their order and everything already written on them. The sub-node decides the grouping on its own; the node runs it once per cluster and writes back what it gets. Ids are kept unique across the clusters in one execution: each Edges dataset gets its own block of a million, so two clusters sharing one Vtx dataset never land on the same id. A Vtx the rule did not place keeps the attribute's default of -1.

off_label.claim: Because each cluster's ids sit in their own block of a million, integer-dividing a written CellID by a million recovers which Edges dataset the Vtx belonged to, which is a cluster index the Vtx would otherwise not carry.
off_label.grounded_in: the per-cluster offset applied before the id is written, taken from the Edges data's index within the input collection

off_label.claim: The cell count attribute carries the whole group's population onto every one of its members, so removing Vtx whose count falls below a threshold discards the small fragments a rule produced without ever inspecting the ids themselves.
off_label.grounded_in: the per-group node count written to every member Vtx alongside the id

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx. The cell attributes are written here.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges. Read for connectivity and forwarded untouched.

inputs.label: Heuristics
inputs.note: Edge scoring for the rules that consult it. **Decompose : Spectral** always asks for it; **Decompose : Max Boxes (Extended)** asks only with its heuristic merge gating turned on. The pin sits under the advanced pins for every other selection.
inputs.condition: when the selected decomposition asks for heuristics

inputs.label: Overrides : Decomposition
inputs.note: Attribute set whose entries overwrite the selected rule's own properties by name. Sits under the advanced pins.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, carrying the cell attributes.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The Edges dataset, forwarded unchanged.

Decomposition.semantics: The node has no grouping rule of its own and errors out until one is picked. What is selected here also decides two things outside its own settings: whether the Heuristics pin is required, and what the cell size attribute measures, since the box-shaped rules report their own quantised box and the rest report the bounding box of their members' positions. The node subtitle in the graph names whichever rule is currently selected.

HeuristicScoreMode.tooltip: Scoring mode for combining multiple heuristics.
HeuristicScoreMode.semantics: Reaches anything only when the selected rule asks for heuristics and more than one is wired in, in which case it is how their scores fold into a single number. It stays visible and editable in every other configuration, where nothing reads it.

CellIDAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the decomposition cell ID written to each node.
CellIDAttributeName.semantics: Written to every Vtx of the incoming dataset, including any the rule did not place, which keep -1. Values already stored under this name are not carried over.
CellIDAttributeName.trap: This name, the cell count name and the cell size name have to be three different names. The node warns when two of them match, then writes both to the same attribute, and whichever flushes last is what survives.

CellCountAttributeName.tooltip: Optional attribute name for per-node cell count (how many nodes share this cell). Empty = disabled.
CellCountAttributeName.semantics: It counts Vtx, and every member of a group carries the whole group's total, so the value is constant across a group and directly comparable between them. A Vtx the rule did not place keeps 0, which is what separates it from a group of one.

CellSizeAttributeName.tooltip: Optional attribute name for per-node cell bounds size (FVector, full extent). Empty = disabled. The meaning is algorithm-specific: - Box-like algorithms (Grid, Max Boxes, BSP Occupancy) report their quantized cell box. For the three that have a transform space (Max Boxes, Max Boxes Extended, BSP Occupancy) that box is measured along the grid's LOCAL axes, so with Best Fit or Custom it is in that rotated (and, for a scaled Custom transform, scaled) frame and is NOT world-axis-aligned. Grid has no transform space: its boxes are world-axis-aligned. The value is the enclosing box: a non-cuboid cell (an L-shaped BSP Occupancy region, or a Grid cell merged from non-adjacent cells) reports the AABB that contains it, which can exceed its filled volume. - Node-grouping algorithms (Convex BSP, Spectral, Threshold) report the world-space AABB of the member node positions, so a single-node cell reports a zero-size vector.

hints.text: The ids are assigned per execution and mean nothing beyond the grouping. Changing the decomposition, changing any of its settings, or feeding the Edges datasets in a different order all renumber them, so a CellID is a key for this run and never a name to match against a stored value.

UPCGExClusterDiffuseSettings.name: Cluster : Diffuse
UPCGExClusterDiffuseSettings.purpose: Spreads attribute values outward from seeds across a cluster and reconciles them where the spreads overlap. Every seed grows its own diffusion and none of them claims anything, so a Vtx touched by four seeds carries all four contributions and one weighted blend decides what it ends up with. The node writes no attributes of its own: what lands on the Vtx is entirely the doing of the blend operations wired to its two blending pins, one reading from each seed's own Vtx and one reading from the seed points themselves.
UPCGExClusterDiffuseSettings.situation: Several sources need to paint values across a cluster and their reaches have to meet in a graded boundary rather than a hard one.

mechanism.text: Each seed claims one Vtx and grows a diffusion outward along edges from it, recording on every Vtx it reaches how many hops and how much edge length it took to get there. A Vtx reached by several diffusions keeps one contribution per diffusion, and after growth those contributions are weighted and blended onto the Vtx in a single pass. Vtx in, the same Vtx out with whatever the blend operations wrote; the Edges pass through untouched. A Vtx no diffusion reached, or one whose contributions all weigh nothing, is left exactly as it came in.
steps: Every diffusion grows to its full extent, limited only by the fill controls.
Weighting turns each contribution's depth or path length into a raw weight, and Weight Space decides whether those weights are normalized against each other or read as absolute intensities.
The blend runs once per reached Vtx, over both layers at once.

off_label.claim: Set Fill Rate to zero and every diffusion parks on its seed Vtx without spreading, which turns the node into a way of writing seed-point attributes onto the Vtx those seeds landed on, picked by proximity rather than by index.
off_label.grounded_in: TDiffusionGrowthProcessor::ProcessRange marks a diffusion stopped when the fill rate reads zero or less, and the seed's own capture is already in Captured from FDiffusion::Init

off_label.claim: Wire only Seed Blend Ops with a Copy operation and leave the other pin empty, and the diffusion becomes an assignment of seed identity: every Vtx receives the values of whichever seed dominates it, so the boundary between diffusions reads as a partition rather than a gradient.
off_label.grounded_in: The Relative path normalizes so the strongest seed reaches weight one and orders contributors dominant-first, and the multi-blend copies the first as its base

inputs.label: Edges

inputs.label: Seeds

fields.name: SeedPicking
fields.tooltip: Drive how a seed point selects a node.

fields.name: Ordering
fields.tooltip: Defines the sorting used for the vtx

fields.name: SortDirection
fields.tooltip: Sort direction

Seeds.semantics: A seed claims one Vtx and grows from there, so seeds are start points rather than regions, and Max Distance is a hard cut past which a seed claims nothing. Two seeds resolving to the same Vtx do not both diffuse: the one earlier in the Seeds dataset takes it and the other is dropped, and that outcome is fixed rather than left to whichever thread got there first. A cluster left with no diffusion at all is dropped from the output with a warning.
Seeds.trap: Ordering here changes which seed grows, not which one wins a contested Vtx later. Overlap is settled by the weights, not by order.

Processing.tooltip: Defines how each vtx is diffused
Processing.semantics: Diffusions never take a Vtx away from each other, so with nothing on the Fill Controls pin that couples them the set each one reaches comes out the same under either mode and this is a scheduling choice. It starts to matter once a control shares state between diffusions, Branch Limit being the one that does, at which point who arrives at a fork first decides who spends its budget there.

fields.name: Priority
fields.tooltip: Which data should be prioritized to 'drive' diffusion

fields.name: FillRateSource
fields.tooltip: Diffusion Rate type.

fields.name: FillRate
fields.tooltip: Diffusion rate -- how many steps each vtx grows per iteration. Zero preserves the vtx from being diffused on.

Diffusion.semantics: Priority decides which candidate a diffusion takes next, and Heuristics only means anything once a scoring fill control is supplying scores; with none wired every candidate scores the same and the order falls back to depth, which is what the Depth setting does outright. Fill Rate is how many Vtx a diffusion takes per iteration, and a rate of zero or less parks the diffusion on its seed without spreading at all.

Weighting.tooltip: What drives each seed's contribution weight when blended onto a vtx.
Weighting.semantics: Distance means the length of the route the diffusion actually travelled to the Vtx, not the straight line between seed and Vtx, so two diffusions meeting on the far side of a detour both weigh weakly there and the blend between them comes out smooth. Depth counts edges crossed instead, which ignores edge length entirely and suits a cluster whose spacing is irregular. Count gives every contribution the same weight, so the Vtx becomes the plain mean of everything that reached it, and Count plus Depth splits the difference by handing out half the weight equally and half by depth.
Weighting.trap: Under Falloff, Count has nothing to fade with: every contribution stays at full intensity to the diffusion's furthest reach, so the absolute space behaves like the relative one. Count plus Depth fades only to half intensity there, never below.

WeightSpace.tooltip: How the weights are interpreted. Relative = normalized/territorial (single seed always full). Falloff = absolute intensity that fades from each seed to its furthest reach.
WeightSpace.semantics: The dividing question is whether the weights are read against each other or against a fixed scale. Relative rescales each Vtx so its strongest seed reaches full intensity, which makes a lone seed a straight copy and turns Weighting into a tie-break that only bites where diffusions overlap. Falloff leaves the intensities as computed: each seed is full at its own Vtx and falls to nothing at the far edge of its own reach, so intensity carries real meaning per Vtx and overlaps add up rather than compete.
WeightSpace.trap: The two disagree about what a low value means. Under Relative there is no such thing as a weakly reached Vtx, because normalization pulls the strongest contributor back up to full every time; a falloff away from the seeds only exists under Falloff.

VtxParticipates.tooltip: Whether the vtx's own (pre-diffusion) value participates in the blend, alongside the seeds that reached it. When off, reached vtx are fully replaced by the seed blend.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

VtxParticipates.semantics: Adds the Vtx's own incoming value to the blend as one more contributor, so the result is a mix of what was there and what arrived rather than a replacement. Under Relative it joins as a peer of the strongest seed, which at Seed Factor 1 means an even split between the original and the winning seed. Under Falloff it takes whatever intensity the seeds left unspent, so it acts as a background the diffusion fades back into at its edges; without it, a Falloff Vtx at low intensity fades toward nothing instead.

SeedFactor.tooltip: Per-seed multiplier on each seed's contribution, read from the seeds point cloud. Scales how strongly each seed competes where diffusions overlap (1 = neutral). Has no effect on a vtx reached by a single seed.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SeedFactor.semantics: A per-seed multiplier read from the seed point, so one seed can be made to push further into a contested region than its neighbours. Under Relative it changes nothing on a Vtx only one seed reached, because a single contributor is normalized to full whatever its factor. Under Falloff it is an absolute multiplier and does bite there: a factor below one dims that seed's whole territory, and a factor of zero removes the seed's contribution altogether, leaving the Vtx untouched where nothing else reached it.

bUseLocalFalloffCurve.tooltip: Whether to shape the Falloff intensity with an in-editor curve or an external asset.
bUseLocalFalloffCurve.semantics: Switches between the curve authored on the node and a curve asset. Both rows are always present in the panel under Falloff and the one not selected is hidden, so a curve authored locally is kept when the toggle is flipped back and forth.

LocalFalloffCurve.tooltip: Curve that shapes the Falloff intensity (input: 1 at the seed, fading to 0 at the diffusion's furthest reach). Linear = no shaping.
LocalFalloffCurve.semantics: Shapes the intensity Weighting produced, before Seed Factor is applied. The input runs 1 at the seed to 0 at the diffusion's furthest reach, and a straight line through those two corners is what an unset curve behaves as.

FalloffCurve.tooltip: Curve that shapes the Falloff intensity (input: 1 at the seed, fading to 0 at the diffusion's furthest reach). Linear = no shaping.
FalloffCurve.semantics: Shapes the intensity Weighting produced, before Seed Factor is applied. An unset asset behaves as a straight line from 1 at the seed to 0 at the furthest reach.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: Curve lookup mode

fields.name: Samples
fields.tooltip: Number of samples in the lookup table.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.

hints.text: With neither blending pin wired the node still runs every diffusion and then writes nothing, so the Vtx come out exactly as they went in. The blend operations are what turn a diffusion into an output.

The furthest reach a Falloff intensity fades to is per diffusion, measured after growth finished. A seed whose fill controls stopped it after two hops fades to nothing across those two hops, while an unconstrained seed beside it fades across the whole cluster. Two seeds with different reaches do not share a scale.

UPCGExClusterDiffusionSettings.name: Cluster : Flood Fill
UPCGExClusterDiffusionSettings.purpose: Grows a spread outward from each seed until the fill controls stop it, then hands back what the spread learned. Every Vtx a spread reaches belongs to exactly one seed, so what comes out is a partition of the cluster into territories, each recorded on the Vtx as depth, normalised depth, capture order, travelled distance and whether the lane ended there. It also turns those territories into paths: one per lane end, either the whole run from the seed or cut into segments that meet at the branch points. **Cluster : Diffuse** shares the same growth engine and answers the other question, letting spreads overlap and blending what meets.
UPCGExClusterDiffusionSettings.situation: A branching structure has to be grown across a cluster from a handful of starting points, and both the reach and the lanes it took are wanted.

mechanism.text: Each seed point resolves to one Vtx and grows a diffusion from it along edges. A diffusion keeps a queue of candidate Vtx, takes the best one each step, claims it, and probes its neighbours for new candidates; a Vtx already claimed by any diffusion is refused, so nothing is ever reached twice. What decides the best candidate is its score when a heuristic fill control is supplying one, and its depth otherwise. Vtx in, the same Vtx out carrying whichever outputs were enabled, the Edges passing through unless the edge direction output is on, and one Paths dataset per lane when path output is asked for.
steps: Every seed resolves to its nearest Vtx, and a Vtx two seeds both resolve to goes to the earlier seed while the other seed is dropped.
All diffusions grow, under whichever of the two Processing rules is chosen.
Blend operations run once per claimed Vtx, and the seed attributes named by Seed Forwarding are copied onto it.
Lane ends are derived from the finished tree, and the path output walks back from each of them.

off_label.claim: Set Fill Rate to zero and every diffusion parks on its seed Vtx without spreading, which reduces the node to a proximity assignment: each seed claims one Vtx and forwards its attributes onto it.
off_label.grounded_in: TDiffusionGrowthProcessor::ProcessRange marks a diffusion stopped when the fill rate reads zero or less, and the seed capture is already in place from FDiffusion::Init

off_label.claim: With one seed per connected component and no fill controls, the diffusion depth written on every Vtx is a hop count from that component seed, and the endpoint flag marks the leaves of the spanning tree the fill happened to build.
off_label.grounded_in: FDiffusion::Grow captures until its candidate queue empties, and BuildEndpoints marks every capture with no child

fields.name: SortDirection
