Seeds.semantics: Seed Picking resolves each seed point to a Vtx and its Max Distance is a hard cut past which a seed claims nothing. Two seeds landing on the same Vtx do not both grow: the one earlier in the Seeds dataset takes it and the other is dropped, and that outcome is fixed rather than left to whichever thread arrived first. A cluster left with no diffusion at all is dropped from the output with a warning.
Seeds.trap: Ordering and Sort Direction are inert. Nothing reads either one, so seed order is always the order of the Seeds dataset.

Processing.tooltip: Defines how each vtx is diffused
Processing.semantics: Diffusions here compete for Vtx, so this changes the result rather than only the schedule. Parallel advances every diffusion by Fill Rate captures per round, so territories grow at comparable rates and settle wherever two fronts meet. Sequential runs each diffusion to exhaustion in seed order, so the first seed takes everything it can reach and later seeds are left with whatever survived.

fields.name: Priority
fields.tooltip: Which data should be prioritized to 'drive' diffusion

fields.name: FillRateSource
fields.tooltip: Diffusion Rate type.

fields.name: FillRate
fields.tooltip: Diffusion rate -- how many steps each vtx grows per iteration. Zero preserves the vtx from being diffused on.

Diffusion.semantics: Priority decides which queued candidate a diffusion takes next. Heuristics only means anything once a scoring fill control is supplying scores; with none wired every candidate scores the same and the order falls back to depth, which is what the Depth setting does outright. Fill Rate is how many Vtx a diffusion claims per round under Parallel, and a rate of zero or less parks that diffusion on its seed without spreading at all.

DiffusionDepthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute to write diffusion depth to.
DiffusionDepthAttributeName.semantics: Hops from the seed, 0 on the seed Vtx itself. Vtx no diffusion reached keep the writer default of -1, which is what separates them from a seed.

NormalizedDiffusionDepthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write normalized diffusion depth to.
NormalizedDiffusionDepthAttributeName.semantics: Divided by the deepest capture of the diffusion that claimed the Vtx, so every diffusion runs its own 0 to 1 whatever its reach. Two territories of very different sizes both read 1 at their far edge, and the values are not comparable across territories.

DiffusionOrderAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute to write order to.
DiffusionOrderAttributeName.semantics: The position of the Vtx in its own diffusion capture sequence, 0 at the seed. Counted per diffusion, so two territories both start at 0 and the numbers say nothing about which of them got there first in wall-clock terms.

DiffusionDistanceAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write diffusion distance to.
DiffusionDistanceAttributeName.semantics: The length of the route the diffusion actually travelled to reach the Vtx, summed edge by edge, rather than the straight line from the seed. A territory that had to go around an obstacle records the detour.

DiffusionEndingAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'bool' attribute to write diffusion ending to.
DiffusionEndingAttributeName.semantics: True on a capture that no later capture grew from, which is where a lane stopped. The seed is never marked, even when it is the only Vtx its diffusion took, and the count of marked Vtx is the number of lanes the path output will try to write.

EdgeDirectionOutput.tooltip: Output the diffusion traversal direction onto each edge, in propagation order (away from the seed).
EdgeDirectionOutput.semantics: Each diffusion counts depth from its own seed, so an edge whose two endpoints were claimed by different diffusions is oriented by comparing counters that started in different places. Turning this on is also what makes the node copy its Edges rather than forwarding them.

SeedForwarding.tooltip: Which Seed attributes to forward on the vtx they diffused to.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Is forwarding enabled.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

SeedForwarding.semantics: Copies attributes from the seed point onto every Vtx that seed claimed, which is the only route by which data living on the seeds alone reaches the cluster. The Blend Ops pin reads the seed Vtx instead, so the two carry different data even when they target the same rows.

PathOutput.tooltip: Controls how flood fill results are output as paths.
PathOutput.semantics: Full walks back from every lane end to the seed, so paths near a seed share most of their points and a busy seed produces a thick bundle. Partitions walks back only as far as the first point another path already took, so the same coverage arrives as segments meeting at the branch points, one per lane end either way. Both produce open paths whose points are copies of the Vtx, carrying the diffusion attributes written above and with the cluster tagging stripped.
PathOutput.trap: A walk that yields fewer than two points is discarded, so a lane end one hop from its seed can produce no path at all.

PathPartitions.tooltip: Criteria used to partition paths into separate outputs.
PathPartitions.semantics: Decides the order lane ends are processed in, which is what decides who claims the shared trunk. The first lane end processed writes the longest segment, all the way back to the seed, and every later one stops where it meets that path. Sorting by Depth descending, the default pair, gives the trunk to the deepest lane.

PartitionSorting.tooltip: Sort direction for partitioned output paths.
PartitionSorting.semantics: Reverses which end of the sorted list is served first, so it flips which lane keeps the trunk and which ones become short branches off it.

bWriteNormalizedPathDepth.tooltip: Write the normalized path depth (0-1) on output paths.

NormalizedPathDepthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write normalized path depth to.

NormalizedPathDepthMode.tooltip: How to normalize the path depth.
NormalizedPathDepthMode.semantics: Full Diffusion divides by the deepest capture in the whole diffusion, so a short path never reaches 1. Full Path divides by the depth of its own lane end, so a partitioned segment keeps its place inside the original run and might span 0.4 to 0.7. Partition rescales each segment to a full 0 to 1 of its own. Cascade builds a hierarchical falloff instead: the first segment written runs 1 at the seed down to 0 at its end, and every branch starts from whatever value its branch point already held and falls to 0 at its own end.
NormalizedPathDepthMode.trap: Cascade is only computed on the partitioned path writer. Under Full path output the attribute is still created and every point in it stays at 0.

SeedAttributesToPathTags.tooltip: Copy seed point attributes as tags on output paths.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Only affects how seed points are matched to Vtx. It changes nothing about the fill itself.

hints.text: Blending here is flat. Each blend operation reads its own `Weight` on the seed Vtx and applies the same result to every Vtx that diffusion claimed, so nothing fades with depth or distance. The graded version of that question belongs to **Cluster : Diffuse**, which carries the weighting and falloff machinery.

Every cluster resolves the whole Seeds dataset against itself, so a seed intended for one cluster also tries to start a diffusion in each of the others. `Max Distance` on Seed Picking, 200 by default, is what keeps a seed from reaching a cluster it was never meant for.

UPCGExClusterFilterFactoryData.name: Cluster Filter Definition
UPCGExClusterFilterFactoryData.purpose: The branch of the filter contract that is handed the cluster. A **Vtx Filter :** or **Edge Filter :** node emits on its own pin, **Vtx Filter** or **Edge Filter**, and that label is the passport: the **Vtx Filters** and **Edge Filters** pins take it, and no other pin does. Holding the cluster is what buys the tests a plain point filter cannot make, degree, neighbour direction, edge angle, endpoint comparison, and it is the same reason these filters go nowhere a cluster is absent.
UPCGExClusterFilterFactoryData.situation: Deciding whether a condition belongs on a Vtx Filters pin, on an Edge Filters pin, or on a plain point filter that would serve either.

mechanism.text: A consumer builds its stack once per cluster, after that cluster exists, and hands every filter three things rather than one: the cluster, the Vtx dataset and the Edges dataset. A Vtx filter is asked about one Vtx and reads the cluster for everything that Vtx connects to. An Edge filter is asked about one edge, reads that edge's own attributes from the Edges dataset, and keeps the Vtx dataset for values at the two endpoints. Neither family stands in for the other, so a Vtx filter is never asked about an edge, and the family label on the pin is what guarantees it. Given no cluster, binding fails outright and the filter is gone from the stack before any element is tested.

outputs.label: Vtx Filter
outputs.note: What every **Vtx Filter :** node emits. Read by **Vtx Filters** pins, and by a **Filter Group** that is itself headed for one.

outputs.label: Edge Filter
outputs.note: What every **Edge Filter :** node emits. Read by **Edge Filters** pins, and by a **Filter Group** headed for one.

hints.text: A Vtx filter and an Edge filter never stand in for each other, and swapping the two pins is a wiring the editor accepts. The wrong family is dropped when the node runs, so a pin left holding only the wrong one ends up empty: an optional pin then falls back to its default verdict, and a required one errors for missing input. A point filter is the only thing that serves both pins.

A cluster filter reaching a consumer that has no cluster does not fall back to point behaviour. Binding fails, the log says a Cluster filter is being used without cluster data, and `Initialization Failure Policy` then decides whether that filter is dropped, replaced by an always-true one, or collapses its whole pin to a single always-false.

**Filter Group** is the one carrier that crosses families. Its own **Filters** pin accepts every family, and the check on its children is deferred to whichever pin the group is wired into: the same group passes on a **Vtx Filters** pin and drops its Vtx children on an **Edge Filters** pin, warning that a grouped filter is of an unexpected type.

Cluster filters are shut out of dataset-level evaluation whatever their settings read. The `@Data` promotion that lets a **Filter :** node serve **Uber Filter (Data)**, **Uber Branch** and **Break** never reaches this branch, because binding to a cluster is per-cluster work by definition.

UPCGExClustersProcessorSettings.name: Edges Processor Settings
UPCGExClustersProcessorSettings.purpose: The shared surface behind every node that takes a cluster on its own two pins, from **Cluster : Refine** to **Pathfinding : Edges**. It owns the **Vtx** and **Edges** pin pair, the rules that sort a tangle of datasets on those pins into cluster pairs, and the model where each Edges dataset is processed as its own cluster against a shared Vtx dataset. Generators are the other half of the family and do not inherit it: they take points in and emit a cluster, so they have no pair to resolve. Two settings of its own live here, both advanced, and every other setting on a cluster node belongs to that node or to the plugin-wide surface.
UPCGExClustersProcessorSettings.situation: A cluster node was handed several Vtx and Edges datasets at once, and the question is which of them it paired, which it dropped, and how many times it ran.

mechanism.text: One execution takes everything on both pins at once. Datasets are sorted into pairs by their tags before any work starts, so a Vtx dataset and every Edges dataset carrying the same pair id become one group, and anything that cannot be placed in a group is dropped instead of forwarded. Each Edges dataset in a group is then handled as its own cluster against the shared Vtx dataset, so a node handed one Vtx and four Edges runs four times over one set of vertices, and the work that depends on the Vtx dataset alone is done once for the whole group. The output keeps the input's shape: the Vtx dataset on **Vtx**, one dataset per surviving cluster on **Edges**. Pairing is by tag rather than by wire, so several unrelated clusters can travel down one pair of wires and be processed in a single execution.

off_label.claim: Toggling a cluster node off forwards Vtx and Edges to their own output pins rather than only the primary one, so the pair survives the bypass and everything downstream still sees a cluster.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExClustersProcessorElement::DisabledPassThroughData, which appends the Edges inputs onto the Edges output pin after the base class forwards the main pin.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster to process. Accepts several datasets, matched to their Edges by tag rather than by wire order.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Every Edges dataset that finds its Vtx is one cluster and one run of the node.

inputs.label: Direction Sorting
inputs.note: Sort rule factories deciding which endpoint of an edge comes first. Rules are applied by their own priority value, ascending, and wire order is discarded.
inputs.condition: on nodes carrying an Edge Direction Settings block, only while its Direction Method is Endpoints Sort, and required whenever it appears

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The Vtx dataset, re-tagged with a fresh pair id.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per cluster the node kept, all sharing the Vtx dataset's pair id.

ScopedIndexLookupBuild.tooltip: Whether endpoint index lookups are built per-scope rather than upfront. Default follows the plugin's Performance settings (disabled unless changed there).
ScopedIndexLookupBuild.semantics: It changes how a Vtx dataset's endpoint lookup is built, never what that lookup resolves to, so no result depends on it either way. It is also consulted only once the Vtx dataset reaches `Small Cluster Size` (project settings, 512 by default): below that the single-pass build is used whatever this says.

bQuietMissingClusterPairElement.tooltip: Suppress warning when a cluster pair (vtx/edges) cannot be found.

hints.text: Pairing rejections are reported whether or not the rest of the execution succeeded, including edges that landed on the **Vtx** pin, vtx that landed on the **Edges** pin, a second Vtx dataset sharing a pair id, edges whose Vtx dataset never arrived, and data carrying a role tag without the attributes to back it. The report is one line per kind of problem, so it names what went wrong and never which dataset or how many.

A Vtx dataset of one point or fewer is skipped along with every Edges dataset paired to it, and the node logs an invalid-input warning naming the cause. Below two points there is nothing an edge could join, so the pair produces no output rather than an empty cluster.

Data rejected during pairing is disabled, not forwarded. A dataset that fails to pair does not reappear on the output pins, so an output that is short of what went in is the first symptom of a pairing problem.

A cluster node's filter pin is declared here too, and everything about it is the node's own: its label (**Vtx Filters**, **Point Filters**, **Break Conditions** and others), the filter families it accepts, and whether it is optional or required. A name ending in Conditions decides where something happens rather than which elements are processed.

UPCGExCollectionStagingPipeline.name: Collection Staging Pipeline
UPCGExCollectionStagingPipeline.purpose: A staging pipeline is a Blueprint or C++ object attached to a collection, running your own logic every time its staging data is rebuilt in the editor. Subclass this base, add an instance to the collection's Staging Pipelines array, and override the three hooks: once before the session, once per re-staged entry, once after. Derived classes expose their own properties inline in the collection's details panel, so a pipeline carries its configuration next to the collection it serves. Everything here is editor-side: the array is never serialized into a cooked target and the hooks never fire while cooking.
UPCGExCollectionStagingPipeline.situation: A convention a team would otherwise enforce by hand across every entry, naming-driven tags or a derived cost property, has to re-apply itself on every rebuild.

mechanism.text: Every valid slot of the collection's Staging Pipelines array runs at each hook point, in array order, so a later pipeline observes what earlier ones changed and empty slots cost nothing. Hooks receive the collection and, in the per-entry hook, the entry index and whether that row references a sub-collection; the same values come back from the context accessors, which hide their self pin so they can be dropped anywhere on the canvas. Only the collection whose rebuild was triggered dispatches: sub-collections re-staged along the way run none of their own pipelines. A rebuild started from inside a hook completes without re-firing hooks, so a pipeline that restages cannot re-enter itself.
steps: On Pre Rebuild fires once, before the session touches any entry.
Each re-staged entry is sanitized and its staging data is baked, then On Process Entry fires for that entry.
The native post-rebuild work runs: actor component schema merges and shared-collection compaction.
On Post Rebuild fires once, on that final state.

off_label.claim: On Post Rebuild sees the collection after the native post-staging work has run, so a pipeline that writes nothing is still useful as a validation pass reporting on final state.
off_label.grounded_in: EDITOR_FinalizeStagingRebuild calls EDITOR_OnPostStagingRebuild before EDITOR_DispatchPipelinePostRebuild

off_label.claim: The context accessors answer null and -1 outside hook execution, so the same subclass can be instantiated in an editor utility widget and driven from a wired collection instead of the dispatch context.
off_label.grounded_in: TargetCollection and TargetEntryIndex are stamped only inside the dispatchers' scope guards; the collection Blueprint library takes its collection as a parameter

hints.text: Three things on a collection can be addressed, and the Blueprint nodes split along them. A collection member is a reflected field on the collection object itself, reached by Get and Set Collection Member. An entry member is a reflected field on one entry row, addressed by raw index, reached by Get and Set Entry Member. An entry property is a declared custom property, resolved across the entry, category and collection tiers, reached by Get and Set Entry Property. Switch on Collection Type branches a pipeline shared between collection types.
Adding or removing entries from On Process Entry mutates the array the session is iterating. The per-entry hook is for entry values; structural edits belong in On Pre Rebuild or On Post Rebuild.

Writes through the collection Blueprint nodes snapshot the collection for undo and mark its package dirty whether or not the value changed, and member writes also invalidate the pick cache. A pipeline that rewrites values it did not need to change leaves the asset modified after every rebuild.

UPCGExCollocationCountSettings.name: Collocation Count
UPCGExCollocationCountSettings.purpose: Counts how many other points share each point's position. Duplicates arrive from merges, copies and rounding, and they are invisible in the viewport because they sit on top of each other. This makes them countable, so a filter downstream can act on them without anything being removed here.
UPCGExCollocationCountSettings.situation: Data merged from several sources where the same location may have been produced more than once, and it matters how often.

mechanism.text: Every point is compared against the others by position, within `Tolerance`, and the number of matches is written to an attribute. Nothing is removed, reordered or moved. The optional linear occurrence output numbers the duplicates at a shared position in the order they were encountered, so a set of coincident points can be told apart afterwards.

off_label.claim: The linear occurrence output plus a filter keeping only zero is a deduplicate that removes nothing here: the first point at each position keeps 0 and every later copy takes a higher number, so one comparison downstream leaves exactly one point per location.
off_label.grounded_in: The linear occurrence value is the index of the point among those sharing its position, so it is unique per coincident group.

CollicationNumAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write collocation to.

LinearOccurencesAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write linear occurences to.
LinearOccurencesAttributeName.semantics: Numbers the points sharing a position rather than counting them, so the first at a location gets 0 and each later one takes the next number. Read alongside the collocation count it tells a point both how crowded its position is and which of the crowd it is.

Tolerance.tooltip: Distance tolerance for considering two points as collocated.
Tolerance.semantics: How near two points must be to count as the same place. It is a world-space distance, so the same figure behaves differently on data authored at a different scale, and the shipped value is a small epsilon meant to catch exact duplicates rather than merely close neighbours.

UPCGExConnectClustersSettings.name: Cluster : Connect
UPCGExConnectClustersSettings.purpose: Joins the separate components of one cluster by inserting edges between them. A generator that emits one Edges dataset per connected component leaves islands, and this is the node that bridges them. It works on connectivity alone: the Vtx it joins are the ones already in the input, none is created, moved or welded, and clusters that arrived on different Vtx datasets are not candidates for each other. **Cluster : Fuse** is the node for that second case.
UPCGExConnectClustersSettings.situation: A generator returned four islands where one navigable network was wanted, and they need joining at their nearest points.

mechanism.text: The unit of work is one Vtx dataset together with the several Edges datasets paired with it, each of which is one connected component. `Connect Method` decides which pairs of components get joined, and each join becomes exactly one new edge, laid between the closest Vtx of one component and the closest Vtx of the other. Nothing else is added: the Vtx dataset comes through as a copy with the same points in the same order. What does change shape is the Edges pin, because components the new edges tied together come back as a single dataset. A Vtx dataset with only one Edges dataset has nothing to bridge and is forwarded untouched, and when that is true of every input the node warns that no bridge was created.

off_label.claim: Set `Connect Method` to Most Edges, flag the bridges, and the output carries every possible connection between the components with the new ones marked. A refinement or an edge filter downstream then picks which bridges survive by its own rule, which moves the choice off this node.
off_label.grounded_in: The Most Edges branch stages a bridge for every ordered pair of components, and the edge flag is written on exactly the inserted edge points.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx dataset shared by the components to be joined. Two clusters can only be bridged when this dataset is the same for both.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges datasets paired with it, one per component. A single dataset here means there is nothing to bridge.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: A copy of the input Vtx dataset, unchanged except for the optional bridge count attribute.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component of the result, so components the bridges joined arrive merged into one.

BridgeMethod.tooltip: Method used to find & insert bridges
BridgeMethod.semantics: Decides which pairs of components get a bridge, judged on the centre of each component's bounds rather than on its geometry. **Delaunay 3D** and **Delaunay 2D** triangulate those centres and bridge every resulting connection, which reads as an organic mesh between the islands. **Least Edges** builds a minimum spanning tree over the same centres, so every component is reachable and the bridges total the shortest set that achieves it. **Most Edges** bridges every pair.
BridgeMethod.trap: Both Delaunay methods fall back to Most Edges when there are too few components to triangulate: four or fewer for 3D, three or fewer for 2D. A small input therefore comes out fully cross-connected whichever Delaunay you picked.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: The plane the component centres are flattened onto for Delaunay 2D. Centres that collapse onto each other in that projection cannot be triangulated, and the node warns that the triangulation failed rather than bridging them.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: Governs the merge, not the copy. Components joined by a bridge have their Edges datasets combined into one, and this decides which attributes and tags of the originals survive that combination.

VtxConnectorFlagName.tooltip: Attribute name for the vertex bridge count.
VtxConnectorFlagName.semantics: An integer count of the bridges landing on each Vtx, not a flag: a Vtx that two bridges chose reads 2. Every other Vtx reads 0. The name is checked before the node runs, and one the metadata cannot take stops the node with an error.

EdgeConnectorFlagName.tooltip: Attribute name for the bridge edge flag.
EdgeConnectorFlagName.semantics: A boolean written true on the inserted edges alone, which is the only way downstream to tell a bridge from an edge the generator made. Every other edge reads false.

bQuietNoBridgeWarning.tooltip: If enabled, won't throw a warning if no bridge could be created.
bQuietNoBridgeWarning.semantics: The warning it silences fires when no Vtx dataset had more than one Edges dataset, which is the ordinary case for input that was already connected. The node then forwards both halves unchanged, so silencing it is safe where the node sits in a graph that sometimes has nothing to do.

hints.text: Two clusters that arrived on separate Vtx datasets are invisible to each other here, whatever their positions. This node only ever bridges components of one Vtx dataset. Merging distinct clusters is **Cluster : Fuse**, which rebuilds them into one by welding Vtx that coincide.

UPCGExConnectPointsSettings.name: Cluster : Connect Points
UPCGExConnectPointsSettings.purpose: The open-ended generator: it holds no opinion about what should connect, and takes that decision from probe sub-nodes wired to its Probes pin. Hand it a loose point cloud and a probe or two, and it returns a cluster made of the connections those probes asked for. Two filter pins split the points by role, one deciding which points may start a connection and one deciding which may be named at the far end, which is what makes asymmetric connectivity possible.
UPCGExConnectPointsSettings.situation: A scatter of points that has to become a cluster under a rule you choose, whether that rule is proximity, direction, index arithmetic or an attribute comparison.

mechanism.text: One point dataset in, one Vtx dataset and one Edges dataset per connected component out. Every probe on the pin proposes connections for the points it is given, and the result is the union of all of them: a probe adds connections, none removes another's, and the same pair asked for twice appears once. A connection carries no direction, so A to B and B to A are one edge. Points that end up with no connection are dropped, and the Vtx that survive come out grouped by cluster. An input holding fewer than two points is skipped with a warning, and if no input qualifies the node cancels.
steps: Generator Filters decide which points may start a connection; Connectable Filters decide which points may be named at the far end of one.
Each starting point is offered the accepting points inside a probe's own search radius, nearest first.
A probe with `Do Chained Processing` on is the exception: it sees candidates as they are found, not nearest first, and contributes at most one connection per starting point, the one it ranked best.
Probes answer in the order they arrive on the pin, and while Prevent Coincidence is on, a direction one probe connects in is closed to the probes after it.

Every connection any probe asked for is kept once, the result splits into one Edges dataset per connected component, and Cluster Output Settings discards the components falling outside its size limits.

off_label.claim: Wire one permissive probe, take only the Vtx output, and the node becomes a density prune: a point with nothing inside the probe's reach gets no connection and does not survive to the output.
off_label.grounded_in: FGraph::BuildSubGraphs invalidates edgeless nodes and FGraphBuilder::Compile prunes them out of the Vtx data before staging

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to connect. Each input dataset is handled on its own and yields its own cluster; an input of fewer than two points is skipped.

inputs.label: Probes
inputs.note: The probe sub-nodes deciding what connects. At least one is required and the node does not execute without one.

inputs.label: Generator Filters
inputs.note: Points failing these never start a connection. Point filters only.

inputs.label: Connectable Filters
inputs.note: Points failing these are never offered as the far end of a connection. Point filters only.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The input points that ended up with at least one connection, carrying the pairing attribute and tags.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component, all paired with the single Vtx dataset.

CoincidenceTolerance.tooltip: Quantization cell size for the direction hash; smaller values allow closer directions to count as distinct.
CoincidenceTolerance.semantics: At the default of 0.001 the grid is fine enough that only points stacked on one another, or lying along a direction already taken, collide. Raising it toward the maximum of 1 coarsens the grid until a point can hold no more than a couple of dozen distinct directions in total.
CoincidenceTolerance.trap: The claim is shared by every probe answering at that point, which is what makes probe order change the result. G-Probe sub-nodes propose their connections outside it.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Projection changes what the node measures and leaves the output transforms alone: positions are flattened onto the plane for every distance, direction and radius test, and the points come out where they started. A probe's search radius becomes a radius in the plane, and two candidates separated only along the projection normal read as one direction for coincidence prevention.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: The size limits are per connected component and they discard the whole component, its Vtx included, instead of trimming it. Min Vtx Count defaults to 3, so a component of two points and one edge goes the moment Remove Small Clusters is on.
GraphBuilderDetails.trap: When no component survives, the input yields neither Vtx nor Edges and the node reports nothing.

hints.text: Both filter pins advertise the general filter type, which is broader than what they take, so a Vtx Filter or an Edge Filter connects and is then dropped at execution with an invalid-input warning naming the pin. Narrowing at execution rather than at the wire is how every factory pin here works; on these two the effect is that the role runs unfiltered, so every point keeps the role the filter was meant to restrict.

The two filter pins assign roles and never remove points. Because a connection carries no direction, a point barred from starting one can still be an endpoint of a connection some other point started.

UPCGExConnectVtxSettings.name: Cluster : Connect Vtx
UPCGExConnectVtxSettings.purpose: The second consumer of the probe family, and the one that starts from a cluster instead of a point cloud. It runs the same Probe : and G-Probe : sub-nodes over Vtx, keeps every edge that was already there, and writes what the probes asked for into the input's own Edges data. What it adds over **Cluster : Connect Points** is reach control: `Scope` decides which Vtx can see each other, `Edge Relation` restricts which pairs may be joined, and both role filter pins take Vtx filters as well as point filters, so a rule phrased in degree or neighbourhood terms is expressible here and not there. It can also mark the edges it created and count the new connections each Vtx gained.
UPCGExConnectVtxSettings.situation: Several clusters that have to be stitched into one, or a cluster that needs extra connections a probe rule can describe.

mechanism.text: Vtx and Edges in, Vtx and Edges out, and every edge that arrived is still there: the node only adds. Probes propose connections between Vtx, a proposal naming a pair that is already joined is dropped, and the rest are written into the input's own Edges datasets. Clusters that a new edge joins come out merged into one Edges dataset, clusters nothing reached stay as they were, and Vtx belonging to no cluster never take part. A new edge point inherits nothing, because an appended edge has no source edge to copy from, so it arrives with the Edges data's default values. There is no Cluster Output Settings on this node, so nothing is pruned for size and a Vtx left unconnected still reaches the output.

off_label.claim: Under All Inputs the vtx merge and the endpoint renumbering run whether or not a probe connects anything, so a pass whose Generator Filters reject every Vtx hands back the same clusters rebuilt against one shared Vtx dataset. `Quiet No Connection Warning` is what makes that a clean run.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExConnectVtxElement::LaunchVtxMerge, LaunchProbing, LaunchPatching and CommitAndOutput advance in sequence regardless of the staged-edge count, and FGraphPatcher's merged-sources mode renumbers the endpoint attributes into the merged domain at Commit

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster vertices. Each Vtx dataset is handled with the Edges datasets tagged as its pair.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The clusters' edges, and where the new connections are written.

inputs.label: Probes
inputs.note: The probe sub-nodes deciding what connects. At least one is required and the node does not execute without one.

inputs.label: Generator Filters
inputs.note: Vtx failing these never start a connection. Point filters and Vtx filters both, filter groups and collection filters included.

inputs.label: Connectable Filters
inputs.note: Vtx failing these are never offered as the far end of a connection. Same acceptance as the other filter pin.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The input vertices, carrying the connection count when that output is on. Under All Inputs a single merged dataset takes their place.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component once the additions are in, so two clusters a new edge joined arrive as one.

Scope.tooltip: Which vtx can see each other when probing.
Scope.semantics: `Vtx Group` runs the probes once per Vtx dataset, over every cluster paired with it at once, so a new edge can join two clusters that share that Vtx data and never two separate inputs. `Cluster` narrows the same pass to one cluster at a time: a candidate in another cluster is never offered, and `Edge Relation` is hidden and ignored. `All Inputs` merges every input Vtx dataset into one first and probes across the lot, so anything can reach anything and the Vtx pin carries a single dataset. Inputs whose clusters could not be read sit out of that merge and are forwarded untouched, so the pin can still carry more than one dataset.

EdgeRelation.tooltip: Additional constraint on which vtx pairs probes may connect. Cluster scope enforces same-cluster connections and ignores this.
EdgeRelation.semantics: A second constraint layered on the pool `Scope` opened. `Cross-Cluster Only` requires a new edge to join Vtx of two different clusters, so nothing is added inside one. `Cross-Data Only` requires the two Vtx to come from different input datasets, which only has meaning once they have been merged.
EdgeRelation.trap: `Cross-Data Only` under `Vtx Group` cancels the node with an error rather than falling back, because no pair can satisfy it there. Under `Cluster` the property is hidden and whatever value it holds is ignored.

CoincidenceTolerance.tooltip: Quantization cell size for the direction hash; smaller values allow closer directions to count as distinct.
CoincidenceTolerance.semantics: The same direction claim **Cluster : Connect Points** uses: a candidate's direction from the Vtx is quantized onto a grid whose step is this value, and a claimed cell is closed to every later probe at that Vtx. At the default of 0.001 only Vtx stacked on one another, or lying along a direction already taken, collide.
CoincidenceTolerance.trap: The claim covers only the connections made in this pass. Edges the cluster already had never claim a direction, so a probe can add one lying alongside an existing edge; the existing set is consulted for identical pairs and nothing else.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Projection changes what the node measures and leaves the output transforms alone: positions are flattened onto the plane for every distance, direction and radius test, and the Vtx come out where they started. A probe's search radius becomes a radius in the plane, and two candidates separated only along the projection normal read as one direction for coincidence prevention.

CarryOverDetails.tooltip: Meta filter settings for merged edges.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: Reaches only the edge attributes that survive when several Edges datasets collapse into one component. Clusters that nothing connected are not merged and keep everything they came in with.

VtxCarryOverDetails.tooltip: Meta filter settings for the merged vtx (All Inputs scope only).

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

VtxCarryOverDetails.semantics: The same filtering for the vtx merge that `All Inputs` performs. Attributes it excludes are gone from the single output Vtx dataset, which is the only Vtx data downstream nodes will see in that scope.

VtxConnectorFlagName.tooltip: Attribute name for the vertex connection count.
VtxConnectorFlagName.semantics: An int32 counting the connections this node added at that Vtx, existing edges excluded, so a Vtx the probes never reached reads 0.

EdgeConnectorFlagName.tooltip: Attribute name for the new edge flag.
EdgeConnectorFlagName.semantics: A bool set true on the edges this node created, which is what separates them from the ones that arrived.

bQuietNoConnectionWarning.tooltip: If enabled, won't throw a warning if no connection could be created.

hints.text: Under any constraint at all, which includes `Cluster` scope as well as the two `Edge Relation` values, the halves of the probe family behave differently. Radius-based Probe : sub-nodes never see the disallowed Vtx, so a closest-style probe picks the next allowed one instead. Probe : Index and every G-Probe : name their targets outright, and their proposals are tested against the constraint afterwards, so a disallowed connection is dropped and nothing takes its place. A G-Probe : under Cross-Cluster Only therefore loses connections rather than re-aiming them.

Both flag attributes are created only where there is something to write. The edge flag lands on the Edges datasets that received a new edge and on no others, and neither attribute is written at all when the pass created no connection, so a downstream read has to tolerate the attribute being absent.

Both filter pins advertise the general filter type, which is broader than what they take, so an Edge Filter connects and is then dropped at execution with an invalid-input warning naming the pin. Narrowing at execution rather than at the wire is how every factory pin here works; on these two the effect is that the role runs unfiltered, so every Vtx keeps the role the filter was meant to restrict.
The two filter pins assign roles and never remove Vtx. Because a connection carries no direction, a Vtx barred from starting one can still be the far end of a connection some other Vtx started.

UPCGExConstantEnumSettings.name: Enum Constant
UPCGExConstantEnumSettings.purpose: Reads an enum, native or Blueprint, and hands its values to the graph as data. Each exported value can carry up to three things: its key, the short name the code uses; its description, the display name the editor shows; and its numeric value. `Output Mode` decides whether those land as rows of one attribute set or as one attribute set per value on a pin of its own. A separate toggle also emits the whole selection as a single bitmask.
UPCGExConstantEnumSettings.situation: A graph that has to branch or match on the same enum a Blueprint or a C++ system uses, without the numbers being retyped and left to drift.

mechanism.text: No inputs, one execution. The enum's values are walked in declaration order, skipping any marked hidden or spacer and the trailing maximum, and each surviving value becomes one row carrying whichever of the three attributes are enabled. `Single`, `All` and `Selection` put those rows on one pin; the two separate-output modes give each value its own pin, labelled with its description. With no enum picked, or with all three attributes switched off, the node produces nothing at all.

off_label.claim: `Single` keeps its value on the same shared pin the multi-value modes use rather than making a pin of its own, so the enum value a node emits can be changed without any wire downstream coming loose.
off_label.grounded_in: The EEOM_Single branch of AdvanceWork calls StageEnumValuesSinglePin, and OutputPinProperties declares the same SingleOutputPinName for it as for All and Selection

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: One attribute set with a row per exported value.
outputs.condition: Single, All and Selection modes

outputs.label: One pin per exported value
outputs.note: Labelled with the value's description, carrying a single-row attribute set for that value alone.
outputs.condition: the two separate-output modes

outputs.label: Flags
outputs.note: An attribute set holding one int64 with a bit set for every exported value.
outputs.condition: when Output Bitflags is on

pins.dynamic: The pin set is computed from the enum and the mode, so changing either rebuilds the node's outputs. The labels are cached alongside the settings and reapplied on load, which is what keeps existing wires attached when a pin is renamed rather than removed.

OutputMode.semantics: The three single-pin modes differ only in how many rows arrive: one, all of them, or the ticked ones. The two separate-output modes trade that for a pin per value, which is what makes an enum usable as a router rather than as a table.

SelectedEnum.semantics: Takes native and Blueprint enums alike. Changing it rebuilds both the pin set and the tick list, so a graph that swapped enums loses whatever was ticked before.

EnabledExportValues.semantics: Keyed by description rather than by key, which is what the pin labels use as well. A value whose display name is blank has nothing to be ticked by.

OutputEnumKeys.tooltip: Output the enum value keys (the short names used in C++).

StripEnumNamespaceFromKey.tooltip: Strip the namespace prefix from enum keys. 'SomeEnum::SomeKey' becomes just 'SomeKey'.
StripEnumNamespaceFromKey.semantics: Ships enabled, so keys arrive bare. Switch it off to keep the enum's own name in front of each key, which is what a downstream string comparison against a fully qualified name needs.

KeyAttribute.tooltip: Attribute name for the enum key output.

OutputEnumDescriptions.tooltip: Output the enum value descriptions (human-readable display names).

DescriptionAttribute.tooltip: Attribute name for the description output.

OutputEnumValues.tooltip: Whether to output the numeric enum values. Note: will be output as int64 to match behaviour in native PCG
OutputEnumValues.semantics: The only one of the three that ships enabled, so a node placed and left alone emits numbers and nothing else. It writes int64 to match what vanilla PCG does with enums.

FlagsName.tooltip: Whether to output the enum as a bitmask, and which name should the attribute have in the output attribute set.
FlagsName.semantics: Names the int64 inside the attribute set on the **Flags** pin. The pin label itself is fixed.

FlagBitOffset.tooltip: Bit to start writing the enum bits to.
FlagBitOffset.semantics: The bit a value claims is this offset plus that value's position in the enum, counted before any selection is applied, so ticking fewer values leaves the same bits in the same places. An offset that pushes a value past bit 63 has nowhere to land.

hints.text: The bitmask on the **Flags** pin describes the selection, not a result: it carries one bit per value the node exported, so in `All` mode every bit is set and in `Single` mode exactly one is. It is there so the same enum can drive a **Filter : Bitmask** test without the mask being typed out by hand.

UPCGExConstantFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Constant
UPCGExConstantFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Answers the same way for every element, and reads nothing to do it. This is also the filter the whole family falls back to: when `Missing Data Policy` or `Initialization Failure Policy` is set to Pass or Fail, the filter that could not run is replaced by this one, holding the verdict that policy names, so both policies are this node placed on your behalf. Wired by hand it is a switch, holding a consumer open or shut while the condition that belongs there is still being built, and `Value` is overridable so a graph parameter can throw the switch from outside. Because the answer owes nothing to the element, it holds for a whole dataset and for points that do not exist yet, which is why the collection consumers accept it and why it survives on the Stop Conditions pins of Tensors : Extrude and Tensors Transform, where filters that need real data are dropped with a warning.
UPCGExConstantFilterProviderSettings.situation: A consumer that has to pass or fail everything, either while the real condition is still being built or because something outside the graph decides it.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element and decides what the answer means; the filter reads nothing and writes nothing. The verdict is `Value`, flipped when `Invert` is on, settled once as the filter binds and identical for every element after that. Nothing about the element being tested enters the answer, so the same filter answers for a point, for a Vtx, for an edge, for a whole dataset and for a point that has yet to be built.

off_label.claim: Under an Or group a true constant decides the group on its own, and under an And group a false one does. That makes a single node a temporary short-circuit over a stack you would rather not unwire while diagnosing it.
off_label.grounded_in: FFilterGroupAND short-circuiting on the first failing child and FFilterGroupOR on the first passing one, with no special case for a constant child

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so it is accepted on every filter pin, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included, and it is one of the few also accepted where a whole dataset is judged.

fields.name: Value
fields.tooltip: The constant value returned by this filter.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the filter result.

UPCGExConstantsSettings.name: Constant
UPCGExConstantsSettings.purpose: Emits fixed values as data, one output pin per value. The value is not typed on the node: the palette carries one entry per named list, so picking the entry from the palette is picking what the node emits, and the node title is that list's name. Three kinds of list ship, numbers, axes and booleans, and the kind decides which of the four transforms below it are live.
UPCGExConstantsSettings.situation: A graph that needs pi, an axis or a plain 1 as data, with no field to fill in each time the node is placed.

mechanism.text: No inputs, one execution, and one output pin per constant in the chosen list, each labelled with that constant's name and carrying an attribute set of one entry and one attribute. Numbers are negated, then reciprocated, then multiplied, in that order, and cast last; a reciprocal of a value at or near zero comes out as 0 rather than as infinity. Vectors take the multiplier and the negation and ignore the rest. Booleans are emitted exactly as they are.

off_label.claim: `Custom Multiplier` reaches the vector lists too, so the axis entries double as a source of scaled direction vectors with no maths node behind them.
off_label.grounded_in: The vector branch of FPCGExConstantsElement::AdvanceWork stages the constant multiplied by CustomMultiplier and by the sign NegateOutput selects

outputs.label: One pin per constant in the list
outputs.note: Labelled with the constant's own name, carrying an attribute set of one entry and one attribute of the same name.

NegateOutput.tooltip: Export the negative of the constant instead of the constant itself.
NegateOutput.semantics: Runs first, before the reciprocal and the multiplier, so 2 with both toggles on comes out as -0.5 and not as the reciprocal of a negated-then-scaled value. It greys out on a boolean list.

OutputReciprocal.semantics: Numeric lists only, and greyed out on the others. A value at or near zero yields 0 rather than infinity, so the reciprocal of the `0` entry is 0.

CustomMultiplier.tooltip: Apply a custom multiplier to the output.
CustomMultiplier.semantics: Applied last, so it scales whatever the negation and the reciprocal left rather than the constant itself. Vectors take it; booleans grey it out.

NumericOutputType.tooltip: Cast to a specific type. Double is used by default, ignored for vectors.
NumericOutputType.semantics: Declared without an initial value, so a freshly placed node sits on `Double`. It casts rather than rounds, so an integer type truncates and pi arrives as 3. Greyed out on the vector and boolean lists.

AttributeNameMap.semantics: One row per constant in the list, filled in when the palette entry is placed. The keys are fixed and the values are the names the attributes are written under.
AttributeNameMap.trap: A renamed value becomes the label of the pin the data is staged on as well as the attribute's name, while the pin the node declares keeps the constant's original name. Rename a row and that constant's output has no pin to arrive on.

UPCGExCopyAttributesSettings.name: Copy Attributes
UPCGExCopyAttributesSettings.purpose: Moves attributes from one dataset onto another, one at a time or all at once, and it exists for the case the stock node stops short of: a `@Data` value copied onto per-element data reaches every element rather than only the first. Which source pairs with which target is the `Operation` setting, in the shapes the stock node offers. It also registers what it read as consumable, so a graph can copy a value across and have the original deleted on the way out.
UPCGExCopyAttributesSettings.situation: A value that lives once per dataset has to become a per-point value, or attributes have to travel between two datasets that share nothing but their shape.

mechanism.text: Targets come out, sources do not: the output is one dataset per iteration, carrying the target's points and the target's tags with the copied attributes attached. How many iterations there are is the `Operation` setting's business, and a target used by more than one iteration comes out more than once. A target attribute of the same name is deleted and recreated rather than written into, so the source's type and its interpolation setting win and a failed copy leaves the old attribute standing. Copying something onto itself is detected and skipped.

off_label.claim: Copy an attribute onto the same data under a new name and the node is a rename that keeps the type exactly, which the recreate-from-source-descriptor path does for container and extended types too.
off_label.grounded_in: CopyPair passes bSameOrigin when target and source are the same data, and the promotion path builds the target from the source's FPCGMetadataAttributeDesc

off_label.claim: With `Cleanup Consumable Attributes` on, a successful copy deletes the source name from this node's outputs while protecting the name it wrote, which turns a copy into a move.
off_label.grounded_in: RegisterConsumable adds the domain-qualified source name as consumable and the written name as protected, and only runs on a successful copy

inputs.label: Target
inputs.note: The data attributes are copied onto. What comes out is this, duplicated.

inputs.label: Source
inputs.note: The data attributes are read from. Never modified and never emitted.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: One dataset per iteration, in iteration order, each carrying its target's tags.

pins.dynamic: Both inputs and the output are declared as accepting any data, so points, attribute sets and spatial data all pass through; the output takes the target's type.

Operation.semantics: Decides the output count as much as the pairing. `Respectively` emits one dataset per iteration and runs as many iterations as the larger of the two pin counts, so two sources against one target give two outputs built from that one target rather than one; a count that is neither equal, one-to-many nor many-to-one is an error and the targets are forwarded untouched. `Each Source on Every Target` emits sources times targets. `Merge Sources` emits one per target and copies every source onto it in order, so clashing names are settled by the last source.
Operation.trap: In `Merge Sources` the sources are applied in pin order and each overwrites the last, so two sources carrying the same attribute name leave only the later one's values.

bCopyAllAttributes.semantics: Switches the node from one named attribute to every attribute the source carries, which also switches off the rename: names are copied as they are. `Input Source` and `Output Target` are ignored while it is on, and so is the consumable registration, because the source names and the written names would be the same.

bCopyAllDomains.tooltip: If checked, it is copying all attributes from all domains, as long as the source domain is supported on the target data.

MetadataDomainsMapping.tooltip: When copying all attributes, a mapping can be specified. If it is empty, it's going to be Default -> Default.
MetadataDomainsMapping.semantics: Decides where each source domain lands on the target. Left empty it is the default domain onto the default domain, so `@Data` attributes stay `@Data` and element attributes stay elements. Filling it is how `@Data` on the source is routed onto the elements domain of the target, which is what puts the promotion path in play for every attribute at once.

bMaterializeDataValues.tooltip: When a single-value source (@Data) is copied onto a multi-entry target domain, write a concrete metadata entry for every element. When disabled, the value is only written as the (re)created attribute's default value -- elements inherit it without any materialized entries.
bMaterializeDataValues.semantics: Only reaches the promotion case, where a single-value source domain is copied onto a domain that holds many entries. Off, the value is written as the recreated attribute's default and the elements inherit it without carrying an entry, which reads correctly through most accessors and shows as unset to anything walking stored entries. On, every element gets a concrete entry, all sharing one stored value, so the cost does not scale with element count.

hints.text: `Steal Data` reaches only a target that exactly one iteration uses and that no other iteration reads as its source. Anything else is duplicated as usual, so enabling it on a fan-out operation changes nothing.

A target attribute of the same name is deleted and recreated from the source's descriptor, not written into. Its type, its interpolation setting and any per-element values it held are gone, whatever the source's type was.

`Respectively` with more sources than targets emits one dataset per source, each a fresh copy of the single target. The stock node stops at the target count and drops the extra sources; this one honours the operation's stated contract of producing the larger of the two counts.

UPCGExCopyClustersToPointsSettings.name: Cluster : Copy to Points
UPCGExCopyClustersToPointsSettings.purpose: Puts a complete copy of each input cluster at every target point, moved onto that point's transform. The copies are independent from the moment they are made, each with its own pair tag, so none of them shares Vtx with any other and overlapping copies stay separate clusters. Data Matching is what lifts this above blanket duplication: it decides which cluster reaches which target, so targets carrying different attribute values can each receive a different piece.
UPCGExCopyClustersToPointsSettings.situation: One authored cluster, or a small library of them, has to appear across a scatter of points and be oriented to each.

mechanism.text: Each input cluster is duplicated once per target point that accepts it, and every copy is moved onto that point by `Transform Details`. The copies are whole and independent, each carrying its own pair tag, so no two of them fuse however far they overlap. The output count is the number of accepted targets times the number of input clusters, on both pins. Data Matching decides acceptance and `Cluster Match Mode` decides which half of the pair the rules are tested against; a Vtx copy whose every Edges copy was rejected is dropped rather than emitted with nothing paired to it. Nothing here validates the input, so a cluster whose pairing is already broken is copied broken, once per target.

off_label.claim: Because each copy carries a fresh pair tag and copies never weld, following this node with **Cluster : Fuse** is the way to turn the scatter into one network: the fuse pass welds wherever the copies overlap and hands back a single cluster.
off_label.grounded_in: Each duplicated Vtx dataset is stamped with a new cluster id and its edges marked against it, so the copies stay distinct pairs until something else merges them.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx datasets to copy. Several clusters here are copied to each accepted target, not distributed between targets.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges datasets, matched to their Vtx by the pair tag as usual.

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: One point dataset, and one copy of the cluster is made per point of it. This pin takes a single dataset rather than a collection.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: The rules deciding which cluster a target point accepts. Required once Data Matching is enabled, and tucked under Advanced while it is not.
inputs.condition: required when Data Matching is enabled

inputs.label: Match Rules (Edges)
inputs.note: A second rule set applied to the Edges half alone, so the two halves can be matched on different criteria.
inputs.condition: when Cluster Match Mode is Separate

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One dataset per copy, tagged as its own cluster and carrying whatever the tagging and forwarding blocks added.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per copy, paired with the Vtx copy it was made alongside.

outputs.label: Unmatched Vtx
outputs.note: Vtx data that no target accepted. Under Advanced while Data Matching is disabled, and on the node proper once splitting unmatched data is on.

outputs.label: Unmatched Edges
outputs.note: The Edges half of the same, so an unmatched pair stays a usable cluster instead of arriving as half of one.

DataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, allows you to pick which input gets copied to which target point.
DataMatching.semantics: `Cluster Match Mode` decides which half of the pair the rules are tested against, and the choice is about more than cost. **Vtx** tests the Vtx data alone and lets its Edges follow. **Edges** tests the Edges data alone, so a cluster tagged only on its Vtx matches nothing. **Any** accepts the target if either half passes. **Vtx and Edges** tests both halves against the same rules and needs each to pass. **Separate** puts a second rule set on its own pin and tests each half against its own. The limit inside the block caps how many targets one cluster may reach, which is what turns a library of pieces into a distribution rather than a broadcast.
DataMatching.trap: **Any** tests the Vtx half first and stops there once it passes, and that first test is exempt from the limit. With **Limit Matches** on, the limit under **Any** therefore counts edge-side matches alone, and a cluster reaching its targets through their Vtx data goes uncapped.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: How to scale objects to fit within target bounds.

fields.name: Justification
fields.tooltip: How to align objects within target bounds after scaling.

fields.name: bInheritScale
fields.tooltip: Multiply result scale by the target point's scale.

fields.name: bInheritRotation
fields.tooltip: Rotate result by the target point's rotation.

fields.name: bIgnoreBounds
fields.tooltip: Skip bounds calculations and use position only. Disables scale-to-fit and justification.

TransformDetails.semantics: Decides how much of the target point's transform the copy takes. Inheriting scale is the one to think about, because it scales the Vtx positions and so changes every edge length in the copy, which anything measuring distance downstream will read.

TargetsAttributesToClusterTags.tooltip: Copy target point attributes as tags on output clusters.
TargetsAttributesToClusterTags.semantics: Writes target values onto the copies as data tags, which is what lets a later node sort the copies back out by where they came from. Tags belong to the dataset, so this is the route for a value that identifies the whole copy.

TargetsForwarding.tooltip: Which target attributes to forward on clusters.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Is forwarding enabled.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

TargetsForwarding.semantics: The other route for the same values: forwarded as attributes on the copy rather than as tags. Both halves receive them, so a value forwarded this way is readable from a Vtx filter and from an edge filter alike.

hints.text: The output count multiplies. Three input clusters against a thousand target points is six thousand datasets on the two pins, and every one of them is a full copy of its source. Narrow the targets, or use Data Matching's limit, before pointing this at a dense scatter.

UPCGExCopyTagsSettings.name: Copy Tags
UPCGExCopyTagsSettings.purpose: Copies data tags from reference Targets onto Sources, adding only the tags a Source does not already carry. Which Targets a Source pairs with is decided by the matching rules, so tags can be transferred selectively rather than blanket-applied. The Sources come out sharing their original data pointer, so this is a tag-set edit and nothing else; the Targets are consumed and not forwarded.
UPCGExCopyTagsSettings.situation: Data that lost its tags through a node that does not preserve them, or that needs the tags of some other dataset it can be paired with.

mechanism.text: Targets are read once into a matcher, then every Source is asked which Targets it pairs with. For each pair, the Target's tags are considered in turn and copied when the Source is not already carrying that key, so the first matched Target wins any conflict and a Source never loses or overwrites a tag of its own. A value tag is copied whole, key and value together. Sources that matched nothing pass through unchanged, or leave on the Unmatched pin when the matching rules ask for the split.

off_label.claim: With matching disabled, every Source takes the union of every Target's tags, which turns the node into a way of stamping one authored tag block onto a whole pin from a single empty attribute set.
off_label.grounded_in: a disabled matcher pairs every Source with every Target, and the copy loop walks the matched list in order

inputs.label: Sources
inputs.note: The data that receives tags. Forwarded to the output sharing its own data pointer, with only the tag set copied.

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: The reference data that provides tags. Consumed, never forwarded. Repeated references to one data object are read once.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: The rules pairing Sources with Targets. Required while matching is enabled, advanced while it is disabled.
inputs.condition: when Data Matching is not Disabled

outputs.label: Sources
outputs.note: Every Source, with its added tags.

outputs.label: Unmatched
outputs.note: Sources that paired with no Target, when the matching settings ask for them to be split out. Otherwise they leave on the Sources pin untagged.
outputs.condition: carries data only when the matching settings request the unmatched split

pins.dynamic: Both data pins accept any type and the output mirrors what came in.

DataMatching.tooltip: Matching rules that decide which Targets each Source pairs with. When disabled, every Source pairs with every Target.
DataMatching.semantics: Decides the pairing, and also whether unmatched Sources are split onto their own pin.
DataMatching.trap: When matching is enabled but cannot be set up, because no rule was wired or a rule failed to resolve, the node falls back to pairing everything with everything and warns rather than failing. Over-broad tagging with a warning in the log is the signature.

bProtectClusterTags.tooltip: If enabled, never transfers the reserved cluster identity tags (PCGEx/Vtx, PCGEx/Edges, PCGEx/Cluster), keeping it safe to run on vtx/edge data.
bProtectClusterTags.semantics: Blocks the three tags that carry cluster identity, which are what pair a Vtx dataset with its Edges. Copying them onto unrelated data would claim it as part of a cluster, so this stays on unless the intent is to reassign cluster identity deliberately.

TagFilters.tooltip: Restricts which tag names are eligible to transfer. Leave empty (FilterMode=All) to allow every tag but the protected ones. The filter applies to PCGEx-prefixed tags too; only the three cluster identity tags are force-protected, and only when Protect Cluster Tags is enabled.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

TagFilters.semantics: Screens tag names before transfer, and applies to PCGEx-prefixed tags as well as to authored ones: the three cluster identity tags are the only ones with separate protection.

hints.text: Transfer is add-only. A Source that already carries a key keeps its own value, whatever the Target says, so this node cannot be used to update a value tag.

UPCGExCopyToPathsSettings.name: Copy to Path
UPCGExCopyToPathsSettings.purpose: Bends a set of points along a path, the way a spline mesh bends a mesh. The points keep their arrangement relative to each other and to the bounding box they sit in; that box is what gets wrapped around the target, so a straight row becomes a curved row and a lattice becomes a curved lattice. One input can be copied onto several targets at once, which is where the name comes from: each target it matches produces its own copy.
UPCGExCopyToPathsSettings.situation: A block of points laid out in a straight line has to follow a curve, several curves, or the same curve at several places along it.

mechanism.text: Every input dataset is matched against the targets, and each match produces one full copy of that input, so an input matching three targets leaves as three datasets. Inside a copy, a point's position in the input's bounding box is what decides where it lands: the first axis of `Axis Order` is read as distance along the target and drives how far along the target the point is anchored, while the other two are carried into the frame the target gives at that distance. Point count, order and attributes are untouched; only transforms are rewritten. An input that matches no target is not deformed at all.

off_label.claim: Feeding one point per copy turns it into a distributor rather than a deformer: with a single point the bounding box collapses, the point lands at whatever position the main-axis range resolves to, and the copy count becomes the target count.
off_label.grounded_in: one Dupe is created per matched deformer in FProcessor::Process, independently of how many points the input holds

off_label.claim: The target does not have to be a path in space. Any point data of two points or more is rebuilt into a curve, so a two-point line makes this a straight-line array with orientation taken from the endpoints.
off_label.grounded_in: FBatch::BuildSpline builds an FPCGSplineStruct from any point input passing the two-point floor, using Default Point Type for every control point

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to copy and deform. Each dataset is handled on its own and needs at least two points.

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: What to deform along. Takes both point data, which is rebuilt into a curve using the Spline block, and vanilla spline data, which is used as it is. Anything under two points is skipped.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: Match-rule factories deciding which targets each input is copied onto. With none, every input is copied onto every target.
inputs.condition: required while Data Matching has a mode set; an advanced pin otherwise

inputs.label: Bounds
inputs.note: Point data whose combined bounds replace each input's own bounding box, so several inputs can be deformed as though they were one object. The node ignores the pin unless something is wired to it.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: One copy per input and matched target pair. Two inputs against three targets leave as six datasets.

outputs.label: Unmatched
outputs.note: Inputs that matched no target, forwarded rather than deformed.
outputs.condition: when Data Matching is set to split unmatched data out; an advanced pin otherwise

DataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, allows you to filter out which targets get sampled by which data
DataMatching.semantics: Each input keeps a copy per target it matched, so this decides the output count as much as it decides pairing. An input that matches nothing produces no copy at all, and where it goes instead is this block's unmatched policy.

DefaultPointType.semantics: Applies to point targets only, where the node has to build a curve before it can deform anything. A vanilla spline target arrives with its own point types and this is never consulted for it.

PointTypeAttribute.semantics: Read off the target's points, one value per control point, as the integer form of the spline point type. Values outside 0 to 4 fall back to `Default Point Type` rather than erroring, but a missing attribute aborts that target with a logged error and it produces nothing.

Tangents.semantics: Consulted only where a control point ends up on the custom-tangent point type, which is either the default point type being set to it or the attribute resolving to it.

BoundsSource.tooltip: Which point property to use for bounds calculation.
BoundsSource.semantics: The box this reads is the whole input dataset's bounds, not each point's, and it is what the deformation maps onto the target. It also decides the bounds read from the **Bounds** pin when that is wired.

MinBoundsOffset.semantics: Added to the box after it is measured and before the axis swizzle, in world units and per axis. Growing the box along the main axis leaves slack at both ends, so the points stop short of the range the main axis settings asked for.

MaxBoundsOffset.semantics: The far-side twin of the minimum offset. The default pair grows the box by one unit each way, which matters only when the input is flat on an axis, where it keeps the box from having zero size there.

AxisOrder.semantics: The first letter is the axis that runs along the target, and the other two keep their meaning in the frame the target hands back. It reorders the input's own axes before anything else happens, so changing it re-reads which side of the bounding box is the length.

TransformScale.tooltip: Which scale components from the sampled transform should be applied to the point.
TransformScale.semantics: Per axis, it decides whether the target's own scale at that position reaches the copy. An unticked axis is forced to 1, which is how a target authored with a varying scale can drive thickness on one axis and be ignored on the others.

bPreserveOriginalInputScale.semantics: The last thing applied, and it replaces the finished scale outright rather than mixing with it. While it is on, the copy carries the input point's own scale and nothing the target contributed.
bPreserveOriginalInputScale.trap: It is on by default, and it is applied after both `Transform Scale` and `Preserve Aspect Ratio`, so neither of those changes anything until this is switched off.

bPreserveAspectRatio.semantics: Scales the copy by how much the target stretched it: the length of target covered, divided by the input box's size along the main axis. A copy spread over twice its own length comes back twice as thick.

FlattenAxis.semantics: Rebuilds the frame the target hands back so the named axis stops following the target's roll. It leaves position alone and only straightens orientation, which is the fix for copies that tumble along a target whose own rotation twists.

bWrapClosedLoops.semantics: It changes what happens outside the 0 to 1 range on a closed target: wrapping tiles the position back into range, so a copy longer than the loop keeps going round. Off, and on every open target, the position is clamped instead, which stacks every out-of-range point on the target's end.

fields.name: Usage
fields.tooltip: How the two alpha values define the deformation range.

fields.name: FirstAlphaInput
fields.tooltip: Where first alpha value comes from.

fields.name: FirstAlphaAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute to read start value from.

fields.name: FirstAlphaConstant
fields.tooltip: Constant start value.

fields.name: SecondAlphaInput
fields.tooltip: Where second alpha value comes from.

fields.name: SecondAlphaAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute to read end value from.

fields.name: SecondAlphaConstant
fields.tooltip: Constant end value.

MainAxisSettings.semantics: The portion of the target the copy is spread over, as two alphas. This is what restricts a copy to part of a target, and it is read once per input and target pair rather than per point. Either alpha can be read from the input data or from the target data, so one graph can place each copy differently along its own target.
