TwistSettings.semantics: Two alphas again, and the unit is turns rather than degrees: 0 to 1 is one full revolution spread across the copy. The rotation is applied about the first axis before the copy is placed on the target, so it twists the copy around its own length.

hints.text: This is an ordinary point processor, not a path node. Its main pins are **In** and **Out** rather than **Paths**, it carries no `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs`, and its own two-point floor is hand-rolled: an input under two points is skipped with a warning, and a target under two points is skipped silently.

Nothing about the input has to be a path. The bounding box is what gets deformed, so a cloud of points is bent just as happily as a row, and points sharing a position along the main axis stay together on the target rather than spreading along it.

UPCGExCopyToPointsSettings.name: Copy to Points
UPCGExCopyToPointsSettings.purpose: Stamps a whole dataset onto every target point, sized and placed to fit. The stock copy node repeats data at positions; this one also fits what it copies into each target's bounds and justifies it there, which is what makes it usable for placing authored arrangements into varied spaces rather than only scattering them.
UPCGExCopyToPointsSettings.situation: An authored arrangement of points that should appear at each of many targets, adapted to each target's size.

mechanism.text: Each target point receives a copy of the source, transformed onto it. The transform block decides how much of the target's own transform applies and how the source is fitted into its bounds, so a target's scale can size the copy or be ignored entirely. The matching block narrows which sources pair with which targets, which is what stops a many-to-many wiring producing every combination.

DataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, allows you to pick which input gets copied to which target point.

fields.name: bInheritRotation

fields.name: bIgnoreBounds
fields.tooltip: Skip bounds calculations and use position only. Disables scale-to-fit and justification.

TransformDetails.semantics: Where the fitting happens, and the reason to reach for this node over the stock one. It decides whether a copy inherits the target's rotation and scale or keeps its own, and whether it is fitted into the target's bounds at all.

TargetsAttributesToCopyTags.semantics: Turns target attributes into tags on the copy's dataset rather than attributes on its points, which is what a downstream filter or matching rule can act on.

TargetsForwarding.semantics: Carries attributes from the target onto the copy that landed on it, which is how each stamped instance learns something about where it went. Without it a copy is indistinguishable from every other copy.

hints.text: Output size is the source count multiplied by the target count. A modest source stamped onto a large scatter is where that becomes a problem, and the matching block is the way to narrow it rather than filtering afterwards.

UPCGExCreateHeuristicAttributeSettings.name: Heuristics : Attribute
UPCGExCreateHeuristicAttributeSettings.purpose: Charges whatever a number on the cluster says to charge. Anything you can compute and write onto Vtx or Edges becomes a cost: a danger field baked from gameplay data, a material price, a hand-painted mask. It is the escape hatch the rest of the family exists to make unnecessary, and the one to reach for when no built-in measurement is the thing you actually care about.
UPCGExCreateHeuristicAttributeSettings.situation: The cost of crossing ground is already recorded on the cluster and a route needs to respect it.

mechanism.text: The value is read once per Vtx or once per Edge, turned into a charge, and held for the whole run, so the charge a step pays depends on where it lands and not on how it got there. With `Source` set to Vtx the value comes from the Vtx the step arrives at, so crossing an edge one way and the other way charge different numbers and a seed's own value is never charged at all. `Mode` decides how the raw number becomes a charge, and it is the only thing that varies. The goal half is a constant here, so this heuristic tells a search what a step costs and nothing about how far it still has to go.

off_label.claim: Because the goal half is a constant, a stack of nothing but Attribute heuristics gives A star no look-ahead: it expands outward in order of accumulated cost with nothing pulling it toward the goal. Pairing one with Heuristics : Shortest Distance is what restores that pull.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExHeuristicAttribute overrides GetEdgeScore alone, so the base FPCGExHeuristicOperation::GetGlobalScore returns GetScoreInternal(0) for every Vtx

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

UPCGExCreateMatchAttrToAttrSettings.name: Match : Attributes
UPCGExCreateMatchAttrToAttrSettings.purpose: Pairs data by comparing one value held on each side. It is the rule for a key or an id: give both sides a matching value and the pairing follows from the data rather than from anything authored on the node. The comparison is not limited to equality, so it also covers thresholds, ranges expressed as one bound, and text tests like starts with or contains.
UPCGExCreateMatchAttrToAttrSettings.situation: Twenty inputs and twenty targets that already carry a shared id, and one node that has to work out the twenty pairs.

mechanism.text: One value is read from each side and compared. The candidate value comes from the @Data domain of the data being processed, under the name given in Candidate Attribute Name. The target value comes from Target Attribute Name, which may address either the @Data domain or a per-point attribute on the target. Check decides how both values are read and which comparison dropdown appears, and the operator under it produces the verdict, with the candidate on the left unless Swap Operands turns it around. The node subtitle spells the finished expression out, so the panel shows what will be compared before anything runs.

UPCGExCreateMatchByIndexSettings.name: Match : By Index
UPCGExCreateMatchByIndexSettings.purpose: Pairs data by position rather than by content. Left at its default it is the rule for two ordered sets that already line up, first with first and second with second. Point the Index Attribute at a real attribute instead and one side names the position it wants on the other, which is how a lookup table drives the pairing.
UPCGExCreateMatchByIndexSettings.situation: Two sets of the same length whose ordering already encodes the pairing, and no shared tag or id to express it with.

mechanism.text: One side supplies a number and the other supplies a position, and the rule matches when they are equal. Source decides which is which: under Target the number is read from the target and compared against the position of the candidate, under Candidate the number is read from the candidate and compared against the position of the target. The number is brought into range by Index Safety first, and the range it is brought into comes from the consumer rather than from this node. Left on the default $Index, no attribute is read at all and the number is the position of the side that would have read one, which makes the rule a plain first-with-first pairing.

UPCGExCreateMatchCopyTagsSettings.name: Match : Copy Tags
UPCGExCreateMatchCopyTagsSettings.purpose: The rule that decides nothing. It rides along with the other rules on the pin and appends the tags of the target it was shown onto the data being processed, so the pairing leaves a trace in the tags. It answers yes to every pair it is given, which is what makes it a passenger rather than a constraint, and it carries no settings of its own.
UPCGExCreateMatchCopyTagsSettings.situation: A pairing that is already expressed by other rules, and downstream nodes that need to know which target each input ended up with.

mechanism.text: It always answers yes, and on its way past it appends every tag the target carries onto the candidate. The candidate keeps its own tags and the target ones are added on top, so tags accumulate rather than replace. Copying only happens under data-to-data matching. On a consumer that runs its rules once per element, Copy to Points and Cluster : Copy to Points among them, nothing is copied and the rule reduces to an unconditional yes.

off_label.claim: Alone on the Match Rules pin of a consumer set to Any, it turns matching into a tag broadcast: every input matches every target and comes out wearing that target tags.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExMatchCopyTags::Test returns true unconditionally, and FDataMatcher::Test in Any mode accepts the pair on the first Optional rule that passes

outputs.label: Match Rule
outputs.note: Wire it to the Match Rules pin of a node that does data matching, alongside the rules that do the deciding.

fields.name: Strictness
fields.tooltip: Match Strictness

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the match result (match becomes no-match and vice versa).

hints.text: The copy happens as the rule is reached, before the rest of the stack has finished. Under All mode a rule sitting after this one can still reject the pair, and the tags copied on the way past stay on the data.

The Copy Tags node is a different mechanism with the same name. It has its own tag filtering and copies only what is missing; this rule appends the whole tag set of the target and offers nothing to select with.

UPCGExCreateMatchOverlapSettings.name: Match : Overlap
UPCGExCreateMatchOverlapSettings.purpose: Pairs data by where it sits. The bounds of the whole dataset on each side are tested for intersection, so nothing about the individual points enters into it. It is the only rule in the family that can match transitively: with Recursive on, data that overlaps something already matched joins the same group, which is how a scatter of overlapping datasets collapses into connected clusters of them.
UPCGExCreateMatchOverlapSettings.situation: Datasets tiled or scattered across a level, and an operation that should only pair the ones sharing space.

mechanism.text: Each side is reduced to its axis-aligned bounding box and the two boxes are tested for intersection. Expansion Mode grows the target box first, either by adding to its extents or by scaling them, and the value can be read per target from its @Data domain. Min Overlap Ratio raises the bar from touching to a share of volume, measured as the intersection volume over the volume of whichever box is smaller. A side that carries no spatial data, or no valid bounds, produces the value of Invert rather than a verdict.

off_label.claim: With Recursive on and a consumer that partitions its inputs, this becomes a connected-component grouping over bounds: everything reachable through a chain of overlaps ends up in one group, whatever the chain length.
off_label.grounded_in: FDataMatcher::GetMatchingSourcesIndices runs a breadth-first expansion over the matched set while any rule reports WantsRecursion, which only this rule does

UPCGExCreateMatchRandomSettings.name: Match : Random
UPCGExCreateMatchRandomSettings.purpose: Thins a pairing out. It rolls a number for each pair it is shown and passes when the roll clears a threshold, so a set of pairings that all satisfy the real rules can be reduced to a share of them. The roll is derived from a seed and from which two datasets are in hand, so the same graph run twice produces the same pairs.
UPCGExCreateMatchRandomSettings.situation: Rules that pair correctly but pair too much, and a need for a repeatable subset rather than all of it.

mechanism.text: One number between zero and one is derived for each target and candidate pairing, from Random Seed and from the position of each of the two datasets. The pair passes when that number is at or above Threshold, so raising Threshold lets fewer pairs through and a Threshold of zero lets every pair through. Invert Threshold turns the comparison round. Nothing about the contents of either dataset enters the roll, which is what makes it stable across runs.

UPCGExCreateMatchSharedTagSettings.name: Match : Shared Tag
UPCGExCreateMatchSharedTagSettings.purpose: Pairs data by the tags both sides already carry. Three questions are on offer: do both sides carry one named tag, do they have any tag in common, or does the target carry everything the candidate does. Tags survive most upstream operations, which is what makes this the rule reached for when the pairing was decided somewhere far upstream and has to be recovered here.
UPCGExCreateMatchSharedTagSettings.situation: Datasets tagged by whatever produced them, and a node that has to rebuild the pairing from those tags alone.

mechanism.text: The tag sets of the two datasets are compared and Mode decides what comparison is made. Specific Tag looks for one named tag on both sides. Any Shared passes on the first tag the two sets have in common. All Shared asks whether the target carries every tag the candidate does, which is a one-way test: tags the target has and the candidate lacks are ignored. Tags carrying a value are handled apart from plain tags throughout, and the value checkbox decides whether their values have to agree.

UPCGExCreateMatchTagToAttrSettings.name: Match : Tags × Attributes
UPCGExCreateMatchTagToAttrSettings.purpose: Pairs a tag on one side against an attribute on the other. Tags travel with data through operations that would drop an attribute, and attributes hold typed values that a tag name cannot, so this is the rule for the common case where the two sides recorded the same fact in different places. It can test the tag name alone, or go on to compare the value the tag carries against a value read from the target.
UPCGExCreateMatchTagToAttrSettings.situation: Inputs tagged upstream by whatever produced them, and targets holding the same information as an attribute.

mechanism.text: A tag name is resolved, then looked for on the candidate. Match decides how loosely that name is compared, ignoring case throughout, so anything other than Equals can select several tags on the candidate at once. Without value matching, one selected tag is enough and the rule stops there. With it on, only tags carrying a value are selected at all, every one of them is compared against the value read from the target attribute, and the pair passes only if all of them satisfy the comparison.

UPCGExCreateShapeCircleSettings.name: Shape : Circle
UPCGExCreateShapeCircleSettings.purpose: Builds a ring of points around each seed. The two angles make it an arc as readily as a full circle, so it covers everything from a closed loop to a short curve, and both are read per seed, which is what lets one builder produce a different sweep at every one.
UPCGExCreateShapeCircleSettings.situation: Seeds that should each become a ring, an arc, or a fan of points around themselves.

mechanism.text: Points are placed along the arc from `Start Angle` to `End Angle`, at whatever spacing the shared resolution settles. Both angles are resolved per seed, so the sweep can vary across a scatter from one builder. `Is Closed Loop` decides whether the result is treated as closing back on itself, which matters to everything downstream that distinguishes a loop from an open path.

UPCGExCreateShapeFiblatSettings.name: Shape : φ Sphere
UPCGExCreateShapeFiblatSettings.purpose: Builds points spread evenly over a sphere around each seed. Distributing points on a sphere is not something a grid can do without bunching at the poles; a Fibonacci lattice avoids that by walking a spiral whose turn angle never repeats a pattern, so the spacing stays near-uniform everywhere.
UPCGExCreateShapeFiblatSettings.situation: Seeds that need points spread over a sphere without the crowding a latitude and longitude grid produces.

mechanism.text: Points are placed one at a time along a spiral over the sphere's surface, each advanced from the last by a fixed turn. The value of that turn is what keeps successive points from lining up: an irrational proportion never closes into a repeating ring, which is why the constant matters more here than any other setting. `Epsilon` nudges the endpoints, which is where lattices of this kind are least even.

UPCGExCreateShapePolygonSettings.name: Shape : Polygon
UPCGExCreateShapePolygonSettings.purpose: Builds a regular polygon around each seed, optionally with spokes running to its centre. Where **Shape : Circle** places points at even angles along a curve, this places them along straight edges between corners, so the resolution fills the edges rather than the arc. It can also mark which points are corners and where along an edge each one sits.
UPCGExCreateShapePolygonSettings.situation: Seeds that should become regular outlines, stars or wheels, with the corners identifiable afterwards.

UPCGExCreateShapesSettings.name: Create Shapes
UPCGExCreateShapesSettings.purpose: Runs the shape builders. A Shape node describes a form and produces nothing on its own; this is what turns each of your points into an instance of that form. The input points become seeds rather than output, so a scatter of a hundred seeds with one builder wired in leaves as a hundred shapes.
UPCGExCreateShapesSettings.situation: Seed points that should each be replaced by a generated form, sized and oriented from the seed.

mechanism.text: Each seed point is handed to every builder on the pin, and each builder produces one shape around it. The seed supplies the position, the orientation and the bounds the shape is fitted against, so the variety across the output comes from the variety across the seeds rather than from anything random here. The point-count guards drop shapes that came out too small or too large before they reach the output.

off_label.claim: Writing the shape id turns a mixed output into something separable: with several builders wired, every generated point knows which form it came from, so a partition downstream splits them without any tagging upstream.
off_label.grounded_in: The shape id output writes the builder's own identifier onto each generated point.

bForceOutputToElement.tooltip: Force writing to points, otherwise defaults to @Data (even if unspecified)
bForceOutputToElement.semantics: Decides the shape of the output rather than its content: whether the generated shapes arrive as one dataset or split per element. It is what downstream nodes that operate per dataset need, at the cost of many more datasets.

MinPointCount.tooltip: Discarded if point count is less than
MinPointCount.semantics: Shapes that came out with fewer points than this are dropped rather than emitted. It is the guard against a fitting that collapsed, since a shape reduced to a point or two is usually a configuration problem rather than a wanted result.
MinPointCount.trap: The matching upper guard ships off, so nothing limits how large a shape may get until it is turned on. A density-based resolution on large seeds is where that bites.

UPCGExCreateSplineSettings.name: Create Spline
UPCGExCreateSplineSettings.purpose: Turns each path into a spline. One input dataset becomes one spline, one path point becomes one spline control point, and a point type decides what the curve does between them. `Mode` adds a second job on top of that: creating a real spline component on an actor, alongside the data. This is a way out of the paths section rather than a step inside it, and **Spline to Path** is the way back.
UPCGExCreateSplineSettings.situation: A run of points has to leave the graph as a spline, either as data for something that samples splines or as a component in the level.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns one spline for each, on a **Splines** pin typed for spline data. There is no points output at all, so nothing downstream of this node is a path. Each point becomes a control point in the same order, keeping its location, rotation and scale, and its attributes ride along with it; the path's own closed flag decides whether the spline closes. Tags on the input dataset travel with the spline data, and onto the component's tags when one is made. An input of fewer than two points is dropped with a warning, and disabling the node forwards nothing.

off_label.claim: Left on the shipped `Default Point Type` of Linear, the spline traces the input polyline and nothing else: no tangents are ever consulted and no control point moves. That makes the node a type adapter for anything that accepts splines and not points, with no shape change to account for.
off_label.grounded_in: Linear maps straight to the engine's linear spline point type, and the tangent handler is only built when GetApplyTangents returns true, which Linear never does

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to convert. Each dataset becomes one spline.

outputs.label: Splines
outputs.note: One spline per input dataset. A spline pin, not a points pin, so no path node will take it.

Mode.semantics: The **Splines** pin carries the data in every entry. What the entries other than data only add is a spline component on the target actor, attached by `Attachment Rules` and carrying the input dataset's tags as component tags. Those entries also stop the node caching its result and pin its output phase to the game thread, so a graph that regenerates often pays for them on every run.
Mode.trap: A target actor is resolved and required in every entry, data only included, because control-point locations are stored relative to it and the spline data carries its transform as its own. `Target Actor` sits under the node's advanced settings and falls back to the actor the PCG component sits on; where neither resolves, the node stops with an invalid target actor error even though nothing was being spawned.

DefaultPointType.semantics: Carried by every control point of every spline unless the attribute route below overrides it. `Curve Custom Tangent` is the single entry that opens the `Tangents` block; under any other entry the block is shut and the arrive and leave vectors handed to the spline stay at zero.

PointTypeAttribute.semantics: An integer read per point, using the numeric values behind the type entries: 0 Linear, 1 Curve, 2 Constant, 3 Curve Clamped, 4 Curve Custom Tangent. A value outside 0 to 4 is ignored and that point falls back to `Default Point Type` with nothing in the log.
PointTypeAttribute.trap: Turning this route on closes the `Tangents` block for the whole node, and the block being shut means no tangents are computed for any point. A point set to Curve Custom Tangent through the attribute therefore reaches the spline with zero-length arrive and leave vectors. Per-point types and custom tangents cannot be combined here.

Tangents.tooltip: Per-point tangent settings. Can't be set if the spline is linear.
Tangents.semantics: Read under one `Default Point Type` entry and no other, and only while the per-point type attribute is off. Its shipped route reads `ArriveTangent` and `LeaveTangent`, the two names **Path : Write Tangents** writes by default, so wiring that node upstream needs no configuration on either side.

TargetActor.tooltip: Actor the splines are created on, and the frame their control points are placed in. Required in every mode.

PostProcessFunctionNames.tooltip: Specify a list of functions to be called on the target actor after spline creation. Functions need to be parameter-less and with "CallInEditor" flag enabled.
PostProcessFunctionNames.semantics: Called on the target actor in every mode, including data only, so a function here runs whether or not a component was made.

AttachmentRules.semantics: Read only where a component is created, which is every `Mode` entry other than data only.

UPCGExCreateTensorConstantSettings.name: Tensor : Constant
UPCGExCreateTensorConstantSettings.purpose: One authored direction, the same everywhere, with no source geometry and no pin to wire. Two jobs come out of that. It is the background current a field is built on top of, and it is the safety net: because it answers at every position, adding one at a low weight turns a field full of holes into one that always has something to say. **Tensor : Inertia (Constant)** is the other blanket tensor, and it answers with the sampled point's own heading instead of a fixed bearing.
UPCGExCreateTensorConstantSettings.situation: An extrusion stops early in the empty spaces between effectors and the field needs a floor under it.

mechanism.text: Every sampled position gets the same answer: the **Direction** vector, at a length set by **Potency**, claiming a share of the composite set by **Tensor Weight**. There is no reach, no falloff and no way for this tensor to decline, so its share is constant across the whole field and it is the only thing keeping a position covered where nothing else reaches. Held at a low **Tensor Weight** it barely shows where other tensors are present and takes over completely where they are not.

TensorWeight.semantics: Worth keeping well below the other tensors on the pin when this one is present as a floor. It answers everywhere, so its share is paid at every position, not only in the gaps it exists to cover.

Direction.tooltip: The constant direction vector for this tensor.
Direction.semantics: A world-space direction, taken as written. Nothing rotates it: it does not follow an actor, a spline or the point being sampled, which is what makes it usable as a fixed bearing under everything else.

Potency.tooltip: Base potency multiplier for this tensor.

UPCGExCreateTensorFlowSettings.name: Tensor : Flow
UPCGExCreateTensorFlowSettings.purpose: Gives every effector point a heading and blends those headings into a current. Where **Tensor : Pole** points at its effectors, this one points the way they are facing, so a field is authored by placing and rotating points rather than by drawing a curve. The heading is one axis of each effector's own transform, or a vector attribute on it. Its relatives take the heading from a curve instead: **Tensor : Path Flow** from ordered points, **Tensor : Spline Flow** from spline data.
UPCGExCreateTensorFlowSettings.situation: A handful of oriented points have to stand in for wind, current or grain across an area.

mechanism.text: Each effector's heading is resolved once, when this node runs, and stored with the point. At a sampled position every effector in reach contributes its heading, and those contributions are averaged by weight, so the field turns smoothly from one effector's heading toward the next across the gap between them. A position no effector reaches leaves this tensor out of the field entirely. The **Guide Curve** rotates each contribution before it is summed, so a curve with a sideways component fans the heading out with distance instead of holding it straight.

inputs.label: Effectors
inputs.note: The points the headings are read from. Each one reaches as far as its own scaled bounds and contributes nothing past that.

UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaConstantSetting.name: Tensor : Inertia (Constant)
UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaConstantSetting.purpose: Hands back the heading the sampled thing already had, everywhere, with an optional twist applied to it. It takes no source geometry: there is no pin to wire, and it answers at every position in the field, which is the whole difference from **Tensor : Inertia**, whose effectors decide where the same reading applies. The **Offset** turns a straight coast into a steady curve, because a fixed angle added to a heading that keeps updating is a turn rate.
UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaConstantSetting.situation: Extrusions should hold their heading across the whole field, or bend at a constant rate along it.

mechanism.text: At every sampled position this tensor reads the transform it was handed, applies the **Offset** rotation to it, and answers with the chosen axis of the result. There is no reach and no falloff: it always answers, so it always counts toward the composite and its share is decided by **Tensor Weight** and **Potency** alone. Because the reading is taken fresh at each step and the offset is applied on top of it, a non-zero offset compounds into a spiral rather than a one-off deflection.

off_label.claim: It always answers, so like **Tensor : Constant** it keeps a field from having gaps. Unlike Constant, the fallback direction it supplies is the sampled point's own heading, which reads as coasting rather than as a sudden turn onto a fixed bearing.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExTensorInertiaConstant::Sample emplaces one sample unconditionally, giving the tensor a non-zero source count at every position

Axis.semantics: Names the axis of the sampled transform, read after the **Offset** has been applied. **Forward** with a zero offset gives a pure coast; any other axis is a fixed sideways push relative to the heading.

Offset.semantics: Rotates the sampled transform before the axis is read. Applied once per sample against a heading that keeps changing, so a few degrees here becomes a continuous turn along an extrusion rather than a single deflection.

UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaSettings.name: Tensor : Inertia
UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaSettings.purpose: Hands back the heading the sampled thing already had. Every other tensor answers with something the field knows; this one reads an axis of the transform being sampled and returns that, which keeps whatever is being driven going the way it was going. The effectors do not supply a direction here, only a shape: this tensor answers where they reach and nowhere else. **Tensor : Inertia (Constant)** is the same reading with no effectors at all, covering everywhere.
UPCGExCreateTensorInertiaSettings.situation: An extrusion crossing a patch of field should coast straight through it instead of being turned.

mechanism.text: At a sampled position, if any effector reaches it, this tensor answers with the chosen axis of the transform it was handed; if none reach, it drops out of the field entirely. Each effector in reach contributes that same reading, weighted by its own **Potency** and **Weight** and their falloff curves, so the effectors decide how strongly momentum is asserted and where, never which way it points. The direction changes as the thing being driven turns, which is what separates this from a fixed direction: it is momentum, read fresh at each sample.

off_label.claim: Give the effectors small bounds and this becomes a set of coasting patches: an extrusion holds its heading inside them and is steered normally everywhere else, so the same field can be made rigid in places without adding a second field.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExTensorInertia::Sample answers only for effectors returned by the octree reach test, and contributes nothing outside them

UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseBoundedSettings.name: Tensor : Noise (Bounded)
UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseBoundedSettings.purpose: The same noise reading as **Tensor : Noise**, confined to where effector points reach. The noise still comes from the **Noise :** sub-nodes on the **Noises** pin and is still read from world position, so the pattern is continuous across the effectors rather than restarting inside each one; what the effectors add is a boundary and a falloff. Reach for this one when the wander belongs in specific places, and for the unbounded version when it belongs everywhere.
UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseBoundedSettings.situation: A field should stay orderly except in a few marked pockets where it breaks up.

mechanism.text: The noise is evaluated once per sampled position, so every effector reaching that position contributes the same direction and only their **Potency** and **Weight** differ. Those are read from each effector and scaled by their falloff curves against the distance to it, which is where the boundary and its softness come from: strength fades toward the edge of an effector's bounds and stops at it. Outside every effector this tensor drops out of the field entirely, and a **Masks** noise reading zero drops it out too.

UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseSettings.name: Tensor : Noise
UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseSettings.purpose: Reads a 3D noise as a direction, at every position in the field. The **Noise :** nodes wired into its **Noises** pin decide what the field looks like; this node only turns their output into a tensor. It takes no source geometry and covers everywhere, which makes it the usual way to break up a field that is otherwise too orderly. **Tensor : Noise (Bounded)** is the same reading confined to effector bounds, for noise in specific places rather than throughout.
UPCGExCreateTensorNoiseSettings.situation: A flow reads too clean and needs wander added to it without moving any of the points that define it.

mechanism.text: At each sampled position the noise stack is evaluated and its vector becomes the direction, at a length set by **Potency** and claiming a share of the composite set by **Tensor Weight**. There is no reach and no falloff, so with nothing on the **Masks** pin this tensor answers at every position and keeps a field from ever having gaps. A mask changes that: it is read at the same position, and where it comes back at zero this tensor declines to answer at all, so masks are how a noise field gets holes rather than merely quiet patches.

off_label.claim: With no mask wired it answers everywhere, so a noise at a low **Tensor Weight** doubles as the fallback that keeps a gappy field from failing to sample, the job **Tensor : Constant** is usually reached for.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExTensorNoise::Sample emplaces a sample unconditionally when NoiseMaskGenerator is null

UPCGExCreateTensorNullSettings.name: Tensor : Null
UPCGExCreateTensorNullSettings.purpose: The eraser. It has no direction of its own: wherever its effectors reach it answers with nothing, and it claims enough of the composite to drag the rest of the field toward zero there. That is how a field gets dead zones without deleting the tensors that would otherwise fill them. It still answers, so a position inside a null zone counts as covered and an extrusion keeps going rather than failing outright, which is the difference between this and leaving a gap in the field.
UPCGExCreateTensorNullSettings.situation: A field is right everywhere except inside a few volumes where nothing should move.

mechanism.text: Every effector in reach contributes a zero direction, and this tensor's share of the composite grows with how many of them reached. One effector erases lightly, several overlapping erase hard, and **Tensor Weight** scales the whole effect. Because the answer is zero rather than absent, the field still reports as valid inside the zone; what a consumer gets there is a direction shortened toward nothing rather than no direction at all. Outside every effector's reach this tensor drops out and changes nothing.

inputs.label: Effectors
inputs.note: The points the dead zones form around. Each one erases as far as its own scaled bounds, so the zone is shaped by scaling the points.

UPCGExCreateTensorPathFlowSettings.name: Tensor : Path Flow
UPCGExCreateTensorPathFlowSettings.purpose: A current running along a curve, drawn from ordered points. Each dataset on the **Paths** pin is turned into a curve, and near it the field points the way the curve is heading. Two neighbours differ in one thing each: **Tensor : Spline Flow** takes real spline data instead of building a curve from points, and **Tensor : Path Pole** aims at the curve rather than along it.
UPCGExCreateTensorPathFlowSettings.situation: Extrusions or transforms should follow a route that was already authored as a path.

mechanism.text: Every curve on the pin is asked for its closest point to the sampled position. A curve answers when that point is within reach, contributing the chosen axis of the curve's own transform there, and the contributions from several curves are averaged by weight; a position no curve reaches leaves this tensor out of the field entirely. Reach is **Radius** scaled by the point scale at that place on the curve, so the field is a tube whose width follows the path's own scaling. The **Guide Curve** rotates each contribution before it is summed, which fans the flow outward or inward as the tube edge is approached.

Each dataset on the **Paths** pin becomes a curve, and near it the field runs straight out from the nearest place on it, so the shipped behaviour is a push and a pull is one **Invert** away. UPCGExCreateTensorPoleSettings.name: Tensor : Pole
UPCGExCreateTensorPoleSettings.purpose: Turns effector points into a radial field. At any position an effector reaches, the direction runs straight out from that effector, so the shipped behaviour is a push and a pull is one **Invert** away. This is the tensor for a field that has to organise itself around particular places rather than follow a heading. Its two relatives aim at a curve instead of a point: **Tensor : Path Pole** builds one from ordered points, **Tensor : Spline Pole** takes spline data as it comes.

mechanism.text: Every effector whose reach covers the sampled position contributes the direction from itself out to that position, and those contributions are averaged by weight. UPCGExCreateTensorSpinSettings.name: Tensor : Spin
UPCGExCreateTensorSpinSettings.purpose: Turns effector points into vortices. Each effector carries an axis, and the direction at any position it reaches is the one perpendicular to both that axis and the line back to the effector, which is a circle around it. Where **Tensor : Pole** moves toward or away and **Tensor : Flow** moves along, this one moves around. The axis is one axis of the effector's own transform, or a vector attribute on it, and it ships set to **Up**.
UPCGExCreateTensorSpinSettings.situation: Extrusions have to wind around a set of points rather than run at them or past them.

mechanism.text: Each effector's axis is resolved once, when this node runs, and stored with the point. At a sampled position every effector in reach contributes the direction perpendicular to its axis and to the line joining the two, and those contributions are averaged by weight; a position no effector reaches leaves this tensor out of the field entirely. The circulation always lies in the plane the axis is normal to, so tilting an effector tilts its whole vortex, and **Invert** under **Sampling Mutations** reverses which way round it turns.

UPCGExCullOnEmptySettings.name: Cull On Empty
UPCGExCullOnEmptySettings.purpose: Stops a branch from running when there is nothing in it. Empty data still travels down a wire in vanilla PCG and still wakes every node it reaches; this node deactivates its output pin instead, so the branch is culled rather than executed on nothing. Check Only turns it into a pure test that reports the answer as a bool and forwards no data at all, and two palette entries preset that mode with and without inversion.
UPCGExCullOnEmptySettings.situation: A branch whose upstream sometimes produces nothing, where the downstream work is expensive or would write misleading empty results.

mechanism.text: Each input is judged non-empty by its own kind: point data by point count, splines and polylines by segment count, attribute sets by entry count, and anything else by merely existing. The non-empty ones are forwarded and the empty ones are dropped; if none of them were non-empty the output pin is deactivated. The verdict is also available as a bool attribute set, which is what Check Only leaves behind once the data pin is gone.

off_label.claim: The bool pin can be produced alongside the forwarded data, not only in Check Only, which lets one node both gate the branch and hand a downstream override the same answer as a value.
off_label.grounded_in: the Is Empty pin is declared when either bCheckOnly or bOutputIsEmpty is set, and the data pin is removed only by bCheckOnly

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Any data. Every input on the pin is judged separately.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The non-empty inputs, forwarded by reference. Deactivated when none of them were non-empty.
outputs.condition: removed entirely when Check Only is on

outputs.label: IsEmpty
outputs.note: A one-row attribute set holding a bool named by the Output Is Empty setting.
outputs.condition: when Check Only or Output Is Empty is on

pins.dynamic: The In and Out pins accept and mirror any type; the bool pin is always an attribute set.

bCheckOnly.tooltip: Only report whether the inputs were empty. The data output pin is removed, so nothing is forwarded.
bCheckOnly.semantics: Removes the data output entirely, so nothing is forwarded and the node becomes a test that only reports. It also draws the node compact.

bOutputIsEmpty.tooltip: Also emit the Is Empty result on its own pin, alongside the forwarded data.
bOutputIsEmpty.semantics: Adds the bool pin alongside the forwarded data, which is the only way to have both.

OutputIsEmpty.tooltip: Name of the 'bool' attribute the Is Empty result is written to.
OutputIsEmpty.trap: Its edit condition names the Output Is Empty toggle, so in Check Only the field is greyed out in the panel while still deciding the attribute name.

bInvert.tooltip: If enabled, inverts the output bool
bInvert.semantics: Flips the bool before it is written, so the attribute reads true when at least one input had content.
bInvert.trap: Inversion never reaches the pin deactivation, which always follows the real emptiness. In Check Only that is harmless, and outside it the data pin still culls on genuinely empty input however this is set. The same greying applies as to the name field.

hints.text: The two Is Data Empty palette entries switch Check Only on, and the NOT variant switches inversion on with it. Both fields are then greyed out in the panel while still being what the node uses, so a preset node looks unconfigured and is not.
Mixed inputs keep the pin active. A pin carrying one empty and one populated dataset forwards the populated one and stays live; deactivation needs every input to be empty.

UPCGExCutEdgesSettings.name: Cluster : Cut
UPCGExCutEdgesSettings.purpose: Uses paths as cutting geometry against a cluster, removing whatever they run through. It is the geometric counterpart to **Cluster : Refine**, which decides by rule what an edge is worth; here the decision is made by where a path went. `Invert` turns the same tests around and keeps only what the paths touched, which is how a corridor is lifted out of a larger cluster rather than carved from it.
UPCGExCutEdgesSettings.situation: A road network or a set of boundary paths has to open a gap in a cluster that was generated without knowing about them.

mechanism.text: Every cutting path is read as a run of segments, and every element that `Mode` names is tested against all of them. An edge is cut when the closest approach between it and a path segment falls inside the tolerance; a Vtx is cut when a path segment passes within the tolerance of it. The two filter pins are exceptions rather than selections: an element that passes its filters is set aside and never tested. What is left is rebuilt through the graph builder, and an edge reaches that rebuild only when both its Vtx do, so cutting a Vtx takes every edge at it whatever the propagation toggles say. `Invert` runs the same tests and keeps the other side: everything starts removed, and only what a path touched or a filter protected comes back.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx dataset.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges datasets, one per cluster. Each is cut independently against the same paths.

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The cutting geometry, read as segments between consecutive points. Datasets of fewer than two points are dropped with a warning, and the node errors out when none survive.

inputs.label: NodeFilters
inputs.note: Protection, not selection: a Vtx that passes is never tested and never cut. Unconnected, nothing is protected.
inputs.condition: when Mode is not Edges

inputs.label: EdgeFilters
inputs.note: The same contract for edges: passing means exempt from the geometry test. Unconnected, nothing is protected.
inputs.condition: when Mode is not Nodes

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The surviving Vtx, rebuilt through the graph builder.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component of the result, so a cut that severs a cluster in two hands back two Edges datasets against one Vtx dataset.

IntersectionDetails.tooltip: Intersection detection settings for path-to-edge overlap.
IntersectionDetails.semantics: The `Tolerance` inside this block is the only distance that decides a cut, for edges and for Vtx alike, and it is measured in world units. The angle limits apply to edges only: they compare the edge direction against the path segment direction, so a cluster edge running alongside a path can be spared while one crossing it is cut.

bInvert.semantics: Everything starts removed and the tests put things back. An edge that a path touched restores itself and both of its Vtx, so an inverted edge cut hands back a connected strip along the path without further help. A Vtx or edge kept by a preservation filter restores only itself, so a protected edge whose Vtx were not also protected still falls out of the rebuild.

Mode.semantics: Decides which elements are tested, and with it which filter pin is on the node. **Nodes** tests Vtx against the paths and lets the rebuild drop whatever edges that stranded. **Edges** tests edges and leaves every Vtx standing, which usually leaves points behind with nothing attached. **Edges & Nodes** does both, and is the setting the rest of the panel assumes.

NodeExpansion.tooltip: Widens the node's local bounds before they are transformed, so the expansion scales with the point. Only widens the candidate search, never the distance that decides a cut.
NodeExpansion.semantics: It widens the Vtx bounds in the point's own space, before the transform, and `Tolerance` widens that same candidate box in world units after it. The two stack, so a tolerance raised well past the default still gathers the segments it needs without this being raised alongside.

NodeDistanceSettings.tooltip: How to measure distance from path to node center vs bounds.
NodeDistanceSettings.semantics: Where the distance to the path is measured from on the Vtx. **Center** measures from the point location, so the tolerance is the whole story. **Sphere Bounds** and **Box Bounds** measure from the point's bounds toward the path, so a large point is cut by a path that never came near its centre.

bAffectedNodesAffectConnectedEdges.tooltip: When a node is affected, also mark its connected edges as affected.
bAffectedNodesAffectConnectedEdges.semantics: Earns its keep under `Invert`, where a restored Vtx also restores its edges and the Vtx at their far ends, spreading the kept region one step outward from each hit.
bAffectedNodesAffectConnectedEdges.trap: In the ordinary direction it changes nothing that reaches the output. A cut Vtx already loses every edge at it, because the rebuild refuses an edge whose Vtx is gone.

bAffectedEdgesAffectEndpoints.tooltip: When an edge is affected, also mark its endpoint nodes as affected.
bAffectedEdgesAffectEndpoints.semantics: Makes a cut spread the other way: an edge the paths cut takes both of its Vtx with it, and those Vtx take their remaining edges. One path crossing a single edge can therefore open a hole several edges wide.

bKeepEdgesThatConnectValidNodes.display: Keep Edges That Connect Valid Nodes
bKeepEdgesThatConnectValidNodes.tooltip: When inverting, keep edges that connect two preserved nodes even if the edge itself wasn't preserved.
bKeepEdgesThatConnectValidNodes.semantics: Closes the gaps an inverted cut leaves in its own result. Once the tests have run, any edge whose two Vtx both survived is restored, so the kept Vtx come back as a connected sub-cluster rather than as pairs joined only where a path happened to lie along an edge.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: The last thing that can drop a result. A cut usually breaks one cluster into several components, and the small and big cluster limits are measured per component, so fragments the cut created can be discarded here rather than by the cut.

hints.text: An edge cannot outlive its Vtx. The rebuild admits an edge only when both of its endpoints survived, so an edge that passed its preservation filters still disappears when a path cut one of the Vtx it joins. Where an edge has to survive, protect its Vtx as well.

UPCGExDataBoundsFilterProviderSettings.name: Data Filter : Bounds
UPCGExDataBoundsFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Measures the box a dataset occupies and compares one number taken from it, answering for the dataset as a whole. `Operand A` picks which reading: a corner of the box, its size or half-size, the volume it encloses, or the ratio between two of its axis lengths. Vector readings pass through `Sub Operand`, which collapses them to a single scalar, and the result meets `Operand B`, which carries both the number compared against and the operator.
UPCGExDataBoundsFilterProviderSettings.situation: Several datasets on one pin where only the ones big enough, or square enough, deserve the expensive work downstream.

mechanism.text: The box is the world-space bounds the input data reports, which encloses every point's own bounds after its transform and widens as `Steepness` drops, so scale and per-point bounds move the result as much as the positions do. `Operand A` decides what is read off it: `Min` and `Max` are opposite corners, `Size` the full dimensions and `Extents` half of them, and all four hand a vector to `Sub Operand`. `Volume` multiplies the three sizes together, and the two ratio readings divide one axis size by another, so both arrive at a single number without `Sub Operand`.

off_label.claim: `Volume` compared against zero separates datasets with real extent from ones collapsed onto a plane or a line, since a flat dataset leaves one of the three sizes at zero and the product with it.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExDataBoundsAspect::Volume multiplying the three components of the input bounds size in the filter's collection test

outputs.label: Data Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. The Data Filter family qualifies for dataset-level evaluation by construction, with no condition on how the node is configured, so every filter pin in the plugin takes it, **Uber Branch** and **Break** included.

UPCGExDataHashSettings.name: Data Hash
UPCGExDataHashSettings.purpose: One random value derived from the shape of whatever is plugged in, and from nothing else. It reads no attribute: what it hashes is how many datasets arrived, what kind each one is, how many elements or segments it holds, and where its bounds sit. The value therefore stays put while the data keeps its shape and rerolls when the shape changes, which is what makes it a per-region or per-graph random number that survives a regeneration. The output is typed, anything from a boolean to a Transform, and lands as a single attribute on a Param pin.
UPCGExDataHashSettings.situation: A whole branch of the graph needs one random value that stays the same until the upstream data meaningfully changes.

mechanism.text: The input is read for its shape only. Each dataset contributes a category (point, poly line, param, other spatial, or anything else), a count, and its bounds quantised to a fixed grid so that floating-point drift below that grid does not disturb the result; a param contributes its entry count and no bounds. Those are mixed in connection order together with `Salt` and the number of datasets, and the result seeds a random stream from which exactly one value of the chosen type is drawn. The input does not come out: the node's only output is the value.

off_label.claim: Because attribute values are never read, the value survives any amount of editing that leaves counts and bounds alone, which makes it usable as a per-region constant that a re-run of the same layout reproduces.
off_label.grounded_in: HashInput reads only the class category, the element or segment count, and the bounds; no metadata is touched

off_label.claim: Wire nothing at all and the value is still deterministic, derived from Salt and a count of zero, which turns the node into a plain seeded constant of the chosen type.
off_label.grounded_in: the hash starts from the FNV basis, mixes Salt and the input count unconditionally, and the input pin is declared as optional

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Any combination of data. Only its kind, count and bounds are read, and connection order matters.

outputs.label: Value
outputs.note: One attribute set with a single entry, carrying the drawn value under the name given by `Output Attribute Name`.

pins.dynamic: The Value pin reports the metadata type named by `Output Type`, so a downstream node sees the right type without a conversion step.

OutputType.tooltip: Output value type. Drives the output pin's metadata type.
OutputType.semantics: Decides both the drawn value and the type the output pin advertises. Vector, Rotator and Transform draw one number per component from the same range; Quaternion is the exception, drawing a uniformly distributed orientation rather than three angles unless a range is given.

OutputAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the attribute the random value is written to on the output Param Data.

Salt.tooltip: Extra integer salt mixed into the hash. Change this to re-roll the value without touching upstream inputs.
Salt.semantics: The reroll. It is mixed in before anything else, so changing it moves the value without touching the graph upstream, and the same salt against the same data always returns the same value.

RangeMin.tooltip: Minimum value (inclusive). For vector / quat / rotator / transform types, applied per-component. For Quaternion, treated as Euler degrees on each axis.
RangeMin.semantics: Its toggle is what switches the defaults off. Left off, integer types draw across their entire type range, Transform scale draws from zero to one, and everything else draws from minus one to one. Turned on, the pair is sorted before use, applies per component, and is read as Euler degrees per axis for a Quaternion.
RangeMin.trap: Boolean ignores the range entirely and stays an even coin flip.

RangeMax.tooltip: Maximum value (inclusive). For vector / quat / rotator / transform types, applied per-component. For Quaternion, treated as Euler degrees on each axis.

hints.text: Editing attribute values changes nothing here. Only the count of datasets, each one's kind, its element or segment count, and its bounds reach the hash, so a graph that rewrites every attribute in place gets the same number back.
Connection order is part of the input. Reordering the wires into the input pin without changing any of the data produces a different value.

UPCGExDataMatchFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Data Match
UPCGExDataMatchFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Turns a dataset pairing into a filter verdict. The match rules that normally tell a node which target data goes with which input are wired here instead, and the answer they give, whether this dataset pairs with anything on the Targets pin, becomes the pass or fail. The verdict is one per dataset and every element in it inherits the same answer, so this is how tags and data-domain attributes get to decide which datasets a consumer works on. It declares dataset-level support unconditionally, so the consumers that judge whole datasets accept it as it comes: Uber Filter (Data), Uber Branch and Break among them.
UPCGExDataMatchFilterProviderSettings.situation: Whole datasets have to be kept or dropped according to which reference dataset they belong with.

mechanism.text: One verdict per dataset. The dataset being tested is offered to the wired match rules against every dataset on the Targets pin, and pairing with at least one of them is a pass; Mode decides whether every rule has to agree or one is enough, and Invert flips the outcome. Asking this filter about a single element returns the answer computed for the dataset that element belongs to, which is why it behaves the same on a per-element filter pin as on a dataset-level one. Rules compare data to data, so tags and data-domain attributes are all the pairing has to work with.

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: The reference datasets each input is tested against. Every dataset on the pin is a candidate; pairing with one of them is enough.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: The match rule sub-nodes doing the pairing. Required at the default Mode of All, and again at Any.
inputs.condition: when Mode is All or Any, which includes the default

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, and it is also accepted by the consumers that evaluate whole datasets.

CacheData.tooltip: Cache the results of this node. Cached data persists until inputs change, avoiding re-computation.
CacheData.semantics: This node never caches, whatever the setting says. Its answer depends on the target data arriving on the pin, so it is re-derived on every execution.

hints.text: Two separate failures land on Missing Data Policy here: a Targets pin that arrives empty, and a Match Rules pin that arrives empty while Mode is All or Any. Both are settled before any element is tested, and the default of Fail substitutes an always-false filter rather than stopping the graph, so the symptom is an empty result with a quiet log.

UPCGExDebugSettings.name: Flush Debug
UPCGExDebugSettings.purpose: Clears debug drawing from the viewport. Persistent debug lines outlive the graph that drew them, so a viewport can end up holding output from runs that no longer exist. This removes it.
UPCGExDebugSettings.situation: A viewport cluttered with debug drawing from earlier runs or from nodes since disabled.

mechanism.text: Running the node removes the persistent debug drawing. It passes its input through unchanged, so it can be placed anywhere in a chain, and it is normally placed at the front of one: clearing before drawing is what keeps a viewport showing the current run rather than an accumulation of past ones.

bPCGExDebug.tooltip: Debug drawing toggle. Exposed to have more control on debug draw in sub-graph.

CustomColor.tooltip: Debug drawing toggle. Exposed to have more control on debug draw in sub-graph.

hints.text: Debug drawing survives a graph being disabled or deleted, which is why this node exists separately from the one that draws. It is the only way to remove drawing whose source is already gone.

UPCGExDecompBSPOccupancy.name: Decompose : BSP Occupancy
UPCGExDecompBSPOccupancy.purpose: Drops the Vtx into a voxel grid and cuts that block of voxels in two with flat planes, again and again, preferring to cut through empty space. What comes out follows the cluster's own gaps: dense clumps survive whole and the boundaries land in the thin parts. Every group is guaranteed voxel-contiguous, because a closing pass separates any group whose voxels had drifted into islands. Of the three rules built on a voxel grid, this is the one whose groups take any shape at all; the two Max Boxes rules give rectangles.
UPCGExDecompBSPOccupancy.situation: A cluster with visible voids in it, where the pieces should follow those voids instead of a uniform tiling.

mechanism.text: Vtx positions are quantised into a voxel grid and the whole grid is cut in two by a flat plane, over and over. Each candidate cut is judged on how empty the slice it passes through is against how evenly it divides the occupied voxels, the two weighed against each other by `Gap Weight`. Cutting stops at `Max Depth`, or when a region holds no more than `Min Voxels Per Cell` occupied voxels, or when no cut separates anything. A closing pass then walks each region face by face and splits off any voxels that do not touch the rest. Vtx sharing a voxel always share a group, and every Vtx is placed.

off_label.claim: `Min Voxels Per Cell` set above the cluster's total occupied voxel count stops all cutting at the root, which leaves the closing pass to do the whole job: the result is exactly the face-connected voxel islands of the cluster, a proximity grouping that owes nothing to the edges.
off_label.grounded_in: the root region terminating on the occupied-count test before any split, followed by the unconditional contiguity pass

TransformSpace.tooltip: How to orient the voxel grid.
TransformSpace.semantics: The frame is the grid's own, and it carries through to the cell size attribute the consumer can write: those sizes are measured along these axes, so under `Best Fit` or `Custom` they are not world-axis sizes. `Best Fit` derives the axes from the Vtx positions themselves, so it moves whenever the cluster does.

CustomTransform.tooltip: Custom transform for grid alignment. Only used when TransformSpace = Custom.

VoxelSizeMode.tooltip: How to determine the voxel grid resolution.
VoxelSizeMode.semantics: `Edge Inferred` averages the cluster's edge lengths and uses that as a cube, so the resolution follows how densely the cluster was built and shifts when the cluster does. It is the only place this rule reads the edges at all: everything after it works on Vtx positions alone, and two Vtx with no path between them share a group whenever they share a region.

VoxelSize.tooltip: Manual voxel size. Only used when VoxelSizeMode = Manual.

MaxDepth.semantics: The only limit on how far the cutting goes. There is no cap on the number of groups here the way `Decompose : Convex BSP` has one, so a fine grid with a low `Min Voxels Per Cell` can produce a great many.

MinVoxelsPerCell.tooltip: Stop splitting if a region has fewer occupied voxels than this.
MinVoxelsPerCell.semantics: It counts voxels, not Vtx, so several Vtx in one voxel count once and a dense cluster reaches this stop with far more Vtx per group than the number suggests. It is a stop on cutting rather than a floor on the result: the contiguity pass runs afterwards and can break a region that stopped here into smaller groups.

GapWeight.tooltip: Weight for the empty-gap bonus in split scoring. Higher values prefer splits through empty space.
GapWeight.semantics: The emptiness of the slice a cut passes through is multiplied by this and the lopsidedness of the division is subtracted from it, so the two compete inside one score rather than one gating the other. At 0 emptiness stops counting entirely and every cut lands wherever the halves come out most even, which is a plain median split that ignores the gaps.

UPCGExDecompConvexBSP.name: Decompose : Convex BSP
UPCGExDecompConvexBSP.purpose: Cuts the Vtx in half over and over until each piece is close enough to convex. Convexity here is counted, not measured: a piece stops splitting once few enough of its Vtx sit inside its own convex hull. Every cut is a plane through the piece's centroid, square to the direction its Vtx spread furthest. The edges are never read, so a group is a region of space and not a connected piece of the cluster.
UPCGExDecompConvexBSP.situation: Breaking a sprawling or bent cluster into pieces that each sit inside a tidy hull, for anything downstream that wants convex regions.

mechanism.text: The whole cluster starts as one piece. A piece splits into two along the plane through its centroid square to the direction its Vtx spread furthest, and each half is then examined the same way. A piece stops when enough of its Vtx lie on its own convex hull, when it holds no more than `Min Nodes Per Cell` Vtx, when the run already has `Max Cells` pieces open, or at `Max Depth`. Every Vtx is placed, and no group comes out holding fewer than `Min Nodes Per Cell`.

off_label.claim: `Max Cells` at two gives exactly one cut, through the centroid and square to the cluster's longest direction, which is the cheapest way to halve a cluster along its own principal axis without computing that axis yourself.
off_label.grounded_in: the open-region budget starting at one and being charged before descending, so the first split exhausts a budget of two

MaxConcavityRatio.tooltip: Maximum share of a region's Vtx allowed to sit off that region's own convex hull. 0 = all must be on it. This is an interior-point count, not a shape measure: a dense convex blob reads as highly concave.
MaxConcavityRatio.semantics: Because the count is what stops the recursion, this behaves as a fill-density stop as much as a shape one. A piece of four Vtx or fewer always reads zero and never splits on this test, whatever the value is set to.

MinNodesPerCell.semantics: A real floor on the result: a split happens only when both halves would clear it, and a piece at or below it stops, so no group comes out smaller. When the plane square to the longest direction leaves one side short, three planes square to that one are tried before the piece is left whole.

MaxCells.semantics: A hard cap, charged as the recursion goes rather than aimed for. The first half of every split is taken all the way down before the second half is looked at, so a cap tight enough to bite is spent on one side of the cluster and the other side comes back as a few large pieces.

MaxDepth.semantics: With `Max Cells` at its default of 32 this never bites, since 32 open pieces are reached long before a hundred levels of splitting are. It is there for the case where that cap is raised.

UPCGExDecompGridPartition.name: Decompose : Grid
UPCGExDecompGridPartition.purpose: The plainest of the seven. It lays a uniform grid of boxes over the cluster and gives every Vtx the group of the box it lands in. The edges are never read, so a group is a set of Vtx that happen to share a box, connected or not. Boxes that come out with too few Vtx are absorbed into another box rather than dropped, so nothing is ever left out.
UPCGExDecompGridPartition.situation: Cutting a cluster into even spatial tiles of a size you already know, where the tiling matters and the connectivity does not.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx is quantised to a box of `Cell Size`, counted from the corner of that cluster's own bounding box, and every Vtx sharing a box shares a group. The grid is square to the world and has no orientation control. Boxes holding fewer Vtx than `Min Nodes Per Cell` are then absorbed into another box, which is the only step that lets a group stop being a single box, and `Merge Mode` decides which box it goes to. Every Vtx is placed.

off_label.claim: A `Cell Size` larger than the cluster puts every Vtx in one box, which makes this the cheapest way to stamp one constant group id per cluster onto the Vtx, with the consumer's per-cluster offset doing the rest of the work.
off_label.grounded_in: the single-cell quantisation path plus the consumer's per-Edges-dataset id offset

off_label.claim: Under `Adjacent`, a box with no occupied neighbour is left as its own group, so after a merge pass the groups still under the threshold are exactly the spatially isolated ones and the consumer's cell count attribute picks them out.
off_label.grounded_in: the Adjacent branch leaving a cell with no occupied 26-neighbour unmerged

CellSize.semantics: World units, per axis, square to the world axes, with the first box starting at the minimum corner of the cluster's own bounding box. There is no way to turn this grid: a cluster that runs diagonally gets tiled diagonally, and the rules that build a voxel grid are the ones that can be oriented to fit.

MinNodesPerCell.tooltip: Minimum nodes per cell. Cells below this count are merged into a neighbour (see Merge Mode).
MinNodesPerCell.semantics: The floor is enforced by merging, so no Vtx is ever dropped to reach it. A merged group stops being one box, and the cell size attribute then reports the box enclosing everything it swallowed, which can be far larger than `Cell Size`.
MinNodesPerCell.trap: `Adjacent` leaves a box with no occupied neighbour alone, so the floor is not guaranteed in that mode. `Nearest` has no such escape and will merge across any distance.

MergeMode.tooltip: How under-populated cells choose the neighbour they merge into.
MergeMode.semantics: Both modes repeat until nothing more can move, so merges chain: a box still short after absorbing a neighbour goes back in the queue and merges onward. Under `Nearest` that has no floor, and a `Min Nodes Per Cell` no box can reach collapses the whole cluster into a single group. Under `Adjacent` the chain stops wherever the occupied grid does.

hints.text: The grid is anchored to each cluster's own bounding box, not to the world origin. Two clusters in one execution are each tiled from their own corner, so their boxes do not line up and a Vtx near a shared border can be grouped differently on either side.

UPCGExDecompMaxBoxes.name: Decompose : Max Boxes
UPCGExDecompMaxBoxes.purpose: Carves the cluster into solid rectangles. It drops the Vtx into a voxel grid, takes the biggest completely filled box it can find, claims it as a group, and repeats until every occupied voxel belongs to one. That is what separates it from **Decompose : BSP Occupancy**, whose groups are contiguous but any shape: here every group is a box with no holes in it. **Decompose : Max Boxes (Extended)** is this same carving with a per-Vtx weight, a per-axis shape bias, a preferred volume band and heuristic-gated merging added on top.
UPCGExDecompMaxBoxes.situation: Covering a cluster with rectangular regions, for anything downstream that wants boxes rather than arbitrary clumps.

mechanism.text: Vtx positions are quantised into a voxel grid, and the best-scoring box of unclaimed occupied voxels is claimed as a group, over and over, until nothing occupied is left unclaimed. Which box scores best is its volume shaped by `Balance`, and a claimed box larger than `Max Cell Size` is cut into even chunks that each become their own group. A closing pass then puts back together any two touching groups whose union is again a solid box inside that same size limit. Vtx sharing a voxel always share a group.

off_label.claim: Setting `Max Cell Size` to the voxel size on every axis makes every occupied voxel its own group, and the closing merge cannot undo it because any merged pair would exceed the limit. The cell id then reads as a quantised position, one value per voxel of space.
off_label.grounded_in: the world-to-voxel extent flooring to one voxel per axis, and the merge test rejecting any union larger than that extent

TransformSpace.tooltip: How to orient the voxel grid.
TransformSpace.semantics: The frame is the grid's own, and it carries through to the cell size attribute the consumer can write: those sizes are measured along these axes, so under `Best Fit` or `Custom` they are not world-axis sizes. `Best Fit` derives the axes from the Vtx positions themselves, so it moves whenever the cluster does.

CustomTransform.tooltip: Custom transform for grid alignment. Only used when TransformSpace = Custom.

VoxelSizeMode.tooltip: How to determine the voxel grid resolution.
VoxelSizeMode.semantics: `Edge Inferred` averages the cluster's edge lengths and uses that as a cube, so the resolution follows how densely the cluster was built and shifts when the cluster does. It is the only place this rule reads the edges at all: everything after it works on Vtx positions alone, and two Vtx with no path between them share a group whenever they share a box.

VoxelSize.tooltip: Manual voxel size. Only used when VoxelSizeMode = Manual.

MaxCellSize.tooltip: Maximum dimensions for output cells in world units. Extracted boxes larger than this are subdivided. A zero axis means no size limit on that axis.
MaxCellSize.semantics: A positive value is converted to a whole number of voxels by dividing by the voxel size and rounding down, floored at one, so anything under one voxel gives groups one voxel thick on that axis and a value between two multiples lands on the lower one. The same limit gates the closing merge, so it caps how large a group can end up however it got there.

MinVoxelsPerCell.tooltip: Minimum occupied voxels per cell. Cells below this threshold are discarded (CellID = -1).
MinVoxelsPerCell.semantics: Counted in voxels, so several Vtx in one voxel count once. This rule and its Extended sibling are the only two of the seven that drop Vtx: a group below the threshold is discarded outright and its members come out unplaced, which the consumer writes as the unplaced id with a cell count of zero, and nothing is logged. The discard runs after the closing merge, so a group too small on its own can still survive by having been merged into a neighbour first.

Balance.tooltip: Penalizes elongated strips in favor of a square footprint. Compactness is measured on the two LARGEST dimensions only, so a slab scores the same as a cube. 0 = pure volume (largest box first, may produce thin strips).
Balance.semantics: Compactness is the second-longest side of a candidate box over its longest, raised to twice this value and multiplied into the volume, so the score falls away sharply as a footprint stops being square and a box long in one direction alone is the only shape penalised.

UPCGExDecompMaxBoxesExt.name: Decompose : Max Boxes (Extended)
UPCGExDecompMaxBoxesExt.purpose: **Decompose : Max Boxes** with four extra ways to steer the carving. A per-axis bias on what counts as a compact box, a per-Vtx weight that pulls the big boxes toward the Vtx you care about, a soft preferred volume band, and a merge gate that reads the heuristics so groups do not join across edges the stack charges heavily for. Take the plain rule when box shape and size are all that matters; take this one when something written on the Vtx, or the cluster's own connections, should decide where the boxes fall.
UPCGExDecompMaxBoxesExt.situation: Box carving that has to respect something beyond geometry: a weight painted onto the Vtx, a shape budget that differs per axis, or a structural boundary the edges describe.

mechanism.text: The carving is the one **Decompose : Max Boxes** performs: quantise the Vtx into a voxel grid, claim the best-scoring solid box of unclaimed occupied voxels, repeat, cut anything over `Max Cell Size` into chunks, then rejoin any two touching groups whose union is again a solid box. What changes is the score each candidate box is judged by, which now also folds in the average axis bias and weight across the box and how far its volume sits from the preferred band, and the closing merge, which can be gated on what the heuristics charge for the edges running between two groups.

off_label.claim: Merge gating reads the edges to decide where groups may not join, so with a weight attribute left constant and the volume band off, this becomes plain box carving that stops at structural boundaries: the boxes still come out rectangular, but no box straddles an expensive edge.
off_label.grounded_in: the gate rejecting a merge on the average score of the edges crossing the boundary, with the extraction itself untouched

TransformSpace.tooltip: How to orient the voxel grid.

CustomTransform.tooltip: Custom transform for grid alignment. Only used when TransformSpace = Custom.

VoxelSizeMode.tooltip: How to determine the voxel grid resolution.
VoxelSizeMode.semantics: `Edge Inferred` averages the cluster's edge lengths and uses that as a cube. Along with merge gating it is one of only two places this rule looks at the edges at all: the carving itself works on Vtx positions alone.

VoxelSize.tooltip: Manual voxel size. Only used when VoxelSizeMode = Manual.

MaxCellSize.tooltip: Maximum dimensions for output cells in world units. Extracted boxes larger than this are subdivided. A zero axis means no size limit on that axis.
MaxCellSize.semantics: A positive value is converted to a whole number of voxels by dividing by the voxel size and rounding down, floored at one. The same limit gates the closing merge, so it caps how large a group can end up however it got there, and it is a hard limit where `Preferred Max Volume` is only a preference.

MinVoxelsPerCell.tooltip: Minimum occupied voxels per cell. Cells below this threshold are discarded (CellID = -1).
MinVoxelsPerCell.semantics: Counted in voxels, so several Vtx in one voxel count once. Groups below the threshold are discarded and their Vtx come out unplaced, which the consumer writes as the unplaced id with a cell count of zero, and nothing is logged. The discard runs after the closing merge, so a group too small on its own can survive by having been merged first.

Balance.tooltip: Penalizes elongated strips in favor of a square footprint. Compactness is measured on the two LARGEST dimensions only, so a slab scores the same as a cube. 0 = pure volume (largest box first, may produce thin strips).

AxisBias.tooltip: Per-axis compactness penalty. Set low on axes where elongation is acceptable. e.g., (0.1, 0.1, 1) for flat boxes, (1, 1, 0.1) for tall columns. Works in grid-local space (post-transform). Can be per-node via attribute.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

AxisBias.semantics: The bias multiplies a candidate box's sides before compactness is measured, so it reaches the score only through `Balance`: with `Balance` at 0 the exponent is zero and both the bias and compactness stop counting entirely. Read from an attribute, the value applied to a box is the average across its voxels, and a voxel holding several Vtx carries just one of their values.

Weight.tooltip: Per-node weight for box extraction scoring. Higher weight = preferred extraction region.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Weight.semantics: It has to be read from an attribute to do anything. Left on `Constant` the weight is uniform, and a uniform weight cannot change which box scores highest, so the whole weight group is skipped including the two-pass behaviour of `Priority`. Read from an attribute, the value applied to a box is the average across its voxels, and a voxel holding several Vtx carries just one of their values.

WeightInfluence.tooltip: How strongly weights influence box extraction scoring. 0 = ignore weights, 1 = linear influence.
WeightInfluence.semantics: The box's average weight is raised to this before multiplying into the score, so above one the gap between a heavy region and a light one is exaggerated and below one it is flattened. At 0 the weight is dropped before carving starts, which takes `Priority` with it and leaves the extraction identical to the plain rule.

WeightMode.tooltip: How weights affect the extraction algorithm.
WeightMode.semantics: `Priority` does not leave the light regions out. Its first pass stops as soon as the best remaining box falls under `Priority Threshold`, and a second pass then carves everything left over the ordinary way. What it buys is the order: heavy regions get first claim on the big boxes and light regions take what remains.
