inputs.note: The condition evaluated at each endpoint, and the first set when `Two Filter Sets` is on. Vtx filters and point filters are taken here, along with a **Filter Group** carrying either; an **Edge Filter :** node is not.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters (B)
inputs.note: The second condition, matched against the other endpoint.
inputs.condition: when Two Filter Sets is on

outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the edge-family passport, so an **Edge Filters** pin takes it and no other pin does.

fields.name: bUseTwoFilterSets
fields.tooltip: Use two filter sets (one per endpoint) instead of one set on both -- lets each endpoint match a different condition.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: How the single set's two endpoint results are combined. Single-set mode only.

fields.name: bRespectEdgeDirection
fields.tooltip: Bind set A to the Start endpoint and set B to End. If disabled, the sets match either endpoint in any orientation.

fields.name: Expects
fields.tooltip: Expected result for the (first) filter set. Combined per 'Mode' in single-set mode.

fields.name: ExpectsB
fields.tooltip: Expected result for the second filter set ('Vtx Filters (B)'). Two-set mode only.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the filter result (pass becomes fail and vice versa).

hints.text: An **Edge Filter :** node dropped on **Vtx Filters** connects, then is skipped with a warning when the node runs. If it was the only thing on that pin the set comes up empty, this node emits no factory at all, and what the graph reports is a missing filter at the consumer rather than anything about endpoints.

The wired filters bind per cluster, and each one's own `Initialization Failure Policy` runs first: a child set to Pass that cannot bind becomes an always-true child and the set survives. Only when a whole set ends up empty does this node fail to initialize, and its own `Initialization Failure Policy` then decides what the consumer does with it.

UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareNumFilterProvi.name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Compare (Numeric)
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareNumFilterProvi.purpose: Judges an edge by the numbers sitting on the two Vtx it connects. One selector is read twice, at the edge's Start endpoint and at its End endpoint, and the single operator between those two values is the whole condition. Both reads land on the Vtx dataset, so this is the edge filter for a question about the ends of an edge and not about the edge itself. It is the cluster-side counterpart of **Filter : Self Compare (Numeric)**, with the edge choosing the two rows instead of an offset choosing them.
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareNumFilterProvi.situation: A value written per Vtx, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose two ends disagree about it in one particular direction.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. One selector supplies both sides of the comparison, resolved on the Vtx dataset and read at the edge's two endpoint rows: the Start endpoint is the left-hand value, the End endpoint the right. The operator is applied once, so an edge gets a single verdict and nothing here folds two per-endpoint answers together. Any attribute or point property that converts to a number is read through the selector, and one that does not resolve on the Vtx dataset is an initialization failure, never a fallback onto the edge.

off_label.claim: Point the selector at a point property and the node answers a geometric question with no attribute written anywhere. `$Position.Z` under the greater-than operator keeps every edge whose Start Vtx sits above its End Vtx, which is a slope test built out of a comparison filter.
off_label.grounded_in: FFilter::Init broadcasting Config.Attribute over the Vtx facade, which resolves point properties as readily as authored attributes

UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareStrFilterProvi.name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Compare (String)
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareStrFilterProvi.purpose: Judges an edge by the text on the two Vtx it connects. One selector is read twice, at the edge's Start endpoint and at its End endpoint, and the single operator between those two values is the whole condition. Both reads land on the Vtx dataset, so this is the edge filter for a question about the ends of an edge and not about the edge itself. The operator list reaches past equality into length comparison, ordering, substring tests and wildcard matching, which covers most of the shapes that look like they need **Edge Filter : Endpoints Regex**.
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsCompareStrFilterProvi.situation: Names or tags written per Vtx, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose two ends match, differ, or nest one inside the other.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. One selector supplies both sides of the comparison, resolved on the Vtx dataset and read as text at the edge's two endpoint rows: the Start endpoint is the left-hand value, the End endpoint the right. The operator is applied once, so an edge gets a single verdict and nothing here folds two per-endpoint answers together. Every operator ignores case, so Oak and oak are one value to all of them. Any attribute type carrying a conversion to text is read through the selector, and one that does not resolve on the Vtx dataset is an initialization failure, never a fallback onto the edge.

UPCGExEdgeEndpointsRegexFilterProviderSe.name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Regex
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsRegexFilterProviderSe.purpose: Tests the text on each of an edge's two Vtx against one pattern, then folds the two answers into a single verdict for the edge. That fold is what the Endpoints Compare filters do not have: they put the two endpoint values on either side of one operator, while this one puts each endpoint against the same pattern and combines the results, with `Require Both Endpoints` choosing between both and either. Both reads land on the Vtx dataset, so this is the edge filter for a question about the ends of an edge and not about the edge itself. Reach for it where the acceptable shape of a name or tag needs character classes, alternation, quantifiers or anchors.
UPCGExEdgeEndpointsRegexFilterProviderSe.situation: Names or tags written per Vtx with a family structure in them, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose ends belong to that family.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. One selector is resolved on the Vtx dataset and read as text at the edge's two endpoint rows, then the pattern is searched for inside each of the two values. A hit anywhere in a value counts, so a pattern needs `^` and `$` to mean the whole value, and the shipped default of `.*` matches every value including an empty one. `Require Both Endpoints` folds the two answers into the edge's verdict, and `Invert` flips that afterwards. Matching is case-sensitive here, where every operator on the Endpoints Compare filters folds case away; an inline `(?i)` at the front of the pattern folds it back in.

outputs.label: Edge Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the edge-family passport, so an **Edge Filters** pin takes it and no other pin does.

The node subtitle prints the attribute, a match operator and the pattern between slashes, with the inverted flag appended when `Invert` is on. It does not show which way `Require Both Endpoints` is set.

UPCGExEdgeKeepHighestScore.name: Score-based refinements

variants.name: Score-based refinements
variants.summary: Keeps the edge a route would have avoided.

variants.name: Keep Lowest Score
variants.summary: Keeps the cheapest edge at each Vtx.

variants.name: Remove Highest Score
variants.summary: Removes the most expensive edge at each Vtx, leaving the rest.

variants.name: Remove Lowest Score
variants.summary: Removes the cheapest edge at each Vtx, leaving the rest.

UPCGExEdgeKeepHighestScore.purpose:
Four rules that rank the edges at each Vtx by heuristic score and act on the single best or worst one. They are one operation with two switches: whether high score or low score wins, and whether winning means being kept or being removed.

Score comes from the **Heuristics** pin, and a heuristic charges a cost that searches minimise. The highest-scoring edge is therefore the one a route through that Vtx would have avoided, and the lowest-scoring one is the road it would have taken. **Invert** on a heuristic swaps which is which, so any of the four can be made to behave like its opposite without changing the rule.
UPCGExEdgeKeepHighestScore.situation: Reach for these when the cluster carries a cost you already trust and you want one edge per Vtx chosen by it, rather than a global structure like a spanning tree.

mechanism.text:
Each rule runs once per Vtx, over that Vtx's own edges, and picks exactly one of them. What differs between the four is which edge it picks and what picking means. The **Keep** rules start from a cluster with every edge already removed and mark their winner as surviving; the **Remove** rules start from the cluster as it arrived and mark their pick as gone. That is the entire difference in code: `GetDefaultEdgeValidity()` returns false for Keep and true for Remove, and the closing write flips the same flag the other way.

Score is read through `Heuristics->GetEdgeScore` against the roaming seed and goal, so every heuristic wired to the node contributes, weighted as configured.

hints.text: Every edge is judged twice, once from each of its two endpoints, and the two verdicts are never combined. Under a **Keep** rule an edge survives if either endpoint chose it, so a Vtx routinely keeps more than one: the edge it picked, plus every edge its neighbours picked that happens to land on it. Under a **Remove** rule the reverse holds and an edge dies if either endpoint picked it. Neither leaves each Vtx holding exactly one edge, which is what most readers expect on first contact.

A Vtx whose edges all score identically resolves to the first edge in its edge order. These four rules take no edge filters: `SupportFilters()` is left at false, so the **Edge Filters** pin is not offered and no filter can protect an edge from being picked.

UPCGExEdgeKeepShortest.name: Length-based refinements

variants.name: Length-based refinements
variants.summary: Keeps the shortest edge at each Vtx.

variants.name: Keep Longest
variants.summary: Keeps the longest edge at each Vtx.

variants.name: Remove Shortest
variants.summary: Removes the shortest edge at each Vtx, leaving the rest.

variants.name: Remove Longest
variants.summary: Removes the longest edge at each Vtx, leaving the rest.

UPCGExEdgeKeepShortest.purpose:
Four rules that rank the edges at each Vtx by length and act on the single shortest or longest one. They are one operation with two switches: whether short or long wins, and whether winning means being kept or being removed.

Nothing needs wiring and nothing needs configuring. Length is straight-line distance between the two Vtx an edge joins, so what these rules see is pure geometry: no attribute, no heuristic, no filter.
UPCGExEdgeKeepShortest.situation: **Keep Shortest** is the one to reach for first. What comes out is a nearest-neighbour structure: every Vtx joined to whichever Vtx is closest to it, plus whatever its neighbours reached for.

mechanism.text:
Each rule runs once per Vtx, over that Vtx's own edges, and picks exactly one of them. What differs between the four is which edge it picks and what picking means. The **Keep** rules start from a cluster with every edge already removed and mark their winner as surviving; the **Remove** rules start from the cluster as it arrived and mark their pick as gone. That is the entire difference in code: `GetDefaultEdgeValidity()` returns false for Keep and true for Remove, and the closing write flips the same flag the other way.

Distance is compared squared (`GetDistSquared`), which changes no ordering and costs no square root.

hints.text: Every edge is judged twice, once from each of its two endpoints, and the two verdicts are never combined. Under a **Keep** rule an edge survives if either endpoint chose it, so a Vtx routinely keeps more than one: the edge it picked, plus every edge its neighbours picked that happens to land on it. Under a **Remove** rule the reverse holds and an edge dies if either endpoint picked it. Neither leaves each Vtx holding exactly one edge, which is what most readers expect on first contact.

The two **Longest** rules start their search at zero and take a strictly greater value, so a zero-length edge can never win: a Vtx whose neighbours all sit exactly on top of it has no edge picked and is left as the baseline found it. A Vtx whose edges are all the same length resolves to the first edge in its edge order. These four rules take no edge filters, so no filter can protect an edge from being picked.

UPCGExEdgeLengthFilterProviderSettings.name: Edge Filter : Length
UPCGExEdgeLengthFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Judges an edge by how long it is. The length is measured from the two Vtx the edge connects, met against `Threshold` through one operator, and the verdict leaves on the **Edge Filter** pin for an **Edge Filters** pin to consume. Because the measurement comes from the cluster and not from an attribute, it follows anything upstream that moved those Vtx.
UPCGExEdgeLengthFilterProviderSettings.situation: A cluster built by a proximity or triangulation node, where the long connections it produced are the ones to drop.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. The length is the straight-line distance in world units between the two endpoint Vtx positions held by the cluster, so nothing has to be written onto the edges first and nothing goes stale when the Vtx move. That length is the left side of `Comparison` and `Threshold` is the right. Set `Threshold` to Attribute and the value is read from the Edges dataset, at the row belonging to the edge under test, which is the only place a per-edge threshold can come from.

outputs.label: Edge Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the edge-family passport, so an **Edge Filters** pin takes it and no other pin does.

That reads a value captured when the writing node ran; this one measures the positions as they stand, and the two part company as soon as something moves a Vtx in between.

UPCGExEdgeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.name: Edge Filter : Num Vtx
UPCGExEdgeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.purpose: Judges an edge by how connected its two ends are. Each endpoint contributes the number of edges attached to it, `Mode` says whether the two counts are summed or judged one at a time, and the result meets `Threshold` through one operator. The verdict leaves on the **Edge Filter** pin for an **Edge Filters** pin to consume, which is what separates leaf edges, the runs between junctions, and the edges inside a dense knot.
UPCGExEdgeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.situation: A cluster where the edges hanging off dead ends should be treated differently from the ones between busy junctions.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. Each endpoint's count is the number of edges attached to that Vtx inside this cluster, and the edge under test is one of them, so no count is ever below 1 and no sum is ever below 2. `Mode` decides what has to meet the threshold: their sum as a single number, or each count on its own, with the edge passing when either endpoint qualifies or only when both do. Set `Threshold` to Attribute and the value is read from the Edges dataset, at the row belonging to the edge under test, which is the only place a per-edge threshold can come from.

off_label.claim: Because the tested edge counts at both of its own ends, `Sum` with `Strictly Equal` against 2 selects the edges that are a component all by themselves: two Vtx, one edge, nothing else attached at either end.
off_label.grounded_in: FNode::Num returning the node's link count with the tested edge among the links, summed by EPCGExRefineEdgeThresholdMode::Sum

UPCGExEdgeOrderSettings.name: Cluster : Edge Order
UPCGExEdgeOrderSettings.purpose: Decides, once and for the whole cluster, which endpoint of every edge is its start. An edge joins two Vtx and stores them in some order, and that order is arbitrary until something fixes it; anything downstream that reads an edge as directed, a written direction vector, a path traced along edges, a one-way heuristic, reads whatever order happened to be there. This node rewrites the pair so it says what you want it to say, either from a per-edge rule or from a traversal that orients everything away from seed points.
UPCGExEdgeOrderSettings.situation: A cluster is about to feed something that treats an edge as going somewhere, and the edges came from a generator that had no opinion about which way.

mechanism.text: Every edge point has its two endpoint ids rewritten in the chosen order, and nothing else changes: no attribute is added, no point moves, no edge is removed, and the Vtx pass through untouched. The pairing survives because the ids are the same two ids, so a cluster that went in intact comes out intact with its edges pointing the way the rule says. Mode is the whole choice: a rule applied to each edge on its own, or one traversal that orients the cluster as a whole.

off_label.claim: In DFS from Seeds the traversal reaches only the component its seeds landed in, and edges elsewhere keep the order they arrived with, so seeding one component of a multi-component Edges input reorders that component alone.
off_label.grounded_in: RunDFS leaves Depths at minus one outside the reached set and ProcessEdges swaps nothing when either endpoint is unreached

inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster. Read for endpoint ids and for sorting values, never written.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half, and the only thing this node writes to.

inputs.label: Seeds
inputs.note: Where the traversal starts. One dataset, and the orientation runs away from the Vtx these claim.
inputs.condition: appears and is required when Mode is DFS from Seeds

inputs.label: Direction Sorting
inputs.note: Sorting rules deciding which endpoint of an edge ranks first.

outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged.

Mode.tooltip: How edge endpoint order is determined.
Mode.semantics: Direction Settings judges each edge on its own, from what its two endpoints carry, so the answer for one edge owes nothing to the answer for its neighbour and a cluster can come out with edges pointing every which way where the values are noisy. DFS from Seeds answers for the cluster instead: one traversal fixes an order over the whole reached component and every edge follows it, which is the mode for turning a cluster into something that flows.

DirectionSettings.tooltip: Defines the direction in which points will be ordered to form the final paths.
DirectionSettings.semantics: Direction Method picks what is compared and Direction Choice picks which end of that comparison becomes the start. Endpoints Order keeps whatever the edge already stores, so leaving the block alone is a no-op rather than a default ordering. Endpoints Indices ranks by point index, Endpoints Sort hands the ranking to sorting rules on their own pin, and Edge Dot Attribute takes the endpoint whose direction agrees most with a vector read from the edge point.

SeedPicking.tooltip: How seed points select their starting node in the cluster.
SeedPicking.semantics: Each seed claims one Vtx and that Vtx becomes a root of the traversal, so seeds set where the flow originates rather than which edges are touched. Max Distance is a hard cut at 200 by default, and a cluster left with no seed within range is dropped from the output with a warning rather than passed through unordered.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the traversal direction (edges point toward seeds instead of away from them).
bInvert.semantics: Flips the traversal result so edges point back toward the seeds. It reaches only the edges the traversal actually oriented; an edge it left alone is left alone either way.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether to use an octree for closest node search. Depending on your dataset, this may be faster or slower.

hints.text: A traversal cannot orient every edge. An edge whose two Vtx were both reached at the same step of the traversal has no direction to take from it, and neither has an edge outside the reached set, so both keep the order they arrived with. On a dense cluster that leaves a visible minority of edges pointing whichever way the generator left them.

UPCGExEdgeRefineByFilter.name: Refine : Filter
UPCGExEdgeRefineByFilter.purpose: Hands the keep-or-cut decision to a filter stack. It is one of the two rules that read the consumer's **Edge Filters** pin, so any condition you can state about an edge (a length comparison, an attribute test, a direction, a neighbour count) becomes a refinement rule. With **Invert** off the edges that pass are the edges that survive.
UPCGExEdgeRefineByFilter.situation: A cluster has to be thinned by a condition you author about the edges themselves rather than by geometry, length or score.

mechanism.text: Judged one edge at a time, and every edge is judged. Each edge is tested against the whole **Edge Filters** stack, and passing is what keeps it: an edge that fails is removed, whether or not any filter had anything to say about it. **Invert** trades the two outcomes. Nothing about an edge's neighbours enters the test, so the result carries no dependence on edge order.

bInvert.tooltip: If enabled, filtered out edges are kept, while edges that pass the filter are removed.
bInvert.semantics: Both sides of the verdict move together. Left off, the cluster comes back holding the edges that passed and nothing else; turned on, it comes back holding the edges that failed and nothing else. An edge the filters were indifferent about still lands on one side or the other.

hints.text: An empty **Edge Filters** pin reads as every edge passing. With **Invert** off that leaves the cluster untouched, and with **Invert** on it removes every edge in it. A pin emptied at boot behaves the same way, so an invalid-input warning on that pin is worth chasing before the result is.

UPCGExEdgeRefineChainFilter.name: Refine : Chain Filter
UPCGExEdgeRefineChainFilter.purpose: Judges whole runs of edges instead of single edges. A chain is one run with a leaf or a junction at each end, or a closed loop that has neither, and the whole run takes one verdict. Chains are measured on size, length and how much they bend, and this is the second of the two rules that read the consumer's **Edge Filters** pin, where a filter can overrule that measurement for the chains it hits.
UPCGExEdgeRefineChainFilter.situation: A cluster has grown stubs and detours that only read as wrong at the scale of a whole run, so cutting edge by edge would leave the fragments behind.

mechanism.text: The cluster is walked into chains once, over its own topology, and each chain is measured and judged on its own. Every edge starts kept, and every edge a chain covers is then written to that chain's verdict, so nothing is left half-cut in the middle of a run. Chains own disjoint edges, so the order they are judged in changes nothing, and anything no chain reaches keeps its starting value.
steps: Chains are built from the cluster topology, seeded at every leaf and every junction.
Each chain is measured against the criteria enabled under Gating, combined by the chosen Logic.
Invert flips that verdict, and only that verdict.
A wired Edge Filters stack overrules the verdict for any chain that triggers the override.
Every edge of the chain is written to the surviving verdict.

off_label.claim: The curvature criteria measure a run without cutting anything: enable one bound, set the consumer's `Mode` to Attribute, and every edge comes back carrying whether its run was straight, bent or squiggly, which is a cheap way to sort a cluster's runs before deciding what to do with them.
off_label.grounded_in: ComputeChainMetrics computes SharpestCorner, TotalCurvature and EndpointDeviation per chain, and the verdict is written to every edge of the chain; Attribute mode writes it out and resets validity.

Gating.tooltip: Chain selection criteria. Leave all criteria disabled to make the node inert.

fields.name: MaxEndpointDeviation
fields.tooltip: Inclusive upper bound for the net heading change. A symmetric wiggle stays low here; a consistent curve does not. Closed loops report 0 (no endpoints).

Gating.semantics: Each criterion is an independent bound with its own toggle, and only the enabled ones take part. `Logic` set to All requires every enabled bound; set to Any, one is enough. Vtx count, edge count and length are measured on every chain; the three angle criteria cost extra per edge and are computed only when one of their bounds is enabled.
Gating.trap: With no criterion enabled the gating verdict is a fixed keep, and **Invert** has nothing to flip. A wired **Edge Filters** stack still acts in that state, which makes `Force Remove` the only setting that can cut anything from a rule left in its default configuration.

bInvert.tooltip: If disabled, chains that match the criteria are removed. If enabled, matching chains are kept and every other chain is removed.
bInvert.semantics: It reaches the gating verdict alone. Edges no chain covers keep their starting value either way, and the filter override is applied after the flip rather than being flipped with it. This makes it the one **Invert** among the refinements that leaves the starting value alone, so an inverted result and an uninverted one can both hold the same untouched edges.

FilterOverride.tooltip: Behavior for chains hit by the optional edge filters. Overrides the gating verdict. Only applies when the edge filter pin is connected.
FilterOverride.semantics: The override replaces the gating verdict for a chain, so a chain the criteria condemned comes back whole under `Force Keep`, and one they spared goes whole under `Force Remove`. Since the gating verdict is a keep whenever no criterion is enabled, `Force Keep` has nothing to do in that state and `Force Remove` becomes the whole rule: the chains your filters touch are the chains that go.

bRequireAllEdgesPass.tooltip: If enabled, every edge of a chain must pass the filters to trigger the override; otherwise a single passing edge is enough. Only applies when the edge filter pin is connected.

hints.text: A closed loop is a chain like any other. Its closing edge counts in the filter accumulation and takes the verdict with the rest, and it reports zero endpoint deviation, since it has no ends for a heading to change between. Its corners still register under `Min / Max Corner Angle` and `Min / Max Total Curvature`, the wrap corner at the seed included.

UPCGExEdgeRefineGabriel.name: Refine : Gabriel
UPCGExEdgeRefineGabriel.purpose: Keeps an edge only when nothing else stands between its two Vtx. The test is the Gabriel criterion: draw the sphere that has the edge as its diameter, and if any other Vtx of the cluster sits inside it, the edge goes. What survives is a clean proximity structure with the long reaching connections gone and the short local ones intact.
UPCGExEdgeRefineGabriel.situation: A Delaunay or probe-built cluster connects points that have something closer sitting between them, and only the direct neighbours should stay joined.

mechanism.text: Judged one edge at a time. The sphere is centred on the edge's midpoint with the edge length as its diameter, and one Vtx strictly inside it is enough to remove the edge; a Vtx sitting on the surface leaves it alone, which is what keeps the edge's own two Vtx out of its own test. The test reads Vtx positions and nothing else, so the outcome depends on where the points are and never on which edges the cluster happens to carry. That also bounds what you can get out of it: the rule can only take away, so the result is whatever part of the point cloud's Gabriel structure your cluster already contained.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the refinement result (keep edges that would be removed and vice versa).

UPCGExEdgeRefineInstancedFactory.name: Refine Operation
UPCGExEdgeRefineInstancedFactory.purpose: The base every refinement inherits, and the page carrying what all eighteen of them have in common. A refinement is picked from the **Refinement** dropdown inside **Cluster : Refine**: it is not a palette node, it has no pins and no settings of its own here, and its whole job is to answer one question about a cluster it is handed. What it declares alongside that answer is a small fixed set of facts, and those facts are what reshape the consumer around it: where every edge starts, how often the rule is asked, whether the Heuristics pin becomes required, and whether the Edge Filters pin is read at all.
UPCGExEdgeRefineInstancedFactory.situation: Reading any refinement page and needing to know what its rule is handed, what it is allowed to change, and why the node around it looks different from one rule to the next.

mechanism.text: **Cluster : Refine** builds one cluster, sets every edge in it to the starting value the refinement declares, and then asks that refinement for its verdict once, in one of three shapes: once per edge, once per Vtx, or once over the whole cluster. The refinement answers by flipping edges, and whether an edge is kept is the only thing it can change; positions, attributes, counts and ordering are all beyond it. Whichever shape it uses it holds the whole cluster while it works, so a rule handed a single edge can still look at everything around that edge to judge it. Nothing is removed while it runs. The marking is a verdict, and turning a verdict into an output belongs to the consumer.

off_label.claim: Any refinement can be run as a measurement rather than a cut: pick it, set the consumer's `Mode` to Attribute, and the cluster comes back with its structure intact and the rule's verdict on every edge, ready for a filter or a debug pass to read.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExRefineEdgesOutput::Attribute duplicates both facades, and FProcessor::InsertEdges writes each edge's validity out and then resets every edge and Vtx to valid.

hints.text: A refinement has no pins, and it emits no factory for a pin to carry. Where probes, filters and selectors are palette nodes wired into a consumer, a refinement is an instanced object chosen from a dropdown, so it has no wire, no priority and no way to reach a second node. The only wire that touches one is the advanced **Overrides : Refinement** pin on **Cluster : Refine**, which sets the picked rule's properties from an attribute set by matching attribute names against property names.

Every rule declares where edges start, and the two starting points read very differently when a result comes back empty. A subtractive rule starts with every edge kept and takes some away, so an empty result means it matched everything. An additive rule starts with every edge removed and puts some back, so an empty result means it matched nothing. With **Invert** left off, six are additive: **Refine : Filter**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, and the four Keep rules. The other twelve are subtractive.

Seven rules carry an **Invert** toggle, and it means the same thing on each of them: the edges the rule would have kept are the ones it removes instead. On six of the seven it swaps the starting value too, so an inverted rule is the complement of the same rule left alone rather than a variation on it. **Refine : Chain Filter** is the one that does not: it flips its own chain verdict while every edge no chain covers stays kept either way. The seven are **Refine : Filter**, **Refine : Chain Filter**, **Refine : Gabriel**, **Refine : Line Trace**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, **Refine : β Skeleton** and **Refine : DFS (Tarjan)**.

How often a rule is asked is fixed by the rule and cannot be changed on the node. Once per edge: **Refine : Filter**, **Refine : Gabriel**, **Refine : Line Trace**, **Refine : Overlap**, **Refine : β Skeleton**. Once per Vtx, where the rule is handed one Vtx and every edge at it: the four length rules, the four score rules, and **Remove Leaves**. Once for the whole cluster: **Refine : Chain Filter**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, **Refine : DFS (Tarjan)** and **Remove Leaves (Recursive)**. The per-edge group is also the only one where **Restore Edges That Connect To Valid Nodes** on the consumer does anything.

Two of the facts a rule declares change the consumer's pins. A rule that scores edges makes **Heuristics** a required pin and cancels the node when it is empty: **Refine : MST (Prim)** and the four Score rules. A rule that reads filters lifts **Edge Filters** out of the advanced group and is the only reason the node reads that pin: **Refine : Filter** and **Refine : Chain Filter**. Under every other rule both pins are marked unused, and anything wired into them is ignored without a warning.

The dropdown lists rules under two naming shapes. Most carry the **Refine :** prefix; the eight length and score rules and the two leaf rules are named for what they do instead, as **Keep Longest**, **Remove Lowest Score**, **Remove Leaves (Recursive)** and so on. Nothing else separates the two groups.

UPCGExEdgeRefineLineTrace.name: Refine : Line Trace
UPCGExEdgeRefineLineTrace.purpose: The one rule that looks at the level. It traces a line from one of an edge's Vtx to the other and removes the edge when that line hits collision, so a cluster stops connecting through walls, terrain and props. Everything it can see is decided by the collision block: channel or object type or profile, complex geometry or simple, and which actors to ignore.
UPCGExEdgeRefineLineTrace.situation: A cluster generated over a floor plan connects rooms straight through the walls between them.

mechanism.text: Judged one edge at a time, with one trace per edge from Vtx to Vtx. A hit removes the edge and a clear line leaves it. The trace runs against the level as it stands while the graph executes, so anything the same graph has yet to spawn is not there to be hit. **Invert** trades the two outcomes, keeping the edges that hit.

off_label.claim: With **Invert** on, the rule keeps only the edges that hit something, which turns a cluster laid over a level into a map of what blocks what: run it in the consumer's Attribute mode and every edge carries whether the line between its two Vtx is clear.
off_label.grounded_in: GetDefaultEdgeValidity returns !bInvert and ProcessEdge exchanges to 1 on a hit when inverted; Attribute mode writes edge validity out and resets it.

CollisionSettings.semantics: The block is shared with the plugin's other collision consumers, and this rule uses part of it. `Trace Mode` and the `Sphere Radius` and `Box Half Extents` that follow it are read by nodes that sweep a shape; the trace here is always a line, whatever the mode says. Everything else in the block applies: the collision type and its channel, object type or profile, `Trace Complex`, `Ignore Self` and the ignored-actor selection.
CollisionSettings.trap: Setting `Trace Mode` to Sphere or Box changes nothing here, and the thickness you dialled in is never applied. `Scatter` is what widens the test on this rule.

bTwoWayCheck.tooltip: If the first linecast fails, tries the other way around. This is to ensure we don't fail against backfacing, but has high cost.

bScatter.tooltip: Scatter multiple traces around the endpoint to improve hit detection reliability.
bScatter.semantics: Scatter fans several traces at the far Vtx instead of one, all leaving the same near Vtx, each aimed at a random point inside a sphere around it. The first one to hit ends the edge, so scatter can only ever find more hits than a single trace: turning it on removes more edges, never fewer. Which points it aims at is fixed by the edge's own two endpoint ids, so the fan is the same on every execution and no seed setting reaches it.

ScatterSamples.tooltip: How many traces are fired per endpoint.
ScatterSamples.semantics: How many traces at most, since the fan stops at the first hit: an edge that is thoroughly blocked costs one trace and a clear edge costs all of them. This is the setting that decides the cost of the rule, and it multiplies with `Two Way Check`, which doubles the traces that miss.

ScatterRadius.tooltip: World-space radius the extra traces are scattered within, around the endpoint.
ScatterRadius.semantics: The endpoint the samples are scattered around is the far one, so this is a spread on the aim and not a thickness on the line: the test widens at the far Vtx and stays pinned at the near one. Set it near the size of the geometry you are trying to catch; left at its small default it barely changes the single-trace result.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the refinement result (keep edges that hit and vice versa).

hints.text: Collision queries have to run on the game thread, so picking this rule puts the whole of **Cluster : Refine** there. It is the only refinement that does, and on a large cluster it is what makes this rule the slow one.

UPCGExEdgeRefinePrimMST.name: Refine : MST (Prim)
UPCGExEdgeRefinePrimMST.purpose: Cuts a cluster down to the cheapest tree that still reaches every Vtx. Cheap is whatever the **Heuristics** pin says it is, so the same cluster gives a shortest-length skeleton under one heuristic stack and a flattest or straightest one under another. Nothing loops in the result, and there is one route between any two Vtx.
UPCGExEdgeRefinePrimMST.situation: A dense cluster has to become a road, pipe or cable network that reaches everything once and doubles back nowhere.

mechanism.text: Every edge starts removed, and the rule then grows one tree and puts its edges back. It starts at a single Vtx, and at each step takes the cheapest connection leading out of what it has reached so far, until nothing new is reachable. Cost is the heuristics stack's score for that connection, and lower wins, so **Heuristics : Shortest Distance** on its own gives the shortest-total-length tree. The score is asked for in the direction of travel, from the Vtx already reached toward the one being considered, so a heuristic that reads direction can charge one price outbound and another inbound.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the refinement result (keep edges that would be removed and vice versa).
bInvert.semantics: Inverted, the survivors are the edges the tree did not take, which is the cluster's surplus connectivity with the spanning skeleton lifted out of it. On an input that was already a tree that surplus is nothing, so the result comes back empty.

hints.text: Where the tree starts is decided, not random. The starting Vtx is the one nearest a point derived from the cluster's bounds, offset by whatever the heuristics stack asks for: with no directional heuristic wired that lands on the Vtx nearest the cluster centre. The start matters where connections tie on score, since the first one reached wins and the rest of the tree follows from there.

The growth only ever reaches the Vtx connected to that starting one. Several connected components sharing a single Edges dataset therefore lose every edge outside the component the tree started in, since those edges are never put back. Generators emit one Edges dataset per component, so this bites on datasets assembled by hand or re-paired after a Points-mode pass.

UPCGExEdgeRefineSkeleton.name: Refine : β Skeleton
UPCGExEdgeRefineSkeleton.purpose: Removes an edge when another Vtx crowds the space beside it, with one number deciding how much space that is. It is the tunable member of the proximity family, where **Refine : Gabriel** offers a single fixed test and this offers a dial. `Beta` sets both the shape of the region tested and its size, and it is the whole of the rule.
UPCGExEdgeRefineSkeleton.situation: A cluster needs thinning by proximity, and the fixed Gabriel test either cuts too much or leaves too much.

mechanism.text: Judged one edge at a time. A region is built around the edge from the edge's own length and the `Beta` value, the rest of the cluster's Vtx are searched inside it, and one strictly inside removes the edge; the edge's own two Vtx never count against it. `Beta` at or below 1 and `Beta` above 1 build the region in two different ways, which is the thing to read before turning the dial. **Invert** trades the two outcomes, leaving the edges whose region held something as the survivors.

Beta.tooltip: Beta parameter for the skeleton algorithm. Values ≤1 use lune-based tests, >1 use circle-based tests.
Beta.semantics: At or below 1, the region is the lens where two spheres overlap, each centred on one of the edge's Vtx with the edge length divided by `Beta` as its radius, and an edge goes when some other Vtx is inside both. At the default of 1 the radii equal the edge length, which asks whether any Vtx is closer to both ends of the edge than they are to each other. Dividing by a smaller number swells both spheres and the lens between them, so the further below 1 this goes the more is removed, and at the floor of 0.001 the lens is a thousand edge lengths across and next to nothing survives. Above 1, the region becomes two separate spheres, each with the edge length as its radius, sitting the edge length times `Beta` out from the edge's midpoint on either side, and an edge goes when some other Vtx is inside either. Raising `Beta` past 1 pushes those two spheres further from the edge, so the higher it goes the less is removed.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the refinement result (keep edges that would be removed and vice versa).
bInvert.semantics: Inverted, the survivors are the edges that had a Vtx in their region, so the result is the part of the cluster the rule would otherwise have cut. The test still runs, unlike the same toggle on **Refine : Gabriel**.

hints.text: Above 1, the two spheres are placed along the horizontal perpendicular to the edge, taken from world up. The region therefore sits in a horizontal band rather than wrapping the edge evenly, and two edges of the same length in the same neighbourhood can be judged differently for pointing different ways. A perfectly vertical edge has no such direction at all: the offset collapses and both spheres land on the midpoint, so it is judged against a single sphere of the edge's own length however high `Beta` goes, and comes out far more likely to be cut than its neighbours.

UPCGExEdgeRefineTrajanDFS.name: Refine : DFS (Tarjan)
UPCGExEdgeRefineTrajanDFS.purpose: Finds the edges that hold the cluster together, and by default takes them out. A bridge is an edge no cycle passes through, so removing it breaks the cluster into more pieces than it was. What comes back is the edges that lie on at least one cycle, which is the looping part of the structure with every tether, stub and dead end gone.
UPCGExEdgeRefineTrajanDFS.situation: A generator produced a tangle of loops joined by single-edge tethers, and only the loops are wanted.

mechanism.text: One walk of the whole cluster identifies every bridge in it, in a single pass and with no setting to steer it. Every edge starts kept and each bridge is then removed. A leaf's one edge is always a bridge, and so is every edge of a structure holding no cycle at all, which is why running this on a tree empties it. **Invert** trades the two sets, leaving the bridges as the only survivors.

off_label.claim: Set the consumer's `Mode` to Attribute and the cluster comes back intact with a bridge-or-not boolean on every edge, which turns the rule into a connectivity audit: an edge marked here is a single point of failure for whatever the cluster is standing in for.
off_label.grounded_in: The rule only writes edge validity, and Attribute mode duplicates both facades, writes the verdict per edge and resets validity in FProcessor::InsertEdges.

bInvert.tooltip: Invert the refinement result (keep edges that would be removed and vice versa).
bInvert.semantics: Inverted, the survivors are the bridges alone. No cycle passes through a bridge, so that set can hold no cycle either: what comes out is a forest, and on a cluster that had no cycle to begin with it is the whole thing, unchanged.

UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeaves.name: Remove Leaves
UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeaves.purpose: Cuts the dead ends off a cluster in one sweep. A leaf is a Vtx with a single edge, and this takes each of them out along with the whole chain running back from it, stopping at the first junction it reaches. **Remove Leaves (Recursive)** is the one that carries on past that junction once losing its spurs has left it a dead end too.
UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeaves.situation: A generated cluster has grown spurs off its junctions and only the connected body is wanted.

mechanism.text: Visited once per Vtx, and only a leaf acts. From a leaf the rule walks the chain hanging off it, striking out each Vtx it stands on and the edge it leaves along, and it halts at the first Vtx holding three edges or more. That junction keeps its place and every edge it has left. A dead-end chain therefore comes away whole in one sweep however long it is, and a component that is nothing but a chain comes away entirely. Nothing branches on the way, because a Vtx on a chain has only ever one way onward.

UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeavesRecursive.name: Remove Leaves (Recursive)
UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeavesRecursive.purpose: Strips the dead ends off a cluster, then the dead ends that leaves behind, and keeps going. Whole branches come away down to the junction they hang from, so what survives is the part of the cluster lying on loops. `Max Iterations` stops it early, which is how some of the branching is kept.
UPCGExEdgeRemoveLeavesRecursive.situation: A cluster is meant to be all loops, and the generator left branching debris hanging off it.

mechanism.text: Runs once over the whole cluster, in waves. A wave takes every Vtx holding a single edge, removes that Vtx and that edge, and any neighbour the wave leaves holding a single edge joins the next wave. Waves continue until no Vtx holds a single edge, or until `Max Iterations` of them have run. A cluster holding no loop is emptied, since there is always another dead end to reach for. Every Vtx it strikes out has lost its last edge first, so the three consumer modes agree on what survived.

MaxIterations.tooltip: Maximum number of iterations. Set to 0 or less for unlimited iterations until no leaves remain.
MaxIterations.semantics: One iteration is one wave across the whole cluster, so this counts layers peeled inward from the ends rather than Vtx removed. At 1 it takes the dead ends the cluster arrived with and stops. Raise it and the cut walks that many Vtx up each branch, which is the setting to reach for when the branches themselves are wanted but the fine twigs on them are not.

hints.text: A Vtx with three or more edges is reached once its branches are gone. Stripping two of the three leaves it holding one, which makes it a dead end for the next wave, so a junction is only safe while something still loops back to it. This is the difference between running this rule unbounded and running it with `Max Iterations` set.

UPCGExEdgeRemoveOverlap.name: Refine : Overlap
UPCGExEdgeRemoveOverlap.purpose: Removes edges that cross or run too close to another edge. It is the one rule that compares edges against each other rather than against points, geometry or a score, so it is what untangles a cluster whose connections pass through one another. An angle window narrows it to the crossings you care about, square ones or grazing ones.
UPCGExEdgeRemoveOverlap.situation: Probes connected the same neighbourhood from several directions and the result is full of edges crossing over each other.

mechanism.text: Judged one edge at a time, against the other edges near enough to share bounds with it. Two edges overlap when the closest points on the two spans lie within `Tolerance` of each other, their directions fall inside the angle window, and neither closest point lands on a Vtx. Edges meeting at a shared Vtx are skipped outright. When two edges do overlap, `Keep` decides by length and the loser removes itself, which is a verdict each of the pair reaches on its own, so the result carries no dependence on edge order.

Keep.tooltip: Which edge to keep when doing comparison.
Keep.semantics: Only the losing edge acts, and only on itself. An edge that meets one it cannot beat stops looking, so what an edge is compared against is the cluster as it arrived: an edge already removed by some other pairing still counts, and still takes out anything shorter it crosses. A chain of crossings therefore thins further than pairing them off would.
Keep.trap: Two overlapping edges of equal length beat nothing and both survive, since the comparison is strict either way. A grid or a radial pattern is where that shows up, because the crossing pairs there are often the same length by construction.

Tolerance.tooltip: Distance at which two edges are considered intersecting.
Tolerance.semantics: The straight-line gap between the two spans at their closest approach, measured in world units in three dimensions. The default of 1 catches genuine crossings and little else, so two edges that cross in plan view while passing at different heights are left alone until this is raised past the height between them. Raising it also brings in edges running alongside each other without ever meeting.

MinAngle.semantics: The lower end of a window on the angle between the two edge directions, measured unsigned so it runs from 0 for parallel to 90 for square. An overlap below this angle is left alone. Raise it to act only on crossings near square and leave edges that graze past each other in place. Switching it off opens the bottom of the window.

MaxAngle.semantics: The upper end of the same window, and an overlap above this angle is left alone. Lower it to act only on edges running nearly parallel, which is the case where two connections are duplicating the same route. Switching it off opens the top of the window. Left at 0 and 90 the pair admits every angle, which is what makes the rule act on any overlap it finds.

UPCGExEntryCountFilterProviderSettings.name: Data Filter : Entry Count
UPCGExEntryCountFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Compares how many points a dataset holds against a number, and answers for the dataset as a whole. Entries here are the points inside one dataset; the datasets arriving alongside it on a pin are counted by nothing in this family. The number compared against is a constant, or a `@Data` value read on the dataset being counted, which lets each dataset carry the threshold it should be judged by.
UPCGExEntryCountFilterProviderSettings.situation: A pin carrying datasets of wildly different sizes, where the small ones are noise and should be dropped before the expensive work starts.

mechanism.text: The point count of the dataset under test is the left operand and `Comparison` measures it against `Operand B`. Datasets holding no points are discarded when a node gathers its point inputs, so the count that reaches this filter is at least one and a test that only passes at zero passes nothing. Reading `Operand B` from an attribute is a data-level read on the dataset being counted, so each dataset can answer to its own number.

outputs.label: Data Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. The Data Filter family qualifies for dataset-level evaluation by construction, with no condition on how the node is configured, so every filter pin in the plugin takes it, **Uber Branch** and **Break** included.

UPCGExExtrudePathSettings.name: Path : Extrude
UPCGExExtrudePathSettings.purpose: Grows a path past one or both of its ends, adding a new tip and, if asked, the points between the old end and that tip. Everything already on the path survives untouched, so this only ever lengthens. The new stretch can run straight, curve away as an arc that leaves the path smoothly, or take the shape of a profile path wired in, and each end can be gated by a filter so only the ends that pass grow.
UPCGExExtrudePathSettings.situation: A path stops short of where it needs to reach, and the continuation has to leave from its existing end rather than replace it.

mechanism.text: One path in, one path out, always: the point count grows and nothing else about the input changes. The output runs new tip, then the new points working inward, then every original point in order, then the far end's new points, then its tip. New points inherit their nearest original end's rotation, scale and attributes, take their position from the extrusion, and are given a fresh position-derived seed. A closed loop has no ends to grow from and is forwarded as it arrived, with a suppressible warning.

off_label.claim: A negative length extrudes backwards along the resolved direction, which folds the new stretch back over the path instead of away from it. Only a length of zero refuses to extrude.
off_label.grounded_in: ComputeExtrusion rejects on the absolute value of the length and then places the tip at endpoint plus direction times the signed length

off_label.claim: With subdivision off and a length that varies per point, this becomes a way to add exactly one point beyond each end at a distance read from the end itself, which is the cheapest form of an end cap.
off_label.grounded_in: with the profile inactive ComputeExtrusion writes the tip alone, and the length getter is read at the endpoint index rather than as a constant

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to grow. Closed loops are forwarded rather than processed.

inputs.label: Extrude Conditions
inputs.note: Point filters tested at the two ends alone. With nothing wired both ends pass, so the node extrudes by default.

inputs.label: Profile
inputs.note: A single path of two points or more whose shape the new stretch takes. The pin only exists while the profile type is Custom, and it is required there.
inputs.condition: when Type is Custom

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One path per input, longer than it went in unless neither end was extruded.

Endpoint.tooltip: Which endpoints to extrude (start, end, or both).
Endpoint.semantics: It narrows which ends are considered before the filter is consulted, so an end excluded here is never tested. An end that is allowed and passes can still fail to grow, on a zero length or a direction that resolves to nothing.

Length.tooltip: Distance the new endpoint is pushed out by.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Length.semantics: Read at the end point itself, so an attribute gives each end its own distance. A value of zero skips that end entirely, which is the way to leave one end alone using data rather than the `Endpoint` setting.

DirectionMode.tooltip: How the extrusion direction is computed.
DirectionMode.semantics: The terminal direction is found by walking inward past points sitting on top of the end, so a duplicated last point does not flatten it.
DirectionMode.trap: A path whose points are all in one place has no direction to find, and that end is skipped with a warning.

Direction.tooltip: Extrusion direction in Custom mode; offset added to the path direction in Path Direction mode (zero = pure path direction).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

fields.name: Constant
fields.tooltip: Direction vector when using constant input.

fields.name: bFlip
fields.tooltip: Negate the direction vector after reading.

Direction.semantics: It ships as a zero constant, which is the offset `Path Direction` mode wants and a direction `Custom` mode cannot use: switching to `Custom` without touching it warns and extrudes nothing. Switching its input to an attribute hands over a selector already filled in with the end point's own up axis. Its flip toggle is applied first, ahead of `Transform Direction`.

bOffsetMagnitudeMatters.tooltip: If enabled, the offset is added as-read so its length drives how strongly it tilts the path direction; otherwise it is normalized first and weighs equally with it.
bOffsetMagnitudeMatters.semantics: Normalised, the offset and the terminal direction weigh equally, so the extrusion leaves at the bearing halfway between them.

bTransformDirection.tooltip: If enabled, the direction read above is rotated by the endpoint's transform.
bTransformDirection.semantics: Applies in both direction modes, so in `Path Direction` mode it rotates the offset rather than the terminal direction. What it turns the direction by is the end point's own rotation, which makes an authored direction follow whatever orientation the path carries.

Type.tooltip: Type of profile applied to the new segment. Arc & Custom curve the extrusion and require a Custom direction (Path Direction is always straight).
Type.semantics: `Custom` lays the profile in the plane spanned by the extrusion and the path.
Type.trap: The two curved types degrade differently where the extrusion runs straight along the path: an arc straightens out and keeps its subdivision points, while a custom profile is dropped altogether and the end gains its bare tip.

MainAxisScaling.tooltip: Define how the custom profile is scaled on the main axis.
MainAxisScaling.semantics: How the profile's length is sized against the extrusion. `Uniform` matches it to the extrusion length, `Scale` multiplies that length by the value below, and `Distance` sets it in world units outright and ignores how far the tip is.

MainAxisScale.tooltip: Scale or Distance value for the main axis.

CrossAxisScaling.tooltip: Define how the custom profile is scaled on the cross axis.
CrossAxisScaling.semantics: The same three choices for how far the profile is allowed to bulge sideways. Both axes measure against the extrusion length, so a profile scaled uniformly stays proportionally the same shape whatever the length is.

CrossAxisScale.tooltip: Scale or Distance value for the cross axis.

bSubdivide.tooltip: Whether to subdivide the new segment (Line & Arc). Without this an extruded endpoint is just a single new tip point.
bSubdivide.semantics: Without it the extrusion is a single new point at the tip, whatever the shape settings say, so an arc with subdivision off is a straight jump to where the arc would have ended. It is hidden under `Custom`, where the profile supplies the points and subdivision is not a choice.

SubdivideMethod.semantics: `Count` places that many points between end and tip, `Distance` places one every so many world units, and `Manhattan` replaces both with axis-aligned steps and produces at most two points.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SubdivisionAmount.semantics: A count or a world distance depending on the method, read at the end point so it can differ per end. It disappears under `Manhattan`, which takes its shape from its own block instead.

SubdivisionFlagName.tooltip: Name of the boolean flag to write whether the point is a subdivision point or not.
SubdivisionFlagName.semantics: Marks the points added between an end and its tip, and the tips themselves are left unmarked, so the flag names the fill rather than the whole extrusion. On a path where nothing was extruded the attribute is still created, set false everywhere, so downstream tests do not have to check whether it exists.

bQuietDegenerateProfileWarning.tooltip: Suppress the warning raised when an Arc/Custom profile is degenerate (extrusion parallel to the path).

bQuietClosedLoopWarning.tooltip: Suppress warning when attempting to extrude a closed loop path.
bQuietClosedLoopWarning.semantics: The warning it silences fires once per run rather than once per loop, and the forwarding it reports happens whether or not it is silenced.

hints.text: New points share their nearest original end's metadata entry, so they arrive carrying that end's attribute values rather than defaults. The one thing not inherited is the seed, which is recomputed from the new position.

The filter pin is tested at the two end points only, and it defaults to passing. Wiring a stack that happens to fail at both ends leaves every path forwarded unchanged, which looks identical to the node doing nothing at all.

UPCGExExtrudeTensorsSettings.name: Tensors : Extrude
UPCGExExtrudeTensorsSettings.purpose: Turns points into paths by walking them through a tensor field: each seed asks the field which way to go, takes a step, and asks again, leaving a trail behind it. Where it stops is the interesting part, and there are five ways it can happen: running out of steps, running out of length or points, leaving a region a filter allows, hitting a path wired in from outside, or running into another trail from the same run. The paths that come out are ordinary paths, tagged with why they ended.
UPCGExExtrudeTensorsSettings.situation: A field has been authored and something has to follow it: streamlines, growth from a set of starting points, or routes that stop when they meet each other.

mechanism.text: One path per extrusion, and an extrusion per seed point, so the count follows the seeds rather than the datasets. The seeds are consumed and never come back out. Every extrusion advances one step per iteration, all of them in lockstep, which is what lets them see each other while they are still growing; a step takes the field's direction and magnitude from the current head, so step length is the field's and not a setting. A step shorter than `Fuse Distance` still spends its iteration and adds no point, so a path can hold far fewer points than the iteration count. Whichever limit is met first ends that extrusion.

off_label.claim: One iteration turns this into a sampler in path clothing: every seed produces a two-point path from where it started to where one step of the field took it, which reads the field's direction and magnitude at every seed at once.
off_label.grounded_in: an extrusion inserts its head each time it advances and stops once its remaining iterations reach zero, and the output-details floor of two points is what such a path has

off_label.claim: With self-intersections on and no tensor worth following, the stop tags become a proximity map: paths tagged as merged are the seeds that ran into a neighbour, and paths tagged as crossed are the ones that ran across one.
off_label.grounded_in: the tagging callback writes IsSelfMergedTag and IsStoppedBySelfIntersectionTag from the extrusion's own stop reason, independently of what the field did

Iterations.semantics: A step budget rather than a point count: steps spent probing a stop region, and steps too short to clear the fuse distance, are spent all the same. With per-point iterations on it becomes a ceiling on whatever the attribute says.

bUseMaxFromPoints.tooltip: Whether to adjust max iteration based on max value found on points. Use at your own risks!
bUseMaxFromPoints.semantics: The run loops as many times as its budget allows, and that budget is otherwise the constant. Switching this on raises it to the largest value the attribute holds, so the seeds asking for more actually get to spend it.
bUseMaxFromPoints.trap: Left off with a per-point attribute in play, the run still stops after the constant's worth of passes, so every seed asking for more than the constant is cut short and none of them reports why.

bAllowChildExtrusions.tooltip: Whether to stop sampling when extrusion is stopped. While path will be cut, there's a chance that the head of the search comes back into non-stopping conditions, which would start a new extrusion. With this option disabled, new paths won't be permitted to exist.
bAllowChildExtrusions.semantics: A fresh extrusion started this way inherits the remaining budget, so one seed can yield several paths.

bIgnoreStoppedSeeds.tooltip: If enabled, seeds that start stopped won't be extruded at all. Otherwise, they are transformed until they eventually reach a point that's outside stopping conditions and start an extrusion.

bDoExternalPathIntersections.tooltip: Test for intersections with external path data.

bIgnoreIntersectionOnOrigin.tooltip: If enabled, if the origin location of the extrusion is detected as an intersection, it is not considered an intersection. This allows to have seeds perfectly located on paths used for intersections.

bDoSelfPathIntersections.semantics: It makes the extrusions of one run visible to each other while they are still growing, which is why they advance in lockstep. Which of two meeting extrusions gets cut is decided by the order they are sorted into, so the sorting settings below are what make the outcome repeatable rather than a race.

SelfIntersectionMode.tooltip: How to order intersection checks. Sorting is using seeds input attributes.
SelfIntersectionMode.semantics: Under `Path Length` the longer trail survives a meeting. `Sorting only` does nothing at all without sorting sub-nodes wired, leaving the order as it was.

AttributesToPathTags.semantics: Read from the seed point rather than from the extrusion, so the tags on a path describe where it started. A child extrusion inherits its parent's seed index and therefore the same tags.

IsChildExtrusionTag.tooltip: Tag to apply to child extrusion paths.

TensorHandlerDetails.tooltip: Tensor sampling settings. These are applied on the flattened sample, e.g after & on top of individual tensors' mutations.

PathOutputDetails.tooltip: Point-count limits deciding which generated paths are kept. Paths with fewer than 2 points are always dropped.
PathOutputDetails.semantics: The last gate. A path that fails is discarded whole and nothing is logged, so the symptom is arithmetic: fewer paths than seeds.

hints.text: Stop filters are evaluated against a position and an orientation, not against a point with attributes: the head of an extrusion is not a point in any dataset and has no attributes to read. Filters that need one are dropped before the run starts, named in a warning, and the node carries on with whatever survived. If none of them survive the warning says so and nothing stops the extrusions at all.

An extrusion that asks the field for a direction and gets no answer stops there, tagged by nothing, because a position no tensor reaches has nothing to give. A **Tensor : Constant** at a low weight covers the whole field and is the usual fix for runs that end early for no visible reason.

UPCGExFactoryProviderSettings.name: Factory : Provider
UPCGExFactoryProviderSettings.purpose: The base every sub-node inherits. A sub-node produces no data of its own: it emits a factory on a pin, and a consumer node reads that factory and does the work. Filters, heuristics, selectors, probes, blend operations and the rest all share that shape, and what they share is here.
UPCGExFactoryProviderSettings.situation: Reading any of the sub-node pages and needing to know what a factory pin means and how several on one pin combine.

mechanism.text: The provider runs once, builds a factory object from its panel settings, and emits it. Nothing about the node's subject happens then: the factory is a description, and the consumer that reads it is what applies that description per point, per edge or per element. That is why a sub-node's cost belongs to its consumer, and why a sub-node wired to nothing does nothing at all.

hints.text: Several factories on one pin are combined by the consumer rather than competing. Whether that combination is a stack, a sum or a first-match is a property of the consumer, and each family's own base page says which.

Most sub-node families add a `Priority` of their own, which orders the factories on a consumer's pin. What that ordering decides belongs to the consumer, so the same value means something different on a filter stack than on a blend pin.

UPCGExFillControlsAttributeAccumulationP.name: Fill Control : Attribute Accumulation
UPCGExFillControlsAttributeAccumulationP.purpose: Adds an attribute up along a lane and stops the lane when the total passes a ceiling. Given a cost written on the Vtx or the edges, a fill reaches far where the cost is small and stops quickly where it is large, so the reach is shaped by the data rather than by hops or distance. `Mode` decides what the running value is, which turns the same control into a budget, a barrier or a smoothness gate.
UPCGExFillControlsAttributeAccumulationP.situation: The fill should get further through cheap ground than expensive, with cost already written on the cluster rather than expressed as heuristics.

mechanism.text: For each candidate the control reads the chosen attribute from the candidate Vtx or from the edge reaching it, folds it into whatever the lane behind it had accumulated according to `Mode`, and refuses the candidate when the result is over `Max Accumulation`. The running value rides on the candidate, so every lane keeps its own and a fork inherits whatever its branch point held. The raw value read is also added to the candidate's score, so the control nudges the order candidates are taken in whether or not anything is watching that score.

outputs.note: Wire it to the Fill Controls pin on Cluster : Flood Fill or Cluster : Diffuse. Several controls stack there and all of them have to agree.

UPCGExFillControlsAttributeThresholdProv.name: Fill Control : Attribute Threshold
UPCGExFillControlsAttributeThresholdProv.purpose: Reads one number off the Vtx or the edge in front of the fill and compares it against a threshold. It is the plainest way to stop a spread at something the data already says: a height, a density, a mask an earlier node wrote. Where Fill Control : Vtx Filters takes a whole stack of sub-nodes, this takes one attribute and one comparison with nothing to wire.
UPCGExFillControlsAttributeThresholdProv.situation: A single attribute already marks where the fill should stop, and a filter stack is more machinery than one comparison needs.

mechanism.text: For each candidate the control reads the chosen attribute from the candidate Vtx or from the edge reaching it, and keeps the candidate when the comparison against `Threshold` holds. The same test runs at whichever moments `Steps` names. The attribute has to exist and be readable as a number, and the node fails with a message naming it when it is not.

UPCGExFillControlsBranchLimitProviderSet.name: Fill Control : Branch Limit
UPCGExFillControlsBranchLimitProviderSet.purpose: Caps how often a fill forks. A spread across a dense cluster branches at nearly every Vtx and comes out reading as a stain, and capping the branching is what turns it back into a few visible lanes. `Max Branches` counts children beyond the first, so zero is a single unbranched lane and one allows a single fork. Two switches decide whose budget is being spent and what becomes of the neighbour that could not be taken.
UPCGExFillControlsBranchLimitProviderSet.situation: A root, river or crack pattern is wanted and the raw fill covers everything instead of running in lanes.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx the fill spreads from takes its first child for free, and every child after that spends from a budget. `Source` decides whose budget it is, one per Vtx or one shared by the whole diffusion, and `Mode` decides whether an over-budget child is dropped or left where it stands for another route to pick up. Nothing here widens a fill: at a budget of zero every Vtx keeps exactly one child and each diffusion becomes one lane.

UPCGExFillControlsCountProviderSettings.name: Fill Control : Count
UPCGExFillControlsCountProviderSettings.purpose: Caps how many Vtx one diffusion may hold. The count belongs to the diffusion, so several seeds under one Count each get the same allowance rather than sharing one, and the seed Vtx is already inside it. It is the bluntest of the reach limits: nothing about the shape of what gets taken, only how much.
UPCGExFillControlsCountProviderSettings.situation: Several seeds have to claim territories of comparable size regardless of how dense the cluster happens to be around each of them.

mechanism.text: Every time a diffusion is about to commit a Vtx, the control compares how many it already holds against `Max Count` and refuses once the two are equal. That refusal ends the diffusion rather than skipping one Vtx: the rest of its queued candidates fail the same comparison in the same step, and it stops for good. Which Vtx make up the allowance is decided by the priority ordering on the consumer, not here.

UPCGExFillControlsDepthProviderSettings.name: Fill Control : Depth
UPCGExFillControlsDepthProviderSettings.purpose: Stops a diffusion at a set number of hops from its seed. Hops, not distance: a step across a long edge costs the same as a step across a short one, so the reach follows the cluster's connectivity rather than its geometry. Every diffusion counts from its own seed, and the number counted is the same one Cluster : Flood Fill writes out as diffusion depth.
UPCGExFillControlsDepthProviderSettings.situation: A spread has to reach a fixed number of connections out from each seed however far apart the Vtx happen to sit.

mechanism.text: Every candidate carries how many hops it took to reach, the seed at zero, and the control refuses anything past `Max Depth`. The limit is inclusive, so a cap of ten admits Vtx ten hops out and refuses the eleventh. The same comparison runs at all three moments, which makes this the one control where `Steps` changes how far the fill gets rather than what it measures.

UPCGExFillControlsEdgeFiltersProviderSet.name: Fill Control : Edge Filters
UPCGExFillControlsEdgeFiltersProviderSet.purpose: Puts a filter stack on the connections rather than on the Vtx: an edge that fails cannot be crossed. Where Fill Control : Vtx Filters decides which ground a fill may stand on, this one decides which routes between ground are open, which is what walls, seams and severed regions are made of. A Vtx behind a closed edge stays reachable by any other route that leads to it.
UPCGExFillControlsEdgeFiltersProviderSet.situation: The fill has to be held back at a boundary that lives on the edges rather than on the Vtx.

mechanism.text: Every filter on the pin is asked about the edge the fill is about to cross and all of them have to pass, so the stack gates connections and never Vtx directly. It is asked at whichever moments `Steps` names. The seed is exempt: the Vtx a diffusion starts on spreads without any edge having been tested.

off_label.claim: Wire a Data Filter : sub-node here and the control stops being per edge: the verdict is decided once against the whole Edges dataset when the fill starts, and returned unchanged for every edge, which makes it an on or off switch for the fill on that cluster.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExFactories::ClusterEdgeFilters includes the collection filter type, and ICollectionFilter caches its verdict at Init and returns it from every Test overload
