hints.text: So that a filter can tell which way the fill is travelling, the edge is rebuilt before it is handed over with its start set to the Vtx being spread from. That start does not resolve back to a real Vtx, so every filter that reads the two endpoints answers here on a different Vtx than the same filter answers on anywhere else: **Edge Filter : Length**, **Num Vtx**, **Edge Direction**, **Endpoints Check**, **Endpoints Compare (Numeric)**, **Endpoints Compare (String)** and **Endpoints Regex**. Filters reading the edge point's own attributes, point filters included, are unaffected.

A **Vtx Filter :** sub-node dropped on this pin connects, then logs an invalid-input warning and is dropped when the node boots. If it was the only thing wired, the pin is then empty and the node raises a missing-required-input error naming the pin rather than the wire that caused it.

UPCGExFillControlsFactoryProviderSetting.name: Fill Controls Definition
UPCGExFillControlsFactoryProviderSetting.purpose: The base every **Fill Control :** node inherits. It never appears in the palette, and this page carries what the family shares: the **Fill Control** pin they all emit on, the two knobs that decide when a control is asked and where it reads its own limits from, and what a control is allowed to answer. Their consumers are **Cluster : Flood Fill** and **Cluster : Diffuse**, which take them on a pin named **Fill Controls**.
UPCGExFillControlsFactoryProviderSetting.situation: Reading any fill control page and needing to know what Steps and Source do to it, or why a control that looks configured is having no effect.

mechanism.text: A spread with nothing on the pin reaches its whole connected component, so controls are how it acquires a shape. Every factory on the pin becomes one live control per cluster, and each is asked a yes or no question at up to three moments of the spread: when a neighbour is first discovered, when a discovered Vtx is about to be committed, and when a committed Vtx is about to spread further. Any control saying no is enough for the spread to give that step up, and the rest of the queue carries on. A control can also add to a candidate score, which is how the heuristic ones reach the ordering, and none of them can invent a step that the topology does not already offer.

outputs.label: Fill Control
outputs.note: What every Fill Control : node emits. The Fill Controls pin on Cluster : Flood Fill and Cluster : Diffuse is the only place it is read, and several stack there.

hints.text: The three moments **Steps** names read differently on the panel than they do in the spread. `Candidate` is a neighbour just discovered, before it joins the queue, and it is the default. `Capture` is a queued Vtx being committed, which is where a running total such as a count or a budget is checked. `Probing` is a committed Vtx about to look at its own neighbours, so refusing there stops that Vtx becoming a branch while leaving it in the result.

Refusing a step at `Candidate` costs that diffusion the Vtx permanently: it was already marked as seen before the question was asked, so the spread will not come back to it by another route. Refusing at `Capture` costs it nothing, because the Vtx is skipped and stays available. The one exception is a spread running under **Fill Control : Branch Limit** in its fan-out mode, which scores its neighbours before marking any of them.

**Steps** reaches five of the family: **Attribute Threshold**, **Depth**, **Edge Filters**, **Length** and **Vtx Filters**. **Count** and **Attribute Accumulation** show the row and ignore it, because each declares the moments it answers at in code. The remaining six hide the row entirely.

**Source** decides where a control reads its own limit, and both settings point at the seed. `Seed` reads the seed point row and `Vtx` reads the row of the Vtx that seed landed on, so either way one diffusion gets one value for the whole of its run and different seeds can be given different limits. The data a control tests against that limit, an attribute on the candidate for instance, is read separately and is unaffected by this. **Edge Filters**, **Vtx Filters** and **Heuristics Scoring** hide the row because they carry no limit of their own.
Order on the pin does not matter. Every control is asked at each moment it opted into, the first refusal ends the question, and refusals do not compose into anything order could change.

UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsBudgetProvid.name: Fill Control : Heuristics Budget
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsBudgetProvid.purpose: A spending limit on a lane. It scores every step with the heuristics on its pin, adds the cost up along the lane and refuses the candidate that would take the total past `Max Budget`. What comes out reaches far over cheap ground and hardly at all over expensive, which is a falloff expressed entirely in cost rather than in hops or distance. It scores as well as limits, so it can drive the ordering without a separate Fill Control : Heuristics Scoring, and its Heuristics pin is optional: with nothing on it the cost of a step is its length, which turns the control into a distance budget.
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsBudgetProvid.situation: A spread should cover a lot of easy ground and little difficult ground, with difficulty already described by heuristics.

mechanism.text: Each step is scored by the heuristics on the pin, collapsed with `Heuristic Score Mode`, then added both to the candidate's own score and to the running total for its lane. The candidate is refused when the value named by `Budget Source` is over `Max Budget`. The comparison is inclusive and runs when a neighbour is first discovered, which is also the only moment this control answers at.

UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsScoringProvi.name: Fill Control : Heuristics Scoring
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsScoringProvi.purpose: The bridge between heuristics and a fill. It refuses nothing; it scores, and that score is what the consumer orders its candidates by once `Priority` is set to Heuristics. With no scoring control on the pin every candidate scores the same and the fill falls back to taking the shallowest one, so this is what makes a spread prefer cheap ground to expensive. It is also the replacement for the deprecated Heuristics pin on Cluster : Flood Fill.
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsScoringProvi.situation: A fill should run down the cheap routes first, with cheap meaning the same thing it means to the pathfinding nodes.

mechanism.text: Every heuristic on the pin scores the step from the Vtx being spread from to the candidate, the control collapses their answers with its own `Heuristic Score Mode`, multiplies by `Score Weight` and adds the result to the candidate's score. Lower is better throughout, so a candidate scoring less is taken sooner. Nothing here stops a fill: the score changes the order Vtx are taken in and never whether they are taken at all.

off_label.claim: It also decides which lane keeps the trunk, and only under one setting. Cluster : Flood Fill can sort its partitioned path output by Score, and the running score that sort reads is written here only when `Previous Score` is ticked, so a fill scored on `Local Score` alone leaves every lane at zero and that sort has nothing to order by.
off_label.grounded_in: the Score branch of the partition sort compares Captured[A].PathScore, and FPCGExFillControlHeuristicsScoring::ScoreCandidate writes PathScore only under the Previous Score flag

UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsThresholdPro.name: Fill Control : Heuristics Threshold
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsThresholdPro.purpose: A limit on one step rather than on a lane's total. It scores every step with the heuristics on its pin and refuses a candidate whose score fails the comparison against `Threshold`, so a single expensive crossing stops a lane however cheap the route behind it was. Where Fill Control : Heuristics Budget spends an allowance, this one draws a line no single step may cross. It scores while it tests, so it can drive the ordering on its own.
UPCGExFillControlsHeuristicsThresholdPro.situation: A spread must not cross anything the heuristics call expensive, however much cheap ground it has covered getting there.

mechanism.text: Each step is scored by the heuristics on the pin and collapsed with `Heuristic Score Mode`, and the value named by `Threshold Source` is then compared against `Threshold`. Passing the comparison is what admits the candidate, so the operator reads as the rule for continuing rather than the rule for stopping. It is asked when a neighbour is first discovered and at no other moment.

UPCGExFillControlsKeepDirectionProviderS.name: Fill Control : Keep Direction
UPCGExFillControlsKeepDirectionProviderS.purpose: Keeps a lane going the way it was already going. Each step is compared against the heading of the steps behind it and a step that turns too sharply is refused, so lanes run straight or curve gradually instead of doubling back through a dense cluster. It is the one control that reads the route travelled rather than the Vtx or the edge in front of it.
UPCGExFillControlsKeepDirectionProviderS.situation: A fill through a dense cluster comes out as a stain, and what was wanted was a few lanes that hold a heading.

mechanism.text: The control averages the headings of up to `Window Size` steps taken along the lane behind the Vtx now spreading, and compares the heading of the step under consideration against that average. Both headings are quantised onto a grid whose cell size is `Hash Tolerance`, and the step is allowed when the two land in the same cell, so what is tested is an equality on a rounded heading rather than an angle. It is asked when a neighbour is first discovered and at no other moment.

UPCGExFillControlsLengthProviderSettings.name: Fill Control : Length
UPCGExFillControlsLengthProviderSettings.purpose: Stops a diffusion on distance. It measures either the length of the route travelled from the seed to the candidate or the length of the single step about to be taken, and refuses anything over `Max Length`. Distance here is the straight line between Vtx positions summed step by step, so a route bending around an obstacle spends its allowance faster than one running straight, and a cap set here is a reach in world units rather than in connections.
UPCGExFillControlsLengthProviderSettings.situation: A spread has to reach a fixed distance from each seed rather than a fixed number of connections.

mechanism.text: Every candidate carries both the length of the step reaching it and the length of the whole route behind it, and `Use Path Length` picks which of the two is compared against `Max Length`. The limit is inclusive and the same comparison runs at all three moments, so `Steps` decides when the refusal lands rather than what is measured.

UPCGExFillControlsRunningAverageProvider.name: Fill Control : Running Average
UPCGExFillControlsRunningAverageProvider.purpose: Keeps a lane on values close to the ones behind it. It averages one attribute or point property over the Vtx a lane has already taken and refuses a candidate whose own value sits further from that average than `Tolerance`. Shipped pointing at `$Position.Z`, which makes it a contour follower out of the box: gradual climbs are allowed, a step up onto a ledge is not.
UPCGExFillControlsRunningAverageProvider.situation: A spread should follow ground of a consistent height, density or any other single value rather than taking whatever is adjacent.

mechanism.text: The control walks back along the lane from the Vtx now spreading, reads the operand on up to `Window Size` Vtx behind it and takes the mean. The candidate passes when its own operand is within `Tolerance` of that mean, an absolute band in the operand's own units rather than a ratio. The walk starts one Vtx back, so the Vtx doing the spreading is not part of its own average, and the whole test runs when a neighbour is first discovered and at no other moment.

UPCGExFillControlsVtxFiltersProviderSett.name: Fill Control : Vtx Filters
UPCGExFillControlsVtxFiltersProviderSett.purpose: Puts a filter stack in the way of the fill: a Vtx that fails is not taken. It is how a spread is confined to ground it is allowed on, and because the stack is the same one every other filter pin accepts, anything already built for narrowing points works here unchanged. Where Fill Control : Edge Filters gates the connections, this one gates the ground.
UPCGExFillControlsVtxFiltersProviderSett.situation: A fill has to stay inside a region, or out of one, and the boundary is something a filter can already tell about a Vtx.

mechanism.text: Every filter on the pin is asked about the candidate Vtx and all of them have to pass. It is the candidate that is tested, never the Vtx being spread from, and the stack is asked at whichever moments `Steps` names. The seed is exempt on both counts: a diffusion takes its seed Vtx without asking, and that Vtx spreads even when the filters would have refused it.

off_label.claim: Wire a Data Filter : sub-node here and the control stops being per Vtx: the verdict is decided once against the whole Vtx dataset when the fill starts, and returned unchanged for every Vtx, which makes it an on or off switch for the fill on that cluster.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExFactories::ClusterNodeFilters includes the collection filter type, and ICollectionFilter caches its verdict at Init and returns it from every Test overload

UPCGExFilterFactoryData.name: Point Filter Definition
UPCGExFilterFactoryData.purpose: Every filter node emits one factory, and this is the contract the seventy-odd consumers read it through. A condition object carrying no points of its own, asked once per element for a yes or no. Three types branch from here, and they are what decides which consumer pins will accept the factory once the graph runs: the base type a **Filter Group** reports, the point type the **Filter :** family carries on its **Filter** pin, and the data type the **Data Filter :** family carries on its **Data Filter** pin. The data branch answers once for a whole dataset instead of once per element, and that single verdict then stands for every element in it.
UPCGExFilterFactoryData.situation: Working out why a filter that looks right in the details panel is refused, ignored, or quietly replaced by a constant on the pin it was wired into.

mechanism.text: A consumer collects the factories on its pin, keeps the ones whose family that pin accepts, sorts them by `Priority` lowest first, and asks each survivor for one filter bound to a single dataset. Which dataset is the consumer's choice, and each element is tested at its own row in it, so one unchanged factory reads points on a **Filters** pin, Vtx on a **Vtx Filters** pin and edges on an **Edge Filters** pin. The stack that results is an AND, stopping at the first failure. Binding happens once, before any element is tested, and a filter that cannot bind never reaches the stack: `Initialization Failure Policy` decides whether it is dropped, replaced by an always-true filter, or replaces every filter on the pin with a single always-false one. A consumer judging whole datasets keeps it instead, and that policy settles each dataset's verdict as it is read.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: What every **Filter :** node emits. It travels as ordinary parameter data, so reroutes carry it and one output reaches as many consumer pins as you wire it to.

outputs.label: Data Filter
outputs.note: What the **Data Filter :** family emits instead. Same wire and the same reach, with the verdict settled once per dataset rather than per element.

hints.text: The family check is not in the editor. Every filter pin in the plugin declares the same base filter type, so any filter connects to any filter pin, and the wrong family is dropped when the node runs with a warning naming the filter's internal class rather than its node title. The symptom is a condition that had no effect, not a wire that would not connect.

Dataset-level evaluation is opt-in per filter. A filter that implements the data-domain check qualifies once every attribute it names sits in the `@Data` domain, a constant operand counting as satisfied, and it then judges a whole dataset alongside the **Data Filter :** family; the filters that do not implement the check stay per-element wherever their operands point, and the ones that do carry it on their own page. A **Filter Group** qualifies only when every filter inside it does. **Uber Branch** and **Break** require it of every filter they are given and skip one that cannot, warning that it needs per-point evaluation; **Uber Filter (Data)** instead falls back to testing elements and counting the passes.

**Tensors : Extrude** and **Tensors Transform** test their **Stop Conditions** against a point that does not exist yet, so filters needing attribute access cannot answer there. Those are dropped with a warning that they do not support direct evaluation, and when none of them survive the pin behaves as though nothing were connected.

UPCGExFilterGroupProviderSettings.name: Filter Group
UPCGExFilterGroupProviderSettings.purpose: Several filters landing on one pin already mean AND. Everything beyond that goes through this node: it takes the filters on its Filters pin, combines them under a Mode of And or Or, and hands its consumer one verdict. Invert flips that verdict, turning And into NAND and Or into NOR. Because a group answers as a single filter, it can be a child of another group, and it can share a consumer pin with loose filters.
UPCGExFilterGroupProviderSettings.situation: A condition that is not a plain AND of everything on the pin: an either-or, or a whole set of tests inverted together.

mechanism.text: The consumer treats the group as one filter and runs it once per element; the group then runs its own children and returns a single answer. And stops at the first child that fails, Or stops at the first that passes, and Invert flips whatever comes out, so a group costs no more than the child that settles it. Children are sorted by Priority before evaluation, lowest first, the same sort a consumer applies to its own pin, so wire order is discarded inside a group too. Nesting has no depth limit, and a group sitting on a pin beside two loose filters reads as `(X OR Y) AND A AND B`. A group can judge a whole dataset only while every one of its children can, and it then puts each child's dataset-level answer through the same And or Or.

off_label.claim: An And group can earn its place with nothing to decide. It collapses a whole condition set into one wire, so adding a filter to the set reaches every consumer at once instead of being dragged to each of them separately.
off_label.grounded_in: UPCGExFilterGroupFactoryDataAND::CreateFilter returning one FFilterGroupAND whose verdict stands in for the entire child stack, and the group factory travelling as ordinary parameter data

off_label.claim: A group holding a single child is a standalone NOT once Invert is on, and since Invert is overridable the negation itself can be driven from a graph parameter.
off_label.grounded_in: FFilterGroupAND::Test returning bInvert on a failing child and its complement otherwise, which with one child in the stack is plain negation, plus the PCG_Overridable meta on bInvert

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: The filters to combine. Every family is accepted here, so one group can hold point, data and cluster filters together; each child is then checked against what the consumer accepts at the moment the group runs.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The group, presented to its consumer as one filter. It carries the plain filter type, which every filter pin accepts, so a group drops onto point, Vtx and Edge pins alike.

Priority.tooltip: Filter Priority. Will use the highest value between the one set here and from the connected filters.

Mode.semantics: The palette carries this node twice, as And (Combine Filters) and Or (Combine Filters); both drop the same node with Mode already set. Mode is overridable, so a group packaged inside a subgraph can be switched between extending and narrowing the caller's conditions from outside, without opening the subgraph.

bInvert.semantics: And with Invert is NAND and Or with Invert is NOR. The node subtitle reads AND or OR, with (NOT) appended once this is on.
bInvert.trap: To keep everything outside several regions, put the region filters in an Or group and invert the group. Inverting each filter on its own asks for elements outside region A and outside B and outside C, which is a different and usually unintended question.

bDrawAsCompactNode.tooltip: Whether to draw this node as a compact node

InitializationFailurePolicy.tooltip: How the consumer handles this group failing to initialize. Grouped filters apply their own policy, not this one.
InitializationFailurePolicy.semantics: The failure this answers for is the group emptying out. A group initializes fine as long as one child survives, so this is reached only once every child has been rejected for its type or dropped under its own policy. A child set to Fail never gets here either: it replaces the group's stack with a constant, which counts as a working group.

hints.text: A child of a kind the consumer does not accept is dropped from the group at execution, with a log line, and the group carries on with whatever is left. A Vtx filter inside a group wired to a plain point pin is the usual case. The group's answer changes with it: an Or group that loses a child gets narrower, an And group gets looser.

One child failing to initialize, with the `Initialization Failure Policy` on that child's own node set to Fail, replaces the group's whole stack with a constant. The group then answers the same way for every element whatever its Mode is, false unless Invert is on, and an Or group loses the children that would have passed along with it. The rest of the consumer's pin is untouched, which is what separates this from a loose filter set to Fail.

A group is offered to a dataset-level consumer only while every child of it can judge a dataset as a whole. **Uber Branch** and **Break** skip a group that cannot, with a warning, and a group that was the only thing on the pin leaves an empty stack, which passes everything. **Uber Filter (Data)** takes the group either way and falls back to testing elements and counting how many passed.

UPCGExFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Abstract
UPCGExFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Every filter node except **Filter Group** inherits this base, and this page carries the settings they all share: the `Priority` that orders a stack before it runs, and the `Warnings and Errors` policies deciding what a filter does when it cannot do its job. **Filter Group** declares its own copies instead of inheriting them, and the policies mean there exactly what they mean here; only `Priority` resolves by a different rule. Each filter page describes the condition that filter holds; what these mean is stated once here and holds across the family. The same header defines the Data Filter base, abstract parent of the nodes that judge a whole dataset instead of one point, which at this level differs only in the pin it outputs on.
UPCGExFilterProviderSettings.situation: Reading any filter page and needing to know what its `Priority`, `Initialization Failure Policy` or `Missing Data Policy` does, since those three are the same on every filter node.

mechanism.text: A filter node produces one factory on its output pin, and the node it is wired into runs that factory once per element and decides the consequence. Several factories on one pin form a stack sorted by `Priority`, evaluated as AND, stopping at the first failure. A point filter binds to whichever dataset its consumer pin is about, so one factory tests points, Vtx or edges depending on where it lands; a Data Filter resolves once for the whole dataset and hands every element of it that single verdict. Both policies on this page are settled before any element is tested, at different moments: `Missing Data Policy` when the filter node itself runs, `Initialization Failure Policy` when a consumer builds its stack.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The factory the node produces, one per node, carrying the condition and everything on this page. Its data type is Filter (Point), which every filter pin accepts, Vtx and Edge pins included.

outputs.label: Data Filter
outputs.note: What the Data Filter nodes output in place of the pin above. Its data type is Filter (Data), accepted on every filter pin the same way, and the verdict it carries is one per dataset rather than one per element.
outputs.condition: the Data Filter nodes

Priority.semantics: Factories arriving on one pin are sorted by this value before evaluation, lowest first, and the order the wires were drawn in is discarded. Every filter ships at 0 and the sort is not stable, so among equal priorities the order is unspecified; giving a cheap test a lower value than an expensive one is how the cheap test gets to reject first. **Filter Group** declares its own version of this setting, which resolves to the highest value among the group and the filters wired into it, so a group holding one late-sorting filter is itself sorted that late. The setting lives under the node's advanced properties, and a non-zero value shows in the node subtitle as `[N]`.

InitializationFailurePolicy.tooltip: How to handle failed attribute initialization. Usually, the reason is missing attributes, but can also be unsupported filter type.
InitializationFailurePolicy.semantics: This one fires on the consumer's side, when it builds its stack against real data and this filter cannot bind what it needs. What Error logs there is a warning, not an error, and the rest of the stack runs on without this filter. Pass adds a single always-true filter to the pin however many filters failed, which changes nothing in an AND stack unless the pin would otherwise be left with none. Fail replaces the whole pin, this filter and every other one on it, with one always-false, so one filter set to Fail decides the outcome for every filter beside it. A consumer that judges whole datasets takes none of those routes: it keeps the filter on the pin and lets each dataset answer for itself, Pass passing that dataset and Error or Fail failing it.
InitializationFailurePolicy.trap: Left at Error, a filter that cannot bind is removed and the node carries on. If it was the only filter on its pin, the pin is left with an empty stack, and an empty stack passes every element. The symptom is not that nothing came through, it is that nothing was filtered. Set this to Fail wherever a silent pass would be worse than an empty result.

MissingDataPolicy.tooltip: How to handle missing data. This only applies to filters that rely on local data pins to output meaningful results.
MissingDataPolicy.semantics: This one fires on the filter node's own execution, before any consumer sees the factory. Error cancels the node and reports the missing input, which `Quiet Missing Input Error` in this same category suppresses; the node then produces no factory at all, and the consumer's pin behaves as if nothing were wired to it. Pass and Fail keep the node producing, and what it produces is a **Filter : Constant** set to that verdict, carrying this node's `Priority` in place of the condition that was configured. Left at Fail, a distance filter with nothing to measure against rejects every point instead of waving them all through.

UPCGExFilterVtxSettings.name: Cluster : Filter Vtx
UPCGExFilterVtxSettings.purpose: Removes Vtx from a cluster by a condition you author. A filter set goes into **Vtx Filters**, every Vtx that fails leaves, and the edges that met it can be taken out with it. **Cluster : Refine** is the node that cuts edges by a rule; this is the one that judges the Vtx themselves, and it offers the same three shapes for the answer: a rebuilt cluster, the Vtx split into two plain point datasets, or the verdict recorded on the cluster it arrived as.
UPCGExFilterVtxSettings.situation: A cluster was generated across a whole site, and everything outside a volume, below a slope, or missing an attribute has to come out of it.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx is tested once against the **Vtx Filters** set, and `Invert` decides which side of that verdict survives. A Vtx that fails is gone; whether the edges at it go with it is `Node Invalidate Edges`. A Vtx that passed and was left holding no edge then fails as well, which is the one way this node removes something you did not name. `Mode` decides what the verdict becomes, and only Clusters mode rebuilds: Points hands the two groups back as plain points, and Attribute hands the cluster back untouched with the answer written on it.

off_label.claim: Points mode strips the cluster role tags and both cluster attributes off everything it emits, so a filter set that everything passes turns this into a way of getting an ordinary point dataset out of a Vtx dataset, with `Split Outputs By Connectivity` off to keep it as one.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExClusters::Helpers::CleanupVtxData runs on every Points-mode output, and the all-pass branch emits a single duplicated dataset onto Inside.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx dataset, and the thing this node judges.

inputs.label: Edges

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: The condition each Vtx is judged by. The node cancels when the pin is empty. It accepts Vtx filters, point filters, filter groups and collection filters; an **Edge Filter :** node is refused at the pin.

inputs.label: Edge Filters

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The surviving Vtx as a rebuilt cluster half in Clusters mode. In Attribute mode it is the input carried through with the result attribute added.
outputs.condition: Clusters and Attribute modes

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The edges among the survivors, re-split by connected component in Clusters mode, so one cluster in can come out as several. In Attribute mode the input comes through untouched.
outputs.condition: Clusters and Attribute modes

outputs.label: Inside
outputs.note: The Vtx that passed, as plain points with the cluster role tags and both cluster attributes stripped off.
outputs.condition: Points mode

outputs.label: Outside
outputs.note: The Vtx that failed, in the same stripped shape.
outputs.condition: Points mode

Mode.semantics: **Clusters** rebuilds from the survivors: the edges among them are re-split by connected component, and a Vtx that survived on its own merits but ended up with nothing attached is dropped by the rebuild anyway. **Points** replaces the Vtx and Edges outputs with **Inside** and **Outside** and emits no Edges data at all, so what comes out is point data rather than half a cluster. **Attribute** carries the cluster through unchanged and records the verdict per Vtx instead, and it is the one mode where `Steal Data` is permitted, which forwards the input in place rather than copying it.
Mode.trap: `Node Invalidate Edges` is on screen in all three modes and changes the answer in two of them. In Clusters mode the rebuild already drops every edge whose Vtx is gone and then culls whatever that left bare, so the toggle makes no difference to what comes out.

ResultOutputVtx.semantics: What gets recorded is the Vtx's final state, after the no-edges-left check, so a Vtx that passed its own condition can still be written down as a failure. The cluster comes out structurally intact: every Vtx and edge is reset to passing once the value is written, and nothing is removed in this mode. The attribute name is checked before the node runs, and a name the metadata cannot take cancels the node with an error rather than yielding an unnamed attribute.
ResultOutputVtx.trap: The block's own `Enabled` flag governs whether anything is written. The panel keeps that flag hidden here, but it is overridable, and cleared it leaves the node forwarding the cluster and writing nothing, which reads downstream as a filter that matched everything.

bNodeInvalidateEdges.tooltip: If enabled, invalidating a node invalidate connected edges.
bNodeInvalidateEdges.semantics: This is what makes a removal spread. With it on, the edges at a failed Vtx are taken out too, so a neighbour left holding nothing else fails the no-edges-left check and comes out with the failures. With it off, that neighbour keeps its own verdict and only the Vtx you filtered leaves.
bNodeInvalidateEdges.trap: The spread is one step deep. The check runs once, over the edges the failed Vtx gave up, so a leaf hanging off a Vtx that was itself stranded keeps its edge and keeps its pass. In Clusters mode the rebuild covers one further step by culling whatever it left edgeless; in Points and Attribute modes nothing does, and running the node a second time is what walks the next step.

bInvert.semantics: Inverts the Vtx verdict alone. The edge filters carry their own toggle and are untouched by it, and in Points mode the failures still leave on **Outside**; moving them to **Inside** is what `Swap` does.

bInvertEdgeFilters.semantics: Rejected edges are taken out of the working cluster, so in Clusters mode they are absent from the rebuilt Edges. Their other effect lands on the Vtx: one that passed its own condition and is left holding no accepted edge fails the no-edges-left check and comes out with the failures. That is how an edge condition prunes Vtx here.

bSplitOutputsByConnectivity.tooltip: If enabled, inside/outside groups will be partitioned by initial edge connectivity.
bSplitOutputsByConnectivity.semantics: On, each cluster gets its own pair of outputs, so a Vtx dataset paired with four Edges datasets yields up to four datasets on each pin. Off, the whole Vtx dataset is split once and each pin carries one dataset. Either way an empty group is not emitted, so a cluster where everything passed contributes nothing to **Outside**.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: Clusters mode only, and the last thing that can drop a result. Remove Small Clusters and Remove Big Clusters are measured per connected component after the re-split, so a condition that broke one cluster into fragments can have those fragments discarded here rather than by the condition.

hints.text: The two filter pins take different families and refuse each other's. **Vtx Filters** takes Vtx filters, **Edge Filters** takes edge filters, and both take point filters and filter groups. A point filter binds to whichever dataset the pin is about, so the same **Filter : Compare (Numeric)** reads its attribute on a Vtx on one pin and on an edge point on the other, and the attribute has to exist there.

The no-edges-left check is not optional. A Vtx that passed its condition but had every one of its edges taken out, whether by a failed neighbour or by the edge filters, has nothing left to belong to and comes out with the failures regardless of its own verdict.

UPCGExFindAllCellsBoundedSettings.name: Pathfinding : Find All Cells (Bounded)
UPCGExFindAllCellsBoundedSettings.purpose: **Pathfinding : Find All Cells** with the result sorted by how each cell sits against a box. The bound sorts, it does not cut: a cell straddling the edge of the box comes out whole on the touching route, and the cells that fall outside are available too. Sorting them here saves testing for it downstream, which is the usual reason the ones on the rim of a working area need separate treatment. **Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)** is the seeded version of the same sort.
UPCGExFindAllCellsBoundedSettings.situation: A decomposition running past the edge of the area being built, where the cells that hang over it have to be told apart from the ones fully inside.

mechanism.text: The same complete decomposition **Pathfinding : Find All Cells** produces, with one step added after it. Every cell that survived the constraints is compared against the bounds and sorted into one of three: inside when its centre lies within them, touching when its centre is outside but the cell still reaches in, and outside when it does not reach them at all. `Triage Flags` says which of the three are wanted, and the rest are dropped rather than routed anywhere. `Output Mode` then decides whether the survivors leave on a pin each or share one pin carrying a tag. No cell is ever cut by the bounds: each one leaves whole or not at all.

off_label.claim: Enable outside alone and the node inverts into a way of taking everything a box does not cover, with the box supplied as live data rather than as numbers on the panel. Anything with bounds serves: a volume, a mesh, or the output of an earlier branch of the graph.
off_label.grounded_in: TriageFlags is read per category in the classification loop, and the Bounds pin takes any UPCGSpatialData, from which only GetBounds is used.

pins.dynamic: The output pin set is computed from `Output Mode` and the two `Artifacts` switches, so it changes as the node is configured. In Separate mode all six category pins exist whatever `Triage Flags` says, and the ones for categories that are switched off are marked advanced rather than removed.

OutputMode.semantics: `Separate Pins` gives each category its own pin, which is the shape to wire when the three go different ways. `Combined` collapses them back onto the ordinary **Paths** and **CellBounds** pins and puts the answer in a tag instead, `CellTriage:Inside`, `CellTriage:Touching` or `CellTriage:Outside`, which is what a tag-driven downstream setup wants.

TriageFlags.semantics: A category left off is discarded, not sent somewhere else, so this is where cells leave the graph. It ships with inside and touching on and outside off, which means the cells beyond the box vanish by default and nothing says so.
TriageFlags.trap: Switching outside on changes the work as well as the result. While it is off the node can skip building any cell whose extent misses the box; with it on every face in the cluster is built before anything is sorted.

Constraints.semantics: Applied before the sort, so a cell that failed a size or shape limit never reaches a category at all. `Omit Wrapping Bounds` decides whether the cluster's outer boundary is looked for; `Keep If Sole` puts it back when nothing else survived, and it is then sorted like any other cell.

Artifacts.tooltip: Cell output settings (output mode, attributes, OBB settings)
Artifacts.semantics: The two switches inside decide which family of pins exists, so turning `Output Cell Bounds` on in `Separate Pins` adds three more pins rather than changing what the existing three carry.

HoleGrowth.tooltip: Hole growth settings. Expands hole exclusion to adjacent cells.
HoleGrowth.semantics: `Growth` reaches out from a hole point, removing the cells around the one it landed in, counted in cells, and it does nothing without a **Holes** dataset.
HoleGrowth.trap: `Merge Adjacent Cells` on this node is not the setting its own description promises. There are no seeds here, and it is not gated on `Growth`: turning it on fuses every surviving cell into one path per connected run of them, before the sort, so what gets classified is the fused outlines rather than the original cells.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: The decomposition happens in this plane, and the sort does not: centres and extents are compared against the bounds in world space. A cluster projected along one axis is still classified by where its cells sit in three dimensions.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Read by nothing on this node. Nothing here searches for a nearest Vtx or edge, so there is no search for it to switch.

hints.text: The **Bounds** pin uses one box and nothing else: the first dataset on the pin, reduced to its overall axis-aligned extent. A rotated volume is tested as the upright box containing it, a sphere as the cube around it, and a second dataset wired alongside the first is ignored. Combine several regions into one dataset upstream, or run the node once per region.

UPCGExFindAllCellsSettings.name: Pathfinding : Find All Cells
UPCGExFindAllCellsSettings.purpose: The whole decomposition at once: every region the cluster's edges enclose, without anything having to point at them. That makes it the node for treating a network as a set of tiles rather than picking out particular rooms, which is what **Pathfinding : Find Cells** is for. A **Holes** input subtracts from the result, dropping any cell one of those points falls inside, so regions something else already occupies come out of the set before it is handed on.
UPCGExFindAllCellsSettings.situation: A planar cluster whose faces are the point of it, and every one of them is wanted.

mechanism.text: The cluster is flattened onto the projection plane and every closed loop of edges in it is traced, once each. The constraints decide which of those survive, a wired **Holes** dataset then removes any surviving cell that one of its points falls inside, and what remains is the cluster's complete decomposition minus those removals. Nothing here selects regions, so the number of cells out follows the cluster's own structure rather than anything supplied alongside it. What each cell becomes, a closed path or a point carrying its box, is the `Artifacts` block's decision.

off_label.claim: Turn `Merge Adjacent Cells` on with no **Holes** wired and the node stops decomposing and starts outlining: every cell that survived the constraints is fused into one path per connected run of them. A constraint that removes cells in the middle is then what decides where the outlines break apart.
off_label.grounded_in: The MergeAdjacentCells call in PCGExFindAllCells::FProcessor::Process is gated on bMergeAdjacentCells alone, with no test on hole presence or growth depth.

inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx half.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges half. One cluster is processed per Edges dataset.

inputs.label: Holes
inputs.note: One dataset. Any cell containing one of these points is removed from the result.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One closed path per surviving cell. Staged inactive when Output Paths is off or nothing survived.
outputs.condition: when Output Paths is on

outputs.label: CellBounds
outputs.note: One dataset per cluster, holding one point per surviving cell with that cell's oriented box. Staged inactive when Output Cell Bounds is off or nothing survived.

Constraints.semantics: `Omit Wrapping Bounds` decides whether the cluster's outer boundary is looked for at all, not merely whether it is kept, so with it off the boundary comes out as one more cell alongside the interior ones. `Keep If Sole` matters on a cluster with no interior faces, where it is the difference between one boundary path and nothing.

Artifacts.tooltip: Cell output settings (output mode, attributes, OBB settings)
Artifacts.semantics: The point-per-cell output is one dataset per cluster holding the whole decomposition, which is the compact way to read a cluster's faces: one row per region, carrying its area and compactness, with no path to walk.

HoleGrowth.tooltip: Hole growth settings. Expands hole exclusion to adjacent cells.
HoleGrowth.semantics: `Growth` reaches out from a hole rather than from a seed: it removes the cells around the one the hole point landed in, counted in cells, and the depth can differ per hole point when it is read from an attribute. It does nothing without a **Holes** dataset, since there is no hole to grow from.
HoleGrowth.trap: `Merge Adjacent Cells` on this node is not the setting its own description promises. There are no seeds here, and it is not gated on `Growth`: turning it on fuses every surviving cell into one path per connected run of them, which on an ordinary decomposition means the entire output collapses to a single outline.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Every decision here happens in this plane: which loops count as cells, which way an output path winds, and what area and compactness measure.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Read by nothing on this node. Nothing here searches for a nearest Vtx or edge, so there is no search for it to switch.

hints.text: Hole removal tests the hole point against the flattened cell, so a hole point sitting well above or below the cluster still removes the cell it lands over. Bring the hole points into the same plane as the cluster, or expect regions to disappear from directly underneath geometry that was never meant to reach them.

UPCGExFindClusterHullSettings.name: Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull
UPCGExFindClusterHullSettings.purpose: The outer boundary of a cluster rather than anything enclosed inside it. Where the Find Cells nodes hand back interior regions, this one traces the loop that wraps everything and stops, one path per cluster. The line it follows is the cluster's own outermost run of edges, so every concavity in the shape is traced rather than bridged, and a boundary running out along a dead end doubles back along it.
UPCGExFindClusterHullSettings.situation: The silhouette of a cluster is wanted as a path, to inset, offset, or test something against.

mechanism.text: The cluster is flattened onto the projection plane, its faces are traced, and the one enclosing all the others is taken as the hull. That single loop becomes a closed path of the Vtx it runs through, and a point carrying its oriented box, depending on which of the `Artifacts` switches are on. One cluster gives one hull, so a Vtx dataset paired with several Edges datasets gives one path per component. A cluster the boundary could not be traced in emits nothing and logs a warning.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx half.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges half. One hull is produced per Edges dataset.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One closed path per cluster. Staged inactive when Output Paths is off or no hull was found.
outputs.condition: when Output Paths is on

outputs.label: CellBounds

outputs.condition: when Output Cell Bounds is on

Constraints.semantics: `Duplicate Leaf points` is the one field in the block that this node reads. The hull is traced with the rest of the block replaced by defaults, so the size, count, perimeter, compactness and shape limits never run, `Keep Cells With Leaves` is always on, and a boundary that runs out along a dead end and back always comes back with that spike in it.
Constraints.trap: `Output Winding` is among the fields replaced, so the hull always comes back wound the same way whatever it is set to. **Reverse Order** downstream is what turns a finished path round.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Which loop counts as the outermost one is decided in this plane, so a cluster that folds over itself when flattened can hand back a boundary that makes no sense in 3D. Aiming the projection along the cluster's own dominant axis is what keeps the answer readable.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Read by nothing on this node. There are no seeds and nothing searches for a nearest Vtx or edge, so there is no search for it to switch.

bQuietFailedToFindHullWarning.display: Quiet Failed To Find Hull Warning
bQuietFailedToFindHullWarning.tooltip: Suppress warning when a hull could not be found for a cluster.
bQuietFailedToFindHullWarning.semantics: The warning it silences fires per cluster, and a cluster that raised it contributed nothing to either output. Silencing it on a batch where some clusters legitimately have no traceable boundary also silences it for the ones that broke.

hints.text: One hull per cluster means one per Edges dataset, and a generator normally emits one Edges dataset per connected component. A scatter that came back as five islands therefore produces five hulls from a single wire, with no grouping step in between.

UPCGExFindClustersDataSettings.name: Find Clusters
UPCGExFindClustersDataSettings.purpose: Sorts a mixed pile of datasets into cluster pairs and hands each half out on its own pin. Cluster nodes want Vtx and Edges on two pins, so anything that carried both halves down one wire, a named reroute, a loop body, a data asset, arrives needing to be separated again. Nothing is copied: the datasets are forwarded, so the sorting costs the read and no more.
UPCGExFindClustersDataSettings.situation: Both halves of a cluster travelled through one reroute, or a loop is walking Edges datasets and each pass needs the Vtx that goes with it.

mechanism.text: Every dataset arriving on **In** is triaged by its cluster tags. Those that pair up leave on **Vtx** and **Edges**; everything else leaves on **Discarded**, so nothing is silently swallowed. Several Edges datasets sharing one Vtx dataset is the normal shape and all of them come out, one per connected component. `Search Mode` decides how much of the input is considered: the whole pile, or only the pair one named dataset belongs to. The datasets are forwarded rather than duplicated, so what comes out is the same data that went in.

off_label.claim: With nothing paired at all the node errors and produces nothing, and with a partly broken pile it warns per problem while still emitting what survived. Wiring it in front of a cluster node purely to read those warnings turns it into a triage report on data of unknown provenance.
off_label.grounded_in: The element calls FDataLibrary::PrintLogs on success as well as failure, so partial problems surface even when other pairs built fine.

outputs.label: Edges

outputs.label: Discarded
outputs.note: Everything that did not pair: data carrying neither role tag, a Vtx set with no Edges, an Edges set with no Vtx, and the loser of a pair-id collision. The pin is marked advanced, so it sits collapsed until the node is expanded.

SearchMode.semantics: All triages the whole of **In** and emits every pair it finds. The two directed modes add a second required input pin that takes exactly one dataset and return only that dataset's partner; everything else on **In** goes to **Discarded**. That second pin is checked before anything runs, so an Edges dataset on the Vtx search pin, or one carrying no pair tag, stops the node with an error rather than falling back to All.
SearchMode.trap: In the directed modes a search key that is well formed but matches nothing logs an error and the node produces no output at all, not even on **Discarded**.

bSkipTrivialWarnings.tooltip: Warning about inputs mismatch and triage
bSkipTrivialWarnings.semantics: Trivial means the input was never cluster data: it carries neither role tag, or it carries one whose matching attribute is missing, or it is tagged both roles at once. Silence them when **In** is deliberately carrying other data alongside the clusters, which is the usual reason to reach for this node in the first place.

bSkipImportantWarnings.tooltip: Warning that you'll get anyway if you try these inputs in a cluster node
bSkipImportantWarnings.semantics: The three that can fire here all name real damage: edges with no Vtx, Vtx with no edges, and two Vtx datasets sharing one pair id where only one is kept. They fire whether or not anything else went wrong, so a pile that sorted almost cleanly still reports its stragglers.

hints.text: Two Vtx datasets carrying the same pair id are not both kept. The first to be read claims the id, the second is discarded, and the Edges that named that id go to the survivor. Give clusters that descend from one source their own ids before they meet, with **Cluster : Make Unique**.

UPCGExFindContoursBoundedSettings.name: Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)
UPCGExFindContoursBoundedSettings.purpose: **Pathfinding : Find Cells** with the cells the seeds claimed sorted by how each one sits against a box. The bound sorts rather than cuts, so a claimed cell that hangs over the edge arrives whole on the touching route instead of being trimmed to fit. Seeds still decide which regions are taken at all, which is the difference from **Pathfinding : Find All Cells (Bounded)**, where every region in the cluster is sorted.
UPCGExFindContoursBoundedSettings.situation: Seeded regions near the edge of a working area, where the ones that spill past it have to be handled differently from the ones that do not.

mechanism.text: The cluster is flattened, its cells are traced, and the constraints thin them, exactly as **Pathfinding : Find Cells** does. A cell is then kept when a seed's projected position falls inside it, with `Seed Ownership` settling contested cells and `Seed Growth` extending a claim to neighbouring cells. Each kept cell is then sorted against the bounds: inside when its centre lies within them, touching when its centre is outside but the cell still reaches in, outside when it does not reach them at all. `Triage Flags` says which of the three are wanted and the rest are dropped, and `Output Mode` decides whether they leave on a pin each or share one pin carrying a tag. No cell is cut by the bounds.

pins.dynamic: The output pin set is computed from `Output Mode`, the two `Artifacts` switches and `Output Filtered Seeds`, so it changes as the node is configured. In Separate mode all six category pins exist whatever `Triage Flags` says, and the ones for categories that are switched off are marked advanced rather than removed.

OutputMode.semantics: `Separate Pins` gives each category its own pin, which is the shape to wire when the three go different ways. `Combined` collapses them back onto the ordinary **Paths** and **CellBounds** pins and puts the answer in a tag instead, `CellTriage:Inside`, `CellTriage:Touching` or `CellTriage:Outside`.

TriageFlags.semantics: A category left off is discarded rather than routed elsewhere, and the node ships with inside and touching on and outside off, so cells beyond the box vanish by default.
TriageFlags.trap: This is also the one place where the bound restricts rather than sorts. While outside is off, a cell whose extent misses the box is never built, so a seed sitting in one claims nothing and is reported on **SeedGenFailed** as though it had landed on empty space.

SeedPicking.tooltip: Drive how a seed selects a node.
SeedPicking.semantics: `Max Distance` is the only field this node reads. It caps how far a seed may sit off a cell's own plane before that cell will claim it, and how far outside the cluster a seed may sit and still claim the outer boundary in the case where no interior cell was claimed. At the default of -1 neither cap applies.
SeedPicking.trap: `Picking Method` is not consulted here. A seed reaches a cell by falling inside it once both are flattened, never by being nearest a Vtx or an edge.

SeedOwnership.tooltip: How to determine seed ownership when multiple seeds compete for a cell.
SeedOwnership.semantics: A cell goes to one seed, so seeds sharing a cell do not each come away with a copy of it, and a seed that lost every cell it fell inside is reported on **SeedGenFailed**.
SeedOwnership.trap: `Closest (Projected)` measures in world XY rather than in the projection plane the cells were found in, so it agrees with the containment test only while `Projection` is left on its default up vector.

SortDirection.tooltip: Sort direction when using Best Candidate ownership.

Constraints.semantics: Applied before seeds are looked at and well before the sort, so a cell that failed a size or shape limit never gets claimed and never reaches a category. `Omit Wrapping Bounds` takes the cluster's outer boundary out of the running; `Keep If Sole` puts it back when nothing else survived, and it is then claimed and sorted like any other cell.

Artifacts.tooltip: Cell output settings (output mode, attributes, OBB settings)
Artifacts.semantics: The two switches inside decide which family of pins exists, so turning `Output Cell Bounds` on in `Separate Pins` adds three more pins rather than changing what the existing three carry.
Artifacts.trap: Seed reporting is written while a cell's path is being built, so with `Output Paths` off every seed lands on **SeedGenFailed** and `Seed Mutations` never runs, even on a run that claimed its cells and filled the point-per-cell outputs.

SeedGrowth.tooltip: Seed growth settings. Expands seed selection to adjacent cells.
SeedGrowth.semantics: Growth counts cells rather than distance: 1 adds the cells sharing a border with the claimed one, 2 adds theirs, and the depth can differ per seed when read from an attribute. `Merge Adjacent Cells` dissolves the shared borders inside one seed's claim, per seed, and the fused outline is what gets sorted afterwards rather than the cells it came from.

PickCountAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for pick count (how many times a cell was selected by seeds/growth)
PickCountAttributeName.semantics: Counted during growth and never written out. The counts exist on each cell while the node runs, and no attribute is created from them under any configuration.
PickCountAttributeName.trap: `Write Expansion Attributes` and both names under it are inert. Nothing downstream will see `PCGEx/PickCount` or `PCGEx/Depth`.

DepthAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for depth (minimum depth at which cell was picked, 0 = direct seed)
DepthAttributeName.semantics: Inert, for the same reason as `Pick Count`.

bOutputFilteredSeeds.tooltip: Output a filtered set of points containing only seeds that generated a valid path
bOutputFilteredSeeds.semantics: The two pins arrive together and between them carry every seed point. Success means this seed owned at least one cell whose path was built, which a category being switched off in `Triage Flags` can take away from it.

SeedMutations.semantics: Runs on the point heading to **SeedGenSuccess** once that seed's cell has been built, which is what lets it move the point onto the cell and size it to the cell's own bounds. Points heading to **SeedGenFailed** arrive as they came in.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: The cells and the claiming happen in this plane, and the sort does not: centres and extents are compared against the bounds in world space.

SeedAttributesToPathTags.tooltip: Copy seed point attributes as tags on output paths.

SeedForwarding.tooltip: Which Seed attributes to forward on paths.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Read by nothing on this node. Seeds are matched by containment rather than by proximity, so there is no closest-element search for it to switch.

hints.text: The **Bounds** pin uses one box and nothing else: the first dataset on the pin, reduced to its overall axis-aligned extent. A rotated volume is tested as the upright box containing it, a sphere as the cube around it, and a second dataset wired alongside the first is ignored.

UPCGExFindContoursSettings.name: Pathfinding : Find Cells
UPCGExFindContoursSettings.purpose: Takes the cell around each seed you hand it, and nothing else. Every closed region a cluster's edges enclose is found first, and a seed's projected position is what picks one out, so this is the node for naming the regions you want by dropping points in them. **Pathfinding : Find All Cells** is the exhaustive counterpart, taking every region whether anything points at it or not, and **Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)** is this same seeded pick with a spatial classification added on top.
UPCGExFindContoursSettings.situation: A cluster whose interior regions matter one at a time, and points already sitting in the ones that matter.

mechanism.text: The cluster is flattened onto the projection plane, and every closed loop of edges in it becomes a candidate cell. The constraints decide which of those survive, then a survivor is kept when at least one seed's projected position falls inside it, with `Seed Ownership` settling a cell that several fall into. A seed landing in no surviving cell claims nothing, and a cell no seed landed in is dropped, so at most one cell comes out per seed until `Seed Growth` lets a seed claim its cell's neighbours as well. What each owned cell then becomes, a closed path or a point carrying its box, is the `Artifacts` block's decision.

off_label.claim: Wire a single seed far outside the cluster, turn `Omit Wrapping Bounds` on and leave `Keep If Sole` on, and the node emits the cluster's outer boundary and nothing else, which is **Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull** with the constraint block still applying and a seed to forward attributes from.
off_label.grounded_in: HandleWrapperOnlyCase runs when no interior cell was claimed, admits seeds that fall in no cell at all, and gates them on SeedPicking.WithinDistanceSquared against the nearest edge.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx half.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges half. One cluster is processed per Edges dataset.

inputs.label: Seeds
inputs.note: One dataset, and the points in it are what pick the cells. Only the first dataset on the pin is read.

inputs.label: SortRules
inputs.note: Sorting rules ranking the seeds against each other.
inputs.condition: when Seed Ownership is Best Candidate, and advanced otherwise

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One closed path per owned cell.
outputs.condition: when Output Paths is on, and advanced otherwise

outputs.label: CellBounds
outputs.note: One dataset per cluster, one point per owned cell carrying that cell's oriented box.
outputs.condition: when Output Cell Bounds is on, and advanced otherwise

outputs.label: SeedGenSuccess
outputs.note: The seed points that ended up owning a cell, after Seed Mutations.
outputs.condition: when Output Filtered Seeds is on

outputs.label: SeedGenFailed
outputs.note: Every other seed point, unchanged.
outputs.condition: when Output Filtered Seeds is on

SeedPicking.tooltip: Drive how a seed selects a node.
SeedPicking.semantics: `Max Distance` is the only field this node reads. It caps how far a seed may sit off a cell's own plane before that cell will claim it, and it caps how far outside the cluster a seed may sit and still claim the outer boundary in the case where no interior cell was claimed at all. At the default of -1 neither cap applies.
SeedPicking.trap: `Picking Method` is not consulted here. A seed reaches a cell by falling inside it once both are flattened, never by being nearest a Vtx or an edge, so changing the method changes nothing.

SeedOwnership.tooltip: How to determine seed ownership when multiple seeds compete for a cell.
SeedOwnership.semantics: A cell goes to one seed, so seeds sharing a cell do not each come away with a copy of it. The seeds that lost claim nothing from it, and a seed that lost every cell it fell inside is reported on **SeedGenFailed** next to the seeds that landed nowhere.
SeedOwnership.trap: `Closest (Projected)` measures in world XY rather than in the projection plane the cells were found in. It matches `Closest` projected flat only while `Projection` is left on its default up vector; tilt that vector or switch to a per-face projection and the two stop agreeing.

SortDirection.tooltip: Sort direction when using Best Candidate ownership.

Constraints.semantics: Applied before any seed is looked at, so a cell that fails a size or shape limit is gone by the time claiming happens and the seed inside it is reported as a failure rather than falling through to the next cell out. `Omit Wrapping Bounds` takes the cluster's outer boundary out of the running by default; `Keep If Sole` puts it back only when nothing else survived, and a seed then has to be outside every cell and within `Max Distance` of an edge to claim it.

Artifacts.tooltip: Cell output settings (output mode, attributes, OBB settings)
Artifacts.semantics: The two output switches inside are independent, and cells reach them already owned, so the point-per-cell output carries one point per seed that won something rather than one per cell in the cluster.
Artifacts.trap: Seed reporting is written while a cell's path is being built, so with `Output Paths` off every seed lands on **SeedGenFailed** and `Seed Mutations` never runs, even on a run that found its cells and filled the point-per-cell output.

SeedGrowth.tooltip: Seed growth settings. Expands seed selection to adjacent cells.
SeedGrowth.semantics: Growth counts cells rather than distance: 1 adds the cells sharing a border with the claimed one, 2 adds theirs, and the depth can differ per seed when it is read from an attribute. `Merge Adjacent Cells` dissolves the shared borders inside one seed's claim, per seed, so two seeds that grew into each other still come back as two paths.

PickCountAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for pick count (how many times a cell was selected by seeds/growth)
PickCountAttributeName.semantics: Counted during growth and never written out. The counts exist on each cell while the node runs, and no attribute is created from them under any configuration.
PickCountAttributeName.trap: `Write Expansion Attributes` and both names under it are inert. Nothing downstream will see `PCGEx/PickCount` or `PCGEx/Depth`.

DepthAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for depth (minimum depth at which cell was picked, 0 = direct seed)
DepthAttributeName.semantics: Inert, for the same reason as `Pick Count`.

bOutputFilteredSeeds.tooltip: Output a filtered set of points containing only seeds that generated a valid path
bOutputFilteredSeeds.semantics: The two pins arrive together and between them carry every seed point, so the pair partitions the input rather than trimming it. Success means this seed ended up owning at least one cell whose path was built.

SeedMutations.semantics: Runs on the point heading to **SeedGenSuccess** once that seed's cell has been built, which is what lets it move the point onto the cell and size it to the cell's own bounds. Points heading to **SeedGenFailed** arrive as they came in.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Every decision here happens in this plane: which loops count as cells, which cell a seed is inside, which way an output path winds, and what area and compactness measure.

SeedAttributesToPathTags.tooltip: Copy seed point attributes as tags on output paths.

SeedForwarding.tooltip: Which Seed attributes to forward on paths.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Is forwarding enabled.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Read by nothing on this node. Seeds are matched by containment rather than by proximity, so there is no closest-element search for it to switch.

hints.text: A cluster where no cell was claimed emits nothing for that cluster, and a run where no cluster claimed anything emits nothing at all. There is no warning for either, so **SeedGenFailed** is the way to tell a bad seed placement from a cluster that produced no cells to begin with.

UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsClustersSettings.name: Cluster : Find point on Bounds
UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsClustersSettings.purpose: Reduces each cluster to a single point: the Vtx, or the point on an edge, nearest a spot you choose on that cluster's own bounding box. It is how you get one representative per cluster placed consistently, at the same corner or face of every one of them, rather than at an average that lands wherever the vertices happen to be dense.
UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsClustersSettings.situation: Every cluster in a batch needs one marker, and it has to sit on the same side of each of them.

mechanism.text: A target spot is built inside each cluster's bounding box from `UVW`, whose components run from minus one at the low face through zero at the centre to one at the high face. The nearest Vtx, or the nearest point along an edge, is found, the source point it belongs to is copied out, and `Offset` pushes that copy away from the bounds centre. One point comes out per cluster, and `Output Mode` decides whether they arrive together in one dataset or one dataset at a time.

off_label.claim: With `UVW` at zero on all three axes the target spot is the bounds centre, so the node returns the cluster element nearest its own middle. That is a cheap stand-in for a centroid when what you need is a real Vtx rather than a computed position.
off_label.grounded_in: The search position is Bounds.GetCenter() + Bounds.GetExtent() * UVW, so a zero UVW reduces to the centre with the same nearest-element search.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx dataset. Its positions define each cluster's bounds, and in Closest vtx mode the result is copied from here.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges datasets, one per cluster. In Closest edge mode the result is copied from here.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The picked points. One dataset holding one point per cluster in Merged Points mode, or one single-point dataset per cluster in Per-point dataset mode. There is no Edges output pin: the node emits points, not clusters.

SearchMode.tooltip: What type of proximity to look for
SearchMode.semantics: It decides what is searched and also which dataset the result is copied out of: Closest vtx copies a Vtx point, Closest edge copies an edge point. Closest edge measures to the closest point along the edge rather than to the edge point's own position, so the winner can be an edge whose two ends are both further away than some Vtx.

OutputMode.semantics: Merged Points builds one new dataset and writes one point into it per cluster, carrying that point's transform, its point properties, and whatever attributes `Carry Over Settings` admits. Per-point dataset instead reduces each source dataset to a single point in place, so the pick keeps every attribute its source carried and `Carry Over Settings` never applies.
OutputMode.trap: Per-point dataset with Closest vtx writes into the Vtx dataset, and a Vtx dataset is shared by every cluster paired with it. Several clusters on one Vtx dataset therefore produce one point between them, from whichever finished last, rather than one each. Merged Points does not have that problem, and neither does Closest edge.

AxisOrder.tooltip: Whether to use best fit plane bounds, and which axis ordering should be used.
AxisOrder.semantics: With best-fit bounds on, the box is fitted to that cluster's Vtx positions and oriented to the plane they lie closest to, and `UVW` is then read in that fitted frame rather than in world axes. The axis order decides which of the fitted directions counts as X, Y and Z, which is what makes a `UVW` written for one cluster mean the same thing on another.

UVWValue.tooltip: UVW position of the target within bounds. Attribute source is read from the @Data domain.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

UVWValue.semantics: The default source is the `@Data` domain, so a UVW read from an attribute is one value for the whole dataset rather than one per point. `Element` decides which of the two datasets it is read from.

ClusterElement.tooltip: Cluster element the UVW attribute is read from when using attribute input.

Offset.tooltip: Offset to apply to the closest point, away from the bounds center.
Offset.semantics: A distance along the direction from the cluster's bounds centre out to the picked point, so it pushes the result further outward and does not scale with the cluster. The centre it measures from is the cluster's axis-aligned bounds centre even when best-fit bounds are on.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: Merged Points mode only, where it narrows the attribute set gathered from the inputs before the merge. The set is collected across every input dataset at once, so an attribute only some of them carry still becomes a column on the merged output, defaulted on the rows whose source lacked it. The block is on screen in Per-point dataset mode and nothing reads it there.

bQuietAttributeMismatchWarning.tooltip: Suppress warnings about attribute type mismatches during merging.
bQuietAttributeMismatchWarning.semantics: The mismatch it reports is between input datasets, not between an input and the output: two of them carrying the same attribute name at different types. Whichever type is met first wins for the whole merge.

hints.text: In Merged Points mode the output is sized up front, one slot per Edges dataset, so an Edges dataset that produced no pick leaves a default point sitting in the result rather than leaving a gap. Check the output count against the cluster count when clusters are being dropped upstream.

UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsSettings.name: Find point on Bounds
UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsSettings.purpose: Finds the point in a dataset that sits nearest a chosen spot on the dataset's own bounds. Where **Points to Bounds** measures the box, this searches inside it: name a corner and the node returns the real point closest to it, so the answer is a member of the input rather than a synthesised position. One point comes back per dataset.
UPCGExFindPointOnBoundsSettings.situation: A scatter that needs a representative at a known corner or face, chosen from the points that are actually there.

mechanism.text: The dataset's bounds are measured, the normalised coordinate names a spot on them, and the point nearest that spot is the answer. `Output Mode` decides the shape of the result: one dataset holding a point per input in input order, or a separate single-point dataset per input keeping that input's own attributes. `Offset` pushes the target spot outward from the bounds centre before the search, which changes which point is nearest.

off_label.claim: Run several times with different coordinates and the results are a set of extremes for the same data, which is a cheap way to get the corner points of a cloud without a hull.
off_label.grounded_in: Each run resolves one UVW coordinate against the dataset bounds and returns the nearest member, so distinct coordinates return distinct members.

OutputMode.semantics: Decides whether the results arrive together or apart, and that choice costs something either way. `Merged` gives one dataset in input order, which is convenient to iterate but has to reconcile attributes that differed between inputs. `Per-point dataset` keeps each result with its own input's attributes intact, at the cost of one dataset per input.

AxisOrder.tooltip: Whether to use best fit plane bounds, and which axis ordering should be used.
AxisOrder.semantics: Only consulted while best-fit bounds are on, where the box is measured along the cloud's own orientation rather than the world axes. It settles which fitted axis counts as which, and that is what makes a UVW coordinate mean the same corner between runs on data whose orientation shifted.

UVWValue.tooltip: UVW position of the target within bounds. Attribute source is read from the @Data domain.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

UVWValue.semantics: Normalised across the dataset's bounds, so the same setting means the same corner whatever the data's size or position. Its attribute source is read from the data domain rather than per point, which is consistent with the node answering once per dataset.

Offset.tooltip: Offset to apply to the closest point, away from the bounds center.
Offset.semantics: Moves the target spot away from the bounds centre before the search runs. Because the answer is whichever real point is nearest, pushing the target further out tends to sharpen the choice toward the true extreme rather than changing the result to something outside the data.
