off_label.claim: Set `Index Safety` to `Ignore` and the picker becomes a cap: every seed whose row runs past the last goal answers with -1 and produces no query at all, so trimming the Goals data limits how many paths a large Seeds dataset can generate.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExMath::SanitizeIndex under EPCGExIndexSafety::Ignore returns -1 for an out-of-range index, and PCGExPathfinding::ProcessGoals skips any index below zero

IndexSafety.semantics: Measured against the last valid goal index, so it only ever acts once a seed's row runs past the end of the Goals data. `Tile` and `Yoyo` reuse goals in a repeating order, `Clamp` sends every surplus seed to the last goal, and `Ignore` drops them. The other pickers inherit this row and only **Index Attribute** consults it: **All** and **Random** produce indices that are already in range.

hints.text: The picker is an instanced dropdown on the node rather than a sub-node on a pin, so it is configured in place. Both consumers also carry an advanced **Overrides : Goal Picker** pin, an attribute set whose names are matched one to one against the selected picker's own settings, which is how a picker is driven from data.

An empty Goals dataset stops the node before any picker rule runs, with `Missing goal points.`, whichever picker is selected. A picker that answers every seed with nothing stops it a moment later with `Could not generate any seed/goal pairs.` Neither case yields an empty Paths pin: the node fails outright.

UPCGExGoalPickerAll.name: Goal Picker : All
UPCGExGoalPickerAll.purpose: Every seed routes to every goal. The picker answers each seed with the whole Goals data, so the query count is seeds multiplied by goals and the result is the full set of routes between the two datasets. It has no settings of its own.
UPCGExGoalPickerAll.situation: The routes between two sets of points are all wanted, not just one pairing of them.

mechanism.text: Asked about a seed, this picker returns every goal index in Goals order, from 0 to the last. Ten seeds against ten goals is a hundred queries, each solved separately and each producing its own path. The answer is the same for every seed, so nothing on the seed points changes what it returns.

off_label.claim: Feed a single point on the Goals pin and the picker collapses to a hub query: every seed routes to that one goal, without the row-matching that **Goal Picker : Default** would impose.
off_label.grounded_in: GetGoalIndices fills the output with 0 to GoalsNum - 1, which is the single index 0 when the Goals data holds one point

IndexSafety.semantics: Inherited from the base and never consulted here. The indices this picker returns are generated from the goal count itself, so none of them can fall out of range.

hints.text: The query count is the product of the two inputs, and every one of them is a full search. Six hundred seeds against six hundred goals is three hundred and sixty thousand searches per cluster, run once for each Edges dataset on the input.

UPCGExGoalPickerAttribute.name: Goal Picker : Index Attribute
UPCGExGoalPickerAttribute.purpose: Each seed names its own goal, by reading a row index out of an attribute it carries. One attribute gives one goal per seed; a list of attributes gives one goal per attribute per seed. This is where a pairing computed upstream, by sampling, sorting or a filter chain, is handed to pathfinding.
UPCGExGoalPickerAttribute.situation: Which goal a seed should reach was already worked out by earlier nodes and written onto the seed.

mechanism.text: The values are read from the Seeds data and broadcast to `int32`, so any numeric attribute works and a float is truncated on the way in. Each value is a row index into the Goals data, run through `Index Safety` before it becomes a query. Two attributes holding the same value on one seed produce two identical queries rather than one, since nothing compares the answers against each other.

off_label.claim: Write the same index onto every seed and the picker becomes a hub query with the hub chosen from data, which is a way to drive **Goal Picker : All**'s single-goal case from an attribute instead of from the Goals data's length.
off_label.grounded_in: GetGoalIndex reads the value per seed and applies no uniqueness rule, so a constant attribute yields the same goal for every query

GoalCount.semantics: `Single Attribute` reads `Single Selector` alone and answers one goal per seed. `Multiple Attributes` ignores that row entirely and reads the `Attribute Selectors` list instead, answering with one goal per bound selector, so the query count per seed is the length of the list rather than anything on the points.

CommaSeparatedNames.tooltip: A list of attribute names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. They will be added to the in-place array of selectors.
CommaSeparatedNames.semantics: Merged into `Attribute Selectors` rather than replacing it, and merged uniquely, so a name that is already in the list adds nothing. Being the only overridable row of the three, it is the route by which the goal attributes are chosen from data at run time.

AttributeSelectors.semantics: Order decides nothing about the search, only the order the queries are created in, which surfaces later as the order of the output paths.
AttributeSelectors.trap: A selector that names an attribute the Seeds data does not carry fails the whole node. The error reports the name held in `Single Selector`, which in this mode is usually blank, rather than the selector that actually failed, so the message points at the wrong row.

hints.text: `Index Safety` is the only picker setting that acts here, and it acts on the value the attribute holds. Against a Goals dataset of ten points, an attribute reading 12 becomes goal 2 under `Tile`, goal 9 under `Clamp`, goal 8 under `Yoyo`, and no query at all under `Ignore`.

UPCGExGoalPickerRandom.name: Goal Picker : Random
UPCGExGoalPickerRandom.purpose: Each seed draws its goals at random. One goal, a fixed number of them, or a number that is itself drawn per seed. The draw is deterministic for a given set of seed points, so a graph re-run gives the same routes as long as the seeds keep their positions and their `Seed` values.
UPCGExGoalPickerRandom.situation: Routes are wanted between two sets of points without any particular pairing, only coverage.

mechanism.text: The random stream is built from the seed point's own `Seed` property together with its row index, so the goals a seed draws follow that point and nothing else. Each pick is an independent draw across the whole Goals data, so one seed can draw the same goal twice and the resulting duplicate queries both run and both produce a path.

off_label.claim: Because the draw is keyed on the seed point's `Seed` property, running the points through any node that rewrites seeds, or writing `Seed` directly, re-rolls every pairing without touching this picker's settings.
off_label.grounded_in: GetGoalIndex and GetGoalIndices both build their stream from PCGExRandomHelpers::GetRandomStreamFromPoint(Seed.Data->GetSeed(Seed.Index), Seed.Index)

LocalSeed.semantics: Declared on the panel and never read. Nothing in the picker consults it, so changing it re-rolls nothing.
LocalSeed.trap: Reach for the seed points' own `Seed` values when a different draw is wanted. This row cannot produce one.

GoalCount.semantics: `Single` draws once and ignores `Num Goals` entirely. `Multiple Fixed` draws exactly `Num Goals` times. `Multiple Random` first draws a count between zero and `Num Goals` inclusive, then draws that many goals, so a seed can come out of it with no query at all despite `Num Goals` refusing values below 1.

NumGoalsType.tooltip: Fetch the smoothing from a local attribute.
NumGoalsType.semantics: Switching to an attribute reads the count per seed from the Seeds data, which is what lets a few seeds fan out widely while the rest draw once. Under `Multiple Random` the per-seed value is still only the upper bound of the count.

IndexSafety.semantics: Inherited from the base and never consulted here. Every draw is taken across the valid range already.

hints.text: Draws are independent, so nothing stops a seed drawing the same goal several times. Under `Multiple Fixed` with a `Num Goals` close to the size of the Goals data, expect repeats rather than a sample without replacement.

UPCGExHeuristicFeedbackProviderSettings.name: Heuristics : Feedback
UPCGExHeuristicFeedbackProviderSettings.purpose: Charges for traffic. Every other heuristic in the family measures the cluster, and this one measures what routes have already done to it, raising the cost of Vtx and edges that have carried a route so later ones are pushed onto fresh ground. It is what separates a bundle of queries that all collapse onto the single best corridor from a set that spreads out and looks deliberate.
UPCGExHeuristicFeedbackProviderSettings.situation: Several routes across one cluster should not end up on top of each other.

mechanism.text: It keeps a visit count per Vtx and per edge, both starting at zero on an untouched cluster. Nothing is recorded while a search is running: the counts rise once a query has resolved, across the Vtx and edges of the route it settled on, which is why the first route through a cluster is charged nothing at all. The edge half then reads the count of the Vtx a step lands on and the count of the edge it crosses, and the goal half reads the count of the Vtx being considered. **Pathfinding : Grow Paths** is the exception to the timing: it records each step as it takes it, so a growing route pushes away from itself.

off_label.claim: With Invert on it does the opposite job, making used ground the cheapest, which consolidates a bundle of routes onto shared trunks instead of spreading them. In Binary mode this is exact: a used edge drops to the bottom of the curve and an unused one sits at the top.
off_label.grounded_in: the binary branch of FPCGExHeuristicFeedback::GetEdgeScore routes both outcomes through GetScoreInternal, which applies bInvert to the value entering the curve

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin. It is the one heuristic that can be alone on that pin, and only with `Global Feedback` on.

UPCGExHeuristicsAzimuthProviderSettings.name: Heuristics : Azimuth
UPCGExHeuristicsAzimuthProviderSettings.purpose: Measures heading. Both halves of its answer compare a direction against the straight line to the goal, which is a different question from how far the goal is: a step can be short and aimed away, or long and aimed straight at it. Distance and heading are the two things a route can be judged on before anything else about the cluster is read, and this is the heading one.
UPCGExHeuristicsAzimuthProviderSettings.situation: A route wanders sideways across a dense cluster because every local edge is short, and what it needs is a sense of which way the destination lies.

mechanism.text: The edge half takes the direction of the step being crossed and the direction from the Vtx it leaves toward the goal, and turns their agreement into a number running from zero when the step points directly at the goal to one when it points directly away. The goal half compares the direction from the Vtx to the goal against the direction from the seed to the goal, reading zero while the Vtx still lies along the seed-to-goal heading and one once it has gone past. Both land in a zero-to-one range on their own, so nothing about the cluster's size or extent enters either number.

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: Its answer collapses to a constant in any consumer that hands it the far end of the edge as the goal, because the step's direction and the direction to the goal are then the same vector. That covers **Cluster : Edge Properties**, **Cluster : Centrality**, **Decompose : Spectral** and **Pathfinding : Grow Paths**. The constant is the cheapest score rather than a middling one, so in those consumers the heuristic adds a flat discount to every edge and changes no ordering, while still counting toward the divisor in the score modes that divide by weight.

UPCGExHeuristicsFactoryProviderSettings.name: Heuristics Definition
UPCGExHeuristicsFactoryProviderSettings.purpose: The base every **Heuristics :** node inherits. It never appears in the palette, and this page carries what the family shares: the **Heuristics** pin they all emit on, the four settings that reshape any score without changing what it measures, and what a consumer does with a pin carrying several of them at once. The consumers reach well past the four search algorithms: **Cluster : Refine**, **Cluster : Decomposition**, **Cluster : Centrality** and **Cluster : Edge Properties** all take the same pin, and flood fill reaches the same factories through **Fill Control : Heuristics Scoring**, **Heuristics Budget** and **Heuristics Threshold**.
UPCGExHeuristicsFactoryProviderSettings.situation: Reading any heuristic page and needing to know what Weight Factor and Invert do to its number, or what happens to three of them wired onto one pin.

mechanism.text: A heuristic answers with a cost, and every consumer minimises it. It is asked twice in a step: once for the edge about to be crossed, and once for how far the Vtx on the far side still is from the goal. Whatever it measures is normalised against the cluster first, so a distance score and a steepness score arrive on the same scale, then read through the **Score Curve**, floored at zero, and multiplied by **Weight Factor**. Several heuristics on one pin each answer independently, and the consumer collapses their answers with its own **Heuristic Score Mode**.

off_label.claim: Wire a stack onto Cluster : Edge Properties and it writes the combined score onto the edges as an attribute, which turns any heuristic setup into something inspectable before a search ever runs.
off_label.grounded_in: UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings declares the same Heuristics pin as Required and passes its own HeuristicScoreMode to SetWantsHeuristics

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: What every Heuristics : node emits. Consumers read it on a pin of the same name, and several factories stack on that one pin.

hints.text: **Weight Factor** scales the finished score, and what that buys depends on the consumer's score mode. Under **Weighted Average** the total is divided by the summed weights, so only relative values matter and weights of 1 and 2 behave as 0.5 and 1. Under **Weighted Sum** nothing is divided out, so the absolute value carries. **Geometric Mean**, **Harmonic Mean**, **Minimum** and **Maximum** each divide a score back out by its own weight before combining, so there the weight decides what each heuristic is being compared against rather than how loudly it speaks.

**Weight Factor** accepts zero and negative values. At zero the heuristic stops contributing under **Weighted Average** and **Weighted Sum**, and the other four modes divide each score by its own weight, so a zero there produces a combined number the consumer cannot rank. A negative weight sends the whole contribution below zero, which every mode carries through unchanged.

**Invert** mirrors the measurement before the curve reads it, replacing a normalised value with one minus itself. Against the default straight line from 0 to 1 that reads as a flipped score. Against a shaped curve the shape is mirrored too, so a curve tuned to punish the top of the range ends up punishing the bottom.

**Local Weight Multiplier** reads a per-Vtx or per-Edge attribute and multiplies both the score and the weight it counts for, once per edge. Three things follow: the value is read from the Vtx the step is heading towards rather than the one it left, its sign is discarded and only the magnitude is used, and it reaches the edge score alone. The goal-distance half of the answer is never multiplied.

A consumer that asks for heuristics refuses to run without at least one. An empty **Heuristics** pin stops the cluster with `Missing valid base heuristics`, and a pin carrying only **Heuristics : Feedback** with `Global Feedback` off stops it with `cannot work with feedback alone`: a local feedback factory is held aside for per-query use and never joins the stack the check counts. Turning `Global Feedback` on puts it in the stack, so a global feedback on its own does pass the check.

Consumers that only sometimes need a stack advertise the pin accordingly. **Cluster : Refine**, **Cluster : Decomposition** and **Cluster : Centrality** each promote it to required when the configuration in hand consumes scores and demote it to advanced otherwise, and **Cluster : Flood Fill** keeps its own pin permanently advanced because it is deprecated in favour of the heuristic fill controls.

UPCGExHeuristicsGradientProviderSettings.name: Heuristics : Gradient
UPCGExHeuristicsGradientProviderSettings.purpose: Charges for how much a Vtx attribute changes across a step, and in which direction. **Heuristics : Attribute** charges for where a step lands; this charges for the difference between where it left and where it lands, which is what lets a route climb a value field, descend one, hug a plateau or hunt for the boundaries in it. The attribute has to be on the Vtx, because the difference is taken between two Vtx.
UPCGExHeuristicsGradientProviderSettings.situation: A value is painted across the Vtx and a route should follow its slope rather than its level.

mechanism.text: The edge half is the destination Vtx's value minus the origin Vtx's, and `Mode` decides what that difference costs. Crossing an edge one way gives the negative of crossing it the other, so the two directions of the same edge are charged differently under the two Follow modes and identically under the two Change modes. The goal half compares the goal Vtx's value against the current one: the Follow modes charge the maximum when the goal sits the wrong side and nothing when it sits the right side, and both Change modes charge a flat half.

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

UPCGExHeuristicsInertiaProviderSettings.name: Heuristics : Inertia
UPCGExHeuristicsInertiaProviderSettings.purpose: Charges for changing direction. It averages the headings of the last few steps a route took and compares the candidate step against that average, so carrying straight on is free and doubling back costs the most. Where **Heuristics : Turn Penalty** looks at one corner, this looks at a run of them, which is what keeps a route flowing instead of merely avoiding sharp angles.
UPCGExHeuristicsInertiaProviderSettings.situation: A route reaches its goal by the right general course but zigzags between neighbouring Vtx the whole way there.

mechanism.text: The edge half averages the directions of up to `Samples` steps already taken into the Vtx, then charges by how far the candidate step turns away from that average: zero for carrying straight on, one for a reversal, half for a right angle. The average is a direction, so nothing about the cluster's size enters the number and it already sits in a zero-to-one range. The goal half is the flat `Global Inertia Score` for every Vtx, because a look-ahead has no route behind it to average.

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: Route history exists only inside a consumer building a route: the search algorithms, **Pathfinding : Grow Paths**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, and the heuristic fill controls. Everywhere else there is no direction to average and every edge is charged `Fallback Inertia Score`, so this heuristic contributes a flat number on the score-based refinements, **Cluster : Centrality**, **Cluster : Decomposition** and **Cluster : Edge Properties**. The same is why a heuristics heatmap cannot preview what it will actually cost.

UPCGExHeuristicsLeastNodesProviderSettin.name: Heuristics : Least Nodes
UPCGExHeuristicsLeastNodesProviderSettin.purpose: Charges the same amount for every step, whatever it spans. Minimising a flat per-step charge is minimising the number of steps, so a route made of four long edges beats one made of six short ones. Stacked against **Heuristics : Shortest Distance** it is the dial between fewest stops and least ground covered.
UPCGExHeuristicsLeastNodesProviderSettin.situation: Every stop along a route costs something and the distance between stops does not, as with transfers, waypoints or anything paid for per hop.

mechanism.text: Both halves of the answer are a fixed value of 0.5 read through the `Score Curve` and multiplied by `Weight Factor`, so the heuristic reduces to one number charged identically on every edge in every cluster. Nothing about the cluster is measured, so there is nothing to normalise against and nothing that changes between components, queries or directions of travel. The goal half is that same fixed number, which adds a constant to every look-ahead and can rank nothing by proximity.

off_label.claim: Because its answer is a constant, wiring it alone into Cluster : Edge Properties writes the same value onto every edge, which is a cheap way to confirm a Heuristics pin is reaching a consumer at all before a real stack is wired.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExHeuristicNodeCount::GetEdgeScore returns GetScoreInternal(0.5) unconditionally, ignoring From, To and Edge

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: `Invert` does nothing on this heuristic. It mirrors the value entering the curve, and the value entering the curve is always 0.5, which mirrors to itself. `Score Curve` still matters: it decides what the constant is, so a curve reading low at the halfway mark makes each step cheap against the rest of the stack and one reading high makes each step expensive.

UPCGExHeuristicsShortestDistanceProvider.name: Heuristics : Shortest Distance
UPCGExHeuristicsShortestDistanceProvider.purpose: Charges for length. The edge half of the answer is the length of the edge being crossed, and the goal half is the straight-line distance from the Vtx to the goal. Both are measured in world units and divided by the same number, which is what lets a search weigh ground already covered against ground still to cover. This is the heuristic the familiar shortest route falls out of, and the one most stacks are built around.
UPCGExHeuristicsShortestDistanceProvider.situation: A route should take the shortest way across a cluster, or should treat length as one cost among several.

mechanism.text: Both halves are divided by the diagonal of the box around this cluster's Vtx, so an edge spanning the whole cluster scores near one and a short one near zero. A generator emits one Edges dataset per connected component, and each component is measured against its own box, so an edge of a given length is charged more inside a small component than inside a large one. Nothing else varies: the edge half reads the edge's own length and gives the same answer wherever the seed and goal happen to be.

off_label.claim: Wired alone into Cluster : Edge Properties with the default curve and a Weight Factor of 1, the attribute it writes is each edge's length as a fraction of the cluster's bounding diagonal, which is a normalised edge-length attribute nothing else produces in one node.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExHeuristicDistance::GetEdgeScore returns ScoreCurve->Eval(EdgeLengths[Edge.Index] * InvBoundsSize) * ReferenceWeight; UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings writes the handler's edge score to the Heuristics output attribute

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

UPCGExHeuristicsSteepnessProviderSetting.name: Heuristics : Steepness
UPCGExHeuristicsSteepnessProviderSetting.purpose: Charges for slope. A step is measured against an up direction you choose, and with `Absolute Steepness` on a level step is free while a vertical one costs the most, whichever way it goes. Turning `Absolute Steepness` off keeps the sign, which is how a stack asks for downhill or for uphill instead of for level. It is the terrain half of a stack whose other half is usually **Heuristics : Shortest Distance**.
UPCGExHeuristicsSteepnessProviderSetting.situation: A route over uneven ground should stay level, or should climb, and the shortest line does neither.

mechanism.text: The measurement is the tilt of the step's direction against `Up Vector`, which already lands in a zero-to-one range before the curve reads it, so nothing about the cluster's size or extent enters the number. The goal half applies the same measurement to the straight line from the Vtx to the goal, charging for the tilt of the direct line still to be covered rather than for its length. Both halves read positions alone, so under `Absolute Steepness` an edge costs the same whichever way a route crosses it, and under the signed range the two directions cost opposite amounts.

off_label.claim: Wired alone into Cluster : Edge Properties it writes each edge's tilt as an attribute, which is a slope-per-edge channel no dedicated node produces and that ordinary attribute filters can then threshold.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExHeuristicSteepness::GetEdgeScore falls through to GetDot(GetPos(From), GetPos(To)) when no travel history is supplied, and UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings supplies none

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: Accumulation needs a route to walk back along, and only a consumer building one has it: the search algorithms, **Pathfinding : Grow Paths**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, and the heuristic fill controls. Everywhere else the walk-back finds nothing and the single-step tilt is what gets charged, so the score-based refinements, **Cluster : Centrality**, **Cluster : Decomposition** and **Cluster : Edge Properties** all read this heuristic as though accumulation were off.

UPCGExHeuristicsTensorProviderSettings.name: Heuristics : Tensor
UPCGExHeuristicsTensorProviderSettings.purpose: Charges for disagreeing with a field. It samples the tensors wired into it at the Vtx a step leaves, then charges by how far the step departs from the direction the field points there. It is the one heuristic in the family with an input of its own, and the way to make a route follow flow lines that exist nowhere in the cluster's own geometry.
UPCGExHeuristicsTensorProviderSettings.situation: A field already describes which way things should run through this space, and a route across a cluster should obey it.

mechanism.text: Both halves sample the combined field at the Vtx being considered and compare the sampled direction against a direction of their own: for the edge half that is the step about to be taken, and for the goal half the straight line to the goal. Travelling along the field is free and travelling across it is the most expensive, with `Absolute` deciding whether running against the field counts as along it. The measurement is an agreement between two directions, so nothing about the cluster's size enters the number.

inputs.label: Tensors
inputs.note: The tensor factories to sample. They are combined into one field before anything is measured against it, and `Tensor Sampling Settings` acts on that combined sample.

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: Where the sample finds nothing, because the Vtx falls outside the reach of every tensor wired in, the measurement comes back as zero, which is the same number a step running perfectly along the field would produce. Unreached ground therefore reads as ideal rather than as neutral or as an obstacle, and a search will happily route through it. Cover the cluster, or pair this with a heuristic that has an opinion where the field has none.

The **Tensors** pin is required, and an empty one fails this node with `Missing tensors.` while it is preparing its factory. Nothing then reaches the consumer's **Heuristics** pin, so the consumer fails in turn with its own missing-heuristics error and the second message is the one most likely to be read first.

UPCGExHeuristicsTurnPenaltyProviderSetti.name: Heuristics : Turn Penalty
UPCGExHeuristicsTurnPenaltyProviderSetti.purpose: Charges for the corner between one step and the next, in degrees, with a tolerance band at each end. Below `Min Angle Threshold` a turn is free, at or above `Max Angle Threshold` it costs the maximum, and between them the charge rises evenly. Where **Heuristics : Inertia** measures against an averaged heading over several steps, this measures one corner against the step that arrived, which is what makes the thresholds meaningful in degrees.
UPCGExHeuristicsTurnPenaltyProviderSetti.situation: A route may bend as much as it likes up to some angle and must never exceed another, as with anything that has a turning radius.

mechanism.text: The edge half measures the angle between the step that arrived at the Vtx and the candidate step, then maps it against the two thresholds: at or below `Min Angle Threshold` it charges nothing, at or above `Max Angle Threshold` it charges the top of the curve, and in between it rises linearly across the band. Angles are the whole of the measurement, so nothing about the cluster's size enters the number. The goal half is the flat `Global Score` for every Vtx, because a look-ahead has no arriving step to turn from.

outputs.label: Heuristics
outputs.note: The factory, read by any consumer with a Heuristics pin and stackable alongside other heuristics on it.

hints.text: The arriving step exists only inside a consumer building a route: the search algorithms, **Pathfinding : Grow Paths**, **Refine : MST (Prim)**, and the heuristic fill controls. Everywhere else every edge is charged `Fallback Score`, so this heuristic contributes a flat number on the score-based refinements, **Cluster : Centrality**, **Cluster : Decomposition** and **Cluster : Edge Properties**. The same is why a heuristics heatmap cannot preview what it will actually cost.

UPCGExInclusionFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Inclusion (Path/Splines)
UPCGExInclusionFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Answers whether each element falls inside a shape drawn by path-like data. The reference shapes arrive on the Targets pin and may be point paths, splines or 2D polygons, mixed freely; each is flattened onto a plane and treated as a closed outline, so the verdict is a two dimensional one. The node produces a filter on its Filter pin, and eight checks cover inside, outside and on the outline together with their combinations, each carried in the palette as its own drop-in entry. An element can also be required to land inside at least, or at most, a given number of shapes.
UPCGExInclusionFilterProviderSettings.situation: A spline or a closed path marks out a region, and whether an element survives depends on falling within it.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element, and every shape on the Targets pin is searched as one pool. Each shape is flattened onto a plane and closed back on itself, so an open path bounds an interior exactly as a closed one does; what an open path lacks is an outline along the closing span, because it has no segment there. Each shape answers inside or outside, and whether the element sits within `Tolerance` of its outline; those answers are pooled, so a single shape can satisfy the check while the rest contribute nothing. The shapes are flattened once, on this node, and every consumer wired to its Filter pin shares that work.

off_label.claim: Feed an open path, set `Check Type` to `Is On` and raise `Tolerance` to the width you care about, and the filter becomes a corridor test: the band follows the path's own segments and skips the closing span, so it selects elements near a route rather than inside a region.
off_label.grounded_in: the distance-only path taken for EPCGExSplineCheckType::IsOn in PCGExPathInclusion::FHandler::Init, whose band is measured to the closest transform on the shape's segments, and FPath::BuildPath omitting the wrap segment for an open path

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: The reference shapes. Point paths, splines and 2D polygons are all accepted here, and several datasets are searched as one pool. A path of fewer than two points, or a spline with no segment, is dropped with a warning.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: Match rules deciding which reference shapes each tested dataset is allowed to see. The pin is always present, sitting among the advanced pins until Data Matching is switched on.
inputs.condition: when Data Matching Mode is All or Any

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node produces. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: An empty Targets pin routes through Missing Data Policy rather than Initialization Failure Policy, and so does a pin whose every shape was dropped: a path of fewer than two points, or a spline with no segment. Each drop logs its own warning, but the empty result that follows logs nothing at all unless that policy is set to Error.
The node subtitle reads back the check, with a flag prepended when Invert is on, so a graph carrying several of these can be read without selecting them one at a time.

UPCGExIsoEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSett.name: Edge Filter : Edge Direction
UPCGExIsoEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSett.purpose: Judges an edge by which way it runs. The filter measures the edge's own direction from the positions of the two Vtx it connects, tests that against a reference direction you supply as a constant or read per edge, and emits the verdict on the **Edge Filter** pin for an **Edge Filters** pin to consume.
UPCGExIsoEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSett.situation: A cluster whose edges run in every direction, and the node downstream should only see the ones within some angle of a chosen axis.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per edge; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. The edge's own direction is measured from the two endpoint positions held by the cluster, so it follows anything upstream that moved those Vtx, and it is never read from an attribute, including one a previous node wrote onto the edge point. `Direction Settings` settles which endpoint the edge calls Start, and the measured vector points at that endpoint, which is what makes an asymmetric comparison read one way or the other. The reference direction is the `Direction` constant or a vector read from the Edges dataset at the edge's own row, and `Comparison Quality` decides which of the two comparison blocks turns the pair into a verdict.

inputs.label: Direction Sorting
inputs.note: Sorting rules deciding which endpoint an edge calls Start. They resolve on the Vtx dataset.
inputs.condition: when Direction Settings has Direction Method set to Endpoints Sort

outputs.label: Edge Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the edge-family passport, so an **Edge Filters** pin takes it and no other pin does.

fields.name: DirectionSettings
fields.tooltip: Defines how the edge's endpoints are ordered to establish its direction.

fields.name: ComparisonQuality
fields.tooltip: Type of check. Dot compares angles precisely; Hash (Fast) compares quantized directions.

fields.name: CompareAgainst
fields.tooltip: Where to read the compared direction from.

fields.name: Direction
fields.tooltip: Direction to compare the edge against -- Read as an FVector direction.

fields.name: bInvertDirection
fields.tooltip: Flip the direction vector before comparison.

fields.name: DirectionConstant
fields.tooltip: Direction to compare the edge against.

fields.name: bTransformDirection
fields.tooltip: Transform the reference direction with the local point' transform

fields.name: DotComparisonDetails
fields.tooltip: Dot comparison settings

fields.name: HashComparisonDetails
fields.tooltip: Hash comparison settings

hints.text: **Vtx Filter : Edge Direction** asks a direction question at a Vtx, folding every edge that reaches it together through adjacency settings. This node asks it of one edge and never aggregates, so the two share a name and a settings block without standing in for each other.

UPCGExIterationsSettings.name: Iterations
UPCGExIterationsSettings.purpose: Emits a chosen number of empty datasets so a loop node has something to iterate over. Vanilla PCG loops once per data entry on their input, which ties the iteration count to whatever the data happens to hold; this node breaks that tie by producing exactly the count you ask for. Each entry can also carry its own index and progress values, and the output pin can be typed so the same subgraph works as a loop body and as a plain subgraph.
UPCGExIterationsSettings.situation: A subgraph that has to run a fixed number of times, where the count is a setting rather than a property of the incoming data.

mechanism.text: One empty data object of the chosen type is created and staged Iterations times, each entry tagged Iteration with its own index and NumIterations with the total. All the entries reference that single object, so the cost of a large count is the collection, not the data. Output Utils changes that for attribute sets only: each entry becomes its own attribute set carrying Iteration, NumIterations, Progress and OneMinusProgress on a single row. Nothing is read from anywhere, so the output depends on the settings alone.

off_label.claim: The Iteration and NumIterations tags are on the entries whether or not Output Utils is on, so a downstream node that reads tag values can recover the index without paying for one attribute set per iteration.
off_label.grounded_in: both staging branches pass the same Iteration and NumIterations tag pair into StageOutput

outputs.label: Iterations
outputs.note: One entry per iteration. The pin's accepted type follows the Type setting: untyped for Any, attribute set, points, spline or texture for the rest.

Type.tooltip: Type of data to generate. This is useful if you build subgraphs that are meant to be used as both loops and regular subgraphs, so you can have properly typed pins.
Type.semantics: Changes what the output pin will connect to, which is the point of it: a loop body that also has to work as an ordinary subgraph needs its entry pin typed. Any and Attribute Set both produce attribute sets; Any only widens what the pin will accept.

Iterations.semantics: The number of entries emitted, and so the number of loop passes. It defaults to zero, which emits nothing at all.
Iterations.trap: With Output Utils on and a count of exactly one, Progress divides by zero and the emitted value is not a number.

bOutputUtils.tooltip: Output per-iteration params with useful values. Less optimized than the non-value version
bOutputUtils.semantics: Replaces the shared empty object with one attribute set per iteration, each holding Iteration, NumIterations, Progress and OneMinusProgress. Progress runs from zero on the first entry to one on the last.
bOutputUtils.trap: It is honoured only when Type is Attribute Set. Its edit condition is malformed, so the checkbox stays enabled under the other types while the element ignores it.

hints.text: Every entry points at the same object unless Output Utils is on, so nothing downstream should treat one iteration's data as distinct from another's. What distinguishes them is the Iteration tag.

UPCGExLaplacianRelax.name: Laplacian (Poisson)
UPCGExLaplacianRelax.purpose: Places every Vtx on the average position of the Vtx it shares an edge with. That one rule is the whole thing: it has no settings of its own, and the move is the full distance to that average rather than a step toward it. It is the rule to pick when the spacing along a cluster's chains is ragged and evening it out matters more than holding the shape the cluster came in with, because the same averaging that smooths a chain also draws the whole cluster inward on every iteration.
UPCGExLaplacianRelax.situation: A cluster whose Vtx sit at uneven intervals along its chains, where regular spacing is worth more than the outline.

mechanism.text: One turn over the Vtx per iteration. Each Vtx is placed on the average of its directly connected neighbours as those neighbours stood when the iteration began, so nothing one Vtx does inside an iteration is visible to any other until the next one starts. There is no strength or step size on the rule: the whole distance to that average is travelled every time, and `Influence` on **Cluster : Relax** is the only thing that damps it. Nothing here holds a length or an outline, so where a Vtx is pulled depends only on where its neighbours happen to be.

off_label.claim: Wire a filter into the Vtx Filters pin on Cluster : Relax and this becomes a fill: the Vtx that fail keep their positions and act as a boundary, while the ones that are free are pulled onto the average of whatever surrounds them, iteration after iteration.
off_label.grounded_in: RelaxScope restores a filtered-out Vtx to its read-buffer position after Step1, while Step1 reads every neighbour position from the read buffer whether that neighbour was filtered out or not

hints.text: A leaf has one neighbour, so the average it is placed on is that neighbour's previous position and nothing else. Chain ends and thin branches close up first, and two Vtx joined by a single edge trade places on every iteration without ever stopping.

UPCGExLevelCollection.name: Collection | Level
UPCGExLevelCollection.purpose: A collection whose entries are level assets, so one pick places a whole arrangement instead of one asset. The rebuild reads each level rather than asking you to describe it: the actors inside fold into the entry's bounds, and socket-provider actors placed in the level become the entry's sockets. From there the entry behaves like any other collection row, and the pick spawns through Staging : Spawn Level.
UPCGExLevelCollection.situation: A level was dressed by hand and now has to be placed repeatedly, as one weighted option among others.

mechanism.text: An entry names a level asset, or flips to a sub-collection like an entry of any other type. A staging rebuild loads the level and walks the actors of its persistent level, baking two values onto the entry: the union of the bounds the surviving actors contribute, and one managed socket per socket-provider actor found. Which actors survive, and what each one contributes, are the two Import objects' decisions, so what a level measures is configured rather than fixed. Everything downstream reads those baked values, and the level itself stays unloaded until something spawns it.
steps: Socket-provider actors contribute their socket, before anything is rejected.
Actors tagged StaticIgnore, and socket providers set to strip from export, are dropped from the rest of the walk.
Content Filter decides which of the remaining actors count.
Bounds Evaluator turns each surviving actor into a box, and their union becomes the entry's bounds.

off_label.claim: Tagging an actor StaticIgnore keeps it out of the walk before any filter is consulted, which is a per-actor opt-out that still works under a custom Blueprint content filter that knows nothing about tags.
off_label.grounded_in: UPCGExActorContentFilter::StaticPassesFilter rejects on the StaticIgnore actor tag ahead of delegating to the assigned filter

ContentFilter.tooltip: Actor content filter for bounds computation. If null, default infrastructure checks are used.
ContentFilter.default:
Cast<UPCGExActorContentFilter>(
		ObjectInitializer.CreateDefaultSubobject(this, TEXT("ContentFilter"),
		                                         UPCGExActorContentFilter::StaticClass(), FilterClass, false, false))
ContentFilter.semantics: A new collection does not start with this empty: the constructor instantiates the class named by Default Content Filter Class in the project's Collections settings, falling back to Default Actor Content Filter, whose tag and class include and exclude lists are its whole panel.
ContentFilter.trap: A custom Blueprint filter replaces the infrastructure rejections instead of adding to them, so hidden actors, editor-only actors, main-world-only actors, level script actors, Info actors, non-volume brushes, navigation data and registered system actor classes all start counting toward bounds unless the Blueprint rejects them itself.

BoundsEvaluator.tooltip: Bounds evaluator for bounds computation. If null, bounds default to empty.
BoundsEvaluator.default:
Cast<UPCGExBoundsEvaluator>(
		ObjectInitializer.CreateDefaultSubobject(this, TEXT("BoundsEvaluator"),
		                                         UPCGExBoundsEvaluator::StaticClass(), EvalClass, false, false))
BoundsEvaluator.semantics: Same shape as the filter slot: the constructor instantiates Default Bounds Evaluator Class from the project's Collections settings, falling back to Default Bounds Evaluator, which accumulates world-space primitive bounds and skips light and editor-only components by default. It runs only on actors the filter already kept.
BoundsEvaluator.trap: Clearing this to empty leaves every entry with empty bounds, and empty bounds travel: fitting has nothing to solve against and size-aware selectors read zero extents.

Entries.semantics: Add Content Browser Selection appends level assets as level rows and any collection asset, of any type, as a sub-collection row; everything else in the selection is ignored, and a level the collection already lists is skipped rather than duplicated.

hints.text: Baking a level entry is editor work. Outside the editor the rebuild logs an error and leaves the entry's bounds empty, so bounds and sockets have to be baked in an editor session and shipped with the asset.

An entry whose staging data was authored by an external system is left alone: rebuilds refresh only its path and internal index, and its bounds and sockets survive untouched. No rebuild path re-walks the level for it.

addenda.title: Level Collection or PCG Data Asset Collection?
addenda.text: Level Collections are a good fit for static, editor-time baked level instances. For the general case, prefer a [PCG Data Asset Collection](pcg-data-asset-collection/README.md) using a level as its entry source.

UPCGExLevelDataExporter.name: Level Data Exporter
UPCGExLevelDataExporter.purpose: Level export is a replaceable step, and this is the class that replaces it. One exporter instance sits on a PCG Data Asset Collection and serves every level-sourced row on it, so what a subclass decides here is what capture means for that whole collection: which actors count, what shape the data comes out in, what runs alongside. A subclass declares its own settings, and they appear in the collection's details panel underneath the exporter field. The class is abstract, so something always stands in it: the shipped Default Level Data Exporter when nothing else is assigned.
UPCGExLevelDataExporter.situation: A project needs its levels captured on its own terms, and the shipped exporter's rules are not those terms.

mechanism.text: Rebuilding staging hands the exporter one loaded world and one empty PCG data asset, and expects tagged data on that asset in return. The row then stages what came back: the produced asset's path becomes the row's staged path, and the combined bounds of its spatial data become the row's bounds. An export that reports failure leaves the row staging nothing. There are two entry points into the same job: the simple one, which is what a Blueprint subclass overrides, and the full one, a C++ override that additionally reports which meshes and which nested level instances the level contributed. Those contributions are what lets the collection pool that storage across its rows, write the pick hashes and build the Collection Map afterwards, none of which the exporter does itself.

hints.text:
## A Blueprint exporter cannot produce picks

Blueprint reaches the simple entry point only. A subclass written there still runs and its asset still stages, but the mesh and level points come out carrying raw asset paths, with no pick hashes and no Collection Map for the staging routes to resolve against. Reporting contributions is a C++ override of the full entry point.
The exporter field is editor-only data. Capture runs when staging rebuilds, and what ships is the asset it produced.

UPCGExLloydRelax2DSettings.name: Lloyd Relax 2D
UPCGExLloydRelax2DSettings.purpose: Evens out a scatter on a plane rather than in a volume. Points are relaxed against their neighbours as seen from the projection, so a set spread over undulating ground spaces out as it would look from above while keeping the heights it already had. **Lloyd Relax 3D** is the same idea with no projection, where height participates in the spacing.
UPCGExLloydRelax2DSettings.situation: Points scattered across terrain that should read as evenly spread when seen from above, without the ground's slope pulling them together.

mechanism.text: The points are projected onto a plane, relaxed there by repeatedly moving each to the middle of the region nearest to it, and the result is carried back. Because the spacing is decided on the plane, two points at the same projected spot are as close as can be however far apart they are vertically. `Iterations` is the pass count and `Influence` scales how much of each move lands.

Iterations.tooltip: Number of relaxation iterations to perform. More iterations = more uniform spacing.
Iterations.semantics: Passes over the whole set. The first few do most of the evening out and later ones move points less and less, so raising this past convergence spends time without changing the result.

InfluenceDetails.semantics: Scales how much of each pass's move is applied, per point when driven by an attribute. That is what lets part of a scatter relax while the rest holds position.

ProjectionDetails.semantics: Decides the plane the spacing is judged on, and therefore what evenly spread means here. A projection along the world up gives spacing as seen from above; any other plane gives spacing as seen from that direction, which is rarely what a ground scatter wants.

hints.text: Only the projected position is relaxed, so heights are untouched. On steep ground the result looks even from above and can still read as clustered from a low angle, which is what **Lloyd Relax 3D** avoids.

UPCGExLloydRelaxSettings.name: Lloyd Relax 3D
UPCGExLloydRelaxSettings.purpose: Evens out a scatter by repeatedly moving each point to the middle of the space it owns. Clumps spread and gaps fill, and the result is a set that still follows the shape of the original but with the lumpiness taken out. It works in all three dimensions, which is what separates it from **Lloyd Relax 2D**, where the same idea runs on a projected plane.
UPCGExLloydRelaxSettings.situation: A random scatter that reads as blotchy and needs to look evenly spread without becoming a grid.

mechanism.text: Each pass divides space into the regions nearest to each point and moves every point to the centre of its own region. Doing that once removes the worst clumping; doing it repeatedly converges toward even spacing. `Iterations` is how many passes run, and `Influence` decides how much of each move is actually applied, so a low influence approaches the same destination more slowly. Nothing is added or removed, and every point keeps its attributes.

off_label.claim: One iteration at low influence is a de-clumping nudge rather than a relaxation: the worst overlaps ease apart while the scatter keeps the character of its original distribution.
off_label.grounded_in: Iterations is a plain loop count over the same centroid step, and the influence block scales how much of each computed move is applied.

Iterations.tooltip: Number of relaxation iterations to perform. More iterations = more uniform spacing.
Iterations.semantics: Passes over the whole set, and the cost is linear in them while the visible change is not: the first few passes do most of the evening out and later ones move points less and less. Raising this past the point of convergence spends time without changing the result.

InfluenceDetails.semantics: Scales how much of each pass's move is applied, per point when driven by an attribute. That is what lets part of a scatter relax while the rest holds position, so a mask can protect points that were placed deliberately.

hints.text: Relaxation moves points toward the middle of the volume they occupy, so an unbounded scatter tends to pull inward at its edges. Points meant to hold the outline of a shape usually need their influence turned down.

UPCGExMakeClustersUniqueSettings.name: Cluster : Make Unique
UPCGExMakeClustersUniqueSettings.purpose: Gives each cluster passing through it a pair id nothing else shares. Two clusters that descend from one source still carry the id they were born with, and a node handed both keeps one of them and drops the other, so branches that fanned out from one cluster have to be told apart before they meet again. Nothing about the data changes: points, attributes and connectivity all come through as they were.
UPCGExMakeClustersUniqueSettings.situation: One cluster was fanned out to several branches, each branch did something of its own, and the results are about to arrive on one pin together.

mechanism.text: Both halves are forwarded untouched and the `PCGEx/Cluster` tag on each pair is rewritten to a value taken from that Vtx dataset's own identity. Endpoint ids, the two cluster attributes, point order and point count are all left alone, so the only thing that differs downstream is which datasets read as belonging together.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx datasets to re-stamp. Each one's identity becomes its cluster's new pair id.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges datasets. Each is re-stamped with the new id of the Vtx dataset it was already paired to.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The input dataset, forwarded, carrying a new pair id.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The input datasets, forwarded, carrying their Vtx dataset's new pair id.

hints.text: This prevents a collision, it does not resolve one. Two Vtx datasets that already share a pair id and arrive on this node's **Vtx** pin together are triaged before the node runs: one is kept, the other is dropped with a warning, and no re-stamping brings it back. Put this node in each branch before they merge, not after.

Every cluster node re-stamps the pair id as part of its own run, so a branch that already ends in a cluster node does not need this one in front of the merge. Reach for it when a branch touched the cluster with vanilla nodes, or did not touch it at all.

UPCGExMatchRuleFactoryProviderSettings.name: Match Rule Definition
UPCGExMatchRuleFactoryProviderSettings.purpose: The base every Match : node inherits. It never appears in the palette, and this page carries what the family shares: the Match Rule pin they all emit on, the two settings sitting on every rule, and how a pin holding several of them resolves to one verdict. A consumer collects these factories on a pin named Match Rules and uses them to work out which of its targets belongs with which of its inputs.
UPCGExMatchRuleFactoryProviderSettings.situation: Reading any Match : page and needing to know what Strictness actually changes, or how three rules on one pin add up to a single yes or no.

mechanism.text: A consumer turns every factory on its Match Rules pin into a live rule, then works one pair at a time. Each rule's own settings name the two sides: the target is what the consumer matches against, usually the data on its Targets pin, and the candidate is the data being processed. Both sides are whole datasets, so a rule reads tags and @Data attributes rather than anything per point, and a handful of consumers run the same rules once per element instead. Each rule answers yes or no about the pair, the consuming node's Mode adds those answers up, and Strictness and Invert shape what one answer contributes. Rules keep the order they were wired in, which is the order the answers are collected.

outputs.label: Match Rule
outputs.note: What every Match : node emits. Consumers read it on a pin named Match Rules, and cluster nodes set to Separate read a second stack on Match Rules (Edges).

hints.text: Strictness only bites in Any mode. In All mode every rule on the pin has to pass, Required and Optional alike, so switching a rule to Required changes nothing there. In Any mode the split is real: an Optional rule passing is what opens the match, and the Required ones are then checked on top of it. A stack of nothing but Required rules in Any mode therefore matches nothing at all, because no Optional rule is present to open it.

Most rules answer with Invert's own value when they cannot read the thing they were pointed at, so a misspelled attribute or a tag that is not there reads as a failed match with Invert off and as a passing match with Invert on.

A sub-node from another family dropped onto a Match Rules pin connects, logs an invalid-input warning and is discarded, after which the node runs with whatever survived. When it was the only thing on the pin, the next thing reported is a missing-required-input error naming Match Rules, which names the emptied pin rather than the wire that emptied it.

Match : Overlap is the only rule that can match transitively. Its Recursive setting lets a match propagate through overlapping chains, and the whole matcher follows once any rule on the pin asks for it.

UPCGExMeanFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Mean
UPCGExMeanFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Judges each element against a statistic of the data it sits in rather than against a number you set. One attribute is read across the whole dataset, a reference value is derived from it, and an element passes on how far its own value sits from that reference. The reference is settled again for every dataset the consumer holds, so one filter draws a different line on each of them. Mean Method chooses which statistic, and Fixed is there for the case where a plain constant was what you wanted after all.
UPCGExMeanFilterProviderSettings.situation: A dataset where what counts as too long, too dense or too far is only definable against the rest of it.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element, but the number every element is compared against is settled once per dataset before any of them is tested: every value of the target attribute in that dataset is read, and Mean Method turns them into one reference. Two optional margins open a band around that reference, one below and one above, and an element passes when its value lands inside the band. A margin left switched off leaves that side of the band open, so with both off every element passes. Nothing crosses a dataset boundary: a consumer holding several datasets gets a separate reference for each, and merging two of them upstream moves every verdict.

off_label.claim: Set Mean Method to Fixed and leave Measure at Relative, and the threshold stops being a statistic and becomes a fraction of the dataset's own largest value: every value is divided by that maximum before the band is applied, so one Fixed reference with a single margin open cuts at the same proportion of the biggest element in every dataset it meets.
off_label.grounded_in: FMeanFilter::PostInit dividing every value by the buffer maximum under EPCGExMeanMeasure::Relative, before the Fixed reference and its margins are applied

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

hints.text: Both margins ship switched off. A freshly dropped node therefore has no band at all, passes every element, and reads downstream as a filter that had no effect rather than as one that was never configured.

UPCGExMergePointsSettings.name: Merge Points
UPCGExMergePointsSettings.purpose: Collapses several point datasets into one, or into one per group when the matching rules say which datasets belong together. It also solves the two things that go wrong when data is merged: attributes that only some inputs carried, and tags, which have nowhere to live once the datasets holding them are gone. Sorting rules can be wired in to fix the order the inputs are concatenated in.
UPCGExMergePointsSettings.situation: Many datasets that have to become one before something that reasons over the whole set, with the per-dataset identity preserved somehow rather than lost.

mechanism.text: The inputs are first put in order, by the sorting rules if any are wired and otherwise in arrival order, then split into groups by the matching rules. Each group of two or more becomes one new dataset holding every point of its members, concatenated in that order; a group of one is forwarded untouched rather than copied. Carry Over decides which attributes survive, and unlike everywhere else in the plugin it promotes @Data values onto the points by default, since after a merge there is no per-dataset domain left to hold them.

off_label.claim: With matching enabled and non-exclusive partitions, a dataset that satisfies two groups is merged into both, so the node can fan one input into several overlapping supersets in a single pass.
off_label.grounded_in: the partition helper takes the exclusivity flag and, when it is off, allows a facade index into more than one partition

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The point datasets to merge.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: The rules deciding which datasets group together. Required while matching is enabled, advanced while it is disabled.
inputs.condition: when Matching Details is not Disabled

inputs.label: Sorting Rules
inputs.note: Sorting Rule sub-nodes ordering the inputs before they are grouped and concatenated, which is what fixes the point order inside each merged result.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: One dataset per group. Groups of a single dataset are forwarded rather than rebuilt.

outputs.label: Unmatched
outputs.note: Datasets that grouped with nothing else, when the matching settings ask for them to be split out. Otherwise they leave on the main pin.
outputs.condition: carries data only when the matching settings request the unmatched split

MatchingDetails.tooltip: Matching settings to determine which data should be grouped together. When disabled, all inputs merge into one output.
MatchingDetails.semantics: Disabled merges everything into one output. Enabled, it partitions first and merges within each partition, and also decides whether lone datasets are split onto the Unmatched pin.

bExclusivePartitions.tooltip: If enabled, each data can only belong to one group (first match). If disabled, data can appear in multiple groups.
bExclusivePartitions.semantics: On, a dataset joins the first group that accepts it and no other. Off, it joins every group it satisfies, so its points appear in more than one output.

SortDirection.tooltip: Controls the order in which data will be sorted if sorting rules are used
SortDirection.semantics: Applies to the sorting rules that order the inputs. With no rules wired it has nothing to act on and the inputs keep their arrival order.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: Ships with @Data promotion switched on here and nowhere else in the plugin: each input's data-level attributes are written onto its own points before the concatenation, so a value that identified a dataset survives as a per-point value.

TagsToAttributes.tooltip: Tags to convert to attributes: simple tags become boolean (presence), tag:value pairs become their typed value.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

TagsToAttributes.semantics: The tag equivalent of the same problem. A plain tag becomes a bool recording whether the point's original dataset carried it; a value tag becomes an attribute of the value's own type.

hints.text: Tags belong to datasets, not to points, so a merge loses every tag that did not apply to all of its members. Turn on the tag conversion before the merge if any of them still matters afterwards.

UPCGExMergeVerticesSettings.name: Cluster : Merge Vtx
UPCGExMergeVerticesSettings.purpose: Collapses several Vtx datasets into one, so every cluster that arrives ends up sharing a single Vtx dataset. It is the return trip from **Cluster : Partition Vtx**, and the way to put clusters that were generated apart onto one Vtx dataset when something downstream wants them there. Nothing is welded: two vertices at the same position stay two vertices, and the clusters stay as separate as they arrived.
UPCGExMergeVerticesSettings.situation: Clusters that came from separate generators, or were partitioned earlier, have to be handed to something that reads one Vtx dataset.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx dataset on the pin is concatenated into one new dataset, in input order, and each cluster's connections are re-pointed into it. The Edges datasets come through as they were, one per cluster, all now tagged to the single Vtx dataset that came out. The merged point count is the sum of the inputs, so nothing is removed and nothing is fused. `Carry Over Settings` decides which attributes and tags make it across; the merged dataset carries the union of its sources' tags, filtered by that block.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx datasets to concatenate. Their order on the pin is the order they land in.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges datasets, which come through unchanged apart from their pair tag.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One dataset holding every input vertex, in input order, under a fresh pair id.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per cluster, as they arrived, re-tagged to the merged Vtx dataset.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: What it governs is the concatenation, not the Edges datasets, which come through untouched either way. An attribute present on one input Vtx dataset and absent on another still lands on the merged dataset, with the rows from the datasets that lacked it left at the attribute's default. Tags are gathered from every source and then filtered, so the merged dataset carries the union of what its inputs were tagged with rather than the first one's.

hints.text: The merge does not renumber endpoint ids: the merged dataset carries each source's ids exactly as they were. Vtx datasets from separate generators are each numbered from zero, so merging them puts repeated ids in one dataset, and anything that rebuilds a cluster from the two attributes, **Cluster : Repair** among them, then resolves a repeated id to a single vertex. Vtx datasets that came from one **Cluster : Partition Vtx** do not collide, because their ids were already disjoint.

UPCGExMeshCollection.name: Collection | Mesh
UPCGExMeshCollection.purpose: A weighted list of static meshes, where each entry also carries the component settings and the material variants its mesh spawns with. That payload is the whole difference from the other collection types: a Static Mesh reference, an ISM and an SM descriptor, and an optional set of weighted material overrides picked alongside the entry itself. Weights, categories, tags, sub-collections, fitting and properties are the shared collection anatomy and behave here exactly as they do everywhere else.
UPCGExMeshCollection.situation: A prop library that scatters as instanced meshes, where a handful of entries need to come out in more than one material.

mechanism.text: Entries arrive by dropping meshes onto the collection, and a mesh some entry already references is skipped rather than added a second time. Two batch tools act on the whole list at once: one clears collision on every entry's descriptors, the other sets every entry's `Descriptor Source`. A staging rebuild loads each entry's mesh once, bakes its bounding box as the entry's bounds and one managed socket per mesh socket, then releases it; a socket added to a mesh asset afterwards appears on the next rebuild, not before. A pick names the entry and, when that entry has variants, one of them, both travelling in the same hash. At spawn the entry's descriptor is what configures the component: the mesh spawner route builds its instances from ISM Settings with the picked materials applied on top, while Staging : Spline Mesh builds its components from SM Settings.

GlobalDescriptorMode.semantics: Overrule forces every entry through the collection's globals, and an individual entry can also opt in on its own by setting its `Descriptor Source` to `Global` while this rule stays on `Per Entry`. Resolving through the globals additionally appends the collection's `Collection Tags` to the spawned component's tags, which an entry spawning from its own descriptor does not do.
GlobalDescriptorMode.trap: Overrule reaches the mesh spawner route only. Staging : Spline Mesh builds its components straight from the entry's own SM Settings without consulting the collection, so the global descriptors never change what it spawns.

GlobalISMDescriptor.semantics: The globals carry no asset of their own, so an entry resolving through them still spawns its own `Static Mesh`: a mesh set in this descriptor's own mesh field is overwritten during resolution and never spawns.

fields.name: bVisible
fields.tooltip: Controls whether the component is rendered in the scene.

fields.name: MinDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: The minimum distance at which the primitive should be rendered, measured in world space units from the center of the primitive's bounding sphere to the camera position.

fields.name: LDMaxDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: Max draw distance exposed to LDs. The real max draw distance is the min (disregarding 0) of this and volumes affecting this object.

fields.name: IndirectLightingCacheQuality
fields.tooltip: Quality of indirect lighting for Movable primitives.  This has a large effect on Indirect Lighting Cache update time.

fields.name: LightmapType
fields.tooltip: Controls the type of lightmap used for this component.

fields.name: HLODBatchingPolicy
fields.tooltip: Determines how the geometry of a component will be incorporated in proxy (simplified) HLODs.
Controls whether the static mesh component's backface culling should be reversed

fields.name: BodyInstance
fields.tooltip: Physics scene information for this component, holds a single rigid body with multiple shapes.

fields.name: ShadowCacheInvalidationBehavior
fields.tooltip: Control shadow invalidation behavior, in particular with respect to Virtual Shadow Maps and material effects like World Position Offset.

fields.name: CanCharacterStepUpOn
fields.tooltip: Determine whether a Character can step up onto this component. This controls whether they can try to step up on it when they bump in to it, not whether they can walk on it after landing on it. @see FWalkableSlopeOverride

fields.name: LightingChannels
fields.tooltip: Channels that this component should be in.  Lights with matching channels will affect the component. These channels only apply to opaque materials, direct lighting, and dynamic lighting and shadowing.

fields.name: RayTracingGroupId
fields.tooltip: Defines run-time groups of components. For example allows to assemble multiple parts of a building at runtime. -1 means that component doesn't belong to any group.

fields.name: CustomDepthStencilValue
fields.tooltip: Optionally write this 0-255 value to the stencil buffer in CustomDepth pass (Requires project setting or r.CustomDepth == 3)

fields.name: TranslucencySortPriority
fields.tooltip: Translucent objects with a lower sort priority draw behind objects with a higher priority. Translucent objects with the same priority are rendered from back-to-front based on their bounds origin. This setting is also used to sort objects being drawn into a runtime virtual texture. Ignored if the object is not translucent.  The default priority is zero. Warning: This should never be set to a non-default value unless you know what you are doing, as it will prevent the renderer from sorting correctly. It is especially problematic on dynamic gameplay effects.

fields.name: TranslucencySortDistanceOffset
fields.tooltip: Modified sort distance offset for translucent objects in world units. A positive number will move the sort distance further and a negative number will move the distance closer. Ignored if the object is not translucent. Warning: Adjusting this value will prevent the renderer from correctly sorting based on distance.  Only modify this value if you are certain it will not cause visual artifacts.

fields.name: RuntimeVirtualTextures
fields.tooltip: Array of runtime virtual textures into which we draw the mesh for this actor. The material also needs to be set up to output to a virtual texture.

fields.name: VirtualTextureLodBias
fields.tooltip: Bias to the LOD selected for rendering to runtime virtual textures.

fields.name: VirtualTextureCullMips
fields.tooltip: Number of lower mips in the runtime virtual texture to skip for rendering this primitive. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture. This culling method doesn't take into account primitive size or virtual texture size.

fields.name: VirtualTextureMinCoverage
fields.tooltip: Set the minimum pixel coverage before culling from the runtime virtual texture. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture.

fields.name: VirtualTextureRenderPassType
fields.tooltip: Controls if this component draws in the main pass as well as in the virtual texture.

fields.name: BoundsScale
fields.tooltip: Scales the bounds of the object. This is useful when using World Position Offset to animate the vertices of the object outside of its bounds. Warning: Increasing the bounds of an object will reduce performance and shadow quality! Currently only used by StaticMeshComponent and SkeletalMeshComponent.

fields.name: RayTracingGroupCullingPriority
fields.tooltip: Defines how quickly it should be culled. For example buildings should have a low priority, but small dressing should have a high priority.

fields.name: CustomDepthStencilWriteMask
fields.tooltip: Mask used for stencil buffer writes.

fields.name: OverrideMaterials
fields.tooltip: Material overrides.

fields.name: OverlayMaterial
fields.tooltip: Translucent material to blend on top of this mesh. Mesh will be rendered twice - once with a base material and once with overlay material

fields.name: OverlayMaterialMaxDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: The max draw distance for overlay material. A distance of 0 indicates that overlay will be culled using primitive max distance.

fields.name: SplineMeshAxis
fields.tooltip: Relevant when used with PCGEx' spline mesh nodes

fields.name: ForcedLodModel
fields.tooltip: If 0, auto-select LOD level. if >0, force to (ForcedLodModel-1).

fields.name: MinLOD
fields.tooltip: Specifies the smallest LOD that will be used for this component. This is ignored if ForcedLodModel is enabled.

fields.name: WireframeColorOverride
fields.tooltip: Wireframe color to use if bOverrideWireframeColor is true

fields.name: WorldPositionOffsetDisableDistance
fields.tooltip: Distance at which to disable World Position Offset for an entire instance (0 = Never disable WPO).

fields.name: OverriddenLightMapRes
fields.tooltip: Light map resolution to use on this component, used if bOverrideLightMapRes is true and there is a valid StaticMesh.

fields.name: DistanceFieldIndirectShadowMinVisibility
fields.display: Distance Field Indirect Shadow Min Visibility
fields.tooltip: Controls how dark the dynamic indirect shadow can be.

fields.name: DistanceFieldSelfShadowBias
fields.tooltip: Useful for reducing self shadowing from distance field methods when using world position offset to animate the mesh's vertices.

fields.name: StreamingDistanceMultiplier
fields.tooltip: Allows adjusting the desired resolution of streaming textures that uses UV 0.  1.0 is the default, whereas a higher value increases the streamed-in resolution.

fields.name: LightmassSettings
fields.tooltip: The Lightmass settings for this object.

Entries.semantics: On top of the shared entry fields, a mesh entry adds `Static Mesh`, its material variants, and a pair of component descriptors. `Single Slot` holds a flat weighted list of materials, all written to the one slot named by `Slot Index`; `Multi Slots` makes each weighted variant a small list of slot-and-material pairs, so a single roll can restyle several slots at once. The variant is rolled per point at pick time and rides in the same hash as the entry, which is what lets materials be re-rolled later without disturbing which mesh was chosen.
Entries.trap: A `Multi Slots` override row left at the default `Slot Index` of -1 writes to slot 0 rather than to its position in the row list, so a variant authored without setting indices puts every material on slot 0 and the last row wins.

hints.text: The first time an entry is staged its ISM and SM collision is forced to No Collision, once, because the `Disable Collision By Default` project setting in the plugin's Collections section is on out of the box. Later rebuilds leave it alone, so collision re-enabled on an entry sticks; only an entry that has never been staged starts from No Collision.

UPCGExMeshSelectorStaged.name: Staging Data
