UPCGExMeshSelectorStaged.purpose: Instanced-mesh spawning is what the vanilla Static Mesh Spawner already does, and this is what teaches it to read staged picks. It is not a node: it is picked as the spawner's Mesh Selector Type, where it is listed as Staging Data, and from there it resolves every point's pick against the Collection Map and hands the spawner its instance lists, carrying the entry's mesh, its tags, its component descriptor and the pick's material variant. Custom properties the collections declare can also be packed into the spawned component's Custom Primitive Data, which puts collection-authored values in reach of materials with no attribute plumbing. Picks that resolved to something other than a mesh entry contribute nothing, so a mixed staged dataset can be wired straight in, and skinned mesh entries have their own selector for the vanilla Skinned Mesh Spawner, configured the same way.
UPCGExMeshSelectorStaged.situation: A staged dataset reaches a Static Mesh Spawner, and the meshes have to come out with the descriptors, tags and material variants their collections authored.

mechanism.text: One execution takes the points on the spawner's input and the Collection Map on the spawner's override pin: every attribute set wired there is examined, the ones carrying a Map are read, and anything else on that pin stays the spawner's business. Points are grouped by their pick, and the spawner receives one instance list per distinct entry and material variant, however many points share it, which is what decides how many instanced components come out. Picks that resolve to an entry which is not a mesh contribute no instances, and their points are otherwise untouched.
steps: The entry's component descriptor is resolved: the Descriptor Override struct while Use Template Descriptor is on, the entry's own descriptor (or its collection's globals) when it is off.
The entry's tags are appended to the component tags either way.
Force Disable Collisions clears collision on the resolved descriptor, so it wins over whichever descriptor supplied it.
The pick's material variant is written into the descriptor's material slots, over whatever the descriptor put there.
Custom properties are packed into the component's Custom Primitive Data.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this selector reads staged picks from (and strips from output points). None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>). Other layers' attributes pass through untouched.

bApplyMaterialOverrides.semantics: This governs the pick's material variant and nothing else. An entry's own descriptor materials belong to its descriptor, so turning this off does not strip materials: it spawns every instance of an entry with that entry's descriptor materials, whichever variant the pick recorded.

bForceDisableCollisions.semantics: Applied after the descriptor is resolved, so it clears collision whichever descriptor supplied it, the override struct or the entry's own.

TemplateDescriptor.tooltip: Ignores per-entry collection descriptors, pushing only mesh, materials & tags. On by default for legacy reasons -- turn it off if your collections set per-entry details.
TemplateDescriptor.semantics: On, every instance is built from the Descriptor Override struct and the entry contributes only its mesh and its tags. Off, each entry brings its own component descriptor, or its collection's globals when the entry defers to them or the collection overrules, and its tags are appended to that.
TemplateDescriptor.trap: Collections that author per-entry component details have every one of them ignored while this is on, and it is on by default.

bUseTimeSlicing.semantics: Spreads the grouping of points across several executions instead of doing it in one pass, so a large staged dataset does not hold the editor for the duration. The result is identical either way.

bOutputPoints.semantics: On, the spawner's point output is a copy of its input with this layer's pick attribute removed. Picks on other layers survive, so points staged on several layers stay staged for the consumers of those layers.
bOutputPoints.trap: Off skips the copy rather than emptying the pin. The editor always builds an output for inspection, so the pin still carries one point per input point, none of them written.

bQuietMissingStagingDataWarning.tooltip: When enabled, silently skips input data that is missing the staging hash attribute instead of logging an error.
bQuietMissingStagingDataWarning.semantics: Skipped data produces no instances and comes out with zero points, silently.

CustomPrimitiveDataLayout.tooltip: No ShowOnlyInnerProperties: it re-categorizes promoted members under THEIR own Category, scattering them into "Settings" instead of showing them here.

fields.name: bQuietMissingPropertyWarnings
fields.tooltip: Silences the not-declared warning -- expected when one layout spans differing collection schemas.

fields.name: PopulateFromSchema
fields.tooltip: Assign to append its properties as rows; cleared on use, so it never becomes a live dependency.

CustomPrimitiveDataLayout.semantics: Each row names a custom property declared on the collections in play and reserves as many floats as that property's type needs. An offset of -1 appends the row after the previous one; a pinned offset holds its slot, which is what keeps a material reading a fixed index reading the same value after the rows above it change. Rows no collection declares keep the property's default instead of closing the gap they held, and rows that do not fit the engine's Custom Primitive Data float budget are dropped. Populate From expands a Property Schema asset into rows once, at authoring time, then clears itself, so editing the schema later never re-lays-out the graph.
CustomPrimitiveDataLayout.trap: One layout serves every collection in the Map, including collections whose entries this spawner never instances. When two of them declare the same property name with different types, the first in asset-path order decides the slot and the others fall back to their defaults.

bDebugCustomPrimitiveData.tooltip: Logs the resolved layout and each entry's floats. PCGNoHash: hashing diagnostics would rebuild every ISM on toggle.

hints.text: A mesh selector is a vanilla concept: the swappable brain inside the Static Mesh Spawner. It is unrelated to the Selector sub-nodes that decide picks upstream, which are a PCGEx system of their own. The two meet in this one place.

## The Map goes into the spawner's override pin

The Static Mesh Spawner has no Map input of its own, so wire the Collection Map into the node's override pin. Without it the selector resolves nothing, reports that it found no Map in the overrides, and spawns nothing, while its point output still carries the points as if the node had run.

UPCGExMeshToClustersSettings.name: Mesh to Clusters
UPCGExMeshToClustersSettings.purpose: Reads a static mesh asset and hands back its topology as a cluster, once per target point. The mesh supplies the structure and the points supply the placement, so one point with a mesh reference gives one cluster shaped like that mesh and a thousand points give a thousand copies of it. `Graph Output Type` decides what the structure is: the mesh's own vertices joined by its triangle sides, the dual made of triangle centroids, a hollow version joining centroids to their corners, or the open border of a surface that is not closed. **Dynamic Mesh to Clusters** is the sibling for geometry arriving on a wire rather than named by asset.
UPCGExMeshToClustersSettings.situation: A static mesh already carries the connectivity wanted, and it has to become cluster data at one or more places in the world.

mechanism.text: One point dataset in, and each point of it names a static mesh. Every distinct mesh named is read once and turned into a cluster, and every target point then receives its own copy of that cluster, moved onto the point by `Transform Details`. The output holds one Vtx dataset per target that resolved a mesh, paired with one Edges dataset per connected component of the mesh, alongside the untransformed originals on **BaseMeshData**, one per distinct mesh. `Graph Output Type` alone decides what becomes a Vtx and what becomes an Edge. The target point contributes its transform and nothing else: none of its attributes reach the cluster.

off_label.claim: A mesh is a way of authoring a cluster shape by hand, which makes this a stamper: the asset is read once however many targets there are, and every target gets its own copy at its own transform.
off_label.grounded_in: FGeoStaticMeshMap::FindOrAdd keys unique meshes by asset path and extracts each one once, and PCGExGraphTask::FCopyGraphToPoint duplicates the compiled vtx and edges per target before transforming the copy

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: The points naming the meshes and placing the results. A single dataset, and the pin takes one connection.

inputs.label: UV Imports
inputs.note: Attribute sets pairing a name with a channel index, adding to the mappings authored inline.
inputs.condition: when Import Details has Import UVs on

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One dataset per target point that resolved a mesh.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component of each target's copy.

outputs.label: BaseMeshData
outputs.note: The clusters before any copy or transform, one per distinct mesh named across the targets. Advanced, and off the main flow.

GraphOutputType.semantics: `Raw Triangles` maps the mesh's vertices onto Vtx and each triangle's three sides onto Edges, with a side shared by two triangles arriving as one edge; triangles themselves are not carried, so a quad reads as four sides plus the diagonal that split it. `Dual Graph` replaces all of that: one Vtx per triangle, sitting at its centroid, and an Edge wherever two triangles share a side, so the mesh's own vertices are gone. `Hollow Graph` keeps the mesh vertices and adds the centroids, joining each centroid to its triangle's three corners and dropping the triangle sides, so the result is a fan per triangle and no closed triangle outline. `Boundaries` keeps only the vertices sitting on a side that belongs to a single triangle, joined by those sides.
GraphOutputType.trap: `Boundaries` reads the open border of a surface rather than a silhouette or an outer shell, so a closed mesh has no such side and produces nothing at all for that target. For an outer shell of a point set, **Cluster : Convex Hull 3D** is the node.

StaticMesh.tooltip: Mesh source. Attribute path can be FString, FName or FSoftObjectPath.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

StaticMesh.semantics: As a constant it names one mesh for every target and a mesh that fails to load cancels the node outright. Switched to an attribute it is read per target, so one Targets dataset can carry several meshes and each point brings its own.

AttributeHandling.semantics: Reads only when `Static Mesh` is on its attribute setting. `StaticMesh Soft Path` takes the value as the asset path of the mesh. `Actor Reference` resolves the value to an actor and takes the mesh off the first Static Mesh Component it finds on it, so an actor holding several meshes contributes one of them and the rest are not read.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: How to scale objects to fit within target bounds.

fields.name: Justification
fields.tooltip: How to align objects within target bounds after scaling.

fields.name: bInheritScale
fields.tooltip: Multiply result scale by the target point's scale.

fields.name: bInheritRotation
fields.tooltip: Rotate result by the target point's rotation.

fields.name: bIgnoreBounds
fields.tooltip: Skip bounds calculations and use position only. Disables scale-to-fit and justification.

TransformDetails.semantics: Applies to the copy as a whole, mesh-local coordinates moved onto the target. With `Inherit Scale` and `Inherit Rotation` both off, which is how they ship, only the position moves and every Vtx keeps the orientation and scale the mesh gave it, which is what leaves an imported vertex normal pointing where it was. The scale-to-fit and justification rows above them fit the whole cluster into the target point's bounds.

ImportDetails.tooltip: Which data should be imported from the static mesh onto the generated points

bIgnoreMeshWarnings.tooltip: Skip invalid meshes & do not throw warning about them.
bIgnoreMeshWarnings.semantics: A target whose mesh cannot be resolved is skipped and produces no cluster, so the output can hold fewer Vtx datasets than there were target points. This decides whether that is announced, never whether it happens.

VertexMergeHashTolerance.tooltip: Set tolerance for merging vertices, such as those found at split vertices along hard edges or UV seams. The value is clamped to be no less than a small positive value to prevent division by zero errors.
VertexMergeHashTolerance.semantics: The cell size of the grid that decides which of the mesh's raw vertices are the same Vtx. A mesh splits its vertices at hard edges and UV seams, so the raw count is well above the visible one, and this is what puts them back together. Too large and distinct vertices weld into one, which shows up as edges that were never in the mesh; the value is held above zero, so some merging always happens.

bPreciseVertexMerge.tooltip: Use two overlapping spatial hashes to detect vertex proximity. More accurate, but slightly slower and uses slightly more memory during processing. (Specifically, the overhead is two hash lookups versus one per vertex, and memory overhead is on the order of 2 to 3 MB for 100K vertices.)
bPreciseVertexMerge.semantics: Adds a second lookup half a cell offset from the first, so two vertices inside the tolerance of each other but on opposite sides of a cell boundary still land on one Vtx. Off, that pair comes through as two.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: Runs on the mesh's cluster once, before any copy is made, so a component it discards is missing from every target rather than from some of them. It applies in every `Graph Output Type`.

hints.text: The mesh read is LOD 0 of the asset's render data, which is the built geometry rather than the source model, so what arrives as Vtx is what the engine renders at full detail.

UPCGExMetaCleanupSettings.name: Meta Cleanup
UPCGExMetaCleanupSettings.purpose: Deletes attributes and tags by name, with two independent name filters and string matching rather than an exact list. Attributes and tags are decided separately, so one node can strip every working attribute while leaving the tags alone, or the reverse. It works on anything, points or attribute sets alike, and its usual job is trimming the debris a long graph accumulates before the data is handed on.
UPCGExMetaCleanupSettings.situation: A subgraph is about to return data carrying a dozen intermediate attributes nobody downstream should see.

mechanism.text: Everything on the input pin comes out on the output pin, same order, same count, same points. The only change is which attributes and which tags survive. Each attribute name and each tag is tested against its own filter, and what fails the test is deleted. Nothing is renamed, no value is touched, and the node has no opinion on element data at all. A dataset with nothing to delete is passed straight through without being copied.

off_label.claim: Set the attribute filter to Include with a list of the names to survive and the node becomes a whitelist gate for a subgraph boundary, deleting anything a caller was not meant to see, including names nobody anticipated.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExAttributeFilter::Include returns a keep verdict only for matched names, and GetPrunableIdentifiers deletes everything the test rejects

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Anything carrying metadata: points, attribute sets, spatial data.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same data, mirroring the input type, minus the attributes and tags the filters rejected.

pins.dynamic: The output pin takes the type of whatever is wired to the input, because the node never changes the shape of what passes through it.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

Filters.semantics: Two filters, read independently: one for attribute names, one for tags. Both are name tests, not value tests, so nothing here can decide by what an attribute contains. The rows this block carries for carry-over work are hidden on this node, which is the delete-only form of the same settings.

bDrawAsCompactNode.tooltip: Whether to draw this node as a compact node

hints.text: `Preserve PCGEx Data`, on both filters, is what keeps the plugin's own attributes and tags out of the deletion. Turning it off on cluster data removes the endpoint ids and the pair tags, which is what makes a Vtx and Edges pair a pair: every cluster node downstream then refuses the data.

UPCGExModularSortPointsSettings.name: Sort Points
UPCGExModularSortPointsSettings.purpose: Reorders the points inside each dataset by a stack of rules wired in as sub-nodes. Order is a real property of point data in PCGEx, since a path is only an ordered set of points, so this is how an arbitrary set becomes a sequence. The rules are composable: each one compares one attribute, and the next only speaks when the previous ties.
UPCGExModularSortPointsSettings.situation: Points that arrived in whatever order a generator produced, and need a deliberate order before something downstream reads them as a sequence.

mechanism.text: The rules on the Sorting Rules pin are put in ascending Priority order, and each dataset's points are compared pairwise against them: the first rule whose values differ by more than its tolerance decides, and equal values fall through to the next. Sort Direction flips the whole comparison rather than any single rule, which each rule can then invert for itself. Every dataset is sorted independently and none of them exchange points; the output is a duplicate with the same points in a new order.

off_label.claim: A rule reading a data tag rather than a point attribute gives every point in one dataset the same value, which does nothing here on its own but makes a useful outermost rule when a later rule breaks the tie: the points end up grouped by dataset within one merged set.
off_label.grounded_in: the sort rule config's data-tag mode resolves one value per data, documented as shared by every point in that data

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The point datasets to reorder.

inputs.label: Sorting Rules
inputs.note: Sorting Rule sub-nodes. Required: with none wired the node reports that it has no attributes to sort over and cancels.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: A duplicate of each input, same points and same count, in the new order.

SortDirection.tooltip: Controls the order in which points will be ordered.
SortDirection.semantics: Applied to the stack as a whole. A rule that needs to run against the grain carries its own inversion, so mixed directions are expressed per rule rather than here.

hints.text: A dataset whose rules cannot bind, a misspelled attribute being the usual cause, is reported once and left in its original order rather than failing the node. The warning is the only sign it happened.

UPCGExModuloCompareFilterProviderSetting.name: Filter : Modulo Compare
UPCGExModuloCompareFilterProviderSetting.purpose: Divides a value by a base and tests what is left over, which is how a repeating pattern becomes a pass or fail. Three operands carry it: Operand A is the value, Operand B the base, Operand C what the remainder is measured against, and each of the last two is a constant or an attribute read on the element. All three are doubles, so this is a floating-point remainder with no rounding and no integer step anywhere in it, and a base of 2.5 is as valid as a base of 3. Point Operand A, and any operand you read from an attribute, at `@Data.` attributes and the filter answers once per dataset instead of once per element, which is what Uber Branch and Break require of every filter they are handed and what lets Uber Filter (Data) judge a dataset in one question.
UPCGExModuloCompareFilterProviderSetting.situation: Every Nth element of an ordered set, or every value that lands near a multiple of some angle or spacing.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. The remainder of Operand A divided by Operand B is compared against Operand C with the chosen operator. That remainder keeps the sign of Operand A, so a negative value yields a negative remainder and the ordering operators see it that way. A base that comes out as zero once its offset is added is the one case with nothing to divide, and the verdict is then Zero Result; every other value goes through the comparison, an Operand A of zero included.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so it is accepted on every filter pin, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

fields.name: OperandA
fields.tooltip: Operand A for testing -- Will be translated to `double` under the hood.

fields.name: OperandBSource
fields.tooltip: Type of OperandB

fields.name: OperandB
fields.tooltip: Operand B for testing (Modulo base) -- Will be translated to `double` under the hood.

fields.name: OperandBConstant
fields.tooltip: Operand B for testing

fields.name: OperandBOffset
fields.tooltip: A static constant offset added to OperandB. Useful when dealing with angle or wider multples of (i.e 180d)

fields.name: Comparison
fields.tooltip: Comparison

fields.name: CompareAgainst
fields.tooltip: Type of OperandC

fields.name: OperandC
fields.tooltip: Operand C for testing -- Will be translated to `double` under the hood.

fields.name: OperandCConstant
fields.tooltip: Operand C for testing

fields.name: Tolerance
fields.tooltip: Near-equality tolerance

fields.name: bCyclicRemainder
fields.tooltip: Treat the modulo remainder as cyclic for ~= / ~!= : a remainder near 0 or near B both count as "near a multiple". No effect on ordering comparisons.

fields.name: ZeroResult
fields.tooltip: Result to return when the modulo base (Operand B + Offset) is zero.

hints.text: The strict operators are exact comparisons on a floating-point remainder. `==` against 0 holds only where the division comes out exact, which integer-valued attributes manage and measured or scaled values mostly do not; the near variants exist for that reason and are the shipped default.

UPCGExMovePivotSettings.name: Move Pivot
UPCGExMovePivotSettings.purpose: Moves a point's origin somewhere else inside its own bounds, without moving what the bounds enclose. A point's position is where its pivot sits, so relocating the pivot changes where the point reports itself to be and what everything downstream measures from, while the volume stays put. It is the node for making a point report its own base, corner or top rather than its centre.
UPCGExMovePivotSettings.situation: Points that need to sit on the ground by their base rather than by their middle, before anything spawns or samples from them.

mechanism.text: The pivot is named as a normalised position inside the bounds, so the same setting means the same corner whatever size a point is. Moving it shifts the position and rebalances the bounds around the new origin, leaving the enclosed volume where it was in the world. Nothing is scaled or rotated, and no point is added or removed.

UVW.tooltip: Normalized position within bounds where the pivot should be placed.
UVW.semantics: Normalised across the bounds rather than measured in world units, so 0 is one face, 1 is the opposite face and 0.5 is the middle on each axis. Points of different sizes therefore land on the same relative spot rather than the same offset, which is what makes one setting work across a varied scatter. Values outside the zero-to-one range put the pivot outside the bounds, which is legal and reports a position the volume does not contain.

hints.text: Everything that reads a point's position reads the new pivot, so a graph that samples or measures after this node is measuring from somewhere else than it was before. Moving pivots late, after the measuring is done, avoids having to reason about which stage saw which origin.

UPCGExMovingAverageSmoothing.name: Moving Average
UPCGExMovingAverageSmoothing.purpose: Averages a run of consecutive points around each point. `Smoothing` on **Path : Smooth** is a count of points to either side, and a contributor's weight falls off in a straight line from the target out to the edge of that run. It reaches points by their place in the order and by nothing else, so two stretches of a path that pass close to one another never touch. This is the rule a fresh **Path : Smooth** ships with.
UPCGExMovingAverageSmoothing.situation: A path whose points are noisy step to step and whose order is meaningful, a traced or generated run where near in the sequence is what near should mean.

mechanism.text: For each point it walks the run from `Smoothing` points before it to `Smoothing` points after it, the point itself included, and weights each one by how far it sits from the centre: full weight at the target, falling in a straight line to nothing at the two ends of the run. The outermost slot on each side therefore contributes no weight at all, so the effective reach is one point short of `Smoothing` on each side. `Smoothing` is read as a whole number of points and anything below one leaves the point exactly as it arrived. A closed path wraps the run around the seam; an open path has to decide what to do where the run overhangs the end, and `Index Safety` is that decision.

off_label.claim: Set `Index Safety` to `Tile` on an open path and the two ends start feeding each other, which pulls them together: it is a way to prepare an open path for closing without moving anything else by hand.
off_label.grounded_in: The open-path branch runs SanitizeIndex with the chosen mode, and Tile wraps an out-of-range index around to the far end of the array

IndexSafety.semantics: Reaches open paths only: a closed path wraps its run around the seam whatever this says. What each entry supplies where the run overhangs the end is the whole of its effect. `Ignore` drops the slots that do not exist, so an endpoint gets half a run and is dragged inward by the neighbours it does have. `Clamp` fills every missing slot with the endpoint itself, which weighs the endpoint heavily against its own neighbours and holds it close to where it started. `Tile` reaches around to the far end of the path, so the two ends of an open path start blending into each other. `Yoyo` folds the run back into the path, mirroring the points just inside the end.
IndexSafety.trap: `Ignore` is the shipped default and it is the entry that moves the endpoints. Holding them exactly still is `Preserve Start` and `Preserve End` on **Path : Smooth**, not a value here.

UPCGExNearestPointCheckFilterProviderSet.name: Filter : Check Nearest
UPCGExNearestPointCheckFilterProviderSet.purpose: Redirects the question to a different point. Every other point filter asks something about the element in front of it; this one locates the nearest point on the Targets pin and runs a whole filter stack against that point instead, so an element's verdict describes its neighbour. Any filter goes on the Point Filters pin, Filter Group included, which is what separates this from the Compare Nearest filters: those read one named value off the nearest target, this runs an arbitrary condition on it. Any In Range widens the question from the single closest target to every target inside the search radius, passing as soon as one of them satisfies the stack.
UPCGExNearestPointCheckFilterProviderSet.situation: Whether an element survives depends on what the point nearest to it looks like, not on anything the element itself carries.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element. The nearest point on the Targets pin is found, and the filters wired to Point Filters are run against that point inside its own dataset, so every attribute they name has to exist on the target data rather than on the data being filtered. Those filters combine as an AND stack: the element passes when the target satisfies all of them, and Invert flips that answer. Max Distance, read on the element being tested, bounds the search; when no target qualifies the stack never runs and No Target Fallback supplies the verdict, which Invert leaves alone.

off_label.claim: Turn Ignore Self off and wire one dataset into both the consumer and the Targets pin: each element then finds its nearest neighbour inside its own set, and the sub-filters become a description of what that neighbour has to look like.
off_label.grounded_in: the bSelf plus matching-index skip in PCGExMatching::FTargetsHandler::FindClosestTarget, which excludes only the probe element, while FNearestFilter::Init adds the whole dataset to IgnoreList only when bIgnoreSelf is set

inputs.note: The points searched for the nearest one. Several datasets are accepted and pooled into a single search.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: The filters run against the candidate target. Anything carrying the point-filter type goes here; several of them on the pin all have to pass.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: Match rules deciding which target datasets each tested dataset is allowed to see. The pin is always present, sitting among the advanced pins until Data Matching is switched on.
inputs.condition: when Data Matching Mode is All or Any

outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: An empty Targets pin does not stop the node. Holding a data input of its own is what makes Missing Data Policy live here, and its default of Fail replaces this node's output with an always-false filter, so every element is rejected with nothing in the log to explain it.

The sub-filters bind against the target datasets, so an attribute name that exists on the data being filtered but not on the targets is a binding failure on the targets, settled before any element is tested.

UPCGExNeighborSampleBlendSettings.name: Sampler : Vtx Blend
UPCGExNeighborSampleBlendSettings.purpose: Blends attribute values from a Vtx's neighbours back onto it. What blending means per attribute is not fixed here: the blend operations wired to its own pin decide that, so one sampler can average some attributes, take the maximum of others and copy the rest in a single pass. It is the sampler for smoothing and propagating values along a cluster.
UPCGExNeighborSampleBlendSettings.situation: Values that should even out along connections, or spread outward from where they were authored.

mechanism.text: For each Vtx the shared walk gathers its neighbours, and every blend operation on the pin folds that neighbourhood's values into one result per attribute. The weights come from the shared config, so how much a distant neighbour counts is settled there rather than here. An attribute no operation names is left alone.

off_label.claim: Running it repeatedly is diffusion along the cluster: each pass carries values one neighbourhood further, so a value authored on a few Vtx spreads outward a controlled distance per run.
off_label.grounded_in: Each pass reads the current attribute values and writes blended results back, so a later pass reads what the previous one wrote.

inputs.label: Blend Ops
inputs.note: Per-attribute blend operations. Without any, the sampler has nothing to fold and writes nothing.

outputs.label: Sampler
outputs.note: The sampling definition, read by **Cluster : Sample Neighbors**.

hints.text: The operations on the Blend Ops pin are the whole configurable surface here: this sampler contributes the neighbourhood and the weights, and the operations contribute everything about the result. An attribute no operation names is left alone.

UPCGExNeighborSampleFiltersSettings.name: Sampler : Test Neighbors
UPCGExNeighborSampleFiltersSettings.purpose: Counts how many of a Vtx's neighbours pass a test. Where **Sampler : Vtx Blend** carries values across connections, this carries a verdict: the filters decide what qualifies and the result is a number per Vtx, which a filter downstream can then act on. It is how a graph asks structural questions like how many neighbours are of a kind.
UPCGExNeighborSampleFiltersSettings.situation: Vtx that should be classified by what surrounds them rather than by anything they carry themselves.

mechanism.text: For each Vtx the shared walk gathers its neighbours, each one is put to the filters, and the count that passed is written. The shared config decides which neighbours are gathered in the first place, so the count is over the reached set rather than over the whole cluster. A Vtx with no neighbours in reach counts zero, which is the same answer as a Vtx whose neighbours all failed.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: The test each neighbour is put to. Without any there is nothing to count against.

outputs.label: Sampler
outputs.note: The sampling definition, read by **Cluster : Sample Neighbors**.

UPCGExNeighborSampleProviderSettings.name: Sampler : Abstract
UPCGExNeighborSampleProviderSettings.purpose: The base every Sampler sub-node inherits, and the page for the settings they all share. A sampler describes what to read from a Vtx's neighbours; **Cluster : Sample Neighbors** is what runs it. How far the walk reaches, what counts as a neighbour, and how distance turns into weight are the same questions on every sampler and are answered here.
UPCGExNeighborSampleProviderSettings.situation: Reading one of the Sampler nodes and needing to know which of its settings are its own and which reach it from here.

mechanism.text: A sampler emits a factory on the Samplers pin. When the consumer runs, each Vtx walks outward through the cluster to `Max Depth` and gathers what it reaches, and the sampler decides what to do with the gathered values. The shared config settles the walk: how deep it goes, whether it collects Vtx or edges, and how each neighbour's contribution is weighted, either by how many steps away it is or by how far in world units. The weight curve reshapes that falloff.

Priority.semantics: Orders the samplers on the consumer's pin. It matters when two samplers write the same attribute, since the later one lands on top, and not otherwise.

hints.text: `Max Depth` ships at 1, so out of the box a sampler reads only a Vtx's immediate neighbours. Raising it grows the gathered set by roughly the cluster's branching factor per step, which is the setting that turns a cheap pass into an expensive one.

`Blend Over` decides whether the falloff is measured in steps or in world distance. Over index, a neighbour two edges away always counts the same wherever it is; over distance, `Max Distance` decides, and long edges can put an immediate neighbour beyond reach.
`Neighbor Source` decides whether the walk collects the Vtx it reaches or the edges it crosses, which changes what the sampler is reading from rather than how far it goes.

UPCGExNodeAdjacencyFilterProviderSetting.name: Vtx Filter : Adjacency
UPCGExNodeAdjacencyFilterProviderSetting.purpose: Judges a Vtx by the numbers carried on the things it touches. One value read on the Vtx is compared against a value read on each neighbouring Vtx, or on each edge reaching it, and `Adjacency` settles how those per-neighbour answers become a single verdict: every neighbour has to satisfy the test, or a count of them, or a share of them. The same setting can instead collapse the neighbours into one number first, their average, smallest, largest or total, and run the comparison once against that. Those two shapes are what make a local maximum, or a Vtx sitting under its neighbourhood mean, expressible.
UPCGExNodeAdjacencyFilterProviderSetting.situation: A cluster where the test that matters is against the neighbourhood: above every neighbour, below their average, or matching enough of them.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per Vtx and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. Operand A is read on the Vtx under test, from the Vtx dataset. Operand B is read once per neighbour, from the neighbouring Vtx or from the edge that reaches it, and both sides are converted to doubles whatever type they are stored as. `Adjacency` is the only thing deciding how those readings turn into a verdict. Every Vtx the filter is asked about has at least one neighbour, because a point only becomes part of a cluster by being an endpoint of an edge.

off_label.claim: Set Operand A to a constant and the Vtx stops contributing a value at all: with `Consolidation` on `Min`, `Max`, `Sum` or `Average` the filter is then asking a question about the neighbourhood alone, and the Vtx is only the place the question is asked from.
off_label.grounded_in: FNodeAdjacencyFilter::Init taking A from the Constant branch of GetValueSettingOperandA, with the four aggregating sub-tests reading only the neighbour side

outputs.label: Vtx Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the Vtx passport, so **Vtx Filters** pins take it and no other pin does.

hints.text: This node carries no `Invert`, and flipping the comparison operator does not stand in for one. Under `All` the flipped operator asks whether every neighbour satisfies the opposite test, which is a different question from whether any neighbour failed the original. To negate the whole verdict, put the filter alone in a **Filter Group** and invert the group.

UPCGExNodeEdgeAngleFilterProviderSetting.name: Vtx Filter : Edge Angle
UPCGExNodeEdgeAngleFilterProviderSetting.purpose: Sorts a Vtx by how sharply the cluster turns at it. Where exactly two edges meet, the angle between them is measured and compared, which is what separates a Vtx running straight through from a corner or a fold-back. Anywhere else there is no single angle to take, so `Leaves Fallback` answers for a Vtx with one edge and `Non Binary Fallback` for a Vtx with more than two.
UPCGExNodeEdgeAngleFilterProviderSetting.situation: A chain of Vtx running through a cluster, where the corners have to be told apart from the straight runs.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per Vtx and decides what the verdict means; the filter takes no data input of its own and writes nothing. Only a Vtx with exactly two edges is measured. For those, both edges are read as directions leaving the Vtx towards the Vtx at the far end, so the reading is the angle of the corner itself: a Vtx running straight through reads 180 degrees, a square turn reads 90, and two edges folded back onto each other read 0. Positions come from the Vtx transforms as the cluster holds them, in three dimensions and never projected, so a bend out of the working plane counts for as much as one within it. `Dot Comparison Details` turns that reading into a pass or a fail; every other Vtx is answered by one of the two fallbacks with no angle taken at all.

outputs.label: Vtx Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the Vtx passport, so **Vtx Filters** pins take it and no other pin does.

UPCGExNodeEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSet.name: Vtx Filter : Edge Direction
UPCGExNodeEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSet.purpose: Judges a Vtx by where its edges point. One reference direction is settled for the Vtx, either the constant typed into the panel or a vector attribute read on that Vtx, and every edge at the Vtx is compared against it. `Adjacency` then decides how those per-edge answers become a single verdict, which is what lets one node express a Vtx whose every edge climbs, a Vtx with at least two edges heading north, and a Vtx whose edges average out to a given heading. The constant ships as the world up vector, and `Transform Direction` turns whichever reference is in play into one read in the Vtx's own frame.
UPCGExNodeEdgeDirectionFilterProviderSet.situation: A cluster where the Vtx worth keeping are the ones whose connections head a particular way: uphill, along an authored flow vector, or along the Vtx facing.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per Vtx and decides what the verdict means; the filter takes no data input of its own and writes nothing. One reference direction is resolved per Vtx, from the Vtx dataset, and normalised, so only its bearing counts and its length never does. Each edge at the Vtx becomes a direction between the two endpoint positions, read from the Vtx transforms in three dimensions and never projected, with `Direction Order` picking which end it starts at. Every edge is compared against the reference, and `Adjacency` is the only thing that turns those per-edge readings into one verdict for the Vtx.

outputs.label: Vtx Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the Vtx passport, so **Vtx Filters** pins take it and no other pin does.

hints.text: This node carries no verdict-level `Invert`. ` └─ Invert` flips the reference direction, and flipping the operator inside `Dot Comparison Details` negates the per-edge test, but neither negates the verdict: under `Mode` `All` the negated test asks whether every edge fails the original one, which is a different question from whether any edge did. To negate the whole verdict, put the filter alone in a **Filter Group** and invert the group.

UPCGExNodeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.name: Vtx Filter : Num Edges
UPCGExNodeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.purpose: Tests how many edges reach a Vtx. That count is its degree, and the plugin's three named cases sit directly on it: one edge is a leaf, two is binary, more than two is complex. The number the count is measured against can be a constant or an attribute read on the Vtx, so one filter can hold a different expectation at every Vtx.
UPCGExNodeNeighborsCountFilterProviderSe.situation: A cluster where the next node should act on the leaves, on the junctions, or on the runs between them.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per Vtx and decides what the answer means; the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. The count is the number of edges in the Edges dataset naming this Vtx as an endpoint, and it goes on the left of the comparison operator with `Operand A` on the right. Every Vtx the filter is asked about has at least one edge, because a point only becomes part of a cluster by being an endpoint of one, so a test looking for a count of zero matches nothing.

outputs.label: Vtx Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the Vtx passport, so **Vtx Filters** pins take it and no other pin does.

hints.text: The shipped configuration compares the count against 0 with the near-equal operator, and the count is never 0, so an untouched node rejects every Vtx. The symptom shows up at the consumer, which appears to have done nothing at all.

UPCGExNoise3DCausticProviderSettings.name: Noise : Caustic
UPCGExNoise3DCausticProviderSettings.purpose: Not noise in the lattice sense at all: a sum of sine sheets, each rotated by an equal share of a full turn, then sharpened by a power and lifted by a gain until the peaks flatten against the top of the range. Nothing is hashed and nothing is random, which is why Seed does nothing here and the pattern is exactly repeatable and exactly periodic.
UPCGExNoise3DCausticProviderSettings.situation: A regular interference pattern of bright ridges and dark gaps, laid out on a fixed geometry rather than a random one.

mechanism.text: Wave Layers sheets are laid down, layer n turned by n shares of a full turn. Each sheet is three sines of the projected coordinate at related wavelengths, added together, and the sheets are averaged. The result is folded into 0 to 1, raised to the power of Focus, multiplied by Intensity, and clamped to 1. Because the pattern comes from sines rather than hashes, it is fully periodic and Seed never enters it.

UPCGExNoise3DCurlProviderSettings.name: Noise : Curl
UPCGExNoise3DCurlProviderSettings.purpose: The one noise in the family that answers with a real vector rather than one scalar sampled three times. It builds a three-channel Perlin potential field and takes its curl, which gives a field whose vectors circulate instead of converging, and it is what Tensor : Noise is built to read. A scalar consumer gets only the X component of that vector.
UPCGExNoise3DCurlProviderSettings.situation: A direction field that should swirl rather than point at or away from anything, read by a tensor or written to a vector attribute.

mechanism.text: Three Perlin channels, decorrelated by fixed offsets, make up a potential field. Its curl is taken by central differences a distance of Epsilon apart on each axis and scaled by Curl Scale, and each of the three components is then folded into 0 to 1 and put through the shared shaping chain independently. A scalar consumer receives the X component alone, and a four-component consumer receives X, Y and Z plus the length of that already-folded triple.

UPCGExNoise3DFactoryProviderSettings.name: Noise3D Definition
UPCGExNoise3DFactoryProviderSettings.purpose: The base every Noise : node inherits. It never appears in the palette, and this page carries what the sixteen of them share: the Noise pin they all emit on, the position-to-value contract each one answers, the shaping every one applies afterwards, and what happens when several land on one pin. Five nodes read them, and each names the pin differently: Uber Noise and Filter : Noise call it Noises, Tensor : Noise and Tensor : Noise (Bounded) call it Noise nodes, and Selector : Noise Field calls it Noise.
UPCGExNoise3DFactoryProviderSettings.situation: Reading any Noise : page and needing to know what Frequency, Seed, Scale or Blend Mode do, or what two noises on one pin add up to.

mechanism.text: A noise is handed one world position and answers with one number, nominally between 0 and 1. Nothing clamps that, so a noise whose shaping overshoots leaves the range and Scale multiplies whatever came out. A consumer wanting two, three or four components does not get that many independent fields: it gets the same scalar field sampled again at fixed world offsets, and Noise : Curl is the only member of the family that answers with a genuine vector. Several noises on one pin fold into a single value, in Priority order, lowest first.
steps: The position passes through Transform when Apply Transform is on, then is multiplied by Frequency. One lattice cell covers one over Frequency units of that space, so at the default of 0.01 a cell is 100 units wide.
The noise samples its own field there, layering octaves onto it where the node exposes them.
Invert flips the result, the Remap Curve reshapes it, Contrast bends it around 0.5, and Scale multiplies it. Always in that order.
The first noise in Priority order is the base layer. Each later one folds onto the running result through its own Blend Mode, weighted by its own Weight Factor against the running total of weights.

off_label.claim: One factory feeds as many consumers as it is wired to, and each builds its own sampler from the same configuration, so the field they read is identical point for point. Uber Noise writing the field to an attribute and Filter : Noise gating on it are looking at the same numbers.
off_label.grounded_in: UPCGExNoise3DFactoryData::CreateOperation, called per consumer from FNoiseGenerator::Init, carries no state beyond the config

off_label.claim: Weight Factor at 0 mutes a stacked noise without unwiring it, because the weight is clamped up to a value near zero and the blend factor collapses with it. It does nothing to the first noise in Priority order, whose weight is never read.
off_label.grounded_in: FMath::Max(SMALL_NUMBER, ConfigBase.WeightFactor) and BlendFactors[i] = Weight / TotalWeight in FNoiseGenerator::Init

outputs.label: Noise
outputs.note: What every Noise : node emits. Wire it to the Noises pin on Uber Noise or Filter : Noise, to Noise nodes on either Tensor : Noise, or to Noise on Selector : Noise Field.

Priority.tooltip: Noise priority, matters for blending and weighting.
Priority.semantics: Sorts the stack, lowest first. Whichever noise ends up first is the base layer the rest composite onto, and a base layer never has its own Blend Mode or Weight Factor read, so moving a noise to the front of the stack silences two of its settings.

hints.text: Seed does not reseed the field, it slides it. Every noise here that reads Seed at all folds it into the first coordinate of its lattice lookup as a whole number of cells, so at a single octave two noises differing only in Seed carry the same pattern, translated. The ones built on the shared permutation table repeat every 256 seeds, and Noise : Tiling repeats every Period X. Stacking two copies of one noise to get uncorrelated layers wants a different Transform, a different Frequency or a different noise, not a different Seed.

The extra components a vector consumer receives come from resampling the same field at three fixed world offsets of a few hundred units, added before Frequency scales the position. At the default Frequency of 0.01 those land a few cells apart, which decorrelates them. An order of magnitude lower and all three fall inside one cell, so the components come back nearly equal and the vector collapses toward its diagonal.

The 0 to 1 range is a convention each noise keeps on its own, not a floor and ceiling the base enforces. Ridged and Hybrid on Noise : FBM overshoot by design, a Remap Curve authored outside 0 to 1 rescales the output to wherever its keys sit, and Scale multiplies whatever survives. A consumer writing the result straight onto Density takes the overshoot with it.
The Remap Curve is evaluated on every sample whether it was touched or not. Its default is the identity ramp from 0 to 1, so leaving it alone costs a lookup and changes nothing.

UPCGExNoise3DFBMProviderSettings.name: Noise : FBM
UPCGExNoise3DFBMProviderSettings.purpose: A generator, not a modifier. It takes no noise on any pin and layers a Perlin core of its own, which is what makes it the sibling of Noise : Perlin rather than a wrapper around it. What it adds is Variant: five different ways of shaping each octave before it is summed, four of which no other node here offers.
UPCGExNoise3DFBMProviderSettings.situation: Layered Perlin whose octaves need shaping into ridges, bulges or a warped domain rather than plain summation.

mechanism.text: Every variant walks the same octave loop over the same Perlin core, each pass at Lacunarity times the frequency and Persistence times the amplitude of the one before, and folds the sum from minus one to one into 0 to 1. Variant decides what happens to each octave value before it is added, and two of the five replace the normalisation as well, which is why their output leaves the 0 to 1 range.

UPCGExNoise3DFlowProviderSettings.name: Noise : Flow
UPCGExNoise3DFlowProviderSettings.purpose: Perlin with the corner gradients spun in place. Each lattice corner rotates its gradient in the XY plane at a rate of its own, by an angle that Time and Rotation Speed set, so the pattern deforms continuously as Time moves instead of being replaced. At the shipped Time of 0 the gradients are unrotated and this is Noise : Perlin exactly.
UPCGExNoise3DFlowProviderSettings.situation: A field that has to evolve smoothly across a sequence of runs rather than jump to a fresh pattern each time.

mechanism.text: The lattice, the interpolation and the range fold are all Perlin. The difference is the gradient table: instead of the sixteen fixed directions, a 256-entry table of them is built once per execution, each rotated in the XY plane by Time multiplied by Rotation Speed and by that entry own hash. The Z component is never rotated. Time is a setting rather than a clock, so a single execution samples one still field.

off_label.claim: Because Time is an overridable setting, driving it from an attribute or a graph parameter and re-running is what animates this. Nothing inside the node advances it, so two runs at the same Time produce the same field.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExNoiseConfigFlow::Time carried into FPCGExNoiseFlow::PostInitDerived, which builds the rotated gradient table once

UPCGExNoise3DGaborProviderSettings.name: Noise : Gabor
UPCGExNoise3DGaborProviderSettings.purpose: A sum of Gabor kernels, each a cosine wave running along Direction under a bell-shaped envelope, scattered through the lattice. It is the only noise here with a direction setting, and the one whose useful range of Frequency is nothing like the rest of the family: the stripes it exists to produce only appear at a Frequency around 1 or above.
UPCGExNoise3DGaborProviderSettings.situation: A field with a grain to it, running along an axis you choose rather than isotropic in every direction.

mechanism.text: Impulses Per Cell impulses are placed in every cell of the block around the sample, a block whose half-width is Kernel Radius rounded up. Each impulse carries a signed weight and contributes a Gaussian envelope times a cosine of the offset projected onto Direction, and impulses beyond Kernel Radius contribute nothing. The sum is normalised by the square root of the impulse count and folded into 0 to 1. Bandwidth sets the envelope width and the carrier rate together, so the number of stripe cycles inside one kernel comes out equal to Frequency alone.

UPCGExNoise3DMarbleProviderSettings.name: Noise : Marble
UPCGExNoise3DMarbleProviderSettings.purpose: A sine wave along one axis, or out from the origin, whose phase is pushed around by Perlin turbulence. The veins are the sine and the wander is the turbulence, and the two are controlled separately, which is what makes it the node to reach for when a pattern needs a dominant direction that noise alone will not give.
UPCGExNoise3DMarbleProviderSettings.situation: Banded structure with a direction to it: veins, grain, strata, rings.

mechanism.text: One coordinate is picked according to Direction, the three axes or the distance from the origin, and multiplied by Vein Frequency. Perlin turbulence, the absolute value of the noise summed over Turbulence Octaves at a fixed doubling of frequency and halving of amplitude, is scaled by Turbulence Strength and added to that coordinate as a phase offset. A sine of the result gives the bands, optionally sharpened, and is folded into 0 to 1. Bands repeat every 2 over Vein Frequency times Frequency world units, which is 40 at the shipped defaults.

UPCGExNoise3DOpenSimplex2ProviderSetting.name: Noise : OpenSimplex2
UPCGExNoise3DOpenSimplex2ProviderSetting.purpose: Gradient noise sharing Noise : Simplex exact lattice skew and differing in what happens inside the cell. There is no tetrahedron selection here: all eight corners of the surrounding skewed cube contribute every time, through a wider attenuation radius and a set of twenty-four gradient directions laid out on a rhombic dodecahedron rather than the sixteen the rest of the family shares.
UPCGExNoise3DOpenSimplex2ProviderSetting.situation: The same job as Simplex, from a denser gradient set and without the corner-selection branch.

mechanism.text: The position is skewed by the same one-third factor Simplex uses, then unskewed back to give the offset from each of the eight corners of the containing cube. Every corner contributes its gradient dotted with its offset, attenuated by a radial falloff wider than Simplex own so that neighbouring cells overlap; corners far enough out contribute zero and drop out on their own. The sum is normalised and folded into 0 to 1. Octaves above 1 sum successive passes at Lacunarity times the frequency and Persistence times the amplitude.

UPCGExNoise3DPerlinProviderSettings.name: Noise : Perlin
UPCGExNoise3DPerlinProviderSettings.purpose: Gradient noise on the plain cubic lattice, and the reference point the rest of the family is easiest to read against. Four other noises here are built on this exact core: Noise : FBM layers it, Noise : Swiss (Erosion) layers it with derivatives, Noise : Marble displaces a sine with it, and Noise : Curl differentiates three copies of it. Reach for it when nothing about the pattern needs to be special.
UPCGExNoise3DPerlinProviderSettings.situation: A smooth, unremarkable spatial field to drive a mask, an offset or a density falloff.

mechanism.text: Each sample sits inside one cell of the integer lattice. The eight corners each get a gradient direction pulled from a fixed table of sixteen, the sample offset from each corner is dotted against that corner gradient, and the eight results are interpolated with a quintic ease before the range is folded from minus one to one into 0 to 1. Octaves above 1 sum successive passes, each at Lacunarity times the frequency and Persistence times the amplitude of the one before, normalised by the total amplitude.

off_label.claim: Perlin at more than one octave and Noise : FBM on its Standard variant compute the same number for the same settings, because the octave loop and the normalisation are shared and the range fold is affine. FBM is the node to reach for only when one of its other four variants is wanted.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExNoise3DOperation::GenerateFractal against FPCGExNoiseFBM::GenerateStandard, both over PCGExNoise3D::Math::Perlin3D with the same FractalBounding

UPCGExNoise3DSimplexProviderSettings.name: Noise : Simplex
UPCGExNoise3DSimplexProviderSettings.purpose: Gradient noise on a skewed tetrahedral lattice rather than a cubic one, reading four corners per sample where Noise : Perlin reads eight. mechanism.text: The position is skewed so that the cubic lattice maps onto a tetrahedral one, and comparing the three unskewed coordinates picks out which of the six tetrahedra in that cell the sample landed in. Octaves above 1 sum successive passes at Lacunarity times the frequency and Persistence times the amplitude.

UPCGExNoise3DSpotsProviderSettings.name: Noise : Spots
UPCGExNoise3DSpotsProviderSettings.purpose: One shaped blob per lattice cell against a flat zero background. It reads the same cell lattice as Noise : Worley and answers a different question: Worley measures distance everywhere, Spots asks whether the sample is inside a shape and returns nothing where it is not. Five shapes, and the gaps between them are genuinely empty rather than dark.
UPCGExNoise3DSpotsProviderSettings.situation: Discrete marks scattered on a background, where the background has to be exactly zero rather than merely low.

mechanism.text: Every lattice cell holds one spot, its centre offset from the cell centre by Jitter and its radius a fraction of the cell taken from Spot Radius plus a per-cell draw from Radius Variation. Each sample tests the 27 cells around it against the chosen Shape, keeps the closest claim, and answers 0 where no spot claims it. The two hard shapes answer with the spot own value inside and 0 outside; the three soft shapes fall from that value at the centre to 0 at the edge.

off_label.claim: Because the background is an exact 0 and the spots carry a value of 1 by default, the output works as a mask without any thresholding: multiply anything by it and only the points inside a spot survive.
off_label.grounded_in: the MinDist sentinel of 1.0 in FPCGExNoiseSpots::GenerateRaw, which yields a spot value of 0.0 for any sample no spot claims

UPCGExNoise3DSwissProviderSettings.name: Noise : Swiss (Erosion)
UPCGExNoise3DSwissProviderSettings.purpose: Layered Perlin that feeds its own slope back into itself. Each octave is sampled at a position pushed along the slope the octaves before it built, and its amplitude is cut where that slope is steep, so detail collects in the flats and thins out on the faces. It is Noise : FBM with a feedback loop, and with both of its feedback settings at 0 it is exactly that.
UPCGExNoise3DSwissProviderSettings.situation: Layered noise that should read as carved rather than piled, with detail unevenly distributed by slope.

mechanism.text: Every octave evaluates Perlin together with its analytic derivative. Before sampling, the position is displaced by the running sum of derivatives times Warp Factor; after sampling, the octave amplitude is divided by one plus the square of that running derivative magnitude times Erosion Strength. The derivative sum then takes this octave derivative, weighted by its own amplitude and frequency, so the feedback compounds. The sum is normalised by the total amplitude and folded into 0 to 1.

off_label.claim: Set Warp Factor and Erosion Strength both to 0 and the feedback drops out completely, leaving plain layered Perlin: the same numbers Noise : Perlin and the Standard variant of Noise : FBM produce at the same octave settings, with Apply Transform off.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExNoiseSwiss::NoiseWithDerivatives value term expanding to the same trilinear form as PCGExNoise3D::Math::Perlin3D, with the warp and erosion terms vanishing at zero

UPCGExNoise3DTilingProviderSettings.name: Noise : Tiling
UPCGExNoise3DTilingProviderSettings.purpose: A generator, not a modifier: Perlin-style gradient noise whose corner lookups wrap, so the field repeats exactly on a box you choose. The period is counted in lattice cells rather than world units, which means the tile you actually get is Period divided by Frequency, and at the shipped defaults that is 400 units on each axis.
UPCGExNoise3DTilingProviderSettings.situation: A field that has to repeat over a known box without a visible join, for tiled layouts or a pattern that must line up with a grid.

mechanism.text: Each of the eight corner lookups has its lattice index wrapped by the period for its axis before hashing, so opposite faces of the box read the same gradients and the field meets itself with no discontinuity. Everything else is Perlin: gradient dot products interpolated with a quintic ease, folded into 0 to 1. The tile spans Period cells on each axis, which is Period divided by Frequency world units.

off_label.claim: Set two periods high and one low and the field repeats fast on one axis while staying varied on the other two, which is a way to get layered banding out of a gradient noise without a sine anywhere.
off_label.grounded_in: the independent Mod against PeriodX, PeriodY and PeriodZ in FPCGExNoiseTiling::GenerateRaw

UPCGExNoise3DValueProviderSettings.name: Noise : Value
UPCGExNoise3DValueProviderSettings.purpose: Lattice noise with no gradients: one hashed value per lattice corner, interpolated. It reads the same lattice as Noise : White and separates from it on one point, interpolation. Value blends the eight corners of the containing cell and comes out smooth; White returns the containing cell single value flat, so it comes out as blocks.
UPCGExNoise3DValueProviderSettings.situation: A smooth field whose extrema sit on lattice corners rather than between them, or a cheaper stand-in for gradient noise.

mechanism.text: The eight corners of the containing lattice cell are hashed into the shared permutation table, and each hash becomes a value by dividing the byte by 255. Those eight values are interpolated trilinearly with a quintic ease. The result is already in 0 to 1 and no range fold is applied. Octaves above 1 sum successive passes at Lacunarity times the frequency and Persistence times the amplitude.

off_label.claim: Corner values come from a 256-entry byte table, so the field only ever interpolates between 256 discrete levels. Push Contrast or a steep Remap Curve hard enough and the quantisation shows as banding that no amount of Frequency will smooth out.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExNoise3D::Math::HashToDouble dividing the uint8 permutation entry by 255

UPCGExNoise3DWhiteProviderSettings.name: Noise : White
UPCGExNoise3DWhiteProviderSettings.purpose: One hashed value per lattice cell, held flat across the whole cell. It is per-cell random, not per-point random: two points inside the same cell get the same number, and at the shipped Frequency of 0.01 a cell is 100 world units across. Getting one value per point out of it means shrinking the cell below the point spacing.
UPCGExNoise3DWhiteProviderSettings.situation: A blocky random field, or a per-region random draw keyed to position rather than to point order.

mechanism.text: The scaled position is floored to a lattice cell and the cell integer coordinates are hashed with a 32-bit mixer, which becomes a value by dividing by the largest 32-bit integer. There is no interpolation and no smoothing, so the field is constant inside a cell and jumps at every cell boundary. The hash is a wider one than the rest of the family uses, so the values are spread across the full 32-bit range rather than 256 levels.

off_label.claim: Because the value is constant per cell and the cell is keyed to world position, this doubles as a spatial partition: raise Frequency until a cell is the block size you want, and every point in a block draws the same number.

UPCGExNoise3DWorleyProviderSettings.purpose: Cellular noise built from the distance to a jittered feature point per lattice cell. mechanism.text: One feature point sits in every lattice cell, offset from the cell centre by up to half a cell according to Jitter. Each sample measures the 27 cells around it, keeps the nearest distance and the second nearest, and Return Type decides what those two become. Every return except Cell Value divides by a constant that depends only on the metric and then clamps at 1, so the values are a rough normalisation rather than an exact 0 to 1.

off_label.claim: Jitter at 0 puts every feature point exactly at its cell centre, which turns the whole node into a distance field over a perfect grid. With Chebyshev and F1 that is a field of nested axis-aligned boxes with no randomness in it at all.

UPCGExNoiseFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Noise
UPCGExNoiseFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Turns a noise field into a pass or fail. The noise sub-nodes wired into the Noises pin define the field, the filter samples it at each element's world position, and that one sample is compared against a threshold. Several noise sub-nodes on the pin stack into a single field instead of becoming several tests, so a broad shape and a fine one can decide one verdict together. It also answers for whole datasets: while the threshold is a constant or a `@Data` attribute, the same field is sampled once at a dataset's bounding-box centre, which is what lets Uber Branch and Break route datasets by where they sit and lets Uber Filter (Data) ask once instead of counting elements.
UPCGExNoiseFilterProviderSettings.situation: Elements should be kept or dropped in coherent patches decided by where they sit in the world.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element, and the filter reads no data of its own and writes nothing. Every noise sub-node on the Noises pin contributes to one field, ordered by their own Priority and mixed by each one's Weight Factor and blend mode; the field is sampled once at the element's world location, and that single number meets the threshold. Nothing but the position and the sub-nodes' own settings enters the sample, so a graph re-run over unchanged points reproduces every verdict, and moving a point is what changes its answer. A consumer judging whole datasets samples the same field at the dataset's bounding-box centre, and that one sample decides for every element in it.

off_label.claim: A single White noise sub-node turns this into a keep-or-drop that looks random but is keyed by position: two elements at the same location always agree, and reordering or reindexing the data changes nothing.
off_label.grounded_in: FNoiseFilter::Test sampling at InTransforms[PointIndex].GetLocation(), with no seed and no index reaching the sample

inputs.label: Noises
inputs.note: The noise sub-nodes that define the field. Several are accepted and blend into one field rather than being tested one at a time.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so it is accepted on every filter pin, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

hints.text: If the Noises pin brings nothing usable the node produces no filter at all and its Filter pin goes empty. A consumer left with an empty filter pin falls back to its own default verdict, and on a pin that chooses what to process that default is everything passing, so the symptom is an unfiltered result rather than an empty one. The log names the pin.

UPCGExNormalizeSettings.name: Normalize
UPCGExNormalizeSettings.purpose: Turns each point's position into a figure between 0 and 1 across the data's own bounds, and writes it to an attribute. That converts world coordinates, which mean nothing without knowing where the data sits, into a place within the set, which is comparable between runs and across datasets of different sizes. Points do not move: this reads positions, it does not change them.
UPCGExNormalizeSettings.situation: A gradient, mask or lookup that should follow the extent of whatever data arrives rather than fixed world coordinates.

mechanism.text: The bounds are measured, each position is expressed as its fraction across them, and the result is written to the named attribute. `Tile` multiplies that fraction so the range repeats, and `Wrapping` decides what happens to the values that then fall outside 0 to 1. `One Minus` flips chosen components afterwards. A Bounds pin lets several datasets share one set of bounds, which is what keeps their normalised values comparable with each other.
steps: The position is transformed, then expressed as a fraction of the bounds.
Tiling multiplies the fraction and wrapping resolves whatever left the range.
One Minus flips the chosen components last.

off_label.claim: Tiling with wrapping turns the output into a repeating ramp across the data, which is a gradient generator that needs no texture and rescales itself to whatever arrives.
off_label.grounded_in: Tile multiplies the normalized position componentwise and the wrapping mode resolves out-of-range values, so a tile factor of N produces N repeats across the bounds.

inputs.label: Bounds
inputs.note: Point data whose bounds replace each input's own, so several datasets normalise against one shared extent. Without it every dataset is normalised against itself and their values are not comparable.

BoundsSource.tooltip: Which point property to use for bounds calculation.
BoundsSource.semantics: Which bounds the fraction is measured across. The shipped `Center` treats points as positions with no volume, so the normalised range spans the outermost point centres; the volume-aware options push the extremes out to the edges of the outermost points' bounds instead.

Offset.tooltip: Offset applied to the normalized position.

Tile.tooltip: Tiling factor applied to the normalized position.
Tile.semantics: Multiplies the fraction per axis, so a value of 3 makes the range cross 0 to 1 three times over the same data. It is applied before wrapping, which is what turns the repeats into a usable ramp rather than values running to 3.

Wrapping.semantics: Resolves values that tiling or an offset pushed outside 0 to 1. The shipped `Tile` repeats them, which is what produces a continuous ramp; clamping instead flattens each repeat's ends, and ignoring lets values run past the range.

OneMinus.tooltip: Which components should be one minus'd

Transform.tooltip: Transform applied to the position before processing.

Output.semantics: The attribute the normalised position lands on. Nothing is written back to the point's own position, so this node never moves anything and can be read alongside the original world coordinates.

hints.text: Without the Bounds pin each dataset is normalised against its own extent, so the same output value means a different place in each one. Anything comparing normalised values across datasets needs them sharing one bounds source.

UPCGExNumericCompareFilterProviderSettin.name: Filter : Compare (Numeric)
UPCGExNumericCompareFilterProviderSettin.purpose: Compares one number read on the element against a second number, either a constant you type or another attribute on that same element. Both operands come from the element being tested, which is what separates this from its two siblings: Filter : Self Compare (Numeric) moves the second operand to another index of the same dataset, and Filter : Compare Nearest (Numeric) moves the first one onto a separate dataset. Point both selectors at `@Data.` attributes and the filter answers once per dataset instead of once per point, which is what lets Uber Filter (Data) route whole collections on it.
UPCGExNumericCompareFilterProviderSettin.situation: A number already written onto the points, and the next node should act only where it sits above, below or near a threshold.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element and decides what the answer means; the filter itself reads no data of its own and writes nothing. Operand A is read on the element being tested, Operand B is either the constant or a second attribute read on that same element, both as doubles whatever type they are stored as. The verdict is the chosen operator applied to the pair in that order, so Operand A is always the left-hand side.

UPCGExNumericCompareNearestFilterProvide.name: Filter : Compare Nearest (Numeric)
UPCGExNumericCompareNearestFilterProvide.purpose: Judges each element by a number carried on the closest point of another dataset. That other dataset arrives on the Targets pin, and reaching outside the data being filtered is what this node has that the other two numeric comparisons do not: Filter : Compare (Numeric) reads both operands on the element, Filter : Self Compare (Numeric) reads one attribute at two indices of the same dataset. Because it holds target data of its own, it also carries the whole spatial apparatus: a search radius, a choice of how distance is measured against bounds, and rules pairing target datasets with the inputs they apply to.
UPCGExNumericCompareNearestFilterProvide.situation: Two datasets in play, where the number deciding each element of the first one is stored on the second.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element, and the comparison spans two datasets: Operand A is read on the closest point found on the Targets pin, Operand B on the element being tested. Every dataset wired to Targets joins one pool and the closest point can come from any of them, minus the tested element's own data while Ignore Self is on. Max Distance, read on the tested element and multiplied by the scale under it, bounds the search, and at its default of 0 the search is unbounded. An element with no qualifying target inside that radius fails, without the comparison running at all. The verdict is always one per element: Uber Branch and Break skip this filter with a warning that it cannot be used with collections, and Uber Filter (Data) falls back to counting element passes.

UPCGExNumericSelfCompareFilterProviderSe.name: Filter : Self Compare (Numeric)
UPCGExNumericSelfCompareFilterProviderSe.purpose: Compares one attribute against itself at a second index of the same dataset. There is one selector and no Operand B: the two sides of the comparison are the same attribute read at two positions, which is what this node has instead of the second operand that Filter : Compare (Numeric) gives you, and instead of the separate dataset that Filter : Compare Nearest (Numeric) reaches into. Index Mode decides whether that second position is an offset from the element's own index or a position named outright.
UPCGExNumericSelfCompareFilterProviderSe.situation: An ordered dataset where the question is how a value changes from one element to the next, or how each element stands against one reference element.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element; the filter reads nothing else and writes nothing. One selector supplies both sides: Operand A is read on the element being tested and read again at a second index of the same dataset, so this node can only ever compare an attribute with itself. Index Mode decides which index that is, adding the Index value to the element's own position under Offset or naming a position outright under Pick, and Index Safety then folds anything landing outside the dataset back inside. The second index never leaves the dataset the element belongs to, so a consumer holding several datasets runs a separate copy of the filter over each one, each with its own ends.

off_label.claim: An attribute-driven index under Pick turns this into a general pairwise test inside one dataset. Write a partner index upstream, the index a sampler resolved for instance, and each element is compared against the element that index names rather than against a neighbour.
off_label.grounded_in: FNumericSelfCompareFilter::Test using the per-point Index value directly as the target index when Index Mode is Pick, read through GetValueSettingIndex over Config.IndexAttribute
