outputs.label: Unmatched Edges
outputs.note: Edges data no plot reached. Advanced until Data Matching is set to split the unmatched off.

OutputMode.tooltip: Whether to output paths, or to forward Vtx & Edges with a per-element visited count instead.
OutputMode.semantics: Changes the node's pin set the same way it does on **Pathfinding : Edges**: `Paths` gives a single Paths output, `Visited` replaces it with the forwarded Vtx and Edges. One plot counts as one path for the tally even though it is solved leg by leg, so a junction two consecutive legs share is worth a single increment rather than two.

HeuristicScoreMode.tooltip: Scoring mode for combining multiple heuristics

DataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, allows you to filter out which plots get associated to which clusters
DataMatching.semantics: Decides which plots are attempted on which clusters, which is what turns a batch of plots and a batch of clusters into a pairing rather than a cross product. A cluster no plot matches is skipped, and under `Visited` its Edges are still emitted carrying an all-zero count so the output stays uniform.

bAddSeedToPath.tooltip: Add seed point at the beginning of the path
bAddSeedToPath.semantics: The seed here is the plot's first point, copied from the plot data. `Add Goal To Path` appends the plot's last point in the same way.

bAddGoalToPath.tooltip: Add goal point at the end of the path
bAddGoalToPath.semantics: Suppressed under `Closed Loop` when `Add Seed To Path` is also on, because the two would name the same waypoint and the path would end where it started. Leave the seed off and the closing waypoint is appended as usual.

bAddPlotPointsToPath.tooltip: Insert plot points inside the path
bAddPlotPointsToPath.semantics: Inserts each intermediate waypoint into the run at the place its two legs meet, as a copy of the plot point, so the path passes through the authored location and not only through the Vtx that location snapped to.
bAddPlotPointsToPath.trap: Turning it on also stops the legs being trimmed against each other, so the shared junction Vtx is written by both legs and the waypoint is inserted between the two copies. Every intermediate waypoint therefore arrives as three points where the setting off gives one.

bClosedLoop.semantics: Adds one more leg, from the last waypoint back to the first, and marks the output as a closed path so downstream path nodes treat it as a loop. It is the one path-shaping toggle that stays visible under `Visited`, where the extra leg still contributes to the counts.

PathComposition.tooltip: What are the paths made of.
PathComposition.semantics: `Vtx` copies the Vtx each leg ran through, trimmed so a junction is written once. `Edge` copies the Edges points of the crossed edges instead and does no trimming at all, since consecutive legs never share an edge.
PathComposition.trap: Under `Edge` the plot's own points are still copied in when `Add Seed To Path`, `Add Goal To Path` or `Add Plot Points To Path` is on, so the result mixes points from the Edges data with points from the plot data.

SeedPicking.tooltip: Drive how a seed selects a node.
SeedPicking.semantics: Applied to the first waypoint of each leg and `Goal Picking` to the second, so every intermediate waypoint is resolved twice, once under each block. Giving the two different settings therefore splits a junction into two different Vtx and leaves a jump in the path.

GoalPicking.tooltip: Drive how a goal selects a node.

Statistics.tooltip: Per-element visited counts written onto the forwarded Vtx & Edges.

bUseOctreeSearch.tooltip: Whether or not to search for closest node using an octree. Depending on your dataset, enabling this may be either much faster, or much slower.
bUseOctreeSearch.semantics: Only affects how waypoints are matched to cluster elements. The search itself is untouched.

bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.display: Omit Complete Path On Failed Plot
bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.semantics: Declared on the panel and never read. A plot with a failed leg is emitted whatever this is set to, provided at least one leg resolved.
bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.trap: A failed leg leaves no points behind, so the path jumps straight from the end of one solved leg to the start of the next. Watch for the warning rather than this toggle.

PathOutputDetails.tooltip: Point-count limits deciding which generated paths are kept. Paths with fewer than 2 points are always dropped.

bQuietInvalidPlotWarning.tooltip: Suppress warning when a plot could not be resolved to valid paths.

bGreedyQueries.tooltip: If disabled, will share memory allocations between queries, forcing them to execute one after another. Much slower, but very conservative for memory. Using global feedback forces this behavior under the hood.
bGreedyQueries.semantics: Off, the plots are solved one after another instead of side by side, which changes the result and not only memory once a feedback heuristic is on the pin. Inside a single plot the legs are already grouped, and a global feedback heuristic forces the sequential behaviour whatever this is set to.

hints.text: A leg that cannot be solved is skipped and the rest of the plot is still emitted, so a path can arrive with a straight jump across the span that failed. The warning naming the plot is the only signal, and `Quiet Invalid Plot Warning` removes it.
Plots carrying fewer than two points are pruned before matching, with their own warning. If every plot is pruned the node stops with a missing-input error rather than emitting nothing.

UPCGExPathfindingPlotNavmeshSettings.name: Pathfinding : Plot Navmesh
UPCGExPathfindingPlotNavmeshSettings.purpose: Routes through waypoints already in order, over the level's navigation mesh. A plot is an ordered point dataset read as a list of waypoints: each consecutive pair is one leg, solved on its own, and the legs are joined end to end into a single output path. One plot dataset in, one path out, so there is no Goals input and no Goal Picker here: the ordering inside the dataset is the pairing. Like **Pathfinding : Navmesh**, it takes no cluster, and therefore no heuristics, no search algorithm and no node picking.
UPCGExPathfindingPlotNavmeshSettings.situation: A patrol or a delivery order is authored as a sequence of places, and the level geometry has to decide how to get between them.

mechanism.text: A plot of N points becomes N-1 navigation queries, plus a closing one back to the first waypoint when `Closed Loop` is on. Each answered query contributes its corridor, thinned by `Fuse Distance`, and the node trims the ends where two legs meet so a junction is written once. Several plot datasets are accepted and each becomes its own path, independently of the others. A plot carrying fewer than two points is skipped without a word, and so is one whose finished path would hold two points or fewer.

off_label.claim: Feed the output of a spline or a sorted point set straight in and the node becomes a navmesh-conforming resampler: the authored order is preserved and everything between the waypoints is replaced by ground the agent can actually walk.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExPlotNavmeshTask::ExecuteTask pairs each input point with the next in dataset order and writes the corridor positions between them, so the input's ordering is the only pairing rule

inputs.label: Plots
inputs.note: The ordered waypoint datasets. Several are accepted and each becomes its own path.

inputs.label: Overrides : Blending
inputs.note: An attribute set whose names match the selected blending sub-node's settings one to one.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One dataset per plot that resolved at least one leg.

bAddSeedToPath.tooltip: Add seed point at the beginning of the path
bAddSeedToPath.semantics: The seed here is the plot's first point, copied in at its own location. `Add Goal To Path` appends the plot's last point in the same way, and both default on.
bAddSeedToPath.trap: A plot whose finished path holds two points or fewer is discarded outright, extras included. Turning both off is enough to lose a short plot entirely.

bAddGoalToPath.tooltip: Add goal point at the end of the path
bAddGoalToPath.semantics: Skipped under `Closed Loop`, where the closing leg returns to the first waypoint and a copy of the last one would sit in the middle of the run rather than at its end.

bAddPlotPointsToPath.tooltip: Insert plot points inside the path
bAddPlotPointsToPath.semantics: Inserts each intermediate waypoint at its own authored location, so the path passes through the point rather than through the navmesh's nearest walkable stand-in for it. The corridor positions on either side are trimmed back to make room, so each waypoint costs one point rather than three.

bClosedLoop.semantics: Adds one more query, from the last waypoint back to the first. The output is not flagged as a closed path, so downstream path nodes read it as an open run that happens to end near where it began.

bRequireNavigableEndLocation.tooltip: Whether the pathfinding requires a naviguable end location.
bRequireNavigableEndLocation.semantics: Handed straight to every leg's navigation query, so a single waypoint off navigable ground fails both of the legs that touch it and leaves a gap the length of two spans.

FuseDistance.semantics: Applied to each leg's corridor on its own, before the legs are stitched, so it never merges across a junction. Measured sequentially against the previous kept position rather than as a global tolerance.

Blending.tooltip: Controls how path points blend from seed to goal.
Blending.semantics: Decides what the invented corridor points carry. Positions are held fixed whatever is selected, so this only touches attributes and the other point properties.
Blending.trap: Both ends of the blend are read out of the output path at the waypoints' own row numbers rather than from the plot points, so every leg past the first blends between two points the node itself invented. Set it to No Blending where the intermediate points' values matter and carry them in downstream instead.

NavAgentProperties.tooltip: Nav agent to be used by the nav system.

bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.display: Omit Complete Path On Failed Plot
bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.semantics: Declared on the panel and never read. A plot with a failed leg is emitted whatever this is set to, provided at least one leg was answered.
bOmitCompletePathOnFailedPlot.trap: A failed leg leaves no positions behind, so the path jumps straight from the end of one answered leg to the start of the next. Nothing is logged either.

hints.text: Every query needs a live navigation system with a default navigation data instance. Without one, each leg returns nothing, no path is written and no error is raised: the node succeeds with an empty Paths pin.

None of the cluster pathfinding surface reaches this node. There is no Heuristics pin, no Search Algorithm, no Path Composition and no Paths Output Settings, and no tagging or forwarding either. What the navigation system will and will not walk is set by `Nav Agent Properties` and by the level's navigation data.

A plot of fewer than two points is skipped with no warning at all, unlike **Pathfinding : Plot Edges**, which prunes the same case and says so. An empty Paths pin with several plots wired in is worth checking against the point counts first.

UPCGExPathHatchSettings.name: Path : Hatch
UPCGExPathHatchSettings.purpose: Rules a bundle of parallel lines across a closed shape and keeps only the parts that fall inside it, each kept part coming back as its own short path. The input is a silhouette rather than something to be edited: it is consumed for its outline and never appears in the output. Line direction, spacing and offset are all readable from data, so one graph can hatch a set of shapes at a different angle and density each.
UPCGExPathHatchSettings.situation: A closed outline has to be filled with regular runs that stop at its border, and the border is not a rectangle.

mechanism.text: Evenly spaced parallel lines are laid across the shape, each line is intersected with the outline, and the crossings along a line are paired off in order: first with second, third with fourth. Each surviving pair becomes one output path of two endpoints on the outline plus interior points between them. A line crossing the outline four times therefore yields two runs with the hole between them left empty, and a line touching a single corner yields nothing. The output count is the number of kept pairs, or one dataset per input if `Output Mode` merges them, and the input path itself never comes out either way.

off_label.claim: One line and a large spacing turns this into a chord sampler: the bundle collapses to a single line through the box centre, and what comes back is that line clipped to the shape, which is a way to measure a silhouette's width along a chosen angle.
off_label.grounded_in: Count mode clamps the line count to at least 1 with the first offset placed at half a step from the box edge, which for a count of 1 is the box centre

off_label.claim: With the interior spacing set to a count of zero, every output path is exactly its two border points, so the result is a set of chords rather than a fill and the alpha attribute reduces to a 0 and a 1 per pair.
off_label.grounded_in: Count mode takes the interior count from the setting directly, and a segment with no interior points skips the sub-point blending call entirely

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: Closed loops of three points or more. Open paths and shorter ones are refused with a warning and do not reach the output.

inputs.label: Overrides : Blending
inputs.note: An attribute set whose names are matched against the picked `Blending` sub-node's own settings, so the blend can be driven from data.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One dataset per kept run, or one per input in merged mode. Every result is marked open.

ProjectionDetails.tooltip: Projection used to flatten the input path before intersection.
ProjectionDetails.semantics: Flattening is for the intersection test alone. Border points are placed by interpolating the original world segment they landed on, so the result sits on the input's real geometry rather than on the projection plane, and a shape that is not flat keeps its relief.
ProjectionDetails.trap: The crossings are found in the flattened view, so a shape folded over on itself in the projection direction has parts of it overlapping there and produces crossings that make no sense in three dimensions.

BoxFitMode.tooltip: Bounding box used to size and orient the line bundle in projected space.
BoxFitMode.semantics: Decides the frame the line angle is measured in, and nothing else. `Axis Aligned (AABB)` uses the projected bounds, so zero degrees follows the projection's own axes. `Best Fit (OBB)` derives the frame from the spread of the points, so zero degrees runs along the shape's longest direction whichever way the shape is turned, and 90 runs across it. `Best Fit (OBB, Accurate)` solves for the tightest box instead, which differs from the first fit on shapes whose spread does not follow their outline.

AngleOffset.tooltip: Rotation (degrees) of the line direction around the projection plane normal. 0 = aligned with the box X axis; add 90 for the Y axis.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

AngleOffset.semantics: Read once per input dataset rather than per point. What zero looks like is `Box Fit Mode`'s decision.

LineSpacingMode.tooltip: How line spacing along the perpendicular axis is interpreted.
LineSpacingMode.semantics: `Count` divides the shape's width into exactly that many bands and always tiles cleanly. `Distance` honours the spacing literally, so the last band against one edge is whatever is left over, unless a slide with `Wrap Slide` is in play, in which case the spacing is rounded to the nearest whole division so the seam does not show.

LineSpacing.tooltip: Spacing value for lines. Interpreted as count or world distance depending on Line Spacing Mode.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

LineSpacing.semantics: In `Count` mode the value is floored to a whole number and clamped to at least one. Read once per input dataset, not per point.

LineOrigin.tooltip: Where the first line is anchored across the box.
LineOrigin.semantics: It changes the result only in `Distance` mode with the spacing honoured literally.
LineOrigin.trap: It is inert in `Count` mode, where the bands are always centred on the box whatever this says, and inert again in `Distance` mode once a slide is applied with `Wrap Slide` on.

LineOriginSlide.tooltip: Slide the line origin along the cross axis, as a normalized fraction of the available space. Center: 1 = box edge along the cross axis (fraction of the half-extent), signed. Start: 1 = opposite side along the cross axis (fraction of the full extent), signed.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

bWrapSlide.tooltip: If enabled, lines pushed outside the cross-axis extent by the slide wrap around to the opposite side, keeping the box fully tiled. If disabled, shifted-out lines produce no crossings.
bWrapSlide.semantics: With the slide at zero this changes nothing. Where it does apply, the spacing is snapped to a whole division of the box so the two sides meet cleanly.

SegmentSpacingMode.tooltip: How sub-point spacing along each kept segment is interpreted.
SegmentSpacingMode.semantics: `Count` gives every run the same number of interior points however long it is, so short runs come back dense and long ones sparse. `Distance` gives every run the same spacing instead, so the count varies and a run shorter than one step gets none.

SegmentSpacing.tooltip: Spacing value along each kept segment. Interpreted as count or world distance depending on Segment Spacing Mode.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SegmentSpacing.semantics: The count is floored in `Count` mode. Like the other shorthands here it resolves to one value per input dataset, so switching it to an attribute reads a data-domain value and never a per-point one.

bRedistributeEvenly.tooltip: When using Distance mode, evenly redistribute computed sub-points across the segment.
bRedistributeEvenly.semantics: The interior count still comes from the literal spacing; what changes is where those points sit, spread evenly across the run instead of stepped from its start. It is the fix for the gap that otherwise collects at the far end of every run.

MinSegmentLength.tooltip: Minimum world-space length to keep a segment. Shorter clipped segments are discarded.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

MinSegmentLength.semantics: Runs are dropped whole, before any interior points are placed. Runs of no length at all are dropped whatever this is set to, so leaving the filter off does not mean every pair survives.

OutputMode.tooltip: How the generated points are emitted: one data per input, or one data per kept segment.
OutputMode.semantics: A merged result is still one ordered point set, and it is marked open rather than closed.
OutputMode.trap: Anything downstream reading a merged result as a path treats the jump from the end of one run to the start of the next as a segment, which is why merged output suits positions and not path operations.

AlphaAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name receiving the segment alpha (0 at entry, 1 at exit).
AlphaAttributeName.semantics: Per run rather than across the shape, so in merged output it resets at every concatenated run. It is protected from both blenders, so nothing overwrites it.

Blending.tooltip: Blending applied to interior sub-points along each kept segment, using the segment's two endpoints as anchors.
Blending.semantics: Both border points are already settled before it runs, either by inheriting the nearest source point or through endpoint blending, and it fills between them.

bDoEndpointBlending.tooltip: If enabled, segment endpoint attributes are blended along the input polyline edges they intersect (edge-T weighted lerp). Otherwise each endpoint inherits the closest input point's metadata as-is.
bDoEndpointBlending.semantics: Two border points on the same input segment can end up carrying identical values with this off, since each takes the whole payload of the end it is nearer to. Positions interpolate either way; this decides only what the attributes do.

EndpointBlending.tooltip: Blending mode used for endpoint attributes when Endpoint Blending is enabled.
EndpointBlending.semantics: It ships with attributes on `Weight` and the point properties on `None`, so out of the box endpoint blending moves attributes and leaves transforms alone.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

EndpointCarryOver.semantics: Narrows which of the input's attributes endpoint blending is allowed to touch. It has no bearing on the interior points, which answer to the `Blending` sub-node's own filter.

hints.text: A shape that is not closed produces nothing here, and neither does one of two points. Both are refused at the door with a single warning covering the whole run, so an input arriving open comes back as silence rather than as itself. `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` does not change this: the refused input is never forwarded either way.
A line grazing a single corner of the outline is dropped rather than paired with itself, so a spike sticking out of a shape contributes no runs of its own.

UPCGExPathInsertSettings.name: Path : Insert
UPCGExPathInsertSettings.purpose: Threads loose points into a path at the place they belong in its order. Each point on the **Targets** pin finds the segment it is closest to and becomes a new point inside it, so a scatter of points that had nothing to do with the path comes out as part of it. `Snap To Path` decides whether the new point moves onto the path or the path detours out to meet it, and on an open path targets sitting past either end can extend the run rather than crowd its last segment. Five optional attributes record where each insertion came from and how far it had to reach.
UPCGExPathInsertSettings.situation: Points produced somewhere else, doors, junctions or markers, that have to become part of a path already running past them.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and target points, and returns each path with one new point per target that found a home in it. Every original point survives in its original order, so the output count is the input count plus the accepted insertions, and a path that accepted none is passed straight through untouched. A target claims the segment whose closest point to it is nearest, which is a global choice across the whole path rather than a per-segment one, and several targets landing in one segment are laid out along it in the order they sit. An inserted point starts from the attributes of the point its segment begins at, then the `Blending` dropdown decides what it is really worth, then `Target Forwarding` copies anything named from the target that produced it.
steps: Every target picks its closest segment, and `Within Range` drops the ones too far from the path to bother with.
`Limit Inserts Per Edge` then thins each segment down to its cap, keeping the candidates closest to the path.
`Prevent Collocation` runs last, on what survived, and drops anything landing on top of a path point or on an insertion already accepted.

off_label.claim: With Snap To Path off and Prevent Collocation on, the node reads as a stitching pass rather than an insertion: the targets keep their own positions and the path is rerouted through them, so a coarse path plus a set of exact positions becomes one run that visits all of them in order.
off_label.grounded_in: The insert position is the target's original location unless bSnapToPath is set, and the original path points are all retained

off_label.claim: Write Target Index alone and the path becomes a record of which target dataset reached it, since the attribute carries the index of the target data rather than of the point inside it. Points that were already on the path keep the default value, so the two are told apart by that value alone.
off_label.grounded_in: TargetIndexWriter is fed Insert.TargetIOIndex, which is the target data's index, and original points keep DefaultTargetIndex

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to insert into.

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: The points to thread in. Several datasets are accepted and are treated as one pool unless matching rules split them. The node fails outright when this resolves to nothing.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: Match Rule sub-nodes deciding which target data is allowed to reach which path. Sits under the advanced pins while `Data Matching`'s mode is Disabled, and becomes required as soon as it is not.
inputs.condition: required when Data Matching's Mode is anything but Disabled

inputs.label: Overrides : Blending
inputs.note: Attribute set whose entries overwrite the picked blend rule's own properties by name. Sits under the node's advanced pins.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: Each path with its accepted insertions in place.

outputs.label: Unmatched
outputs.note: Paths that matching rules paired with no target at all. Advanced and unused while `Data Matching`'s mode is Disabled.
outputs.condition: carries data only when Data Matching is enabled and set to split unmatched

DataMatching.tooltip: If enabled, allows you to filter which targets get inserted into which paths.

bExclusiveTargets.tooltip: If enabled, each target can only be inserted into one path (the closest one). Otherwise, a target may be inserted into multiple paths.
bExclusiveTargets.semantics: Off, a target is inserted into every path it is close enough to, so one point can end up in several paths at once. On, the paths compete and the one whose segment the target is nearest to takes it.

bSnapToPath.tooltip: If enabled, inserted points will be snapped to the path. Otherwise, they retain their original position.
bSnapToPath.semantics: Decides which of two positions the new point takes: the place on the segment the target projected to, or the target's own location. Off, which is what ships, keeps the target where it was, so the path bends out to reach it and its shape changes. On, the path keeps its shape and the point moves.
bSnapToPath.trap: `Prevent Collocation` measures whichever of the two this setting selected, so flipping it changes which insertions survive that test as well as where they sit.

bEdgeInteriorOnly.tooltip: If enabled, only insert targets that project to edge interiors (not endpoints). Targets at alpha 0 or 1 are skipped.
bEdgeInteriorOnly.semantics: Rejects targets that projected exactly onto a segment's end, which is where every target sitting beyond an open path's ends lands. It therefore also switches off extension, and hides `Allow Path Extension` while it is on.

bAllowPathExtension.tooltip: If enabled, targets beyond path endpoints can extend the path (open paths only).
bAllowPathExtension.semantics: Targets that project past the first or last point of an open path are placed beyond it, on the line the terminal segment continues along, and extend the run. Closed paths never extend, since they have no end to extend past.
bAllowPathExtension.trap: The extension points sit on that continued line whatever `Snap To Path` says about the interior ones, and the `Alpha` written on them is not a 0 to 1 position: it is the projection distance in world units, negative before the start and one plus that distance after the end.

bWithinRange.tooltip: Only insert points that are within a specified range of the path.

Range.tooltip: Maximum distance from path for a point to be inserted.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Range.semantics: Read once per path, from its first point, rather than per target or per segment. An attribute source therefore sets one radius for the whole path, which is the useful behaviour when the value is a data-domain value and a surprise when it varies per point.

bLimitInsertsPerEdge.tooltip: Limit how many points can be inserted per edge.

LimitMode.tooltip: How to interpret the limit value.

InsertLimit.tooltip: The limit value. For Count mode: max inserts. For Spacing mode: minimum distance between inserts.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

InsertLimit.semantics: Also read once per path from its first point. Under `Count` it caps how many insertions each segment keeps; under `Spacing` it is divided into the segment's length to work that cap out, so the cap varies per segment while the value does not.
InsertLimit.trap: It thins by distance to the path, not by position along the segment: when a segment is over its cap the closest candidates are kept and the rest are dropped, so the survivors can be bunched at one end.

LimitTruncate.tooltip: How to round fractional insert counts when using Spacing mode.

bPreventCollocation.tooltip: Skip insertions that would create collocated points (within tolerance of path vertices or other inserts).

CollocationTolerance.tooltip: Minimum distance between inserted points and path vertices.
CollocationTolerance.semantics: Tested against the segment's two end points and against every insertion already accepted in that same segment, so it thins clusters of targets as well as keeping insertions off existing path points. It never looks across segment boundaries.

Blending.tooltip: Blending applied on inserted points using path's prev and next point.
Blending.semantics: The dropdown deciding what every inserted point is worth. It hands the picked rule the two points bracketing a segment and the run of insertions between them. Where a path is extended, the outermost new point is treated as a bracket and keeps what it was given, and the rest blend between it and the path's real endpoint.

TargetForwarding.tooltip: Forward attributes from target points to inserted points.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Is forwarding enabled.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

TargetForwarding.semantics: Copies named attributes from the target point onto the point it became. It runs before the blend rule does, so an attribute name that exists on the path as well as on the targets ends up carrying the blended value; a name that only the targets carry survives the blend intact.

InsertedFlagName.tooltip: Attribute name to mark inserted points (true) vs original path points (false).

AlphaAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the alpha value (0-1 position along edge where inserted).
AlphaAttributeName.semantics: Where along its segment the insertion landed, from 0 at the segment's start to 1 at its end. Points that were already on the path receive `Default Value` instead, which ships at -1 so the two sets never collide.

DistanceAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the distance from target point to path location.

TargetIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the source target collection index.
TargetIndexAttributeName.semantics: The index of the target data the point came from, not the index of the point inside it. With one dataset on the pin every insertion carries 0.

DefaultTargetIndex.tooltip: Target index value for non-inserted (original) points.

DirectionAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the direction from target point to path location (or inverted).
DirectionAttributeName.semantics: The direction from where the target was to where the path took it, which is zero length whenever the target was already on the path. `Invert Direction` turns it around to point from the path out to the target.

bInvertDirection.tooltip: If enabled, writes direction from path to target instead of target to path.

NoInsertsTag.semantics: Applied to a path that accepted nothing, which includes paths of fewer than two points that were never processed at all. It is the only signal separating a path this node left alone from one it never looked at.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: Honoured in the off position. A path of fewer than two points is forwarded untouched and tagged, then dropped again at output time while this is on.

hints.text: `Within Range` and `Limit Inserts Per Edge` both read their value once per path, from its first point. An attribute varying along the path is not sampled per segment or per target, so only its value at index 0 has any effect.

UPCGExPathProcessorSettings.name: Path Processor Settings
UPCGExPathProcessorSettings.purpose: The shared surface behind every node that takes a path on a pin labelled **Paths**. That is most of the paths section, the six Clipper2 nodes, **Path : To Clusters**, **Staging : Spline Mesh**, **Tensors : Extrude** and **Topology : Path Surface**. It names those pins on both sides and settles the one question all of them face, which is what to do with an input too short to be a path. A single setting of its own lives here, under Advanced; everything else on a path node panel belongs to that node or to the plugin-wide surface.
UPCGExPathProcessorSettings.situation: A path node returned fewer datasets than went in, or handed one back untouched, and the question is whether it refused the short ones.

mechanism.text: One execution takes every dataset on **Paths** and handles each on its own, with no pairing and no state shared between them. The single decision this block owns is what happens to an input holding fewer than two points: two points is the floor for describing a run, so every node built on this base refuses to process one, and `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` decides whether that input still leaves through the output pin. Closure is not settled here. `@Data.IsClosed` travels with the data, and each node reads and writes it for itself.

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: Every path to process, as ordinary point data with nothing marking it as a path. Several datasets are accepted and each is handled on its own.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: What the node produced. Results are staged here at the end of the run, which is the second place `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` is read.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: The two halves of the tooltip are not both switches. Refusing to process an input under two points happens on every path node whatever this says; what the toggle decides is only whether that input still comes out. It is then read a second time at the end of the run, and while it is on, any output dataset that ends up under two points is dropped there as well, whether or not the input it came from was short.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.trap: Turning it off asks for the refused input to be forwarded untouched, and the nodes that honour that reach it by two different routes. Nine use the shared entry gate: **Path : Attribute Rolling**, **Path : Bevel**, **Path : Blend**, **Path : Extrude**, **Path : Offset**, **Path : Reduce**, **Path : Slide**, **Path : Solidify** and **Path × Bounds Intersection**. Others forward the short input themselves and are then caught by the staging check instead, which the same toggle governs: **Path : Subdivide**, **Path : Insert** and **Path : Fuse Collinear** among them, and **Path : Spline Mesh (Simple)**, **Path : Orient**, **Path : Split**, **Path : Stitch**, **Path : Shrink** and **Path × Path Crossings** on the same shape. The observable result is the same on both routes, so treat the list as indicative rather than exhaustive and check the node's own page. **Path : Fuse Collinear** additionally carries a second toggle of its own, and both must be off for a short path to survive.

hints.text: **Path × Bounds Intersection** is the one exception among those nine. With the toggle off and the node set to write any of its intersection attributes, it duplicates the short input and writes those attributes at their default values instead of forwarding the data untouched, so what comes back carries the node attributes with none of its work behind them.

Nothing here declares a filter pin. A path node that takes one declares it itself, which is why the label differs from node to node and why some are required and some are not. What this base contributes is the tooltip they share, Path points processing filters.

Not everything that works on paths is built on this base. **Copy to Path**, **Get Path Data** and **Reverse Order** are ordinary point processors, so none of them carries `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` and each settles what a short input means on its own terms.

UPCGExPathReduceSettings.name: Path : Reduce
UPCGExPathReduceSettings.purpose: Takes points out of a path and writes a pair of tangent vectors on the ones left, chosen so a curve drawn through them still follows the run the removed points described. `Mode` decides who picks the survivors: `Preserve` lets `Error Tolerance` do it and treats the filters as points that may not be touched, while `Anchors` hands the whole decision to the filters and reduces the path to exactly what they named. The tangents are the point of the node, and they are what makes this different from deleting points.
UPCGExPathReduceSettings.situation: A dense path that has to survive as a handful of control points, most often because a spline or a curve system is what reads it next.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns them with fewer points, in the same order, in the same places. Nothing is moved and nothing is invented; a survivor keeps its own position and its own attributes, and every point that goes takes its values with it. Two vector attributes are written on what is left, one for the tangent arriving at a point and one for the tangent leaving it, fitted against the points that were removed between it and its new neighbours. A reduction that would leave fewer than two points is abandoned and the path comes back whole, with the two tangent attributes present but unfitted.

off_label.claim: Anchors mode with a filter that passes everything reduces nothing and still fits tangents on every point, which turns the node into a tangent writer for an existing polyline without touching its shape.
off_label.grounded_in: Anchors mode calls the tangent fitting directly on the filter mask, with no simplification pass of its own

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to reduce.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Read differently by the two modes. Under `Preserve` a point that passes cannot be removed, and an empty pin therefore protects nothing. Under `Anchors` a point that passes is the only kind that survives, and the pin becomes required.
inputs.condition: required when Mode is Anchors, optional otherwise

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The reduced paths, carrying the two tangent attributes.

Mode.semantics: Who decides which points survive. `Preserve`, which ships, runs a shape-driven reduction against `Error Tolerance` and treats the filters as a veto over it. `Anchors` skips the reduction entirely: the filters name the survivors and the shape is not consulted, so a path can be cut down to two points however far the result strays from the original run.

ErrorTolerance.semantics: The furthest a removed point is allowed to sit from the straight line between the survivors either side of it, in world units. It is a distance rather than an angle, so on a long straight run it tolerates far more curvature than on a short one.

ArriveName.semantics: Written on every output point, endpoints included. Both tangent attributes are created whether or not the reduction ran, so a path that came back whole still carries them.

SmoothingMode.semantics: Whether the two tangents at a survivor are allowed to disagree. `None (Accurate)` fits each side independently and follows the original points most closely, at the cost of a visible kink at each survivor. `Direction Only (G1)` aligns their directions and refits their lengths, so the curve has no kink but can still change speed. `Full (C1)`, which ships, matches both.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Smoothing.semantics: How far toward the matched tangent each side is pulled, from 0 for the independently fitted pair to 1 for a fully matched one. It ships at 1, so the shipped configuration is as smooth as the node goes and lowering it is what buys accuracy back.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: Honoured in the off position: a path of fewer than two points is forwarded untouched, carrying neither tangent attribute. Output is staged without a size test, so nothing drops it afterwards.

hints.text: Tangents are attributes, not geometry. A reduced path drawn on its own is a polyline through the survivors and looks nothing like the original; the curve only reappears once something reads `Arrive Tangent` and `Leave Tangent`, **Create Spline** and the spline mesh nodes being the usual readers.

UPCGExPathSlideSettings.name: Path : Slide
UPCGExPathSlideSettings.purpose: Moves each point along the path toward one of its two neighbours, by a fraction of that gap or by a fixed distance. It also owns the return trip: the location a point held before the slide is written to an attribute, and the node's second mode reads that attribute back and clears it. Which points move is decided by the **Filters** pin, on the way out as well as on the way in.
UPCGExPathSlideSettings.situation: Points sit on the corners of a run and need to sit part way along the segments instead, without losing the ability to put them back.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns the same points in the same order, moved. Point count, order, rotations, scales and every attribute come through untouched; only locations change. Each point moves from the positions as they arrived, so a slide never compounds along the run and the result does not depend on which point was handled first. A path of fewer than two points is refused with a warning.

off_label.claim: Turn `Write Old Position` on and wire the **Filters** pin to a filter nothing passes: every point records its location into the attribute and none of them move. A position snapshot, taken with the node that owns the attribute rather than by hand.
off_label.grounded_in: ProcessPoints writes RestorePositionBuffer before the PointFilterCache early-out, so the record is unconditional while the move is not

off_label.claim: Restore also reads the **Filters** pin, so a slide can be undone on part of a path and left standing on the rest in one pass.
off_label.grounded_in: ProcessRange skips points whose PointFilterCache entry is false before writing the stored location back

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to slide.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Decides which points move, in both modes. With the pin empty every point moves.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The same points in the same order, at new locations.

Mode.tooltip: Whether to slide or restore position
Mode.semantics: Restore hides the direction and amount rows because the stored vector is the whole answer, and it consumes that attribute: the values are read back and the attribute is then removed from the data, so a second Restore has nothing left to read.
Mode.trap: The removal covers the whole dataset even when the **Filters** pin restricted which points were put back. The points that failed the filter keep their slid location and lose the record that would have moved them.

Direction.tooltip: Slide toward the next or previous point on the path.
Direction.semantics: On a closed path the neighbour always exists, because the run wraps. On an open one it does not, at whichever end faces the chosen direction, and that endpoint reflects its single real neighbour through itself instead: it slides the same distance directly away from the run, off the end of the path. Sliding toward Next moves the last point outward, sliding toward Previous moves the first.

AmountMeasure.tooltip: Discrete means actual distance, relative means a percentage of the segment length
AmountMeasure.semantics: Relative reads `Slide Amount` as a fraction of the gap to the neighbour, so 0.5 lands halfway and 1 lands on the neighbour itself, and the same value moves a long segment further than a short one. Discrete reads it as a world distance along that same direction, identical on every segment. Neither is clamped: past 1 in Relative, or past the segment length in Discrete, the point carries on beyond its neighbour, and a negative value in either sends it the other way.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

bWriteOldPosition.tooltip: Whether to store the old position
bWriteOldPosition.semantics: The record is taken for every point, including the ones the **Filters** pin will reject, so a partial slide is still fully reversible. The attribute is created fresh on each run, so a second Slide node downstream overwrites the first node's record and only the last slide in a chain can be undone.

RestorePositionAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute to write to or restore from
RestorePositionAttributeName.semantics: A vector of world locations, so anything that reads a vector attribute can use it: the distance a point travelled, a lerp back toward where it started, a filter on how far it moved. Restore is one consumer of it rather than the only one.

UPCGExPathSolidifySettings.name: Path : Solidify
UPCGExPathSolidifySettings.purpose: Turns each segment of a path into one oriented box. The point that starts a segment keeps its place in the order and is rewritten: its rotation is built from the direction of that segment, and its bounds are stretched to span the segment's whole length, with `Radius` on the other two axes giving the box its thickness. What comes out is ordinary point data whose bounds happen to tile the run, which is what vanilla bounds-driven spawners and PCGEx's own fitting read.
UPCGExPathSolidifySettings.situation: A path that has to become a physical run of geometry, pipes, walls or rails, where each piece has to reach exactly from one point to the next.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns the same points in the same order, with their transforms and bounds replaced. Since a segment starts at each point and reaches the next, an open path's last point begins none and has no box to build; `Remove Last Point` ships on and drops it, so five points in become four boxes out. Close the path and every point starts a segment, the seam included, and the count is unchanged. The bounds always span the segment's full length whatever `Solidification Lerp` is set to; what the lerp moves is where the point's own pivot sits inside that span. Bounds are written divided by the point's scale, so they measure the same distance in the world however the point was scaled.

off_label.claim: Disable both radius axes and the node stops being about thickness at all: the boxes collapse to a line along each segment while rotations still align to it, which makes it a cheap way to orient a whole path to its own direction with the bounds carrying the segment lengths for anything downstream to read.
off_label.grounded_in: Only the primary axis bounds are written unconditionally; the secondary and tertiary are skipped entirely while their Radius Input is Disabled

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to solidify.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One point per segment, carrying the box for it. Attributes come through untouched from the point the segment started at.

bRemoveLastPoint.tooltip: If the path is not closed, the last point cannot be solidified, thus it's usually preferable to remove it.
bRemoveLastPoint.semantics: The one setting on this node that changes the point count, and it only ever reaches an open path: on a closed one the last point starts the seam segment and is never dropped.
bRemoveLastPoint.trap: Leaving it off keeps a point whose bounds and rotation were never written, so it carries whatever it arrived with while every point before it carries a box.

SolidificationOrder.tooltip: Axis order, as Primary > Secondary > Tertiary. The primary axis aligns to the segment direction, the secondary to (Direction x Normal), and the tertiary to the path normal itself.
SolidificationOrder.semantics: Downstream, this is what decides which axis of a mesh runs along the path.

OrderAttribute.semantics: Read as an integer index into the six orders, per point, so one path can hand different segments different axis roles. A value outside the range is put back in range by `Order Safety`, and only `Ignore` falls back to the constant above.

OrderSafety.tooltip: How to "sanitize" the input value. "Ignore" will pick the default constant specified above if the attribute value is invalid.

RotationMapping.tooltip: Map of rotation construction orders based on selected mapping.
RotationMapping.semantics: Replaces the single construction choice with one per axis order, so a node reading its order from an attribute can still build each rotation the right way. The six entries are fixed and the keys cannot be edited.

RotationConstruction.tooltip: Defines how the selected axis will be used to construct the point' rotation. This will be using remapped axis from the selected order. X = Primary, Y = Secondary, Z = Tertiary
RotationConstruction.semantics: It matters when the three axes are not perfectly perpendicular, which is the usual state on a path whose normal is fighting the segment direction.

ConstructionSafety.tooltip: How to "sanitize" the input value. "Ignore" will pick the default constant specified above if the attribute value is invalid.

PrimaryAxis.tooltip: Primary axis settings (direction aligned to the segment)

fields.name: FlipInput
fields.tooltip: Input value type for flip

fields.name: bFlip
fields.tooltip: Whether to flip this axis or not

fields.name: FlipAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Whether to flip this axis or not

PrimaryAxis.semantics: Carries a flip and nothing else: there is no radius here because the primary axis is sized by the segment, not by a value you set. Flipping it turns the box around so it reaches backwards from the point instead of forwards.

SecondaryAxis.tooltip: Secondary axis settings, relative to the selected order

fields.tooltip: Input value type for flip

fields.name: Slide
fields.tooltip: Slide factor that shifts the bounds along this axis while preserving their size (2*Radius). 0.5 = centered (min = -Radius, max = +Radius), 0   = shifted fully negative (min = -2*Radius, max = 0), 1   = shifted fully positive (min = 0, max = +2*Radius).

SecondaryAxis.semantics: Its `Radius` ships Disabled, and while it is disabled that axis of the bounds is left exactly as it arrived, which on ordinary points is the small default box. Half the reason a solidified path looks like a row of slivers is that only one of the three axes was ever set.

TertiaryAxis.tooltip: Tertiary axis settings, relative to the selected order

fields.tooltip: Slide factor that shifts the bounds along this axis while preserving their size (2*Radius). 0.5 = centered (min = -Radius, max = +Radius), 0   = shifted fully negative (min = -2*Radius, max = 0), 1   = shifted fully positive (min = 0, max = +2*Radius).

TertiaryAxis.semantics: The same block on the axis the normal points along, and it is the one that reads as height or as vertical thickness on a mostly flat path.

Normal.tooltip: Type of arithmetic path point cross direction.
Normal.semantics: The four computed modes derive their frame per segment from the world up vector in the plugin settings, so a segment running close to vertical has nothing left to derive from and the roll jumps.
Normal.trap: A segment of zero length has no direction to build a frame from, so it borrows one from the nearest segment that has one. Its box still collapses to nothing along the primary axis, since that length is what sized it.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

fields.name: Constant
fields.tooltip: Direction vector when using constant input.

fields.name: bFlip
fields.tooltip: Negate the direction vector after reading.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SolidificationLerp.semantics: Where the point sits inside the box, not how long the box is. At 0, which is what ships, the point stays where it was and the box reaches forward to the next point; at 1 the point moves onto the next point and the box reaches back; at 0.5 it sits at the segment's midpoint with the box split evenly. It is clamped to 0 through 1.
SolidificationLerp.trap: The point is moved, so the output positions no longer describe the original path. Anything reading the run after this node reads the pivots this setting chose.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: Reaches the input side only here. Output is staged without any size test, so a two-point path solidified with `Remove Last Point` on comes out as a single point carrying one box, which no gate removes.

UPCGExPathSplineMeshSettings.name: Staging : Spline Mesh
UPCGExPathSplineMeshSettings.purpose: Path segments get meshes, deformed along them. One spline mesh component per pair of consecutive path points, each taking its mesh from a collection entry, so a run of points comes out as continuous geometry that bends with the path and not as assets standing at its points. The mesh comes from one of two places, and that choice reorganizes the rest of the node: staged points arriving with a pick already recorded, or a live pick made here from a Mesh Collection with a Selector wired to the node. The path sibling Path : Spline Mesh (Simple) does the same segment work from a mesh path attribute or a constant mesh, with no collection involved.
UPCGExPathSplineMeshSettings.situation: A path has to become a continuous run of geometry, with the mesh for each span chosen from a collection.

mechanism.text: One spline mesh component per segment, a segment being a point and the one after it: an open path of N points yields N-1 components, a closed one yields N. Each segment takes its mesh from the point it starts at, so the trailing point of an open path, a point the Point Filters rejected, and a point whose pick is missing or resolves to something other than a mesh entry each leave a gap in the run. Components attach to the Target Actor and are PCG-managed, so a regeneration replaces them. The paths pass through on Paths one dataset for one, carrying the picked asset path on every point. Which of the two sources supplies the mesh is decided by Use Staged Points, and the fitting half of the node follows from it.

off_label.claim: Point Filters punch holes in a run. A rejected point produces no component, and the span missing is the one that would have started at it, so a filter over path points authors gaps without splitting the path or moving anything.
off_label.grounded_in: the PointFilterCache test at the head of the point loop routes the index to HandleInvalidPoint, which writes an empty asset path and leaves the segment slot without a mesh entry

off_label.claim: With Weight To Attribute on, every point that produced no component is written as -1, or as 0 in the two Density options, so the weight attribute doubles as a per-point map of where segments actually exist, including the trailing point of every open path.
off_label.grounded_in: HandleInvalidPoint writes -1 through the weight writer or 0 into Density for filtered, unresolved, non-mesh and end-of-path indices

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to build segments along. A dataset with fewer than two points is forwarded untouched and reported, whatever Omit Invalid Paths Outputs says.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the staged picks resolve against. A map that rebuilds no valid mapping is an execution error.
inputs.condition: when Use Staged Points is on; with it off the pin drops to advanced and nothing reads it

inputs.label: Selector
inputs.note: The sub-node deciding which entry each segment gets. Exactly one factory is accepted, and an empty pin is an execution error.
inputs.condition: when Use Staged Points is off and Selector Mode is External; otherwise the pin drops to advanced and nothing reads it

inputs.label: AttributeSet
inputs.note: Feeds the Attribute Set collection source, which builds a throwaway collection from an attribute set. The Collection Source option that makes this pin required is hidden from the dropdown, so on a node configured today the pin stays advanced and unused.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which points start a segment. A rejected point produces no component and no asset path.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The input paths, one dataset for one, with the picked asset path written on every point and the entry weight beside it when that output is on. The components are created as a side effect and are not carried on this pin.

bUseStagedPoints.semantics: The source split, and the panel reorganizes around it. On, the mesh is whatever an upstream staging pass already decided: the Map pin becomes required, the whole Fitting section disappears, and the only fitting value still in play is the offset the earlier pass recorded. Off, the node makes the pick itself from a Mesh Collection, the Selector pin becomes required, and Scale to Fit and Justification are solved here per segment. Either way only mesh entries produce components, so a staged dataset holding actor or level picks leaves those points with a gap instead of an error.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).
StagingLayer.semantics: Producers and consumers pair on the layer name: this node reads the pick attribute of the layer named here, and it has to be the layer the upstream staging pass wrote to.
StagingLayer.trap: A path carrying no pick on the named layer is abandoned before any writing happens, so it comes out with no components and without the asset path attribute the other paths get. Pointing the setting at a layer nothing wrote looks the same as pointing it at unstaged points.

CollectionSource.semantics: Asset builds every path from one Mesh Collection. Path Attribute reads a collection asset path per point, and every collection named across the input is discovered and loaded before processing begins, so one batch can draw from many collections at once. The Attribute Set option is hidden from the dropdown; a node still carrying it builds a collection from the AttributeSet pin, rebuilds its staging data in the graph, and is forced onto the node's Default Descriptor whatever the Force Default Descriptor toggle says.

fields.name: AssetPathSourceAttribute
fields.tooltip: Name of the attribute on the AttributeSet that contains the asset path to be staged

fields.name: WeightSourceAttribute
fields.tooltip: Name of the attribute on the AttributeSet that contains the asset weight, if any.

fields.name: CategorySourceAttribute
fields.tooltip: Name of the attribute on the AttributeSet that contains the asset category, if any.

fields.name: AssetCollectionType
fields.tooltip: Defines what type of temp collection to build from input attribute set

SelectorMode.tooltip: How distribution is configured for this node. Legacy uses the inline settings below -- only set for legacy nodes. External uses a factory on the Selector input pin.
SelectorMode.semantics: Nodes saved before the selector system land on Legacy when they load, where the inline Distribution settings drive the pick, the Selector pin is ignored, and every execution warns that the mode is scheduled for removal. Anything created since is External. Migration is switching the mode and wiring a Selector : Classic configured the way the inline settings were. The setting has no effect at all while Use Staged Points is on, since no pick is made here.

DistributionSettings.tooltip: Distribution details Note : LEGACY Nodes only.

fields.name: Category
fields.tooltip: Category name source (constant or per-point attribute).

fields.name: MissingCategoryBehavior
fields.tooltip: What to do when a point asks for a category the collection cannot serve. A blank key selects the uncategorized entries, and only counts as missing when there are none.

fields.name: Distribution
fields.tooltip: Distribution type

fields.name: IndexSettings
fields.tooltip: Index settings

fields.name: LocalSeed
fields.tooltip: Only accounted for if selected in the seed component.

MaterialDistributionSettings.tooltip: How should materials be distributed and picked. Note : LEGACY Nodes only.

fields.name: Distribution
fields.tooltip: Distribution type

fields.name: IndexSettings
fields.tooltip: Index settings

Tangents.tooltip: Per-point tangent settings. Can't be set if the spline is linear.
Tangents.semantics: A segment's curvature is its two tangents: the near point's leave tangent and the far point's arrive tangent. Attribute, the value this node ships with, reads them from ArriveTangent and LeaveTangent. In-place computes them from the path through a tangents module, with optional separate modules for the first and last point of an open path. No Tangents falls back to unit-length vectors taken from each point's own forward direction, which reads as a straight chord across anything longer than a unit.
Tangents.trap: Plain path points carry neither ArriveTangent nor LeaveTangent. On a freshly placed node the missing attribute is an error and that path builds nothing, which makes the tangent source the first thing to set on this node rather than the last.

ScaleToFit.tooltip: If enabled, will break scaling interpolation across the spline.

fields.name: ScaleToFitMode
fields.tooltip: How scaling is applied to fit within target bounds. None = no scaling, Uniform = same scale all axes, Individual = per-axis control.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: Uniform scaling strategy. Fill = stretch to fill, Min = fit smallest axis, Max = fit largest axis, Avg = average.

fields.name: ScaleToFitX
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for X axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitY
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Y axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitZ
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Z axis when using Individual mode.

ScaleToFit.semantics: This node ships with None, where Staging : Distribute ships with uniform Min: a live pick here places the mesh at its authored size against the point's own scale, and nothing resizes it to the point's bounds until a mode is chosen. The mode does a second thing as well. Anything other than None makes the far end of a segment take the same fitted scale as its near end, so cross-section scale stops interpolating from one path point to the next and a path whose points taper stops tapering.
ScaleToFit.trap: The Fitting section is hidden while Use Staged Points is on, but the stored Scale to Fit value still decides the interpolation half. A node configured with a fit and then switched over to staged points keeps producing constant-section segments, with nothing left in the panel to explain it.

Justification.semantics: Justification produces a translation, and a spline mesh can only take that translation on the two axes across the segment; whatever the alignment asks for along the segment's own axis is dropped. All three axes are active out of the box, aligning centre to centre, so a mesh whose pivot sits off-centre in its bounds shifts sideways as soon as the node picks live, even with Scale to Fit on None.

bReadTranslation.tooltip: Read the fitting translation offset from staged points.
bReadTranslation.semantics: The staged-points counterpart of Justification. Staging : Distribute and Staging : Fitting can record what their fit moved into a FittingOffset attribute, and reading it back here offsets the segment so the deformed mesh sits where the fitted point did. The same two-axis rule applies: only the components across the segment survive, the one along it is dropped.
bReadTranslation.trap: A path missing the named attribute is abandoned the same way a path with no pick is, so turning this on for a batch where only some paths were fitted silently costs the rest their components.

TranslationAttributeName.tooltip: If enabled, applies staged fitting/justification to the spline mesh segment.

fields.name: bPushStart
fields.tooltip: Push the start point of the spline mesh segment.

fields.name: StartPush
fields.tooltip: How far to push the start point.

fields.name: bRelativeStart
fields.tooltip: If enabled, value will relative to the size of the segment

fields.name: bPushEnd
fields.tooltip: Push the end point of the spline mesh segment.

fields.name: EndPush
fields.tooltip: How far to push the end point.

fields.name: bRelativeEnd
fields.tooltip: If enabled, value will relative to the size of the segment

MutationDetails.semantics: Push Start and Push End move a segment's ends outward along its own tangent directions and lengthen the tangents to match, so neighbouring segments overlap through the point they share instead of meeting exactly on it. Relative, on by default, reads Amount as a fraction of that segment's straight-line length, so the overlap scales with the span; off, it is a distance. It runs last, on the segment as already built, so it moves what fitting, offsets and tangents produced without feeding back into any of them.

AssetPathAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write asset path to.
AssetPathAttributeName.semantics: The attribute is written on every run and in both source modes, including staged points where the pick was made elsewhere, so the output paths always report the mesh each span used. Points that produced no component get an empty path, which is what separates a gap from a segment downstream.

TaggingDetails.semantics: Grab Tags reads tags off the picked entry and puts them on the spawned component, and it has something to read only when the node picks live. With Use Staged Points on the resolved entry's tags are not collected, so Forward Input Data Tags, which copies the input dataset's own tags, is the only half still doing anything.

WeightToAttribute.tooltip: Update point scale so staged asset fits within its bounds
WeightToAttribute.semantics: The value written is the picked entry's weight. Raw writes the authored integer, the Normalized options divide by the pool the pick came out of, and the two Density options bypass the attribute entirely and write into the point's Density property. Points that produced no component are written too, as -1 in the attribute or 0 in Density, which always includes the trailing point of an open path.

WeightAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write asset weight to.

SplineMeshUpMode.tooltip: How the spline mesh up vector is determined.
SplineMeshUpMode.semantics: Constant points every segment at the same world direction, Z up out of the box, so a run stays coplanar however the path turns. Attribute reads a vector from the point each segment starts at, letting the orientation bank or twist along the path; a node created today arrives with the selector already pointing at $Rotation.Up, which follows the point's own rotation. From Tangents (Gimbal fix) derives the direction per segment from that segment's two tangents, so it stays perpendicular to the plane the segment bends in, and where the two tangents nearly agree it substitutes a fixed direction built from the start tangent, since no perpendicular is defined there.

SplineMeshUpVectorAttribute.tooltip: Attribute to read the spline mesh up vector from.

SplineMeshUpVector.tooltip: Constant up vector for all spline mesh segments.
