fields.tooltip: Attribute name for the best-fit plane transform.

PointsCountAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute to write points count to
PointsCountAttributeName.semantics: Records how many points went into the box. After a collapse this is the only record of the group's size, since the points themselves are gone.

hints.text: Under `Collapse` an entire dataset becomes one point. Anything downstream that pairs by index against the original data, or expects the same count back, no longer lines up.

UPCGExPreloadResourcesSettings.name: Resources
UPCGExPreloadResourcesSettings.purpose: Asset loading is the cost that lands at spawn time, and this node is where you move it. Preload Resources resolves every asset a set of collections references, plus any standalone assets and any asset paths read off a connected input, loads them, and holds them loaded on the PCG component so later generations find them already resident. Release Resources is the other half: it drops everything this node type is holding on that component, freeing the assets for garbage collection. The palette carries those two entries and nothing else, the node title reports which one it is as a subtitle, and the choice is fixed when you drop it in.
UPCGExPreloadResourcesSettings.situation: A graph spawns from collections whose content is not yet loaded, and the streaming cost has to land somewhere other than the middle of generation.

mechanism.text: Nothing flows through this node. Preload Resources gathers a set of asset paths from the collections, the standalone list and the connected input, loads them, and hands the hold to the PCG component that owns the generation, where it outlives the execution. A later run resolving the identical set keeps that hold and loads nothing; a run resolving a different set replaces it, so paths that fell out of the configuration stop being held on their own. Release Resources drops every hold this node type placed on the component, whatever put them there. The only output is a dependency pin, so downstream nodes can order themselves after the node without receiving data.

off_label.claim: Log Loaded Resources prints the resolved path set rather than what the pass actually loaded, and it prints ahead of the reuse check, so a Preload node pointed at one collection with every flag set doubles as a listing of everything that collection reaches, nested entries and custom-property references included.
off_label.grounded_in: the bLogLoadedResources block in AdvanceWork iterates the sorted Paths array before TryReuseManagedResource is consulted

inputs.label: Sources
inputs.note: Points or attribute sets whose rows carry the asset paths to preload. Every connected dataset is read, and each is resolved for its own attribute.
inputs.condition: on the Preload Resources entry with Load From Inputs on; the pin does not exist otherwise

inputs.label: Execution Dependency
inputs.note: The vanilla ordering pin every node carries. Promoting it to required is how a release is made to land after the work that used the assets, since a Release node has no data pins to order it.
inputs.condition: on the Release Resources entry; advanced and optional on Preload Resources

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: Dependency only. It carries no data; wiring it into a downstream node orders that node after this one and nothing else.

Collections.tooltip: Asset collections whose referenced assets should be preloaded.
Collections.semantics: Every collection listed is loaded so it can be read, and stays resident alongside whatever the flags gather out of it, so a collection listed with all flags cleared is still held. Nested collections are hard references on their parent entries, so they arrive with the parent and never need listing separately.

CollectionLoadFlags.tooltip: Which categories of each collection's referenced assets to preload.
CollectionLoadFlags.semantics: Direct Assets gathers the staged asset path of each top-level entry, skipping entries whose asset is unset. Custom Properties is a separate axis on top of that, adding the soft paths held by the collection's own property values, its category overrides and every entry override.
CollectionLoadFlags.trap: Sub-Collections is a recursion switch, not a source of its own. Set alone it walks the nested collections and gathers nothing out of them, because the entries it reaches are only collected when Direct Assets is set too. A nested tree needs both.

Assets.tooltip: Additional standalone assets to preload, beyond anything referenced by the collections above.

bLoadFromInputs.tooltip: Also read assets to preload from a connected input (points or attribute set). Opt-in: PCG forces the first input pin to be Required, so the input pin only exists while this is enabled.

AssetAttribute.tooltip: Attribute on each input row holding the asset to preload (FSoftObjectPath, or an FString path). Defaults to @Last; clear it to None to use the first FSoftObjectPath attribute found.
AssetAttribute.semantics: The fallback is wider than a cleared selector: a name that does not exist on an input also falls through to the first soft object path attribute on that data, decided per input dataset rather than once for the node.
AssetAttribute.trap: A misspelled name preloads whatever soft path attribute happens to come first instead of failing, and an input carrying none at all is skipped without a message.

bTrackResources.tooltip: Register the preloaded assets for change-tracking so editing a referenced collection/asset forces a graph refresh. Editor-only effect.

bManageOnOriginalComponent.tooltip: Whether to store resources on original component or not. Disable this when working with partitioned graphs that don't have unique per-partitions resources
bManageOnOriginalComponent.semantics: It decides which component the hold is anchored to, and the release path reads the same setting to decide which component to sweep.
bManageOnOriginalComponent.trap: The setting is hidden on the Release Resources entry, where it keeps its default of on. A Preload switched off for partitioned work anchors its holds on the local component, and a Release node dropped from the palette sweeps the original component instead and leaves them held.

bLogLoadedResources.tooltip: Print out the list of loaded assets
bLogLoadedResources.semantics: The list is the resolved path set, printed on every pass including the ones that reuse an existing hold and load nothing. Editor only.

hints.text: Release Resources is not the counterpart of one Preload node. It drops every hold this node type placed on the component, whichever node put it there, so a single release on a component carrying several preloads empties all of them.
Loading here is blocking and runs on the game thread. The preload is itself the stall, which is the point: it happens where you placed the node instead of during spawning.
Holds are anchored to a PCG component. When the generation's execution source is not one there is nowhere to anchor them, and the node warns and does nothing.

addenda.title: Console variables
addenda.text: The resource cache the Preload entry feeds is governed by three console variables, project-wide:

items.note: Seconds an idle, unreferenced cached resource survives before eviction. Default 45.
When enabled, suppresses eviction while any PCG generation is in flight. Default off.

UPCGExPrimitiveFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Primitive Overlap
UPCGExPrimitiveFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Asks whether each element's own box touches the collision geometry of primitive components handed to it on a pin. The components are named by the wire rather than found by a query, so collision channels, profiles and trace settings play no part: the test is a shape overlap run against each component in turn. It also answers for a whole dataset at once, which puts it among the few point filters that Uber Filter (Data), Uber Branch and Break accept.
UPCGExPrimitiveFilterProviderSettings.situation: A set of colliders marks where content belongs or does not, and every element has to be judged against them.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this once per element. The element's chosen bounds become a box, set at its position and turned by its rotation, and that box is overlap-tested against the collision geometry of the components on the Primitives pin. One touch is enough and nothing counts how many, so the verdict is a yes or no about the whole set. A component with no collision geometry can never register a touch, and data on the pin carrying no live component is skipped. Asked at dataset level instead, the same test runs once on the dataset's bounding box, which stays upright whatever the elements are rotated to, and every element in that dataset inherits the answer.

off_label.claim: Its verdict needs nothing beyond the element itself, so it survives on the Stop Conditions pin of Tensors : Extrude and Tensors Transform, which drop filters that cannot answer for a point in isolation. A set of colliders then becomes the wall an extrusion stops against.
off_label.grounded_in: SupportsProxyEvaluation returning true on the factory, which is what PCGExPointFilter::PruneForDirectEvaluation keeps when those two elements gather their Stop Conditions

inputs.label: Primitives
inputs.note: Primitive data, one component per entry. Every dataset on the pin is pooled into one set, and anything that is not primitive data, or whose component has gone, is skipped without comment.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node produces. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: An empty Primitives pin, or one whose data carries no live component, does not stop the node: it is the failure that routes through Missing Data Policy, which defaults to Fail. Under Error this node reports the missing input and cancels.

Filtering an attribute set hands every row to this filter as a default point at the world origin, with no rotation and default bounds. Every row then tests the same box in the same place, so the whole set takes one answer and nothing is logged.

UPCGExProbeAnisotropicProviderSettings.name: Probe : Anisotropic
UPCGExProbeAnisotropicProviderSettings.purpose: Sixteen bearings, 22.5 degrees apart, one connection each. The probe fans a compass around every point and keeps the best-aligned candidate in each of the sixteen wedges, which is how a loose scatter turns into something that reads as a grid or a lattice. The fan is flat, and Transform Direction decides whose plane it lies in: each point's own by default, the world XY plane with the toggle off.
UPCGExProbeAnisotropicProviderSettings.situation: Connectivity that should follow fixed compass bearings rather than proximity, on a layout that is flat or projected flat.

mechanism.text: Each of the sixteen bearings holds one connection at most, so a point asks for sixteen at most and usually far fewer. A candidate qualifies for a bearing when it sits within Max Angle of it, and the best-aligned qualifying candidate takes the slot however far away it is inside the search radius. Distance decides nothing here. Max Angle caps at 11.25 degrees, half the spacing, so the wedges never overlap and a candidate can qualify for one bearing at most.

off_label.claim: Run it projected, with Transform Direction off and Max Angle at its maximum of 11.25, and the wedges meet edge to edge, so every candidate in the neighbourhood falls in exactly one of them. The probe then reads as a sixteen-way angular partition that keeps one representative per sector, rather than as a rule about bearings.
off_label.grounded_in: ClampMax=11.25 against the fixed 22.5 degree spacing of FPCGExProbeAnisotropic::Directions, with MinDot from PCGExMath::DegreesToDot

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: Wire it to the Probes pin on Cluster : Connect Points or Cluster : Connect Vtx.

fields.name: SearchRadius
fields.tooltip: Search radius.

fields.name: SearchRadiusOffset
fields.tooltip: A convenient static offset added to the attribute value.

fields.name: MaxAngle
fields.tooltip: Max angle to search within.

fields.name: bTransformDirection
fields.tooltip: Rotate the sixteen fixed search directions by the point's transform, so the search cones follow point rotation. Scale is ignored.

hints.text: On a point set with any height variation, run the consumer with Project Points on. Projection flattens the positions every distance and bearing test is measured between and leaves the output transforms untouched, which is what lets a flat fan reach candidates that are not level with the point. It does not flatten the fan: with Transform Direction on the bearings are still carried by each point's own rotation, so a projected run over points that do not share an orientation wants that toggle off as well.

UPCGExProbeBitmasksProviderSettings.name: Probe : Bitmasks
UPCGExProbeBitmasksProviderSettings.purpose: Probe : Anisotropic with a bearing set you author. Instead of sixteen fixed compass points it takes its bearings from Bitmask Collection entries and from individually named entries, and keeps one connection per bearing. What it reads off an entry is the Direction vector; the mask value rides along and decides nothing here.
UPCGExProbeBitmasksProviderSettings.situation: A connectivity pattern that has to follow one specific set of bearings, authored once in an asset and reused across several graphs.

mechanism.text: Every bearing in the assembled set holds one connection at most, and it goes to the nearest candidate sitting within Angle of that bearing. Bearings that catch nothing produce nothing, so a point asks for at most as many connections as the set has bearings. Angle carries no cap, so wedges wider than half the spacing between two bearings overlap and one candidate can satisfy several of them; the connections that result collapse into one.

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: Wire it to the Probes pin on Cluster : Connect Points or Cluster : Connect Vtx.

fields.name: SearchRadius
fields.tooltip: Search radius.

fields.name: SearchRadiusOffset
fields.tooltip: A convenient static offset added to the attribute value.

fields.name: bTransformDirection
fields.tooltip: Rotate the bitmask's directions by the point's transform, so the search cones follow point rotation. Scale is ignored.

fields.name: Favor
fields.tooltip: What matters more?

fields.name: Angle
fields.tooltip: Shared angle threshold

fields.name: Compositions
fields.tooltip: Operations executed on the flag if all filters pass (or if no filter is set)

fields.name: Collections
fields.tooltip: Operations executed on the flag if all filters pass (or if no filter is set)

UPCGExProbeChainProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Chain/Path
UPCGExProbeChainProviderSettings.purpose: Puts the points in an order and joins each one to the next, which is the one probe in the family that turns a set into a sequence. Sort Mode picks the order: an attribute value, a distance along an axis, a greedy nearest-point tour, or a space-filling curve index. Closed Loop joins the last back to the first. Every link still has to clear Search Radius, so the sequence can come out in several pieces.
UPCGExProbeChainProviderSettings.situation: A set that has to be walked as a single sequence, where the order comes from an attribute or from the shape of the set itself.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. It orders every point by the chosen rule, drops the ones both role filters excluded, then joins each surviving point to the next in that order. A link is placed only when the two points sit within the larger of their two Search Radii and at least one of them may start a connection, so a step in the order wider than the radius breaks the sequence in two. Excluded points do not break it: the order closes over them and their neighbours join directly.

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: Wire it into the Probes pin of Cluster : Connect Points or Cluster : Connect Vtx.

fields.name: SearchRadius
fields.tooltip: Search radius.

fields.name: SearchRadiusOffset
fields.tooltip: A convenient static offset added to the attribute value.

fields.name: SortAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute to sort by (for ByAttribute mode)

fields.name: ProjectionAxis
fields.tooltip: Axis to project onto (for ByAxisProjection mode)

fields.name: bClosedLoop
fields.tooltip: If true, creates a closed loop connecting last to first

hints.text: A link needs one of its two points to be allowed to start a connection. A point that Generator Filters excluded still takes its place in the order and joins up, as long as the point before or after it may start one.

UPCGExProbeClosestProviderSettings.name: Probe : Closest
UPCGExProbeClosestProviderSettings.purpose: Proximity with a cap. Each point asks for connections to the points nearest it and stops at Max Connections, which can be read per point from an attribute so some points reach for more than others. It carries a coincidence check of its own, on top of whatever the consumer does, which spreads the connections it asks for around the point.
UPCGExProbeClosestProviderSettings.situation: A scatter that should become a cluster on nothing more than proximity, with a per-point say in how many connections each point reaches for.

mechanism.text: Candidates are walked nearest first and connected in that order until Max Connections is reached or the search radius runs out. Nothing is scored and nothing is compared, so the connections a point asks for are the nearest ones that cleared its two coincidence checks.

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: Wire it to the Probes pin on Cluster : Connect Points or Cluster : Connect Vtx.

fields.name: SearchRadius
fields.tooltip: Search radius.

fields.name: SearchRadiusOffset
fields.tooltip: A convenient static offset added to the attribute value.

fields.name: MaxConnections
fields.tooltip: Max number of connections.

fields.name: CoincidencePreventionTolerance
fields.tooltip: Attempts to prevent connections that are roughly in the same direction

UPCGExProbeDBSCANProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : DBSCAN
UPCGExProbeDBSCANProviderSettings.purpose: Sorts a scatter by local density and connects the dense parts of it. A point with enough neighbours inside its Search Radius is a core point; a point that has a core point in reach but too few neighbours of its own is a border point; everything else is left alone. Search Radius is the epsilon of the algorithm and Min Points is the density bar.
UPCGExProbeDBSCANProviderSettings.situation: A scatter of dense clumps with thin strays between them, where the clumps should become clusters and the strays should fall out.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. A point counts the other points inside its own Search Radius and becomes a core point when that count reaches Min Points; the only ones left out of the count are those both role filters excluded. Core points that may start a connection then connect out through that same neighbourhood. Border points attach to core points only, and only while Core To Core Only is off. Nothing here labels or grows clusters: the connections go out flat, and the density-connected groups emerge as the connected components the consumer builds from them.

off_label.claim: Leave Core To Core Only on, wire this as the only probe, and take the Vtx output alone: everything short of core density, along with every core point that has no core neighbour, ends with no connection and never reaches the output, which makes the pass an outlier prune with Min Points as the strength.
off_label.grounded_in: the second pass emits only from IsCore points to IsCore neighbours while bCoreToCorOnly holds, and FGraphBuilder::Compile drops points that ended with no edge

hints.text: This probe reads the two role filter pins differently from the rest of the family. Generator Filters decides which points place connections, in both the core case and the border case, as it does everywhere. Connectable Filters does not bar a point from receiving one here: a point counts toward its neighbours' density and can be connected to unless both pins excluded it.

UPCGExProbeDirectionProviderSettings.name: Probe : Direction
UPCGExProbeDirectionProviderSettings.purpose: One connection per point, along an axis you name. The axis can be a constant for the whole set or read per point from an attribute, and it can be carried by the point's own rotation, which is what turns a field of oriented points into a set of aligned chains. Max Angle sets how far off a candidate may sit and still qualify, and Favor decides which of the qualifying candidates gets the single connection.
UPCGExProbeDirectionProviderSettings.situation: Connectivity that has to follow an axis rather than proximity: aligned rows, oriented chains, a flow read from an attribute.

mechanism.text: At most one connection per point, and only from candidates inside the search radius that clear the angle test. Favor picks the winner among those, and a point whose neighbourhood holds no qualifying candidate asks for nothing at all. The one-per-point cap is what makes this probe produce chains: a Vtx ends up joined to the single candidate it chose, plus whatever connections other points aimed at it.

UPCGExProbeFactoryProviderSettings.name: Probe Definition
UPCGExProbeFactoryProviderSettings.purpose: The base every Probe : and G-Probe : node inherits. It never appears in the palette, and this page carries what the family shares: the Probe pin they all emit on, the Search Radius deciding how far one reaches, and what separates the two prefixes. Their consumers are Cluster : Connect Points, which builds a cluster out of loose points, and Cluster : Connect Vtx, which adds connections to a cluster that already exists.
UPCGExProbeFactoryProviderSettings.situation: Reading any probe page and needing to know what its Search Radius means, or which of the two prefixes is in hand and what that changes.

mechanism.text: The consumer turns every factory on its Probes pin into a live probe for each input dataset, then asks each of them for connections. A Probe : is asked once per point that may start a connection, and answers from that point's neighbourhood alone: the points allowed to receive a connection, falling inside its own Search Radius. A probe reading the whole list is handed it nearest first; one running chained sees candidates as they are found, and commits to the single one it ranked best. A G-Probe : is asked once for the whole dataset, is given every point position and both role masks, and works out a finished set of connections on its own. The two mix freely on one pin, and every connection either kind asks for survives into the result. Search Radius is a per-probe setting, so two probes on one pin reach different distances.

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: What every Probe : and G-Probe : node emits. The Probes pin on Cluster : Connect Points and Cluster : Connect Vtx is the only place it is read.

hints.text: Order matters among Probe : sub-nodes, and only while the consumer's Prevent Coincidence is on: they share one claim on the directions leaving each point, taken in the order the probes arrive on the pin. Within that order the ones running in chained mode answer first, then the rest of the radius-based ones, then Probe : Index, which names its targets by index and never looks at a neighbourhood. A G-Probe : runs in a pass of its own alongside all of that and reads none of the claim, so probe order changes nothing about what one proposes.

A probe that cannot bind what it reads, a misspelled attribute on Search Radius being the usual cause, is dropped from the stack for that input while the rest still run, so the result loses whatever that probe would have added. When every probe on the pin drops, the input produces nothing at all.

Three of the family carry no Search Radius and hide the field: Probe : Index reaches by index arithmetic, and G-Probe : KNN and G-Probe : Greedy Spanner size their own neighbourhoods from their own settings. On the rest it defaults to a constant of 100, and switching it to Attribute reveals the Offset added to whatever the attribute holds.

UPCGExProbeGlobalAnisotropicProviderSett.name: G-Probe : Anisotropic
UPCGExProbeGlobalAnisotropicProviderSett.purpose: Ranks candidates by a distance that is stretched along three axes, so a chosen direction reads as closer than it is and wins the ranking. Primary Axis and Secondary Axis set the frame, the three scales weight each direction, and K decides how many of the top-ranked candidates a point connects to.
UPCGExProbeGlobalAnisotropicProviderSett.situation: A scatter that has to connect along a grain, where plain nearest-neighbour would join across the grain as readily as along it.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. Primary Axis and Secondary Axis are squared up into a frame whose third axis is their cross product, and every candidate's offset from the asking point is divided by the matching scale before its length is taken. A larger scale on an axis shortens what the probe measures along it, so that direction climbs the ranking and reaches further in world units. Each point allowed to start a connection takes the K best-ranked accepting candidates that pass the reach test, and can receive more from others.

off_label.claim: Set the three scales to the same value and the ranking collapses back to plain distance, which leaves a nearest-K probe that does obey a radius.
off_label.grounded_in: BuildTransformMatrix divides each axis by its own scale, so equal scales leave the transformed length proportional to the plain one

UPCGExProbeGradientFlowProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Gradient Flow
UPCGExProbeGradientFlowProviderSettings.purpose: Reads a number off every point and connects along the way that number changes. Candidates are scored by gradient, the difference in value divided by the distance to it, so a small change close by outranks a large change further off. Steepest Only decides whether a point keeps one connection each way or connects to everything in reach, and Uphill Only drops the downhill half.
UPCGExProbeGradientFlowProviderSettings.situation: A scalar spread across a scatter, where the connections should follow which way that value climbs and falls.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. Each point allowed to start a connection reads the flow value off every accepting point inside its Search Radius and scores each one by the difference in value over the distance to it. With Steepest Only on, which is the default, it keeps at most two: the steepest climb and the steepest fall. With Steepest Only off, the score stops deciding anything and every candidate in reach connects, gated only by Uphill Only. A point whose neighbours all hold the same value keeps nothing under Steepest Only, because the comparison is strict.

off_label.claim: Turn both toggles off and the flow value stops deciding anything: every accepting point inside Search Radius connects, which leaves a plain radius connect with no ranking behind it.
off_label.grounded_in: the branch taken when bSteepestOnly is false gates only on ValueDiff above zero, and bUphillOnly being false removes that gate

UPCGExProbeHubSpokeProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Hub & Spoke
UPCGExProbeHubSpokeProviderSettings.purpose: Promotes a handful of points to hubs and attaches everything else to them, which turns a flat scatter into two tiers. Hub Selection Mode decides which points get promoted, Num Hubs decides how many, and Connect Hubs decides whether the hubs also join to each other. Every connection it places has to clear Search Radius, hub to hub and spoke to hub alike.
UPCGExProbeHubSpokeProviderSettings.situation: A scatter that has to route through a small number of collection points instead of joining neighbour to neighbour.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. It ranks the points that may start a connection by the chosen mode, promotes the top Num Hubs of them, then attaches every other participating point to a hub. Connect Hubs adds the hub-to-hub connections, tested pairwise and kept only when the pair is in reach. Nearest Hub Only decides whether a spoke takes its closest hub in reach or every hub in reach. A point with no hub inside its own Search Radius gets nothing, and a point that ends with no connection never reaches the output.

off_label.claim: Turn Connect Hubs off and leave Nearest Hub Only on: every point then carries a single connection naming the hub it was assigned to, so the Edges output doubles as a partition of the set into one group per hub.
off_label.grounded_in: the spoke pass emits one edge per non-hub point while bNearestHubOnly holds, and bConnectHubs gates the whole hub-to-hub pass

UPCGExProbeIndexProviderSettings.name: Probe : Index
UPCGExProbeIndexProviderSettings.purpose: The one probe that never looks at a position. It names its target by index, so it joins point 0 to point 1 to point 2 whatever the geometry is doing, which is how an ordered point set becomes a chain, a ring, or a fan into one hub. Search Radius is hidden on this node because no neighbourhood is ever gathered for it.
UPCGExProbeIndexProviderSettings.situation: An ordered point set that has to be wired by its ordering rather than by where its points ended up.

mechanism.text: One index is resolved per point and Mode decides what it means: a target to connect to, an offset forward, or an offset taken both ways for up to two connections. Index Safety decides what an out-of-range result does. A point never connects to itself, and the target has to be a point the consumer's Connectable Filters accepted, so an index landing on a rejected point yields nothing.

off_label.claim: Wire it alongside a radius-based probe and it becomes a way to guarantee a spine: the proximity probe fills in the mesh while this one holds the ordered chain together, including across gaps too wide for any search radius.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExProbeIndex::IsDirectProbe returns true, so FProbingEngine::ProcessScope runs it through ProcessNode outside the radius-gathered candidate pass entirely

UPCGExProbeKNNProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : KNN
UPCGExProbeKNNProviderSettings.purpose: Joins every point to its nearest few, with no distance limit anywhere in the rule. K sets how many, and Mode decides whether one point naming another is enough or whether the naming has to run both ways. It carries no Search Radius, so a point sitting alone in a sparse corner still reaches across the whole set to find its K.
UPCGExProbeKNNProviderSettings.situation: A scatter with uneven spacing that has to come out connected everywhere, where a fixed radius would leave the thin regions bare while over-connecting the dense ones.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. Each point allowed to start a connection ranks every other point by distance and keeps the K closest that are allowed to receive one. Mode decides what happens to those lists. Default turns each list straight into connections, so a point that asked carries the K it named plus whatever other points named it. Mutual keeps a pair only when both named each other, so most points come out with fewer than K and a point on its own can come out with none. K is read per point, so an attribute can vary the count across the set.

off_label.claim: Set K to 1 while Mode is Mutual and the probe pairs points off: only two points that are each other's single nearest join, and everything else is left with no connection and dropped by the consumer.
off_label.grounded_in: the Mutual branch in ProcessAll keeps a pair only when both NeighborSets name each other, and FGraphBuilder::Compile prunes points that ended with no edge

UPCGExProbeLevelSetProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Level Set
UPCGExProbeLevelSetProviderSettings.purpose: Connects points whose value on a chosen scalar sits close together, and leaves the rest alone. Max Level Difference is the width of the band, Search Radius bounds how far a point looks, and Max Connections Per Point caps how many of the survivors each point takes. Normalize Levels rescales the whole input into 0 to 1 first, which changes what the band width means.
UPCGExProbeLevelSetProviderSettings.situation: A scalar spread across a scatter where points at a similar level should join up and points across levels should stay apart.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. Each point allowed to start a connection looks at the accepting points inside its Search Radius, drops any whose level differs by more than Max Level Difference, then ranks what is left by a score blending the squared distance with the level difference multiplied by a hundred and squared. It takes the best few, up to Max Connections Per Point, and can receive more from others. Level similarity carries far more weight than distance in that score, so a further point at a closer level beats a near point at a different one.

off_label.claim: Set Max Level Difference to 0 and only points holding the same value connect, which groups a set by an integer label into one component per label as long as each label's points are within reach of one another.
off_label.grounded_in: the band test is the absolute level difference compared at or under MaxLevelDifference, so zero admits only equal values

UPCGExProbeNumericCompareProviderSetting.name: Probe : Numeric Compare
UPCGExProbeNumericCompareProviderSetting.purpose: Probe : Closest with a value test on top. It walks the same nearest-first neighbourhood and asks for a connection only where the comparison holds between the probing point's value and the candidate's, so every connection in the result joins a pair standing in the same numeric relation. One attribute is read on both ends of the pair; there is no second attribute to set.
UPCGExProbeNumericCompareProviderSetting.situation: Joining points only where a numeric attribute stands in a chosen relation between the two, on top of proximity.

mechanism.text: Candidates are walked nearest first and each one is tested. A candidate that passes is connected and counts against Max Connections; one that fails is skipped and the walk carries on. The walk ends when the cap is reached or the search radius runs out. The attribute is read once per point and the same value serves whether the point is doing the asking or being asked about.

off_label.claim: Point the attribute at a per-point id and pick the not-equal option, and the probe stops being about magnitude: it joins nearby points only across a boundary, which stitches two interleaved sets together without joining either to itself.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExCompare::Compare is called with the probing point's value and the candidate's, and the full EPCGExComparison set including the not-equal option is available

UPCGExProbeRNGProviderSettings.name: Probe : RNG
UPCGExProbeRNGProviderSettings.purpose: RNG here stands for Relative Neighborhood Graph, and has nothing to do with random numbers. The probe joins two points only when no third point sits in the region between them, which is what produces evenly spread connectivity with no long connection cutting across a cluster of nearer points and no fan of near-parallel connections leaving one point. Beta sets how large that region is, sweeping from Gabriel at 1 to the Relative Neighborhood Graph at 2, and the node's subtitle reads back which of the two you landed on.
UPCGExProbeRNGProviderSettings.situation: A scatter that has to become an evenly connected mesh with no redundant connections, without tuning a connection count by hand.

mechanism.text: A connection between the point and a candidate is asked for unless some third point, nearer to the point than the candidate is, falls inside the region the pair defines. Beta sets that region: at 1 it is the sphere whose diameter is the segment joining the two, at 2 it is the lens where two spheres overlap, each centred on one of the pair and each with the distance between them as its radius. Values in between interpolate. The test is symmetric, so both ends of a pair reach the same verdict and the connection appears once. Every candidate that clears the test is connected, so the probe carries no connection cap of its own and the count it produces comes out of the layout.

Only points the consumer's Connectable Filters accepted are visible here, as blockers just as much as endpoints. Narrowing that role reshapes the result instead of only trimming it: take a point out of the running and the connections it used to block come back.

UPCGExProbeSpannerProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Greedy Spanner
UPCGExProbeSpannerProviderSettings.purpose: Thins a set down to the fewest connections that still leave every pair reachable by a route no longer than Stretch Factor times the straight line between them. It works from whole point pairs and carries no Search Radius: every pair in the set is measured, and Max Edge Candidates decides how many of the shortest ones go on to be tested.
UPCGExProbeSpannerProviderSettings.situation: A set that has to stay navigable end to end while carrying as few connections as the routing quality allows.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. It measures every point pair, keeps the shortest Max Edge Candidates of them, sorts those shortest first and walks the list. A pair is connected when the route already available between its two points is longer than Stretch Factor times the straight-line distance, and skipped when a short enough route already exists. The first pairs all connect because nothing is reachable yet, and every connection kept makes the ones after it harder to justify. Route length is measured only through the connections this probe has placed, so other probes on the pin change nothing about what it decides.

off_label.claim: Push Stretch Factor to its maximum and the pass collapses into a minimum spanning structure: once the shortest pairs have joined the separate pieces, close to nothing else clears the test.
off_label.grounded_in: GetGraphDistance returns the numeric maximum for a pair with no route between them, so every pair spanning two disconnected pieces is accepted while a high StretchFactor rejects the rest

UPCGExProbeTensorProviderSettings.name: Probe : Tensor
UPCGExProbeTensorProviderSettings.purpose: Probe : Direction with the axis sampled from a field instead of set on the node. Every point samples the tensors wired to its Tensors pin at its own location and probes along whatever the field says there, so the connectivity curves as the field does. One connection per point at most, and a point where the field cannot be sampled asks for nothing.
UPCGExProbeTensorProviderSettings.situation: Connectivity that has to follow a field: flow lines along a spline, a swirl around a pole, an axis that changes across the set.

mechanism.text: The field is sampled once per point and normalized, so only the axis it points along matters here. Among the candidates inside the search radius that clear the angle test, Favor picks the single one that gets the connection. Every tensor on the pin contributes to one flattened sample before the probe sees it, so wiring three tensors gives one axis per point and not three.

UPCGExProbeThetaProviderSettings.name: G-Probe : Theta Graph
UPCGExProbeThetaProviderSettings.purpose: Fans a ring of cones around each point and keeps one connection per cone, which caps how many connections a point starts and spreads them evenly around it. The cones ring the plane across Cone Axis, so the result comes out flat whatever the points do in the third dimension. Use Yao Variant changes what counts as the best candidate inside a cone.
UPCGExProbeThetaProviderSettings.situation: A scatter that has to come out evenly connected in every direction around each point, with a hard ceiling on how many connections any one point starts.

mechanism.text: Asked once for the whole dataset. Cone Axis is turned into a plane and Num Cones bisectors are spaced evenly around it. Each point allowed to start a connection looks at the accepting points inside its Search Radius, sorts each one into the cone its direction falls in, and keeps the single best candidate per cone. Every point therefore starts at most Num Cones connections and can receive more from others. Use Yao Variant decides the ranking inside a cone: off, the winner is the candidate whose distance measured along the cone bisector is shortest; on, it is the plain nearest.

off_label.claim: Push Num Cones toward its maximum and the tolerance for sitting off the Cone Axis plane falls under six degrees, which turns the probe into a test for which points lie close to level with each other across that axis.
off_label.grounded_in: the cone test is a dot product against in-plane bisectors at cos(PI / NumCones), so the elevation a candidate may carry is 180 degrees divided by the cone count
