UPCGExPropertyBlueprintLibrary.name: Property Blueprint Library
UPCGExPropertyBlueprintLibrary.purpose: Backs the Blueprint nodes that read and write one property by name on a PCGEx Property Collection component. Get Property and Set Property are the user-facing surface; every function here is marked internal and stays out of the right-click menu, so a Blueprint author never places one directly. The library exists because the value pin has no fixed type: one wildcard slot adopts whatever the author wires and converts against the stored property, with separate typed functions for hard object and class pins, which the wildcard path cannot carry safely.
UPCGExPropertyBlueprintLibrary.situation: A Blueprint needs the value of a named property off an actor's property collection, or needs to write one before something else reads that actor.

mechanism.text: A read takes a component and a property name, finds that property on the component, and converts the stored value into whatever type the value pin resolved to, which is what lets one node serve every property type. A write goes the other way and picks its target the same way: a locally declared property is written in place, while a property that arrived from an imported schema is written into the component's own override for it, and the write switches that override on. The object and class functions read the property as a soft asset path, resolve it, load it when it is not already in memory, and hand back nothing when what resolved fails the expected class. Every function reports its outcome on a success output rather than failing the graph.

off_label.claim: Called from inside the component's prepare event, a write becomes a way to compute a value from the world at read time: whatever is capturing the actor sees the written value, and the component's own locally declared properties are put back afterwards.
off_label.grounded_in: ExtractSchemaFromActor snapshots each local schema's Property, fires PreparePropertyValues, builds the resolved schema, then restores the snapshot.

hints.text: The lookup reads the component in front of it and nothing above it. A property that came from an imported schema and was authored on a parent Blueprint class, without being toggled on this instance, reads here as the schema asset's default, while a capture of the same actor walks the Blueprint class chain and answers with the parent's value.

Writing an imported property leaves it toggled on, which is the same state a hand-authored override has. A value written once from a construction script therefore counts as instance authoring from then on, and survives Blueprint recompiles even after the script that wrote it changes.

UPCGExPropertyCollectionComponent.name: PCGEx Property Collection
UPCGExPropertyCollectionComponent.purpose: Puts a property collection on an actor. The component declares the same named, typed properties a collection declares, locally or by importing Property Schema assets, so an actor can carry data that something else reads later: rebuilding an Actor Collection merges each source actor's properties into the entry built from it, level and data asset export carries them into the exported entries, and Get Properties Data reads them off actors it resolves during a graph run. Blueprint reads and writes the same values by name through the Get Property and Set Property nodes. It is an ordinary actor component with no editor gating, so a spawned actor carries it as readily as a placed one.
UPCGExPropertyCollectionComponent.situation: A placed or spawned actor should carry typed data that the collection built from it, or a graph that resolves it, can read back.

mechanism.text: The component holds one property collection, locally declared properties plus imported Property Schema assets, and does nothing with it on its own: every value it carries is read by something that came looking for the actor. A local declaration is edited on the component in front of you. An imported one resolves through a chain of override layers, first enabled one wins: the instance's own, then each Blueprint class above it in inheritance order, then the imported asset's authored default. Override toggles are instance state and start off on a freshly added component, so an untouched instance surfaces whatever its Blueprint class authored. Readers that capture an actor into a collection or an export fire the prepare event first, which is where a value computed from the world belongs.

off_label.claim: Nothing in the component needs a graph or a collection to be involved at all. Declared properties plus the Blueprint get and set nodes give an actor an inspector-authored, typed, name-addressed value bag, shared through a schema asset across a whole class of actors, in place of a Blueprint variable per field.
off_label.grounded_in: the Blueprint get and set functions read and write the component's own collection directly, and the class is a plain actor component with tick disabled and no PCG-side registration.

Properties.tooltip: Property collection with schema definitions and default values. These compile into runtime property data during cage/pattern builds.

fields.name: Schemas
fields.tooltip: Schema array (locals -- always take precedence over imported entries with matching names)

fields.name: ImportedSchemas
fields.tooltip: Imported schema assets, resolved in array order after locals. Hard refs -- assets stay loaded as long as the owning collection exists. Recursion through imported assets' own ImportedSchemas is supported with cycle detection.

fields.name: ImportOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-entry value overrides for imported entries. EditAnywhere is required so the detail panel's GetChildHandle can reach this property's children -- the registered FPCGExPropertySchemaCollectionCustomization takes over rendering entirely (CustomizeChildren controls every visible row), so this never appears as a top-level array editor in the inspector. The array is kept parallel with the imports-only schema via ReconcileImportOverrides (which delegates to FPCGExPropertyOverrides::SyncToSchema). UE per-instance UPROPERTY delta serialization handles three-layer composition: asset default -> template (collection on CDO) -> instance (collection on actor instance). Each layer overrides the previous via bEnabled toggles on individual entries. Locals do not appear here -- they are edited in-place on Schemas.

Properties.semantics: On a Blueprint's component template this is the authored layer instances of that Blueprint fall back to. On a placed instance each imported row carries its own toggle, and the toggle is instance-owned: turning it on pins that value on this actor, turning it back off hands the property to the class chain again. Editing the template's schema re-syncs every loaded instance to the new shape, so an instance never drifts out of step with the Blueprint it came from.
Properties.trap: A value written from a construction script counts as instance authoring once it differs from the class default, and it then survives Blueprint recompiles, outliving edits to the script that wrote it. Resetting the field back to its class value is what hands control to the script again.

hints.text: On Prepare Property Values fires on the capture path only, when an actor is being read into a collection or an export, and it serves both hook styles: a Blueprint subclass overriding the event, or an instance binding to it. A graph-side read through Get Properties Data resolves the component as it stands and never fires it.

The Blueprint Get Property node reads this component alone. A property that came from an imported schema, was given a value on a parent Blueprint class, and has not been toggled on this instance, answers there with the schema asset's default while a capture of the same actor answers with the parent's value.

UPCGExPropertySchemaAsset.name: Property Schema
UPCGExPropertySchemaAsset.purpose: Declares a set of named, typed properties once so several collections, components and nodes can carry the same fields without redeclaring them. Every consumer holding a property collection has an Imported Schemas list, and listing this asset there merges its declarations into that consumer's own, deduped by name. Schema assets import each other the same way, so a project-wide base library can sit under narrower ones. Two nodes take schema assets directly instead of importing them: Promote Attributes reads one as a list of attribute names, and Get Properties Data uses one as a membership test on the components it resolves.
UPCGExPropertySchemaAsset.situation: Several collections or components need the same property fields, and the declaration should live in one place instead of being copied into each of them.

mechanism.text: A schema asset is a list of named, typed property declarations with default values, plus its own list of imported schema assets, so libraries stack. Nothing reads it on its own: a collection, a component or a node lists it under Imported Schemas, and resolution walks that consumer's local declarations first, then each imported asset in array order, descending into an asset's own imports before moving to the next entry of the list. Names dedupe as the walk goes and the first occurrence wins, so a local declaration beats an imported one and an earlier import beats a later one. An asset reached a second time, whether by a cycle or by being listed twice, is skipped and logged. What the asset supplies is the shape and the default; the value an entry ends up with is resolved on the consumer.

off_label.claim: A schema asset that declares nothing still works as a marker. Get Properties Data keeps only rows whose resolved component imports the assets listed under Required Schemas, so an empty asset imported by a set of components becomes a membership test with no properties attached to it.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExGetPropertiesDataElement resolves RequiredSchemas into a set and walks each component's import tree for asset identity; nothing in that path reads what the asset declares.

off_label.claim: Promote Attributes takes schema assets for their names alone, appending every property name they declare to its selector list, so a schema kept as a naming convention can drive attribute promotion in graphs that never import it.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExPromoteAttributes resolves each entry of Included Schemas and routes one attribute mapping per resolved property name.

Notes.semantics: Editor-only free text, stripped from cooked builds and read by nothing. It is displayed above the schemas, which makes it the place to record what this library is for and who is expected to import it.

Collection.tooltip: Schemas (and further imports) carried by this asset.

fields.name: Schemas
fields.tooltip: Schema array (locals -- always take precedence over imported entries with matching names)

fields.name: ImportedSchemas
fields.tooltip: Imported schema assets, resolved in array order after locals. Hard refs -- assets stay loaded as long as the owning collection exists. Recursion through imported assets' own ImportedSchemas is supported with cycle detection.

fields.name: ImportOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-entry value overrides for imported entries. EditAnywhere is required so the detail panel's GetChildHandle can reach this property's children -- the registered FPCGExPropertySchemaCollectionCustomization takes over rendering entirely (CustomizeChildren controls every visible row), so this never appears as a top-level array editor in the inspector. The array is kept parallel with the imports-only schema via ReconcileImportOverrides (which delegates to FPCGExPropertyOverrides::SyncToSchema). UE per-instance UPROPERTY delta serialization handles three-layer composition: asset default -> template (collection on CDO) -> instance (collection on actor instance). Each layer overrides the previous via bEnabled toggles on individual entries. Locals do not appear here -- they are edited in-place on Schemas.

Collection.semantics: Three surfaces in one: the local declarations, the Imported Schemas list, and a section per imported asset. Imported declarations are never edited in place here; each gets a row with its own enable toggle, so this asset can ship a different default for an imported property without touching the asset it came from. Renaming a local declaration carries every consumer's authored override with it, and changing a declaration's type keeps those overrides enabled while resetting their value to the new default.
Collection.trap: Listing the same asset twice in one import tree does nothing the second time. The second reach is skipped exactly as a cycle is, so a duplicate import is never a way to re-order or re-apply its declarations.

hints.text: An edit here fans out. Every loaded collection that imports this asset, directly or through another schema asset, re-syncs its entry and category override rows against the new shape and re-stages its entries on the spot.

Deleting a declaration from this asset deletes the matching override slot from every entry and every category row of every collection that imports it, as soon as the change reaches them. Adding the declaration back mints a fresh slot, disabled and at the default, so the authored values do not come back with it.

An import chain that loops back to this asset is skipped where it closes, and the declarations behind the skipped hop never reach the consumer. Running data validation on the asset fails it, with a message naming the cycle. Only cycles that route back to this asset are reported here; the others are reported by their own participants.

UPCGExRadiusFittingRelax.name: Radius Fitting
UPCGExRadiusFittingRelax.purpose: The fitting rule whose collision shape is a single number. `Radius` reads one value per Vtx, from an attribute or one constant for the whole cluster, and any two Vtx closer together than the sum of their two radii are pushed apart along the line between them. A sphere has no orientation to get wrong and one number to tune, which is enough wherever the footprints being spaced are roughly as wide as they are long. The springs holding edge lengths, the target lengths and the step size all reach it from **Abstract Fitting**.
UPCGExRadiusFittingRelax.situation: Spacing Vtx whose footprint one number describes well enough, or whose size varies per Vtx and already lives in an attribute.

mechanism.text: This rule contributes the middle turn of the fitting cycle, the separation. Every pair of Vtx is tested, and where the distance between two of them falls short of the sum of their radii, a push is added along the line between them. Its strength is that shortfall divided by the square of the distance, so the same depth of overlap produces a far stronger push between two Vtx sitting close together than between two large ones that barely touch. `Repulsion Constant` scales what comes out, which makes a value tuned on one cluster mean something different on a cluster of another size.

off_label.claim: Set Edge Fitting to Ignore and leave Radius at a constant, and the rule stops caring about connectivity altogether: nothing holds edge lengths, and the cluster keeps opening for as long as any two Vtx are closer than twice the radius.
off_label.grounded_in: Ignore returns from the fitting base's edge turn before any spring is added, leaving this rule's overlap test as the only thing writing into the accumulator

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

RadiusValue.semantics: One number per Vtx, in world units, standing in for that Vtx's whole footprint. A pair is only looked at once the distance between the two drops below the sum of the two radii, so raising the value on one Vtx opens its spacing against every other Vtx by that amount. The shipped setting reads `$Extents.Length` per point, the length of the point's extents vector, which measures from the centre of its bounds out to a corner: that is the sphere containing the box rather than one fitting inside it, so anything that is not round gets generous spacing by default.
RadiusValue.trap: Vtx sitting at identical positions are skipped, so a pair that arrives stacked stays stacked however many iterations run. There is no direction to push along and the rule does not invent one.

hints.text: The push is divided by the square of the distance between the two Vtx, so it grows without limit as a pair closes in. A crowded cluster can throw itself apart in a single iteration at a Repulsion Constant that behaved on a looser one.

UPCGExRadiusSmoothing.name: Radius
UPCGExRadiusSmoothing.purpose: Averages every other point of the same path that falls inside a sphere around each point. `Smoothing` on **Path : Smooth** is that sphere's radius, in world units, and a contributor's weight falls off with the square of its distance, reaching zero at the rim. Order plays no part, so a stretch of path that loops back near another stretch blends into it. It has no settings of its own.
UPCGExRadiusSmoothing.situation: A path that folds back on itself or crowds against its own earlier run, where points close in space should agree with each other whatever their place in the order.

mechanism.text: Gathers every point of the same dataset whose distance to the target is shorter than `Smoothing`, and weights each one by one minus the square of that distance over the square of the radius. The target is excluded from its own set, so the point is replaced by what surrounds it rather than blended with what it was, which is the sharpest difference from **Moving Average**. A point that finds nothing inside the radius is left exactly as it arrived, and so is every point once `Influence` reaches 0. Nothing outside the dataset is ever a source: a second path wired into the same node is smoothed on its own and never contributes.

off_label.claim: Run it on a path that has been folded so two runs sit within the radius of each other and it welds their shapes together without merging any points, which is a way to make a seam agree with itself before a downstream node has to.
off_label.grounded_in: The octree query is over positions with no reference to index, so contributors on the far stretch are admitted on exactly the same terms as immediate neighbours

hints.text: `Smoothing` ships at 5 world units, well under the spacing of most paths, so the first run after switching to this rule usually catches nothing and hands the path back unchanged. Set the radius against the actual spacing between points before judging the result.

UPCGExRandomFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Random
UPCGExRandomFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Gives every element its own coin toss. Each element rolls a number from its own Seed value and passes when that roll reaches the threshold, so what the node guarantees is a probability per element and never a count: about half the set survives at the default threshold of 0.5, and the actual figure drifts with the data. Because the roll is derived from the element and nothing else, one element's verdict never depends on what else is in the dataset, which is what to reach for when points are being added and removed upstream and the ones already chosen should stay chosen. Reach for Filter : Random (Ratio) instead when the number that survives has to be exact. It is also accepted by the consumers that judge whole datasets, as long as the threshold is a constant and no per-element weight is in play.
UPCGExRandomFilterProviderSettings.situation: A share of the elements should be kept at random, and which ones may not shift when the set around them changes.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element. The element's own Seed value is combined with Random Seed to produce a roll between 0 and 1, that roll is passed through the Weight Curve, and the element passes when the result reaches the threshold. Nothing else feeds the roll, so the same Seed and the same Random Seed always give the same answer, on any machine and on any run, and two elements carrying the same Seed value always agree. The graph's own seeds are not folded in, so re-seeding the PCG component leaves every verdict where it was. Asked about a whole dataset instead of an element, the node takes a single roll from the first element's Seed and hands that one answer to the entire dataset.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: Elements that share a Seed value share a verdict. Points duplicated from one source, or written with a constant Seed upstream, are decided together rather than independently, and the symptom is a pattern that looks blocky instead of scattered.

UPCGExRandomRatioFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Random (Ratio)
UPCGExRandomRatioFilterProviderSettings.purpose: The count is settled before any element is looked at, as a share of the set or as a flat figure, and then that many are drawn. Filter : Random cannot promise that: it rolls each element on its own and lands near the requested share without ever committing to it. The price of the promise is that the draw belongs to the whole set, so adding or removing a single element redraws the entire selection. It also serves the consumers that judge whole datasets, where the share applies to the datasets on the pin instead of to the elements inside them.
UPCGExRandomRatioFilterProviderSettings.situation: Exactly a tenth of a set has to be marked, and which tenth does not matter as long as the count holds.

mechanism.text: The count comes first: a share of the element count, rounded, or a flat figure, in either case trimmed to the size of the set and then held inside the optional clamps. Every index is then shuffled and the first however-many are the winners, so which elements are chosen depends on the element count and on their order in the data, not on anything they carry. The draw folds Base Seed together with the seed of the node running the filter and with the PCG component's own seed, so a single copy of this node feeding two consumers picks a different subset for each of them, and re-seeding either one redraws. Used on a whole dataset instead of an element, the same shuffle runs over the datasets on the pin and the share is a share of their number.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, and it is also accepted by the consumers that evaluate whole datasets.

hints.text: The selection is not stable against edits upstream. The shuffle covers every index and the element count feeds into it, so gaining or losing one element redraws the whole set and elements that were passing before can stop. Where the same elements need to keep the same verdict as the set around them changes, Filter : Random rolls each one on its own instead.

UPCGExRaycastFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Raycast
UPCGExRaycastFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Asks whether there is geometry in a given direction from each element, and how far away it sits. The answer comes from tracing into the level's collision rather than from anything arriving on a pin, so this filter reads the world the component is generating into. Two questions are on offer: whether the trace hit anything at all, and whether the hit sits nearer or further than a threshold. The trace can be a line, a sphere sweep or a box sweep, and Surface Source decides which surfaces are allowed to answer it: every one the trace meets, or only those belonging to a list of actors or a set of primitive components handed to it on a pin.
UPCGExRaycastFilterProviderSettings.situation: Elements should survive only where something solid sits in a given direction, or only where the gap before it is short enough.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this once per element. An origin and a direction are read per element, the trace runs from there out to Max Distance, and the test mode decides what a result means: Any Hit passes on a hit and fails on a miss, while Compare Distance measures from the ray origin to the impact point and compares that against a threshold. A miss under Compare Distance leaves no distance to compare, so No Hit Fallback answers instead, and it is the one verdict Invert leaves alone. The collision settings decide what the trace can touch at all, and Surface Source decides which of those touches counts. The verdict is always one per element: Uber Branch and Break skip this filter with a warning that it cannot be used with collections, and Uber Filter (Data) falls back to counting element passes.

off_label.claim: With Origin Mode set to World Position and both the origin and the direction read from attributes, the ray no longer has to start at the element. Each element can then trace a span of its own between two arbitrary places, and the filter answers whether anything blocks it.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExRaycastOriginMode::WorldPosition taking Start wholly from the Origin value, with Direction and Max Distance also read per element in FRaycastFilter::Test

off_label.claim: Compute a direction toward one specific actor, feed it in per element, and Actor Reference with Any Hit becomes a line of sight test: the element passes only when nothing blocking stands between it and that actor.
off_label.grounded_in: DoTraceMulti answering with the first hit in the multi-trace results whose actor is in IncludedActors, those results ending at the first surface that blocks the query

inputs.label: Actor References
inputs.note: Points carrying an attribute with an actor path. The actors they resolve to become the only surfaces a hit is allowed to belong to, and the list is gathered once for the whole node.
inputs.condition: when Surface Source is Actor Reference

inputs.label: Primitives
inputs.note: Primitive data, one component per entry. Every dataset on the pin is pooled into one set, and a hit counts only when the component it landed on is in that set.
inputs.condition: when Surface Source is Primitives

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node produces. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: What the trace can hit is whatever is loaded and collidable in that world at the moment the graph runs, so an actor that is streamed out, or one whose collision is turned off, is not there to be found. Nothing upstream carries that state, and nothing downstream reports it.

An empty Actor References or Primitives pin does not stop the node, and neither does an Actor References set in which nothing resolves: both are missing data, answered by Missing Data Policy, which defaults to Fail. Under Error the node reports the missing input and cancels.

An attribute set carries no positions, so a consumer filtering one hands every row to this filter as a default point at the world origin, with no rotation. Every ray then starts in the same place and points the same way, the whole set takes one answer, and nothing is logged.

UPCGExRecursionTrackerSettings.name: Break
UPCGExRecursionTrackerSettings.purpose: A subgraph that calls itself has no stop condition of its own, and Break supplies one. It maintains a counter carried on an attribute set that travels round the recursion, and reports at every pass whether another one should happen. In Branch it also gates the data: what arrives leaves on Continue or on Stop, and the pin not taken is deactivated, so everything downstream of it is culled instead of running on nothing. Two palette entries preset the Type, Simple for the counter alone and Branch for the counter plus the gate.
UPCGExRecursionTrackerSettings.situation: A recursive subgraph that has to terminate after a bounded number of passes, or as soon as the data it is chewing through runs out.

mechanism.text: A tracker is one attribute set carrying a bool named by Continue Attribute Name, with the counter itself held in two tags on that data, PCGEx/MaxCount and PCGEx/Remainder. Create stamps a fresh tracker at Max Count. Update reads the two tags, adds Counter Update to the remainder, writes the tracker back, and reports Continue while the result is still at least zero. Create or Update chooses between the two by whether the Tracker pin delivered any data at all. Every tracker on the pin is advanced, so a stack of them steps together, and in Branch the gate opens when any one of them can still continue.

off_label.claim: Wire the Remainder pin into any attribute-driven setting and the recursion depth becomes an input to the work each pass does, rather than only a stop condition.
off_label.grounded_in: the bOutputRemainder branch stages an int32 attribute set per updated tracker, carrying the same flattened tags as the tracker itself

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The data to route between Continue and Stop. It is re-pinned, never copied.
inputs.condition: when Type is Branch

inputs.label: Tracker
inputs.note: The attribute sets holding the counter. Empty is a legitimate state in Create and Create or Update; the pin stays required so that a deactivated pin feeding it culls this node along with the rest of the branch.

inputs.label: Tracker Filters
inputs.note: Filters run per tracker collection; trackers that fail are dropped from the pass. This same pin is also what the Test Data check reads.

inputs.label: Test Data
inputs.note: Collections tested by the filters below.
inputs.condition: when Type is Simple, Mode is not Create, and Do Additional Data Testing is on

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Declared as the filters for Test Data, but the element reads Tracker Filters for that test instead, so nothing wired here is consulted.
inputs.condition: when Type is Simple, Mode is not Create, and Do Additional Data Testing is on

outputs.label: Continue
outputs.note: Carries the In data when at least one tracker can still continue. Stop is then deactivated, not merely left empty.
outputs.condition: when Type is Branch

outputs.label: Stop
outputs.note: Carries the In data when no tracker can continue. Continue is then deactivated.
outputs.condition: when Type is Branch

outputs.label: Tracker
outputs.note: The new or advanced tracker(s), tags updated. Nothing is emitted here on an Update pass that found no usable tracker.

outputs.label: Progress
outputs.note: A float attribute set, one per tracker.
outputs.condition: when Output Progress is on and Mode is not Create

outputs.label: Index
outputs.note: An int32 attribute set counting passes taken, one per tracker.
outputs.condition: when Output Index is on and Mode is not Create

outputs.label: Remainder
outputs.note: An int32 attribute set holding passes left, one per tracker.
outputs.condition: when Output Remainder is on and Mode is not Create

pins.dynamic: Only Branch declares dynamic pins: In, Continue and Stop accept any data type and the two outputs mirror whatever the input carried. The Tracker pins are always attribute sets.

Type.tooltip: How is this recursion tracker supposed to be used.
Type.semantics: Simple keeps the counter and nothing else: there is no data input and no Continue or Stop pin, so the verdict has to be read off the tracker's own bool downstream. Branch adds the gate, and is the only mode that deactivates a pin.

Mode.tooltip: How is this recursion tracker supposed to be used.
Mode.semantics: Create belongs outside the recursion and Update inside it. Create or Update decides between them on whether the Tracker pin delivered any data, which is tested before Tracker Filters run: trackers that arrive and are then filtered out leave the node in Update with nothing to advance, which reports Stop rather than creating a fresh tracker.
Mode.trap: An Update pass with no usable tracker emits nothing on the Tracker output, so the recursion loses its counter rather than restarting it.

ContinueAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the bool attribute that will be set on the tracker.
ContinueAttributeName.semantics: Names the bool the tracker carries. In Simple this is the only place the verdict appears, so it is what a downstream Branch on Data or a vanilla branch has to read.

MaxCount.semantics: The value stamped into the PCGEx/MaxCount tag when a tracker is created. Update never reads this field, which is why it is hidden there: the ceiling travels with the tracker.

AddTags.tooltip: Tags to be added to the tracker

RemoveTags.tooltip: Tags to be removed from the tracker(s)

CounterUpdate.tooltip: Value to add to the counter each update. Negative values decrement.
CounterUpdate.semantics: Added to the remainder on every Update pass, so the default of -1 counts one pass down. The remainder is clamped back into zero to Max Count before the addition, so the tracker cannot run away.
CounterUpdate.trap: Because of that clamp, a Counter Update of zero or above can never drive the remainder below zero, and the node reports Continue forever.

bOutputProgress.tooltip: If enabled, will create a pin that outputs the normalized progress value.
bOutputProgress.trap: The value is not a single monotonic ramp. On an Update pass it reports the remaining fraction, one at the start and falling to zero; on the pass that creates a tracker it reports zero, and on the pass where no tracker can be advanced it reports one. Index and Remainder are consistent across all three and are the safer reads.

bOutputIndex.tooltip: If enabled, will create a pin that outputs the current iteration index (Max - Remainder).

bOutputRemainder.tooltip: If enabled, will create a pin that outputs the current remainder.

bForceOutputContinue.tooltip: If enabled, will override the value of the "Continue" attribute to a valid one. Use this is you give the tracker some attribute set that may already have a boolean with the same name and a wrong value.
bForceOutputContinue.semantics: Rewrites the bool on a duplicate of the incoming tracker instead of passing the original through. Worth having when the attribute set feeding the Tracker pin was authored elsewhere and already carries a value under that name.

bDoAdditionalDataTesting.tooltip: If enabled, does additional collection-level filtering on a separate set of datas. If no data passes those filters, the tracker will return a single false value.
bDoAdditionalDataTesting.semantics: Adds a second gate that tests separate collections rather than the counter, intended to stop the recursion when the work runs dry.
bDoAdditionalDataTesting.trap: The result is computed and then never applied: the tracker's bool is still written from the counter alone, and the test cannot stop a recursion the counter would continue. Its only visible effect is that the tracker is emitted as a duplicate rather than in place.

bAddEntryWhenCreatingFromExistingData.display: Add Entry When Creating From Existing Data
bAddEntryWhenCreatingFromExistingData.tooltip: Add metadata entry when creating a tracker from existing attribute set data.
bAddEntryWhenCreatingFromExistingData.semantics: Only reached by Create when the Tracker pin did deliver data, which is the case where the node reuses an existing attribute set as the tracker's body. An attribute set arriving with no rows needs this on, or the bool it carries has no entry to sit on.

RemainderOffsetWhenCreateInsteadOfUpdate.display: Remainder Offset When Create Instead Of Update
RemainderOffsetWhenCreateInsteadOfUpdate.tooltip: An offset applied when creating a tracker in "Create or Update" mode. The default value assume the tracker is created from inside a subgraph and thus that one iteration passed already.
RemainderOffsetWhenCreateInsteadOfUpdate.semantics: Applied to the remainder tag of a tracker created by Create or Update, and to nothing else. The default of -1 charges the creating pass as one iteration, so a subgraph that creates its own tracker gets Max Count passes rather than Max Count plus one.
RemainderOffsetWhenCreateInsteadOfUpdate.trap: The offset lands on the tracker tag only; the Remainder output pin on that same pass still reports the unoffset Max Count.

bGroupBranchPins.semantics: Moves the Stop pin up beside Continue instead of leaving it below the Tracker output. Pin order only; the routing is identical.

hints.text: The branch that is not taken is deactivated, so every node downstream of it is culled for this run. That is the mechanism that ends the recursion, and it also means a node hanging off Stop cannot be used to observe the passes that continued.

Nothing here bounds the recursion except the counter. A Counter Update of zero, or a configuration that keeps re-creating the tracker rather than advancing it, leaves the subgraph calling itself until the editor gives up.

UPCGExReduceDataAttributeSettings.name: Reduce Data
UPCGExReduceDataAttributeSettings.purpose: Collapses one `@Data` attribute, read once per input dataset, into a single value. Where **Attribute Stats** measures the points inside a dataset, this one works a level up: the inputs are datasets, each contributing the one value it carries for that name, and the output is one number, string or hash for the lot. It is how a graph answers a question about a collection of collections, a total, an extreme, a joined label, or a fingerprint that survives reordering.
UPCGExReduceDataAttributeSettings.situation: Twenty datasets each carry a per-dataset value and the graph needs one number standing for all of them.

mechanism.text: Every dataset on the input pin is asked for the named attribute in its `@Data` domain, and a dataset that does not carry it is skipped with a warning rather than counted as zero. Container and extended types are skipped the same way. The surviving values are combined by the chosen method, and the result comes out as an attribute set holding one row, under the target name. The input data does not come out: the only output is that one row. With nothing valid to read at all the node fails rather than emitting an empty set.

off_label.claim: Hash (Sorted) over an id attribute is a fingerprint for a set of datasets that ignores which order they arrived in, so it can be compared against a later run whose pin order changed.
off_label.grounded_in: the UnsignedHash branch sorts the collected value hashes before CityHash64 runs over them

off_label.claim: Join with an empty delimiter concatenates every dataset's value into one string, which is a way to build a compound key out of per-dataset labels.
off_label.grounded_in: the Join branch runs FString::Join over the aggregated values with JoinDelimiter verbatim

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Any data carrying the named attribute in its `@Data` domain. Points, attribute sets and spatial data all count as one value each.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: One attribute set with a single row, holding the reduced value under the target name.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Attribute to read on input

fields.name: Target
fields.tooltip: Attribute to write on output, if different from input

Method.semantics: `Min`, `Max`, `Sum` and `Average` work component-wise on vector types and start from the first valid input rather than from zero, so a Min over positive values is not dragged to zero by the seed. `Average` divides by the number of datasets that carried the attribute, not by the number of datasets wired. `Join` and the two hashes ignore the value type entirely, reading everything as text or as a value hash.

OutputType.semantics: The result's type is taken from the inputs: whichever type the most datasets carried wins, which matters when a name is declared at different types on different inputs. `Join` overrides that with String, and the two hash methods override it with Integer64.
OutputType.trap: The type chosen here is never read. Ticking the toggle only stops the hash methods forcing Integer64, which leaves them writing the most common input type instead of the type named.

hints.text: A dataset missing the attribute is not a zero. It is dropped with a warning and never reaches the reduction, so `Sum` and `Average` count only the datasets that carried something.

UPCGExRefineEdgesSettings.name: Cluster : Refine
UPCGExRefineEdgesSettings.purpose: Removes edges from a cluster by a rule. The node carries no rule of its own: a **Refinement** is picked from a dropdown in its details, and that rule is the only thing here that judges an edge. What the node owns is everything around the verdict, which is the shape the result comes back in and two ways of putting edges back that the rule took out.
UPCGExRefineEdgesSettings.situation: A generator connected far more than it should have, and one rule has to cut it back to the structure the rest of the graph is built around.

mechanism.text: Every edge starts at the value the chosen refinement declares, either all kept or all removed, and the refinement then flips the ones it decides about. Nothing else in the node judges an edge. `Mode` decides what that marking becomes: a rebuilt cluster, two sets of edge points, or an attribute written beside the cluster it arrived as. A Vtx is never judged on its own; it leaves only when it is left with no edge, and only in Clusters mode. Two settings then get to overturn the rule, and both of them put edges back rather than taking more away.
steps: The refinement marks edges, starting from the all-kept or all-removed baseline it declares.
Restore Edges That Connect To Valid Nodes puts back every removed edge whose two Vtx each kept at least one other edge.
Sanitization puts back one edge at every Vtx, or every edge its filters accept.
Mode turns what survived into a rebuilt cluster, into two sets of edge points, or into an attribute.

off_label.claim: Chain several of these in Attribute mode onto one result attribute in Counter mode and every edge ends up carrying how many of the rules kept it, which a later **Refine : Filter** can then threshold.
off_label.grounded_in: Attribute mode duplicates both facades and resets every edge and Vtx to valid after writing in FProcessor::InsertEdges, so the cluster chains through intact; the Counter buffer opens with EBufferInit::Inherit in FPCGExFilterResultDetails::Init.

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx dataset.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges datasets, one per cluster.

inputs.label: Heuristics
inputs.note: The scoring the rule compares edges by. Five rules ask for it, the four Score rules and **Refine : MST (Prim)**, and the node cancels with an error when one of them is picked and the pin is empty. Under every other rule the pin sits under advanced and the node marks it unused.
inputs.condition: when the picked refinement scores edges

inputs.label: Edge Filters
inputs.note: Read by two rules only, **Refine : Filter** and **Refine : Chain Filter**, which is also when the pin leaves the advanced group. It accepts edge filters, point filters, filter groups and collection filters; a **Vtx Filter :** node is refused at the pin.

inputs.label: Sanitize Filters
inputs.note: The edges Sanitization is allowed to restore. Same acceptance as **Edge Filters**. The pin appears on the strength of the Sanitization value alone, so it is still there in Points and Attribute modes where the setting itself is hidden.
inputs.condition: when Sanitization is Filters

inputs.label: Overrides : Refinement
inputs.note: Attribute sets whose attribute names match the picked rule's own property names, one name per property, applied to that rule before it runs. It sets values on the rule already chosen and cannot choose one.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The rebuilt Vtx dataset in Clusters mode, with anything left edgeless gone. In Attribute mode it is the input carried through with the result attribute added.
outputs.condition: Clusters and Attribute modes

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One dataset per connected component of the refined result in Clusters mode, so one cluster in can come out as several. In Attribute mode it is the input carried through with the result attribute added.
outputs.condition: Clusters and Attribute modes

outputs.label: Kept Edges
outputs.note: The edge points the rule kept, one dataset per incoming Edges dataset.
outputs.condition: Points mode

outputs.label: Removed Edges
outputs.note: The edge points the rule removed, in the same one-per-input shape.
outputs.condition: Points mode

Refinement.semantics: The rule is picked here, never wired. The slot ships empty and the node cancels with an error until something fills it, and the node's subtitle carries the picked rule's name, showing three dots while the slot is empty. Only one rule fits: to apply two, chain two of these nodes. The choice also reshapes the node around it, since it is what decides whether the Heuristics pin is required, whether the Edge Filters pin is read, and whether Restore Edges That Connect To Valid Nodes runs at all.

HeuristicScoreMode.tooltip: Scoring mode for combining multiple heuristics
HeuristicScoreMode.semantics: Read only by the five rules that ask for heuristics, the four Score rules and **Refine : MST (Prim)**. It decides how several heuristics arriving on one pin collapse into the single number those rules compare, so with one heuristic wired there is nothing for it to combine. It stays on screen under every other rule, where nothing reads it.

Mode.semantics: **Clusters** rebuilds. Only edges that survived are inserted, an edge whose Vtx did not survive goes with it, the result is re-split by connected component and the Vtx dataset comes out shorter than it went in. **Points** replaces the Vtx and Edges outputs outright with **Kept Edges** and **Removed Edges**, one pair per incoming Edges dataset, holding the original edge points split in two with nothing rebuilt. **Attribute** carries the cluster through unchanged and records the verdict instead, under two separate blocks, one for the Vtx and one for the edges; both attribute names are validated before the node runs, so a name the metadata cannot take cancels the node rather than producing nothing.
Mode.trap: Sanitization, Restore Edges That Connect To Valid Nodes and Cluster Output Settings are shown in Clusters mode only, and just the last of the three stops running when the mode changes. A Sanitization value left behind keeps restoring edges in Points and Attribute modes with no control on screen to say so, and set to Filters it still adds a required Sanitize Filters pin.

ResultOutputVtx.semantics: What gets recorded for a Vtx is whether it still has at least one surviving edge, which is the only thing this node ever concludes about a Vtx. A Vtx the rule itself struck out records as a failure. The block is opened once against the shared Vtx dataset, so every cluster paired with it writes into the same attribute, and what several writes to one name do is the result block's own rule.

ResultOutputEdges.semantics: The edge side records each edge's own surviving state, one write per edge, opened once per Edges dataset. It is a separate block from the Vtx side and starts on the same default attribute name, so leaving both untouched puts the two verdicts on one attribute.

bAllowZeroPointOutputs.semantics: Points mode emits one Kept Edges dataset and one Removed Edges dataset per incoming Edges dataset, and drops the empty ones. A cluster whose edges all survived therefore contributes nothing to Removed Edges, and the two pins stop lining up index for index with each other and with the input. Turn this on and the empty datasets are kept, so position N on one pin is always the same cluster as position N on the other.

Sanitization.semantics: Sanitization runs last and only ever puts edges back. **Shortest** and **Longest** walk every Vtx and restore its shortest or longest edge along with both of that edge's Vtx: the option tooltips describe this as happening where a Vtx was left with nothing, and the pass makes no such check, so every Vtx in the cluster ends up holding at least that one edge. **Filters** instead restores every edge its Sanitize Filters accept, which is the only one of the three that can be aimed at part of a cluster.
Sanitization.trap: Anything other than None overrules the refinement wherever the two disagree, so an edge the rule removed on purpose comes back. Setting it turns a rule that thins a cluster into one that guarantees a minimum degree everywhere.

bRestoreEdgesThatConnectToValidNodes.display: Restore Edges That Connect To Valid Nodes
bRestoreEdgesThatConnectToValidNodes.semantics: A restore pass with a rule of its own, running before Sanitization. Any Vtx left with no surviving edge is written off, and then every removed edge whose two Vtx both survived comes back. It restores nothing along the fringe of the thinning and everything inside it.
bRestoreEdgesThatConnectToValidNodes.trap: It runs only under the rules that judge one edge at a time: **Refine : Filter**, **Refine : Gabriel** with Invert off, **Refine : Line Trace**, **Refine : Overlap** and **Refine : β Skeleton**. Under any rule that decides per Vtx or over the whole cluster the pass is never reached and the toggle changes nothing.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: Clusters mode only, and it is the last thing that can drop a result. Remove Small Clusters and Remove Big Clusters are measured per connected component after the re-split, so a rule that shattered one cluster into fragments has those fragments discarded here rather than by the rule.

hints.text: Losing a Vtx here is always a side effect. Nothing in this node judges a Vtx, and one leaves only when the last edge at it does. **Cluster : Filter Vtx** is the node that removes Vtx by a condition of their own.

**Kept Edges** and **Removed Edges** inherit the source Edges dataset's tags, its cluster role and pair tags among them, and they keep the endpoint attribute the edge points arrived with. Dropped back onto an Edges pin beside the original Vtx they still read as that cluster, now short of most of its edges, and a cluster whose Edge points were deleted does not rebuild.

UPCGExRefreshSeedSettings.name: Refresh Seed
UPCGExRefreshSeedSettings.purpose: Rewrites each point's `Seed` from where the point is, so randomness downstream becomes a property of the location rather than of the order points happen to arrive in. That is what makes a scatter stable under editing: move one point and only that point's randomness changes, while adding, removing or reordering points changes nothing at all. Two points at the same location get the same seed, which is the trade.
UPCGExRefreshSeedSettings.situation: Regenerating the graph reshuffles variation that should have stayed put, because the seeds came from index order.

mechanism.text: Points in, the same points in the same order out, with `Seed` replaced and nothing else touched. The new value is derived from the point's world location and from `Base`, and from nothing else: not the point's old seed, not its index, not the dataset it belongs to. Coordinates are truncated to whole units before hashing, so movement below one unit leaves the seed exactly as it was. The **Point Filters** pin decides which points are rewritten; the rest keep the seed they arrived with.

off_label.claim: Run it after any node that rebuilds points from scratch, cluster conversions and fuses included, and the variation those points had before the round trip comes back, because it was never stored anywhere but the position.
off_label.grounded_in: the seed is computed from the output point transform alone in FProcessor::ProcessPoints, with no reference to the input seed

off_label.claim: Wired with a filter it becomes a partial re-roll: only the points that pass are given position-derived seeds, so a subset can be made position-stable while the rest keep whatever they had.
off_label.grounded_in: the PointFilterCache guard in the per-point loop skips writing entirely for points that fail

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to rewrite.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Point filters deciding which points are rewritten. A point that fails keeps its seed.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, with Seed rewritten on the ones that passed.

Base.semantics: Not an offset added to the result. The value is expanded into a position with the same number on all three axes, hashed like any other position, and combined with the point's own hash, so changing it by one reshuffles every seed rather than shifting them by one. Two different values give two unrelated distributions over the same points.

hints.text: Coincident points get identical seeds, and so do points closer together than one unit on every axis, because each coordinate is truncated to a whole number before it is hashed. Anything downstream that randomises per point will then make the same choice for all of them.

UPCGExRelaxClusterOperation.name: Relax Operation
UPCGExRelaxClusterOperation.purpose: The half every relaxation shares, whichever rule is picked from the Relaxing dropdown on Cluster : Relax. It settles how a rule gets its turn at the cluster, how contributions arriving from several places reach one Vtx, and it carries the one setting all six rules have in common, `Floating Point Precision`. **Cluster : Relax** owns how many iterations run, which Vtx are allowed to move at all, how strongly the result is blended in and what gets written out; a rule owns what one iteration does to positions, and every other setting sitting under the dropdown belongs to it. Three of the six, **Box Fitting**, **Box Fitting v2** and **Radius Fitting**, stack a second shared layer on top of this one and it is documented separately on **Abstract Fitting**; **Force Directed**, **Laplacian (Poisson)** and **Verlet (Gravity)** inherit none of that layer and take everything they share straight from here.
UPCGExRelaxClusterOperation.situation: Reading one of the relaxations and needing to know which parts of its behaviour are its own and which reach it from here.

mechanism.text: A rule gets the whole cluster and takes between one and three turns at it, and one iteration on **Cluster : Relax** is one complete cycle of those turns, so a one-turn rule and a three-turn rule are applied the same number of times. Each turn walks either every Vtx or every edge, and the rule decides which. One turn is enough when a Vtx's new position follows from what that Vtx can read for itself. When contributions arrive from elsewhere, an edge pushing on both of its endpoints being the usual case, the rule spends one turn gathering them and a later turn applying them, and in between they sit in an accumulator that counts whole steps of one fixed size. Counting in whole steps is what lets several threads add to the same Vtx at once and still land on the same total whatever order they arrive in, and `Floating Point Precision` sets how big one step is.

off_label.claim: Dropping `Floating Point Precision` toward 1 turns the rounding floor into a settle threshold: contributions smaller than half a step round away as they go in, so Vtx whose forces have already fallen off stop moving while strongly pushed ones carry on.
off_label.grounded_in: AddDelta rounds each contribution with RoundToInt64(Delta * Precision) before the atomic add, so anything under half a step lands as zero

Precision.tooltip: Under the hood updates are operated on a FInt64Vector3. The regular FVector value is multiplied by this factor, and later divided by it. Default value of 100 means .00 precision.
Precision.semantics: The accumulator counts whole steps of one unit divided by this factor, and each contribution is rounded to a whole number of steps on its way in rather than the running total being rounded at the end. That makes it a floor per contribution: a Vtx collecting twenty pushes that each fall under half a step collects nothing at all, however large their sum would have been. At the default of 100 the floor is half a hundredth of a unit, well under anything a relaxation is trying to resolve, so raising it is for the case where a rule is tuned gently enough that its own pushes disappear and the cluster refuses to move. Each axis counts in a 64-bit integer, so the range given up in exchange is never what bites. The setting sits under the panel's advanced section.
Precision.trap: It only reaches rules that accumulate. **Laplacian (Poisson)** and **Force Directed** work out each Vtx's new position in a single turn and write it straight out, so the setting appears in their panel and changes nothing. It is live on **Verlet (Gravity)**, **Box Fitting**, **Box Fitting v2** and **Radius Fitting**.

UPCGExRelaxClustersSettings.name: Cluster : Relax
UPCGExRelaxClustersSettings.purpose: Moves Vtx while every connection stays exactly as it was. The rule doing the moving is a sub-node picked from the `Relaxing` dropdown, so one node covers Laplacian smoothing, force-directed layout, Verlet physics under gravity and the fitting rules that push overlapping Vtx apart. Positions are the only thing this node writes: rotation, scale, every attribute already on the Vtx and the whole Edges dataset come through untouched. It can also record how far each Vtx travelled, as a vector, a direction or a distance.
UPCGExRelaxClustersSettings.situation: A generated cluster whose Vtx sit exactly where the source points were, and the layout needs to open up without a single edge being added, removed or re-routed.

mechanism.text: One execution takes a cluster and returns the same cluster with new Vtx positions: same point count, same order, same Edges dataset, same connections. `Iterations` is how many times the chosen rule is applied, each application working on the result of the last and producing a position for every Vtx. Whichever rule is selected, the outcome does not depend on the order the Vtx are visited or on how the work is split across threads. What one application costs, and whether it walks Vtx or edges, is the rule's business; the node itself owns the count, the influence blend and the optional outputs.

off_label.claim: Amplitude is the distance a Vtx ended up from where it started, so writing it and sorting or filtering on it downstream locates the parts of the cluster the rule had to work hardest on, which is usually where the crowding was.
off_label.grounded_in: ProcessNodes computes the written displacement against Cluster->GetPos, which reads the input Vtx transforms rather than the relaxed ones

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The cluster's Vtx. This is the half that gets moved.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The cluster's Edges. Read for connectivity and for edge lengths, and passed through without modification.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: Vtx that fail are held at their input position for the whole run. They still take part as neighbours, so a filter set here is how you nail part of a cluster down and relax only the rest around it.

inputs.label: Overrides : Relaxing
inputs.note: Attribute set whose entries overwrite the selected rule's own properties by name. Sits under the node's advanced pins.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, moved, plus whichever displacement attributes were enabled.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The Edges dataset, unchanged.

Iterations.tooltip: Number of relaxation iterations to perform. More iterations = smoother result.
Iterations.semantics: Each iteration is one full application of the chosen rule across the whole cluster, so this multiplies whatever one application of that rule costs, and it means the same thing for every rule whether that rule needs one walk of the cluster or three. It is not a convergence control: none of the rules settle at a fixed point, so a large value keeps pushing rather than sharpening a result that has already arrived.
Iterations.trap: Laplacian (Poisson) moves every Vtx to the average of its neighbours, which draws the whole cluster a little further toward its own centre on every iteration. Past a certain count it contracts the cluster instead of smoothing it.

InfluenceDetails.semantics: With Progressive Influence left on, each iteration is blended toward the position the Vtx held before it, and that blended position is what the next one reads, so a value below 1 damps the movement and compounds across the run. Turned off, every iteration runs at full strength and one blend at the end places the Vtx somewhere on the straight line between where it started and where the rule put it. Influence accepts negative values down to -1, which push the Vtx away from the relaxed position instead of toward it.

Relaxing.semantics: The node ships with nothing selected and reports that no operation is selected until a rule is picked. Everything shown under the dropdown belongs to that rule, so the settings change wholesale when the selection changes, and the node's own surface is the iteration count, the influence blend and the outputs. The node subtitle in the graph names whichever rule is currently selected.

DirectionAndSizeAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write direction and size to.
DirectionAndSizeAttributeName.semantics: Measured against the position the Vtx had on input, so it carries the displacement of the whole run, not of the last iteration. A Vtx held in place by the Vtx Filters writes a zero vector.

DirectionAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write direction to.
DirectionAttributeName.semantics: Normalised from that same displacement. A Vtx that did not move writes a zero vector, so the attribute can be tested for movement on its own.

AmplitudeAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write amplitude to.
AmplitudeAttributeName.semantics: The straight-line distance between where the Vtx started and where it ended. A Vtx that wandered and came back reads low, because this measures displacement and not the total distance travelled to get there.

UPCGExResamplePathSettings.name: Path : Resample
UPCGExResamplePathSettings.purpose: Spaces a path's points evenly along its own length. `Mode` decides whether the count is yours to set or the path's to keep: `Sweep` throws the original points away and walks the run laying down new ones at a fixed interval, so the count comes out of the arithmetic; `Redistribute` keeps every point and slides it to where an even spacing would have put it. Everything is measured along the run rather than straight across, so a path with dense corners and long straights comes out uniform.
UPCGExResamplePathSettings.situation: A path whose spacing came from how it was built rather than from what it has to drive, a spline conversion or a pathfinding result being the usual sources.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns them with their points evenly spread along the run. Under `Redistribute` the point count is untouched and only positions move, so every attribute stays with the point that carried it. Under `Sweep` the output is a fresh set of points whose count comes from the resolution, and each one takes its values by blending the two original points its position fell between, which means an original point's values only survive where a sample happens to land on it. Closed paths are spaced so the wrap from the last point back to the first is the same length as every other gap.

off_label.claim: Redistribute with the blending untouched is a way to normalise spacing without disturbing anything a previous node wrote: the count, the attributes and the order all survive, and only the positions move, so it can be dropped between two nodes that both care about attributes.
off_label.grounded_in: Redistribute initialises the output as a duplicate and writes only the transform and, optionally, the seed

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to resample.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The resampled paths. A path whose resolution works out to fewer than two samples produces nothing at all.

Mode.tooltip: How the path is resampled. Sweep walks along the path at fixed intervals, Redistribute keeps point count.

ResolutionMode.semantics: How the resolution number is read under `Sweep`. `Distance` treats it as a spacing and works out the count from the path's length, so longer paths get more points. `Count` treats it as the number of points outright, so every path comes out with the same count whatever its length.

bRedistributeEvenly.tooltip: Adjust sample spacing so all samples are evenly distributed across the path length.
bRedistributeEvenly.semantics: Ships on. It keeps the count the spacing worked out and then divides the path's length by that count exactly, so the last sample lands on the path's final point and every gap is equal. Turning it off marches the typed spacing from the start and stops wherever it runs out, leaving the end of the path unsampled.

bPreserveLastPoint.semantics: Drags the final sample onto the path's last point, which is the only way to reach that point while `Redistribute Evenly` is off.

SampleLength.tooltip: Resolution -- only support @Data attribute and will try to read from the data domain only.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SampleLength.semantics: One value per dataset; it cannot vary along a path. Under `Distance` it is a spacing in world units and under `Count` it is a point count, which is why the label stays generic.

Truncate.tooltip: How to handle fractional sample counts (round, floor, or ceiling).
Truncate.semantics: Rounds the sample count that the spacing worked out, and ships on `Round` rather than on a floor, so a path that is a whisker over a multiple of the spacing gains a sample rather than losing one.

BlendingSettings.tooltip: Blending settings used to smooth attributes.
BlendingSettings.semantics: The blend weight is where the sample landed relative to the two source points, so `Lerp`, the shipped mode, gives a straight interpolation while `Copy (Target)` takes the later point's value wholesale.

bEnsureUniqueSeeds.tooltip: Ensure each resampled point gets a unique random seed.
bEnsureUniqueSeeds.semantics: Ships on, and rewrites each output point's seed from where it landed. Turning it off under `Sweep` leaves whichever seed the blend produced, which under a copying blend mode means whole runs of points sharing one seed.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: Changes nothing observable here. A path of fewer than two points is refused before any work and never forwarded, and both modes produce at least two points or nothing at all, so there is never anything for the output side of the toggle to catch.

hints.text: A `Sweep` whose resolution works out to fewer than two samples produces no output for that path at all, and nothing is logged. A spacing longer than the path is the usual cause.

UPCGExReversePointOrderSettings.name: Reverse Order
UPCGExReversePointOrderSettings.purpose: Flips the point order of a dataset, which for a path means reversing the direction it runs. The flip can be unconditional, or conditioned on a rule stack, or on the winding a path has once projected to 2D, which is how a pile of paths is made to wind the same way. Attributes that only make sense in pairs, the arrive and leave tangents being the usual case, can be swapped as part of the flip so they stay correct afterwards.
UPCGExReversePointOrderSettings.situation: Paths that came from several sources and need one consistent direction or winding before anything reads them as sequences.

mechanism.text: Every dataset is judged on its own by Method, and only the ones that come out reversed are touched: the rest are forwarded by reference with no copy made. A reversed dataset is duplicated and every native point property is flipped end to end, then any configured attribute pairs are exchanged per point. Tagging records the verdict either way, and the point count never changes.

off_label.claim: With Method left unconditional, the swap pairs and the tag are still applied, so the node doubles as a pair-swapping tool for data whose order also happens to be reversible.
off_label.grounded_in: the unconditional method takes no early-out, so the duplicate, reverse, swap and tag path always runs

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The point datasets to consider. Each is judged separately.

inputs.label: Sorting Rules
inputs.note: The rules used to compare the first point against the last.
inputs.condition: when Method is Sorting Rules

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: Every input. Reversed datasets are duplicates; the ones left alone are forwarded by reference.

Method.tooltip: Method used to determine when to reverse point order.
Method.semantics: Unconditional flips everything. Sorting Rules compares the dataset's first and last point through the rule stack and flips when the first already sorts ahead of the last, so the result ends up running against Sort Direction rather than with it. Winding projects the points and flips only when the resulting winding is not the one selected.

ProjectionDetails.tooltip: Projection settings. Winding is computed on a 2D plane.
ProjectionDetails.semantics: Decides which plane the winding is measured on, so it is what makes the Winding method meaningful for paths that do not lie flat on the world XY plane.

SwapAttributesValues.tooltip: Attribute pairs to swap values between when reversing.
SwapAttributesValues.semantics: Exchanges the per-point values of two attributes that have to trade places when direction flips. Multiply By Minus One additionally negates both, which is what a directional value such as a tangent needs.
SwapAttributesValues.trap: The swap runs only on datasets that were actually reversed. A dataset the method left alone keeps its pairs as they were, which is correct for tangents and surprising for anything else.

IsReversedTag.tooltip: Tag to apply when points were reversed.
IsReversedTag.semantics: Applied per dataset, so a downstream node can restrict itself to what changed. On by default, which is worth knowing before matching on tags further down.

IsNotReversedTag.tooltip: Tag to apply when points were not reversed.
IsNotReversedTag.semantics: The complement, off by default. Enabling both gives every dataset exactly one of the two tags, which is a cleaner thing to match on than the presence or absence of one.

hints.text: A swap pair whose two attributes are missing, or carry different types, is dropped without a word. A pair on a container or otherwise extended type is dropped with a message. Either way the reversal still happens, so the symptom is tangents that survived the flip unchanged.

UPCGExSampleInsidePathSettings.name: Sample : Inside Path
UPCGExSampleInsidePathSettings.purpose: The sampler that runs the other way round. **Sample : Nearest Path** processes points and reads paths; this one processes paths and reads the points inside them, so what comes out is the paths, carrying what their contents added up to. It answers how many points a shape encloses and what their attributes average to, which is the question a per-point sampler cannot answer.
UPCGExSampleInsidePathSettings.situation: Authored outlines that need to know what landed inside them, whether that is a count, an average, or a single representative point.

mechanism.text: Every path is projected flat, and the points on the Targets pin are tested against that projection. Whatever falls inside is the path's sample set, and `Sample Method` decides whether the path keeps one of them or all of them. The outputs and blending are written onto the path's own data rather than onto the points, so a path leaves carrying a summary of its contents. A path that enclosed nothing is a failure, and `Output Mode` decides whether it still leaves on the main pin.

off_label.claim: With no outputs enabled beyond the inside count, it becomes a population test: paths leave tagged with how much they contain, and the Discarded pin collects the empty ones ready to be culled.
off_label.grounded_in: The discarded output is fed by paths that sampled no points despite valid targets, independently of which attribute outputs are enabled.

UPCGExSampleNearestBoundsSettings.name: Sample : Nearest Bounds
UPCGExSampleNearestBoundsSettings.purpose: Samples the target points whose bounds a point is standing inside. Where **Sample : Nearest Point** asks how far away the targets are, this one asks which targets contain you, so the targets are volumes rather than positions and a point either falls in one or it does not. Everything downstream is the same surface: outputs, blending from the targets, and moving the point onto what it sampled.
UPCGExSampleNearestBoundsSettings.situation: Points scattered over regions that were authored as bounded targets, where what each point should inherit depends on which region it landed in.

mechanism.text: Each target's bounds become an oriented box, and a point samples a target when its own position falls inside that box. Containment is the whole admission test, so distance never widens or narrows what qualifies. `Sample Method` decides what happens when a point sits inside several boxes at once: keep one by whichever rule the method names, or keep all of them and weight them. The weight a target contributes comes from how deeply the point sits inside it rather than from a range, and `Weight Remap` reshapes that. A point inside nothing counts as a failure and is still written to.
steps: Boxes that do not contain the point are discarded, whatever their distance.
Weights come from depth inside each surviving box, then outputs and blending are written from them.
Apply Sampling moves the point last.

off_label.claim: Because admission is containment rather than proximity, this is the sampler for asking which region a point belongs to. Wire regions in as targets, write the sampled index, and the result is a region id per point without any distance threshold to tune.
off_label.grounded_in: The octree callback returns early unless OBB::Sample reports bIsInside, so nothing outside a target's oriented bounds ever enters the union.

UPCGExSampleNearestPathSettings.name: Sample : Nearest Path
UPCGExSampleNearestPathSettings.purpose: Samples paths from your points, and by default it samples them as enclosed areas rather than as lines. A path is projected flat and a point is admitted when it falls inside that projection, which is what makes this the node for asking what region a point is in and how far it sits from that region's edge. Turning the inclusion settings off is what turns it back into a plain distance-to-the-line sampler.
UPCGExSampleNearestPathSettings.situation: Points that need to know which authored outline they fall within, and how near its boundary they are.

mechanism.text: Each path is projected onto a plane and each point is tested against that projection. `Only Sample When Inside` decides whether a point outside the shape may sample it at all, and `Always Sample When Inside` decides whether a point inside is exempt from the range band. Whatever survives those two is then handled like any sampler: `Sample Method` picks one path or accumulates them all, weights come from distance to the path, and the outputs and blending read the result. `Inclusion Offset` grows or shrinks the tested shape before any of this.
steps: Paths are projected and offset, and inclusion is decided against the offset shape.
The range band is applied to whatever inclusion admitted, unless the point is inside and exempt.
Weights, outputs and blending are written from the surviving paths.

off_label.claim: With both inclusion settings on, `Max Range` stops governing which paths are found and governs only how far outside a shape a point may still reach. Points inside are always sampled, so the range becomes a rim width around each outline rather than a search radius.
off_label.grounded_in: The range test is skipped when bAlwaysSampleWhenInside is set and the point is inside, and paths a point is not inside are rejected outright when bOnlySampleWhenInside is set.

bAlwaysSampleWhenInside.tooltip: If enabled, will always sample paths if the point lies inside, even if further away from the edges than the specified max range.
bAlwaysSampleWhenInside.semantics: Ships on, and exempts points inside a shape from the range band entirely. A point deep inside a large outline samples it even when the distance to the nearest edge is far past `Max Range`, so the range only ever governs points outside.

bOnlySampleWhenInside.tooltip: If enabled, will only sample paths if the point lies inside

A point outside every path samples nothing however near a path it is and however wide `Max Range` is set, so a graph measuring distance to open lines has to turn this off to get any result at all.
bOnlySampleWhenInside.trap: It reads as a narrowing option and behaves as the node's default mode. The symptom of leaving it on by accident is a whole dataset of failed samples with no warning, since a point outside everything is an ordinary failure.

InclusionOffset.tooltip: If non-zero, offsets the projected shape used for inclusion testing: positive = outset, negative = inset.
InclusionOffset.semantics: Grows or shrinks the projected shape before inclusion is decided, so it moves the boundary rather than adding tolerance to a distance. Positive outsets and negative insets. The distances written to attributes are still measured against the real path, not the offset one.
