They disagree on more than falloff: **Moving Average** walks the array and can only reach points that are near in path order, while **Radius** queries positions and reaches anything near in space, a stretch of the same path that loops back past the point included.

Influence.tooltip: Scales every contributor's weight. Average blending ignores weights, so under the Monolithic default this only distinguishes 0 (no smoothing) from non-zero.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Influence.semantics: A Blend Op set to `Average` under `Individual` discards it exactly as the Monolithic default does: it is the blend mode that decides, not the blending surface. At 0 both rules return before touching the point whatever the mode. The constant is clamped to -1 through 1 in the panel; an attribute source is not.

SmoothingAmount.tooltip: The amount of smoothing applied. Range of this value is highly dependant on the chosen smoothing method.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SmoothingAmount.semantics: **Moving Average** reads it as a count of points to either side and drops anything after the decimal point; **Radius** reads it as a distance in world units. The shipped 5 is a reasonable window and a very small radius, so switching rules without revisiting this is the usual reason a move to **Radius** goes wrong.

ScaleSmoothingAmountAttribute.tooltip: Static multiplier for the local smoothing amount.
ScaleSmoothingAmountAttribute.semantics: Multiplies whatever `Smoothing` resolved to, constant or per point, and the product is what the rule receives. Clamped to 0.001 at the bottom, so it can shrink the reach but never switch smoothing off: `Influence` at 0 is what does that.

BlendingInterface.tooltip: How to blend data from sampled points
BlendingInterface.semantics:
Which blending surface the weights are applied through. The rule never names a channel, so this is where you say what gets smoothed. `Individual` takes its instructions from the **Blend Ops** pin, and the usual recipe is one Blend Op on `$Position` with its blend mode set to `Weight`, which is what makes this a position smoother. Point it at a different attribute instead and the same neighbour weights blur that attribute with positions untouched. `Monolithic` swaps in the inline `Blending Settings` block, which covers every attribute and all nine point properties in one go.

An empty **Blend Ops** pin is a valid configuration rather than an oversight: the ops are optional and can be supplied from outside a subgraph, so a node with nothing wired returns its input unchanged because nothing was asked of it.

BlendingSettings.tooltip: Blending settings used to smooth attributes.
BlendingSettings.semantics: Ships with `Default Blending` on `Average`, which covers every attribute and all nine point properties at once, `Position` and `Seed` among them, and which counts contributors rather than weighing them: the falloff the rule computed is discarded and everything within reach counts the same. `Weight` is the entry that consumes the falloff. The per-property rows underneath override the default one property at a time, which is how positions get smoothed while colour is left alone.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: Turning it off does not bring short paths back here. A path of fewer than two points is refused before it is given an output at all, so there is nothing left for the toggle to pass through and it is dropped either way.

hints.text: The blend mode matters as much as the wiring. `Average` ignores the weight it is handed and divides by the contributor count instead, so the rule's falloff is thrown away and every contributor counts the same. `Weight` is the mode that honours it.

UPCGExSocketStagingSettings.name: Staging : Load Sockets
UPCGExSocketStagingSettings.purpose: Turns the sockets baked into collection entries into points. For every staged point it emits one point per socket the entry carries, on a dedicated Sockets output, so authored attachment points become ordinary points that the rest of the toolkit can filter, stage and spawn at. The staged points themselves pass through untouched on Out. For points carrying a mesh path that never went through a collection, Sample : Sockets reads the same sockets straight off the mesh.
UPCGExSocketStagingSettings.situation: A staged set of props has to grow accessories at their authored attachment points, one per socket, without disturbing the props.

mechanism.text: One execution reads each point's pick, resolves the entry behind it, and emits one point per socket that entry carries; the input points are forwarded on Out untouched. Each socket point sits at the socket transform composed into its host point's frame and takes a seed computed from that world location. Socket points come out grouped by host, in host order, each host's sockets in the entry's own order, and they carry the host point's attributes; beyond transform and seed, point properties are not copied from the host. Points the Point Filters pin rejects, and points whose pick does not resolve, contribute nothing. The Sockets pin carries one dataset per input dataset that produced at least one socket point.

off_label.claim: Socket points inherit their host's attributes wholesale, the staging pick hash included, so the Sockets output is itself a staged dataset: a spawn node or Staging : Type Filter wired to it treats every socket point as another instance of its host's pick. Carry Over Settings is where that gets stripped when it is unwanted.
off_label.grounded_in: the per-socket metadata entry parented to the host point's entry in FSocketHelper::Compile, and the FPCGExCarryOverDetails::Prune pass over the socket data's metadata

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The staged points to expand. Each must carry a pick in the selected staging layer.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. Accepts multiple connections, and the node errors out when it yields no valid mapping.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which staged points get expanded. Rejected points still come out on Out, and contribute no sockets.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The input points, forwarded unchanged, one dataset for one.

outputs.label: Sockets
outputs.note: The socket points, one dataset per input dataset that produced any. An input whose points resolved to entries with no surviving sockets contributes no dataset here.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

hints.text: A dataset carrying no pick in the selected layer produces no socket points and no message. Out still forwards the points and nothing is logged, so an empty Sockets pin is the only symptom of reading the wrong layer.
Each socket point's seed is computed from its own world location, so two sockets landing in the same place get the same seed, and moving a host re-rolls everything downstream that reads it.

UPCGExSortCollectionsSettings.name: Sort Data
UPCGExSortCollectionsSettings.purpose: Reorders the datasets on a pin rather than the points inside them, comparing one @Data value per dataset with the same Sorting Rule sub-nodes that Sort Points uses. The data itself is not touched at all; only its position in the output collection changes. That position matters wherever something downstream reads the pin in order, an index-based picker or a merge among them.
UPCGExSortCollectionsSettings.situation: A pin carrying many datasets whose order was decided by upstream wiring, feeding something that reads them in order.

mechanism.text: Each dataset supplies one value per rule, read from its @Data domain, and the datasets are compared against the rule stack in ascending Priority. Sort Direction flips the whole comparison. The datasets are then re-emitted in the resulting order, by reference: nothing is duplicated, no attribute is written, and no dataset is added or dropped. The node accepts any data type, so attribute sets sort alongside points.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The datasets to reorder. Any type.

inputs.label: Sorting Rules
inputs.note: Sorting Rule sub-nodes. Required: with none wired the node reports a missing input and fails rather than passing the data through.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same datasets, by reference, in the new order.

pins.dynamic: The In and Out pins accept and mirror any data type.

SortDirection.tooltip: Controls the order in which data will be sorted
SortDirection.semantics: Applied to the whole stack; individual rules carry their own inversion when one has to run the other way.

hints.text: The rules read the @Data domain, so an attribute that only exists per point contributes nothing here. Promote it to @Data first if a per-point value should decide the dataset's position.

UPCGExSortingRuleProviderSettings.name: Sorting Rule
UPCGExSortingRuleProviderSettings.purpose: One rule in an ordering. Sorting is rarely by a single value, so the rules are separate nodes wired to one pin and applied in sequence, each breaking the ties the one before it left. A node that sorts reads them all; this describes one of them.
UPCGExSortingRuleProviderSettings.situation: An ordering that needs more than one criterion, or a tie-break behind a value with repeats.

mechanism.text: The rule names a value to compare and emits a factory. Its consumer collects every rule on the pin, sorts them by `Priority`, and compares elements against them in that order: the first rule that distinguishes two elements decides, and the rest are not consulted for that pair. A rule whose value is identical across the data therefore contributes nothing except cost.

Priority.semantics: Where this rule sits in the sequence, which is what makes it a tie-break rather than a criterion. It is the whole of how several rules relate, since nothing else here refers to the other rules at all.

fields.name: Selector
fields.tooltip: Attribute or $Property.

fields.name: bReadDataTag
fields.tooltip: If enabled, reads the sort value from a data tag (tag:value format) instead of a point attribute. Tag values are per-data, so all points in the same data will share the same sort value. The Attribute selector will be used as the tag name to look up.

fields.name: Tolerance
fields.tooltip: Equality tolerance.

fields.name: bInvertRule
fields.tooltip: Invert sorting direction on that rule.

Config.semantics: What this rule compares and in which direction. The direction is per rule rather than per sort, so an ordering can run ascending on one criterion and descending on the next.

hints.text: Consumers differ in whether an unsorted tie falls back to input order. Where reproducibility matters, a final rule on a value known to be unique removes the question.

UPCGExSpatialTriageSettings.name: Spatial Triage
UPCGExSpatialTriageSettings.purpose: Sorts datasets into three piles by where they sit relative to one reference box: this one is mine, this one straddles the border, this one is somebody else's problem. It is a box-against-box test with no settings, meant to run at the head of a partitioned graph so each partition can claim the work it owns outright and treat the border cases separately.
UPCGExSpatialTriageSettings.situation: A partitioned generation where each cell has to decide, cheaply and before doing any real work, which of the incoming datasets it is responsible for.

mechanism.text: The first spatial data on the Bounds pin supplies one box, and every dataset on In is compared against it. A dataset whose own bounds centre falls inside the box goes to Inside; otherwise, if the two boxes overlap at all, it goes to Touching; everything else, including any input that carries no spatial bounds, goes to Outside. Data is re-pinned and never copied or modified. Any of the three pins that received nothing is deactivated, which culls whatever hangs off it.

off_label.claim: Because Inside is decided on the bounds centre alone, feeding it single points rather than datasets turns it into an ownership test with no border case at all: a point is either in the box or out of it, and Touching stays empty.
off_label.grounded_in: the Inside test is a containment check on the input's bounds centre, which for a one-point dataset is that point

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The data to triage. Forwarded by reference to exactly one of the three outputs.

inputs.label: Bounds
inputs.note: One spatial data whose bounds are the reference box. Only the first is used; anything else on the pin is ignored. The node reports an error and stops when nothing spatial arrives here.

outputs.label: Inside
outputs.note: Data whose bounds centre falls within the reference box.

outputs.label: Touching
outputs.note: Data whose box overlaps the reference box without its centre being inside it.

outputs.label: Outside
outputs.note: Everything else, including inputs that carry no spatial bounds at all, such as attribute sets.

pins.dynamic: The In pin and all three outputs accept any data type; only the Bounds pin is restricted to spatial data.

hints.text: Inside means the centre is inside, not that the data fits. A dataset that overhangs the box on every side still lands on Inside as long as its middle is within, so treat Inside as ownership rather than as containment.

UPCGExSpawnDynamicMeshSettings.name: Spawn Dynamic Mesh
UPCGExSpawnDynamicMeshSettings.purpose: Puts a dynamic mesh into the level, with more control over the component than the stock node offers. The topology nodes produce meshes as data, and something has to turn that data into a component an actor owns; this is that step, with the component's properties, its attachment and its post-spawn calls all exposed.
UPCGExSpawnDynamicMeshSettings.situation: A generated mesh that has to exist in the level with specific component settings, rather than merely as graph data.

mechanism.text: Each mesh becomes a component on the target actor, configured from the template descriptor and then adjusted by whatever property overrides are listed. `Attachment Rules` decide how the component sits under its parent. After spawning, the named functions are called on the target actor, which is the hook for anything the component's own settings cannot express.

fields.name: bVisible
fields.tooltip: Controls whether the component is rendered in the scene.

fields.name: MinDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: The minimum distance at which the primitive should be rendered, measured in world space units from the center of the primitive's bounding sphere to the camera position.

fields.name: LDMaxDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: Max draw distance exposed to LDs. The real max draw distance is the min (disregarding 0) of this and volumes affecting this object.

fields.name: IndirectLightingCacheQuality
fields.tooltip: Quality of indirect lighting for Movable primitives.  This has a large effect on Indirect Lighting Cache update time.

fields.name: LightmapType
fields.tooltip: Controls the type of lightmap used for this component.

fields.name: HLODBatchingPolicy
fields.tooltip: Determines how the geometry of a component will be incorporated in proxy (simplified) HLODs.
When true, will not be captured by Scene Capture

fields.name: BodyInstance
fields.tooltip: Physics scene information for this component, holds a single rigid body with multiple shapes.

fields.name: ShadowCacheInvalidationBehavior
fields.tooltip: Control shadow invalidation behavior, in particular with respect to Virtual Shadow Maps and material effects like World Position Offset.

fields.name: CanCharacterStepUpOn
fields.tooltip: Determine whether a Character can step up onto this component. This controls whether they can try to step up on it when they bump in to it, not whether they can walk on it after landing on it. @see FWalkableSlopeOverride

fields.name: LightingChannels
fields.tooltip: Channels that this component should be in.  Lights with matching channels will affect the component. These channels only apply to opaque materials, direct lighting, and dynamic lighting and shadowing.

fields.name: RayTracingGroupId
fields.tooltip: Defines run-time groups of components. For example allows to assemble multiple parts of a building at runtime. -1 means that component doesn't belong to any group.

fields.name: CustomDepthStencilValue
fields.tooltip: Optionally write this 0-255 value to the stencil buffer in CustomDepth pass (Requires project setting or r.CustomDepth == 3)

fields.name: TranslucencySortPriority
fields.tooltip: Translucent objects with a lower sort priority draw behind objects with a higher priority. Translucent objects with the same priority are rendered from back-to-front based on their bounds origin. This setting is also used to sort objects being drawn into a runtime virtual texture. Ignored if the object is not translucent.  The default priority is zero. Warning: This should never be set to a non-default value unless you know what you are doing, as it will prevent the renderer from sorting correctly. It is especially problematic on dynamic gameplay effects.

fields.name: TranslucencySortDistanceOffset
fields.tooltip: Modified sort distance offset for translucent objects in world units. A positive number will move the sort distance further and a negative number will move the distance closer. Ignored if the object is not translucent. Warning: Adjusting this value will prevent the renderer from correctly sorting based on distance.  Only modify this value if you are certain it will not cause visual artifacts.

fields.name: RuntimeVirtualTextures
fields.tooltip: Array of runtime virtual textures into which we draw the mesh for this actor. The material also needs to be set up to output to a virtual texture.

fields.name: VirtualTextureLodBias
fields.tooltip: Bias to the LOD selected for rendering to runtime virtual textures.

fields.name: VirtualTextureCullMips
fields.tooltip: Number of lower mips in the runtime virtual texture to skip for rendering this primitive. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture. This culling method doesn't take into account primitive size or virtual texture size.

fields.name: VirtualTextureMinCoverage
fields.tooltip: Set the minimum pixel coverage before culling from the runtime virtual texture. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture.

fields.name: VirtualTextureRenderPassType
fields.tooltip: Controls if this component draws in the main pass as well as in the virtual texture.

fields.name: BoundsScale
fields.tooltip: Scales the bounds of the object. This is useful when using World Position Offset to animate the vertices of the object outside of its bounds. Warning: Increasing the bounds of an object will reduce performance and shadow quality! Currently only used by StaticMeshComponent and SkeletalMeshComponent.

fields.name: RayTracingGroupCullingPriority
fields.tooltip: Defines how quickly it should be culled. For example buildings should have a low priority, but small dressing should have a high priority.

fields.name: CustomDepthStencilWriteMask
fields.tooltip: Mask used for stencil buffer writes.

fields.name: OverrideMaterials
fields.tooltip: Material overrides.

fields.name: OverlayMaterial
fields.tooltip: Translucent material to blend on top of this mesh. Mesh will be rendered twice - once with a base material and once with overlay material

fields.name: OverlayMaterialMaxDrawDistance
fields.tooltip: The max draw distance for overlay material. A distance of 0 indicates that overlay will be culled using primitive max distance.

fields.name: bUseAsyncCooking
fields.tooltip: Controls whether the physics cooking should be done off the game thread. This should be used when collision geometry doesn't have to be immediately up to date (For example streaming in far away objects)

fields.name: bEnableComplexCollision
fields.tooltip: If true, current mesh will be used as Complex Collision source mesh. This is independent of the CollisionType setting, ie, even if Complex collision is enabled, if this is false, then the Complex Collision mesh will be empty

fields.name: bDeferCollisionUpdates
fields.tooltip: If true, updates to the mesh will not result in immediate collision regeneration. Useful when the mesh will be modified multiple times before collision is needed.

fields.name: bExplicitShowWireframe
fields.tooltip: If true, render the Wireframe on top of the Shaded Mesh

fields.name: WireframeColor
fields.tooltip: Constant Color used when Override Color Mode is set to Constant

fields.name: ConstantColor
fields.tooltip: Constant Color used when Override Color Mode is set to Constant

fields.name: ColorSpaceMode
fields.tooltip: Color Space Transform that will be applied to the colors stored in the DynamicMesh Attribute Color Overlay when constructing render buffers. Default is "No Transform", ie color R/G/B/A will be independently converted from 32-bit float to 8-bit by direct mapping. LinearToSRGB mode will apply SRGB conversion, ie assumes colors in the Mesh are in Linear space. This will produce the same behavior as UStaticMesh. SRGBToLinear mode will invert SRGB conversion, ie assumes colors in the Mesh are in SRGB space.

fields.name: bEnableFlatShading
fields.tooltip: Enable use of per-triangle facet normals in place of mesh normals

fields.name: bEnableViewModeOverrides
fields.tooltip: This flag controls whether Editor View Mode Overrides are enabled for this mesh. For example, this controls hidden-line removal on the wireframe in Wireframe View Mode, and whether the normal map will be disabled in Lighting-Only View Mode, as well as various other things. Use SetViewModeOverridesEnabled() to control this setting in Blueprints/C++.

fields.name: bEnableRaytracing
fields.tooltip: Enable/disable Raytracing support on this Mesh, if Raytracing is currently enabled in the Project Settings. Use SetEnableRaytracing() to configure this flag in Blueprints/C++.

TemplateDescriptor.semantics: The starting configuration every spawned component takes. It is a template rather than a per-mesh setting, so anything that has to differ between meshes belongs in the property overrides instead.

PropertyOverrideDescriptions.semantics: Per-property changes applied on top of the template, which is how components spawned in one pass end up configured differently from each other. They are applied after the template, so an override and a template value naming the same property resolve to the override.

AttachmentRules.tooltip: How to attach the component to their parent actor

PostProcessFunctionNames.tooltip: Specify a list of functions to be called on the target actor after instances are spawned. Functions need to be parameter-less and with "CallInEditor" flag enabled.
PostProcessFunctionNames.semantics: Functions called on the target actor once the components exist. The source notes that the functions have to meet the engine's requirements to be callable this way, so a name that does not resolve does nothing rather than reporting a problem.

UPCGExSplineToPathSettings.name: Spline to Path
UPCGExSplineToPathSettings.purpose: Turns vanilla spline data into path data, one point per control point. It is a conversion and not a sampler: nothing is resampled, interpolated or placed between control points, so the shape you get back is the control polygon rather than the curve. What the spline knew and points cannot store is offered as attributes instead, tangents among them, and closed loops can be forced to a chosen winding on the way through.
UPCGExSplineToPathSettings.situation: A spline needs to go through path nodes, and the curve between its control points is not what the operation cares about.

mechanism.text: One spline dataset in, one path out, point for control point: an open spline gives a point per segment plus a final one, a closed loop gives a point per segment. Positions come from the spline transform at each control point, and closure travels on the output data. Attributes on the spline dataset are carried across, the elements-domain ones one control point at a time. Anything not accepted by `Sample Inputs` is dropped, and a run that matches nothing at all fails with an error rather than passing its input through.

inputs.label: Splines
inputs.note: Vanilla spline data. This replaces the path processor's usual **Paths** pin, so there is nowhere on this node to hand it points.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: One path per accepted spline, in input order.

fields.name: bInheritScale
fields.tooltip: Multiply result scale by the parent's scale.

fields.name: bInheritRotation
fields.tooltip: Rotate result by the parent's rotation.

SampleInputs.semantics: Splines that fail the open or closed test are dropped rather than forwarded. If nothing survives, the node errors out with no output at all, so this doubles as the reason a graph goes empty when a set of splines turns out to be all one kind.

Winding.tooltip: Enforce a specific winding order on closed-loop paths. Open splines are unaffected.
Winding.semantics: Closed loops only, and it works by reversing the whole point order rather than by rotating anything. Winding is measured in a plane fitted to the loop, so a loop that is not flat is judged against its own best-fit plane and not against the world.
Winding.trap: Reversal takes the carried attributes with it, and it swaps and negates the tangent pair so arrive and leave still mean arrive and leave in the new order. An attribute of your own that encodes direction is reversed in position but not in sign.

ArriveTangentAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write Arrive tangent to.

LeaveTangentAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write Leave tangent to.

LengthAtPointAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write the length at point to.

AlphaAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write the length at point to.

PointTypeAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute that store the point type.

TagForwarding.tooltip: Tags to be forwarded from source splines

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

TagForwarding.semantics: Tags are pruned per input spline and land on that spline's own output path, so a tag on one input never reaches the path built from another.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

CarryOverDetails.semantics: Governs the spline dataset's own attributes on the way onto the path's points. Data-domain attributes come across as a single value; per-element ones are read control point by control point.

hints.text: Only vanilla spline data is accepted. Landscape spline components arrive as a different data type, are refused by the cast, and are skipped without a warning of their own; if every input is a landscape spline the run ends on the generic no-targets error. **Get Path Data** reads landscape splines directly off their actors and is the way to convert them.

UPCGExSplitPathSettings.name: Path : Split
UPCGExSplitPathSettings.purpose: Cuts one path into several at the points a filter picks out. Five actions differ only in what becomes of the point that triggered the cut: it can be duplicated into both halves, dropped, or left on one side; two of the five read the filter as a state that flips rather than as an event, which turns a per-point verdict into runs. Everything that comes out is open, whatever went in.
UPCGExSplitPathSettings.situation: One path has to become several, and where it breaks is decided by a per-point test rather than by a count or a distance.

mechanism.text: One path in, a variable number out: as many as the cuts produce, each one a contiguous run of the original points in their original order. Nothing is invented and nothing is moved, so every output point is an input point, and under one action a point appears in two of them. A path whose filter picks nothing out comes back untouched and still closed. A closed loop is handled as a loop, so a cut anywhere in it produces runs rather than leaving a seam at the original first point.

off_label.claim: `Disconnect` with a condition that passes on the last point alone opens a closed loop without touching its point count: the single run covers every point, and closure is dropped because the loop's last segment is the one that was cut.
off_label.grounded_in: the Disconnect action closes the run inclusively at the final index, leaving one sub-path whose count equals the input, which CompleteWork resolves for a closed input as a duplicate with the closed-loop marker cleared

off_label.claim: The even and odd tags number the results rather than describing them, so tagging both and reading nothing else gives a downstream test for which side of an alternating pattern a run fell on.
off_label.grounded_in: Output tags by a running counter over the emitted sub-paths rather than by any property of the run

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to cut. Each is handled on its own.

inputs.label: Split Conditions
inputs.note: Point filters marking where a cut happens. Required: with nothing wired the node has no cuts to make and errors out.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The runs, in the order they occur along the input. Every one is marked open, and a path that was not cut is forwarded with its own closure intact.

SplitAction.tooltip: If both split and remove are true, the selected behavior takes priority
SplitAction.semantics: All five read the same verdict and differ in what happens to the point carrying it. `Split` duplicates that point, so it is both the last point of one run and the first of the next and no length is lost. `Remove` drops it, leaving a gap the width of two segments. `Disconnect` keeps it as the last point of the run it was in and starts the next run at the following point, so one segment goes missing. `Partition` reads the verdict as a state and starts a run wherever the state changes, so consecutive points sharing a verdict stay together and every point ends up in some run. `Switch` reads the verdict as a toggle, so a passing point flips between keeping and dropping and only the kept stretches become runs.

InitialBehavior.tooltip: How the initial value is determined for Switch/Partition modes.
InitialBehavior.semantics: The state the walk enters the path with. `Constant` takes the value below. `From Point` takes the first point's own verdict, which under `Switch` means a passing first point immediately toggles away from it. The two `Preserve` variants start from the opposite value so the first point's verdict is acted on rather than cancelled: under `Switch`, `From Point (Preserve)` is what makes a passing first point open a kept run instead of closing one.
InitialBehavior.trap: `Partition` shows this row and both entries under it and reads none of them. Its first run always opens at the first point, and the state is brought into line with that point's verdict before anything can be closed, so all four entries and every `Initial Value` give the same runs.

bInitialValue.tooltip: The initial switch value to start from. If false, paths only start being created after the first true result. If true, paths start from the beginning and stop at the first true result instead.

bInclusive.tooltip: Should point insertion be inclusive of the behavior change
bInclusive.semantics: Reachable under `Partition` and `Switch` alone, and it decides which side of the change the point sits on. Excluded, the outgoing run ends one point earlier and the point belongs to what follows. Included, the point closes the outgoing run as well: under `Partition` it then appears in both runs, the way a `Split` cut point does, and under `Switch` it becomes the kept run's last point rather than the first casualty of the toggle.

bOmitSinglePointOutputs.tooltip: Whether to output single-point data or not
bOmitSinglePointOutputs.semantics: It governs two separate things: a run that came out one point long, and an input that arrived under two points. Switched off, the short input is forwarded rather than counted as invalid.
bOmitSinglePointOutputs.trap: Switching it off is not enough on its own to see a single-point result. `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` is read again when the results are staged, and while it is on, which is its default, anything under two points is dropped there. Both have to be off.

IsEvenTag.tooltip: Tag to apply to even-numbered split paths.
IsEvenTag.semantics: Even and odd count the results as they are emitted, so the parity is a position in the output list rather than a property of the run. A run dropped for being a single point shifts the parity of everything after it.

IsOddTag.tooltip: Tag to apply to odd-numbered split paths.
IsOddTag.semantics: The other half of the same counter, and off by default while the even tag is on, so out of the box every other result carries a tag and the rest carry nothing.

bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.tooltip: If enabled, collections that have less than 2 points won't be processed and be omitted from the output.
bOmitInvalidPathsOutputs.semantics: The way-in half of the base toggle is not used here: what decides whether a short input is forwarded is `Omit Single Point Outputs`. What this still does is the way-out half, dropping any staged result under two points.

hints.text: A closed loop cut anywhere in its middle comes back as runs whose seam has been healed: the stretch running off the end of the point list is joined to the stretch starting at its beginning, so what would have been two runs meeting at the original first point is one. That join is only made when the first point was not itself a cut.
Closure never survives a cut. Every run is written out marked open, so a closed loop split in two gives two open paths and nothing downstream will treat either as a loop again.

UPCGExStagedTypeFilterSettings.name: Staging : Type Filter
UPCGExStagedTypeFilterSettings.purpose: Routes staged points by what their pick resolved to. The staging spawn nodes already ignore entries that are not their type, so this node exists for the explicit version: splitting one mixed staged dataset into a stream per collection type, or keeping and dropping types by name. It also splits along a second seam: Entry Shape mode separates picks that resolved to a direct asset from picks that resolved to a sub-collection.
UPCGExStagedTypeFilterSettings.situation: An Omni Collection staged one mixed dataset, and the meshes must reach the mesh spawner while the actors reach Staging : Spawn Actors.

mechanism.text: Each point's pick hash is resolved against the Collection Map, and the resolved entry's own type id decides the route; the hosting collection's type is never consulted, so an Omni Collection's rows route by what each row holds. The type roster comes from the collection type registry, so collection types registered by other plugins appear as routes on their own. Points that fail to resolve count as invalid and follow the Include Invalid setting.

off_label.claim: Wire both Entry Shape outputs to debug nodes and the split doubles as an audit of how often distribution entered nested collections.
off_label.grounded_in: EPCGExStagedTypeFilterMode::EntryShape leaf-vs-collection routing in the element

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The staged points to route.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: Points the filter kept.
outputs.condition: Include and Exclude modes

outputs.label: Discarded
outputs.note: Points that matched no enabled type.
outputs.condition: when Output Discarded is on

outputs.label: One pin per enabled type
outputs.note: Labels come from the registry: Mesh, Actor, Level, and any custom types.
outputs.condition: Pin Per Type mode

outputs.label: Leaf
outputs.note: Points whose pick resolved to a direct asset entry.
outputs.condition: Entry Shape mode

outputs.label: Collection
outputs.note: Points whose pick resolved to a sub-collection.
outputs.condition: Entry Shape mode

pins.dynamic: In Pin Per Type and Entry Shape the output pin set is computed from the mode and the enabled types, so the node's pins change as its configuration does.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

FilterMode.semantics: Include and Exclude keep a single Out pin; Pin Per Type and Entry Shape replace it with one pin per route.
FilterMode.trap: In Pin Per Type and Entry Shape the node's default output pin is Discarded, so a wire dropped onto the node without picking a pin carries the leftovers, never a type.

TypeConfig.tooltip: Type configuration - populated from collection type registry

fields.name: TypeFilter
fields.tooltip: Type inclusion map - keys are read-only, populated from registry

fields.name: bIncludeInvalid
fields.tooltip: Include/exclude invalid/unresolved entries

bOutputDiscarded.tooltip: If enabled, output filtered-out points to a separate pin

bDiscardInvalidCollections.tooltip: If enabled, subcollection entries with a null/missing subcollection reference are treated as unresolved (routed to Discarded if enabled, otherwise dropped) instead of going to the Collection pin.

UPCGExStagingFittingSettings.name: Staging : Fitting
UPCGExStagingFittingSettings.purpose: Fitting normally runs inside Staging : Distribute, as the pick is made. This node is the standalone pass, for points whose fit has to be solved a second time or solved for the first time: after a swap rewrote picks to entries with a different footprint, or for points carrying a mesh path that never went through a collection. It runs the same scale-to-fit, justification and variation stack against bounds it resolves itself, and it leaves each fitted point's bounds describing the asset instead of the cell.
UPCGExStagingFittingSettings.situation: A Variant Collection swap replaced entries whose footprint differs from the originals, so the transforms still describe a fit solved against the old bounds.

mechanism.text: Per point, the node resolves an asset box, solves the fit against the point's own bounds, and writes the result back onto the point. Point count is preserved unless Prune Empty Points is on, in which case points that resolved to nothing are gathered out at the end. A fitted point comes out with three things changed: the scale on its transform, its position, and its bounds.

off_label.claim: Every fitted point leaves with its bounds replaced by the resolved asset box, and that holds with Scale to Fit set to None, where the box written is the entry's staged bounds untouched. The node is therefore a way to stamp asset footprints onto staged points for downstream bounds work, overlap tests and packing among them.
off_label.grounded_in: ProcessPoints writes OutBoundsMin/OutBoundsMax from the fitted box for every point that resolves, and PCGExFitting::ScaleToFitAxes returns early leaving OutBounds at Entry->Staging.AlteredBounds when the mode is EPCGExFitMode::None

off_label.claim: With Prune Empty Points on and the fit switched off, the node is a validity gate for staged points: anything whose pick does not resolve to an entry with valid staged bounds is dropped from the output.
off_label.grounded_in: the InvalidPoint marking on a failed FPickUnpacker::ResolveEntry or an invalid Staging.Bounds, and the Gather over the mask in FProcessor::Write

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to fit. They must carry a pick hash in Collection Map source, or the mesh path attribute in Mesh Attribute source.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. The node errors out when the Map yields no valid mapping.
inputs.condition: when Source is Collection Map; the pin does not exist in Mesh Attribute source

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which points get fitted. Rejected points are treated the same as points that failed to resolve, so Prune Empty Points decides whether they survive.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points with fitted transforms and rewritten bounds, one point out per point in unless Prune Empty Points removed the invalid ones. Datasets pass through one for one, with the single exception noted under Source.

Source.tooltip: Where to read bounds from. Collection Map uses staged entry data; Mesh Attribute reads a static mesh path and uses its bounding box.
Source.semantics: Mesh Attribute registers the referenced meshes as asset dependencies and loads them, so cost tracks the number of distinct paths; Collection Map reads bounds baked at staging rebuild and loads nothing. Mesh Attribute also drops the Map pin, and with it every setting that reads entry data.
Source.trap: In Mesh Attribute source an input dataset that lacks the path attribute is dropped whole when Prune Empty Points is on, and forwarded unfitted when it is off. When no mesh loads across any input, the node cancels its own execution.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

AssetPathAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute containing the static mesh path.

fields.name: ScaleToFitMode
fields.tooltip: How scaling is applied to fit within target bounds. None = no scaling, Uniform = same scale all axes, Individual = per-axis control.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: Uniform scaling strategy. Fill = stretch to fill, Min = fit smallest axis, Max = fit largest axis, Avg = average.

fields.name: ScaleToFitX
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for X axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitY
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Y axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitZ
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Z axis when using Individual mode.

ScaleToFit.semantics: The target box is the point's local bounds multiplied by the point's transform scale, so a point's own scale sizes the box it is being fitted into. An axis carrying an active rule has its scale replaced outright by the computed factor; an axis left on None keeps the point's scale as it was. In Collection Map source, an entry defining its own Scale to Fit or Justification override replaces the node values for its points unless the Entry Overrides toggles are off.

bConsiderEntryScaleToFit.tooltip: When enabled, entries that define a Scale to Fit override (entry-local or collection-global) replace this node's Scale to Fit for their points. Collection Map source only.

bConsiderEntryJustification.tooltip: When enabled, entries that define a Justification override (entry-local or collection-global) replace this node's Justification for their points. Collection Map source only.

Variations.tooltip: Variations are only available in Collection Map mode (entries carry per-asset variation limits).

fields.name: Offset
fields.tooltip: When to apply random offset variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.tooltip: When to apply random rotation variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

fields.name: Scale
fields.tooltip: When to apply random scale variation. Before = applied to asset before fitting, After = applied to result.

Variations.semantics: Randomness is drawn per point from the point's own Seed property combined with the node's Seed, so the same points through the same node give the same variations, and re-seeding the points changes them.

bPruneEmptyPoints.tooltip: If enabled, filter output based on whether a staging has been applied or not (empty entry).
bPruneEmptyPoints.semantics: Empty covers four cases: a pick that does not resolve, an entry whose staged bounds are invalid, a mesh whose bounds did not load, and any point the Point Filters pin rejected. With this off, all four pass through with transform and bounds untouched. It also decides whether the node may mutate its input in place, since Steal Data is refused while pruning is on.
bPruneEmptyPoints.trap: Wiring a filter into Point Filters while this is on deletes the excluded points instead of leaving them unfitted.

TranslationAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the FVector attribute to write fitting offset to. This is the translation added to the point transform according to fitting/justification rules. Mostly useful for offsetting spline meshes.
TranslationAttributeName.semantics: The value stored is the justification translation in the point's local frame, before the point's rotation is applied to it; the transform received the rotated version. Variation offsets are excluded, so the attribute records what the fit moved and nothing else.

hints.text: The node rewrites each fitted point's bounds to the asset box. Everything downstream that reads point bounds, spacing, overlap tests, a second fitting pass, sees the asset footprint from here on, not the cell the point started in.

UPCGExStagingLoadLevelSettings.name: Staging : Spawn Level
UPCGExStagingLoadLevelSettings.purpose: Places whole levels at staged points. Level entries stage like any other pick, and this is the node that follows through on them: every point whose pick resolved to a Level entry gets that level's content at its transform, registered with PCG so regeneration cleans it up. The content arrives in one of three forms, duplicated actors, a Level Instance actor, or a streamed-in level, and which one you get depends on the build and on the component's generation trigger. Picks that resolved to any other entry type are ignored, so a mixed staged dataset can be wired straight in.
UPCGExStagingLoadLevelSettings.situation: A level was dressed by hand and listed as one entry in a Level Collection, and every point that picked it has to become that arrangement in the world.

mechanism.text: Points pass through untouched: same count, same order, nothing written onto them. Each point that clears the filters and whose pick resolves to a Level entry with a valid level asset contributes one placement of that level at the point's transform, and every other point contributes nothing and logs nothing. Whatever gets placed is registered as a PCG-managed resource, so regenerating unloads or deletes the previous run's content before the new content lands. When nothing feeding the node has changed since the last run, the previous content stays where it is and no placement happens at all.

off_label.claim: Root Actor resolves per point, and the resolved actor decides which level the placed content is spawned into, so a per-point attribute can spread one execution's output across several sublevels by pointing each point at an actor that already lives in the sublevel it belongs in.
off_label.grounded_in: SpawnParams.OverrideLevel taken from TargetActor->GetLevel() in FProcessor::SpawnAsLevelInstance, and StaticDuplicateObject into TargetActor->GetLevel() in FProcessor::SpawnAsLooseActors

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The staged points. Several datasets can be wired in and each is processed on its own.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. The node errors out when the Map yields no valid mapping.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which points place a level. Rejected points still leave on the Out pin, unchanged like every other point.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The input points, forwarded unchanged. The node writes no attribute, and the Collection Map does not come back out.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

RootActor.tooltip: Optional root actor that owns the spawned levels. Resolves per-point (constant, data-domain attribute, or per-point attribute). When the resolved soft path is null, falls back to the PCG component's target actor. Resolution is by ResolveObject only -- paths must point to live actors.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

RootActor.semantics: What it is for changes with the form. On the two editor forms it is the actor the content parents to and the level the content is spawned into, and a point that resolves neither a Root Actor nor a component target actor places nothing and warns with its point index. On the streamed-in form there is no actor to parent to, and it only decides the Outliner folder the loaded actors are filed under.

AttachOptions.tooltip: Controls where spawned ALevelInstance actors appear in the Outliner and how they are parented to the root actor. On the streaming-level path (no actor to attach), Attached silently behaves like InFolder.
AttachOptions.semantics: It governs the duplicated actors too, on the editor form where Spawn As Level Instance is off: the root actors of each duplicated hierarchy are parented to the target actor per this setting, and their children follow through the hierarchy they were authored with.

LevelNameSuffix.tooltip: Suffix appended to each spawned streaming level's package name to ensure uniqueness. If empty, uses point index.
LevelNameSuffix.semantics: Read on the streamed-in form only, and ignored by both editor forms. A run counter and the point index are appended to whatever is set here, so uniqueness across executions never depends on the value; what the value buys is a readable prefix on the streamed packages.

StreamingLevelClass.tooltip: Streaming level class used for the runtime (non-LevelInstance) path. Override with a custom subclass for advanced streaming behavior. If None, defaults to UPCGExLevelStreamingDynamic. WARNING: Do NOT use ULevelStreamingLevelInstance subclasses here -- they require the ALevelInstance actor path and will not work with raw streaming level spawning.
StreamingLevelClass.semantics: Only the streamed-in form reads it. The default class is what destroys main-world-only and export-only actors as the level finishes loading and files the rest into the generated folder, so a replacement that does not derive from it drops both.
StreamingLevelClass.trap: Pointing this at a Level Instance streaming class fails the node outright with an error before any point is read, so nothing spawns at all.

bSpawnAsLevelInstance.tooltip: When enabled (editor only), spawn ALevelInstance actors instead of raw streaming levels. Gives proper inspector grouping with collapsible entries in the World Outliner. Falls back to streaming if executed in cooked builds.
bSpawnAsLevelInstance.semantics: This picks between two of the three forms, and only in an editor build on a component whose generation trigger is not Generate At Runtime. Enabled, each point gets a Level Instance actor at its transform, parented per Attach Options, with the level streamed in underneath it and collapsible in the Outliner. Disabled, the level's actors are duplicated one by one into the target actor's level as ordinary actors: hierarchy and authored offsets preserved, placed into the point's frame, individually selectable, tagged as PCG-generated and saved with the level. That duplication leaves out the source level's World Settings, anything flagged main-world-only, and socket-provider actors marked as export-only. Generate At Runtime and cooked builds take neither branch and stream the level in whole, the one form that exists outside the editor.
bSpawnAsLevelInstance.trap: The actor filtering the streamed-in form applies is compiled editor-only, so a packaged build keeps the main-world-only and export-only actors that both editor forms remove.

LevelInstanceClass.tooltip: Level instance actor class used for the ALevelInstance path. Override with a custom subclass for advanced level instance behavior. If None, defaults to APCGExLevelInstance.
LevelInstanceClass.semantics: Only the Level Instance form reads it. The default class routes its streaming through the plugin's own streaming class, which destroys main-world-only actors and files the rest into the generated folder; a plain Level Instance subclass gets neither, and its inner actors get no Outliner folder.

bQuietRuntimeFallbackWarning.tooltip: Suppress the warning emitted when Spawn As Level Instance is enabled but the component uses Generate At Runtime (which forces a fallback to streaming levels).

hints.text: What you author against and what a packaged build produces are different forms. Both editor forms put actors in your level; a cooked build streams the level in, with different actor filtering. Verify a level entry in a packaged build before treating the editor result as final.

UPCGExStagingLoadPropertiesSettings.name: Staging : Load Properties
UPCGExStagingLoadPropertiesSettings.purpose: Staged points know which entry they picked and nothing else. This node reads the entry back and writes what it holds onto the points: the custom properties the collection declares, the entry's own data (weight, category, tags, bounds, asset path, and the two type ids), and its grammar block, for graphs feeding vanilla PCG subdivision. Sampleable properties go one step further: a curve authored on the entry is evaluated at a per-point time, so one authored curve becomes a per-point value. A property can also be a pick of its own: a Collection Entry property writes a second pick hash onto the points, on a staging layer named after the output it was mapped to, and the node's Map output carries the collection that resolves it.
UPCGExStagingLoadPropertiesSettings.situation: A cost, a curve or a footprint authored on the collection entries has to drive point math downstream, and the points carry only their pick.

mechanism.text: Each point's pick hash is resolved against the Collection Map, and the requested values are read off the entry it names. Resolution runs once per distinct pick and fans out to every point sharing it, so the work tracks how many distinct entries are in play rather than the point count. Every configured output becomes an attribute across the whole dataset: points whose pick does not resolve, and points the filter rejected, keep that attribute's default value. Point count, order and existing attributes are untouched, and the values come from the collections and their staging data, so none of the assets the entries reference are loaded.

off_label.claim: Enable only the asset path output and the node becomes the exit from the Collection Map ecosystem: it writes the same `AssetPath` soft-path attribute that Staging : Distribute writes in Point Attributes mode and Staging : Fitting reads in Mesh Attribute source, so resolvable picks can be handed to anything that only understands a path, without re-staging.
off_label.grounded_in: the AssetPath field getter reading Entry->Staging.Path into a soft-path attribute defaulting to AssetPath, the same default carried by UPCGExStagingDistributeSettings::AssetPathAttributeName and UPCGExStagingFittingSettings::AssetPathAttributeName

off_label.claim: The bounds outputs stamp each entry's staged footprint onto the points as plain attributes and leave the points' own bounds alone, which is the reading Staging : Fitting cannot give, since that node overwrites the bounds it computes. Spacing, packing and overlap math that has to know an asset's size before deciding anything can read it here first.
off_label.grounded_in: the Extents, BoundsMin and BoundsMax field getters reading Entry->Staging.Bounds into attributes, with no write to the point's own bounds anywhere in FProcessor

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Staged points. Each must carry a pick hash on the layer named by Staging Layer.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. The node errors out when the Map yields no valid mapping. It is consumed and never forwarded, and the node's own Map output is a different set, so a downstream consumer that needs this one takes it from the same source this node did.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which points get values. Rejected points stay in the output carrying each attribute's default value.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, in the same order, with one attribute per configured output.

outputs.label: Map
outputs.note: The collections that this node's own Collection Entry property outputs point at, one row each, in the same index-and-path shape as any Collection Map, so it merges with the Map that came in through the stock Merge Attributes node. Nothing else reaches it: the input Map is not copied through, and property types that reference nothing external contribute no rows.
outputs.condition: declared on every configuration, as an advanced pin while Output Map is off and a normal one once it is on, and carrying data only when it is on

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).
StagingLayer.semantics: This names the layer the node reads, so a dataset carrying picks on several layers needs one Load Properties per layer it wants values from. It has no say in what a Collection Entry property output writes, which takes its layer from that output's own name.
StagingLayer.trap: A dataset whose points carry no pick on this layer passes through with none of the attributes created and no message. When every output is missing downstream, this is the setting to check first.

PropertyOutputSettings.tooltip: Properties to output as point attributes. Property names must match properties defined in the source collection.
PropertyOutputSettings.semantics: Each mapped name is looked up across every collection the Map names, in a stable order, and the first declaration found decides the output attribute's type for every row. A name no staged collection declares is skipped with a warning rather than producing an empty attribute. One type renames its own output: a Collection Entry property writes an int64 pick hash under `PCGEx/CollectionEntry/` followed by the output name, which makes that name a staging layer of its own, and the collection it points at is loaded before the write so the hash resolves instead of coming out 0.
PropertyOutputSettings.trap: Two collections declaring the same property name with different types resolve to one attribute for the whole dataset. The first declaration found decides it, and every point whose entry carries the other type is reported in a warning and left holding the attribute's default. Keep a name to a single type across the collections a graph stages from, or map them to differently named outputs.

bOutputMap.tooltip: Emit the "Map" attribute set describing external resources referenced by written properties. The pin is declared either way (merely demoted to advanced when off), and only Collection Entry properties contribute rows today -- an enabled pin with no such property comes out empty.
bOutputMap.semantics: What lands on the pin is the ordinary Collection Map shape, one row of index and asset path per collection the property picks point at, deduped against itself.
bOutputMap.trap: A graph already carrying a wire off this pin goes quiet the moment the toggle is turned off, with nothing reported.

SampledPropertyOutputs.tooltip: Sampleable properties (e.g. Float Curve) evaluated at a per-point time and written as double point attributes. Independent from Properties Mapping -- a property can be sampled even when it doesn't support raw value output, and the same property can be sampled at several different times (one config each).
SampledPropertyOutputs.semantics: Every entry here writes a double, whatever the property's own type, and the time is read per point, defaulting to the point's density. Points whose entry does not resolve the property, or resolves it to something that cannot be sampled, keep 0; when no staged collection declares the name as a sampleable type at all, the whole output is dropped with a warning.
SampledPropertyOutputs.trap: Two entries whose output attribute names resolve to the same string collide, which is what sampling one property twice without naming both outputs does: the first is kept and the rest are skipped with a warning.

EntryTagsAttributeName.tooltip: Output attribute name for the joined entry tags.

EntryTagsSeparator.tooltip: Separator inserted between tags when joining.

OutputAxes.tooltip: Which subdivision axes to emit per row. Bits are intersected with each entry's own Axes bitmask at write time, so axes the entry doesn't enable produce no output for that row. When exactly one axis ends up being emitted across all rows, the _X/_Y/_Z suffix is dropped from per-axis attribute names (Size, Scalable) for the legacy single-axis shape -- unless bAlwaysSuffixAxes is set.
OutputAxes.semantics: The axes actually emitted are the union of what the entries enable, intersected with this mask, and that union is computed per input dataset. It decides the attribute names too, so one node can write `Size` for one dataset and `Size_X` plus `Size_Y` for the next; Always Suffix Axes is what makes the names stable across both.
OutputAxes.trap: Symbol and Debug Color carry no axis, yet the axis gate decides them too. An entry whose grammar enables no axis, a pick that landed on a sub-collection entry set to Flatten, or nothing ticked here, and those points come out with Symbol and Debug Color at their defaults, while Size and Scalable get no attribute at all.

bAlwaysSuffixAxes.tooltip: Always append _X/_Y/_Z to per-axis attribute names, even when only one axis is emitted. Use this when downstream graphs expect suffixed names regardless of axis count.

hints.text: A point that resolved nothing and a point that resolved a value equal to the default read identically downstream, because both carry the default. When zero or an empty name is a legitimate value for a property, gate the consumer on the pick hash rather than on the value.

A Collection Entry property whose stored entry no longer exists in the collection it points at writes 0. Downstream that reads as a point never staged on that layer, and nothing on this node says otherwise.

UPCGExStagingSpawnActorsSettings.name: Staging : Spawn Actors
UPCGExStagingSpawnActorsSettings.purpose: Puts real actors in the level from staged picks. Every point whose pick resolved to an Actor Collection entry spawns that entry's actor class at the point's transform; points that resolved to anything else are passed over, so one mixed staged dataset can feed this node and the other spawn routes in parallel. The spawned actors are registered as PCG-managed content, so the graph owns their cleanup, and every point comes back carrying a reference to the actor it produced. Entry tags, per-point tags, captured property deltas and generation on the spawned actors' PCG components are all applied here rather than by a follow-up pass.
UPCGExStagingSpawnActorsSettings.situation: An Actor Collection has been staged over a point layout, and those actors now have to exist in the level as content the graph creates and cleans up.

mechanism.text: Each point's pick is resolved against the Collection Map, and every point that landed on an Actor Collection entry spawns that entry's actor class at the point's transform, scale included. Point count and order are preserved, and each point leaves carrying the path of the actor it produced, empty where it produced none. Every spawned actor is parented to a resolved root actor, created in that actor's level, and registered on the PCG component as a managed resource, so the next generation destroys and replaces it like any other generated content. A re-run whose inputs and settings hash to the same value as the previous one keeps the actors already spawned and spawns nothing new. Nothing here fits or offsets anything: the transform the point arrives with is the transform the actor gets.

off_label.claim: Trigger PCG Generation holds this node open until the generations it started report complete, so an Actor Collection of thin actors carrying nothing but a PCG component turns the node into a per-point graph launcher whose results are finished before anything downstream of it runs.
off_label.grounded_in: FGenerationWatcher::Initialize taking a task manager token on the first watched component and releasing it only once all watched components report complete, plus the bHasPCGComponent gate on the watch call in FProcessor::SpawnAtPoint

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The staged points. A dataset carrying no pick hash for the chosen staging layer spawns nothing.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. The node errors out when the Map yields no valid mapping.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Restricts which points spawn. Rejected points stay in the output with an empty actor reference.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, in the same order, with the actor reference attribute written.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer this node reads staged picks from. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

RootActor.tooltip: Optional root actor that owns the spawned actors. Resolves per-point (constant, data-domain attribute, or per-point attribute). When the resolved soft path is null, falls back to the PCG component's target actor. Resolution is by ResolveObject only -- paths must point to live actors.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

RootActor.semantics: Resolved per point, so one dataset can hand different parts of a layout to different root actors. The spawned actor is created in the root actor's own level, which keeps children of a root actor that lives in a sublevel inside that sublevel instead of the persistent one.
RootActor.trap: A path that does not resolve to a live actor, one pointing into a level that is not loaded among them, is not treated as an error. The node falls back to the PCG component's target actor and spawns there.

AttachOptions.tooltip: Controls where spawned actors appear in the Outliner and how they are parented to the root actor. Mirrors UE PCG SpawnActor's AttachOptions semantics.

CollisionHandling.tooltip: How to handle collisions when spawning actors.
CollisionHandling.semantics: A mode that can refuse a spawn refuses it quietly as far as the graph is concerned: the point survives in the output, produces no actor, and keeps an empty actor reference, with only the invalid-entry warning to say what happened.

bApplyPropertyDeltas.tooltip: If enabled, apply per-instance property deltas stored on actor collection entries. Actors with deltas are spawned deferred to set properties before construction completes.
bApplyPropertyDeltas.semantics: The delta lands on the actor after the spawn has finished building it, which is what lets it reach components declared in the Blueprint's Components panel and what makes a post-apply component fixup possible. The actor's own construction script therefore ran against class defaults, so a Blueprint that builds content out of a component it also captured, a spline it walks for instance, builds that content from the class version of the component rather than the captured one.
bApplyPropertyDeltas.trap: Construction scripts run before the delta lands, against class defaults. A Blueprint that generates content in construction from a component the capture also configured builds from the class version of that component, and only the component itself ends up carrying the captured values.

bApplyEntryTags.tooltip: If enabled, apply collection entry tags to spawned actors.
bApplyEntryTags.semantics: Entry tags and per-instance tags both land in the spawned actor's own Tags list and are added without duplicates, so a tag carried by both the entry and the point appears once. Vanilla PCG's generated-actor tag is added on top of them whatever these settings are set to.

TargetsForwarding.tooltip: Attribute forwarding from input points to output points.

fields.name: FilterMode
fields.tooltip: How the names are processed.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Is forwarding enabled.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

TargetsForwarding.semantics: The output points are the input points duplicated, so every attribute that arrived on them is already on the way out. Nothing on the spawn path consumes the forwarding handler this setting builds.

InstanceTagsAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name that contains the per-instance tags string (comma-separated).
InstanceTagsAttributeName.semantics: Read as a String attribute, split on commas, with surrounding whitespace trimmed and blank pieces dropped. A dataset with no attribute of that name gets no per-instance tags and no warning.

bTriggerPCGGeneration.tooltip: If enabled, trigger PCG generation on spawned actors that have PCG components.
bTriggerPCGGeneration.semantics: Only entries whose actor class carries a PCG component on its class defaults are inspected, and that is a flag baked into the entry at staging rebuild rather than read off the spawned actor, so a PCG component added to the class after the last rebuild stays invisible until the collection is rebuilt. The node's execution stays open until every generation it triggered reports complete, so the spawned graphs finish inside this node's run.

GenerateOnLoadAction.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateOnLoad'.

GenerateOnDemandAction.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateOnDemand'.

GenerateAtRuntimeAction.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateAtRuntime'.

ActorReferenceAttribute.tooltip: Name of the attribute to write the spawned actor reference to.
ActorReferenceAttribute.semantics: Written as a soft object path, and left empty on every point that spawned nothing, so the attribute doubles as the record of which points produced an actor and which were passed over.

bQuietInvalidEntryWarnings.tooltip: Suppress warnings for invalid collection entries.
bQuietInvalidEntryWarnings.semantics: One toggle covers four unrelated failures: a pick that resolved to an entry of another type, an actor class that failed to load, a point with no target actor to spawn under, and a spawn the collision handling refused. It is on by default, so a graph quietly producing fewer actors than it has points is diagnosed by turning it off first.

hints.text: At runtime, in PIE, and while the PCG component is in preview mode, the spawned actors are marked transient and never reach the level package. An ordinary editor generation does the opposite: the actors are written into the target actor's level and dirty it.

UPCGExStagingSwapSettings.name: Staging : Swap
UPCGExStagingSwapSettings.purpose: Rewrites picks that a staging node already made, so one layout can spawn several sets of assets. A Variant Collection declares what each source entry resolves to instead, and this node applies that declaration to staged points and emits a Collection Map that includes the variants. Nothing upstream re-runs and no point moves, so two themes of the same dataset are identical down to the transform. Points whose entry has no override keep the pick they arrived with.
UPCGExStagingSwapSettings.situation: One staged layout has to ship as several themes, and every theme must land on the same points in the same places.

mechanism.text: Each variant collection named in the settings is resolved against its own source collections when the graph runs, which yields a mapping from source entry to replacement entry. A staged point is looked up by the collection and entry parts of its pick, the secondary part being ignored, and a hit rewrites those two parts to the variant's collection and its replacement entry. Point count, order and transforms are untouched, and the only attribute written is the staging layer's pick hash. The Map leaving the node is a superset of the one that entered: every original collection plus every variant that contributed at least one mapping.

off_label.claim: With Output Staging Layer set, the node runs even when nothing swaps: every point copies its source pick into the target layer, which makes it a way to duplicate a staging layer under a second name and keep the pre-swap picks readable alongside the swapped ones.
off_label.grounded_in: the bCrossLayer branch in FProcessor::ProcessPoints, which writes every index before the filter and mapping tests, and the `if (!bHasMapping && !bCrossLayer) return true` early-out in FProcessor::Process

off_label.claim: The rewrite never inspects what kind of entry it is writing, so a variant can retarget a whole library of placeholder entries onto real assets of any type, which is what lets layout authoring and asset authoring proceed on separate schedules.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExVariantEntryOverride carries any concrete entry type as its payload, and the swap path only packs the variant GUID and raw index into the hash; nothing on it reads the entry's collection type

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Staged points whose picks are rewritten. Points carrying no pick are skipped.

inputs.label: Map
inputs.note: The Collection Map the incoming picks resolve against, from a staging node or merged from several. Accepts multiple connections.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Restricts which points are considered for swapping. Rejected points keep their pick.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, in the same order, with the staging layer's pick hash rewritten wherever a variant covered it.

outputs.label: Map
outputs.note: The incoming Map plus every variant collection that contributed at least one mapping.

VariantCollections.tooltip: Variant collections to apply -- each slot is a constant path, a `@Data` attribute read once per input data, or a per-point attribute resolving a different variant for every point. The attribute's domain is auto-detected; the node reads a per-point variant only when the attribute actually lives on the point (Elements) domain. Each variant's source groups are matched against the collections present in the input Collection Map; groups whose source isn't in the map are ignored. Later slots win on conflicting mappings (evaluated per point).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

VariantCollections.semantics: Mappings are derived from each variant's sources when the graph runs, so an edit to a source collection's entries shows up on the next run without re-saving the variant. A slot that resolves to nothing, or to a variant whose sources are absent from the incoming Map, is inert rather than an error. When no slot contributes any mapping at all, the points and the Map are forwarded unchanged and the node warns. Slots are walked in order and the last mapping covering a point wins.
VariantCollections.trap: Override rows bind to source entries by a stable id the source assigns during a staging rebuild. A source collection that has not been rebuilt since ids landed carries none, so its whole group resolves no swaps and the node warns; rebuilding and saving the source is the whole fix, since the variant stores no resolved state of its own. A single row pointing at an id the source no longer has is skipped on its own with its own warning.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer whose picks are swapped. None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).

OutputStagingLayer.tooltip: Staging layer swapped picks are written to. None = default layer.
