The collision that survives that check is between resolved names: a Collection Entry column resolves to a derived staging-layer attribute, so a plain column spelled the same way as that derived name collides with it, and whichever the Composition resolves second is skipped with an error of its own.

Values.tooltip: Tuple values. Toggle 'Enabled' per column to include/exclude values. Rows auto-sync with composition changes.

fields.name: Overrides
fields.tooltip: Overrides array - parallel with schema (same size, same order)

Values.semantics: The row count is the entry count of the emitted set, and a row becomes an entry whether or not it enables anything. A disabled cell writes nothing at all, leaving that entry on the column's default from the Composition, so authoring a table means enabling only the cells that deviate from it.
Values.trap: A Collection Entry column breaks that fallback: its attribute defaults to no pick, never to the pick authored on the column, so every row that should carry the pick has to enable the cell.

CommaSeparatedTags.tooltip: A list of tags separated by a comma, for easy overrides.
CommaSeparatedTags.semantics: The tags land on the emitted data itself, not on any of its attributes, so downstream nodes that select by tag see them and no attribute is created for them.

bOutputMap.tooltip: Emit the "Map" attribute set describing external resources referenced by written values (e.g. Collection Entry picks).
bOutputMap.semantics: A Collection Entry column writes its pick under the staging-layer name PCGEx/CollectionEntry followed by the column name, and the pick is meaningless on its own: this is the toggle that emits the Map it resolves against. The Map gathers the collections of every enabled Collection Entry cell, so a table holding no picks emits nothing on the pin however the toggle is set.
bOutputMap.trap: The column name is the staging layer, so a consumer left on the default layer will not see the pick at all; its Staging Layer has to be set to the column name.

hints.text: A Composition with no columns still emits one empty entry per row, and a Values list with no rows emits the attributes with no entries at all. Neither is reported, so a half-configured node reads downstream as data that arrived empty.

A Collection Entry cell whose collection is missing, or whose entry has since been deleted from it, writes a pick of zero, which every downstream consumer reads as no pick. Nothing is reported: the attribute is written either way, and the emitted set looks the same as one carrying valid picks.

UPCGExUberBranchSettings.name: Uber Branch
UPCGExUberBranchSettings.purpose: Sorts whole datasets down numbered pins by asking a stack of filters about each one. Every branch owns a filter pin and an output pin; a dataset takes the first branch that accepts it, and anything nobody claimed leaves on Default. The verdict is per dataset, never per point, so this is the node for deciding where a collection goes rather than which of its points survive.
UPCGExUberBranchSettings.situation: One pin carrying a mixed pile of datasets that each need a different treatment downstream, with the choice expressed as filter rules rather than as tags.

mechanism.text: Num Branches decides how many filter inputs and numbered outputs the node carries, labelled with an arrow pointing in and out. Each input dataset is tested against branch 0, then 1, and so on, and the first branch whose filters pass claims it; the dataset is re-pinned to that branch's output and no later branch sees it. Nothing is copied or merged, so the same datasets come out the far side with the same points and tags. Numbered outputs that claimed nothing are deactivated, which culls the nodes hanging off them.

off_label.claim: Leave every filter pin empty and the node becomes a pass-through that routes everything to Default while still deactivating all the numbered pins, which is a cheap way to disable a whole fan of downstream branches from one place.
off_label.grounded_in: a branch whose filter manager failed to build is skipped in the routing loop, and the per-branch dispatch counters stay at zero, so every numbered pin enters the inactive bitmask

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The datasets to route. Forwarded, never duplicated.

inputs.label: Arrow-in 0, 1, 2 and so on
inputs.note: One filter pin per branch, in order. Filters here are asked about a whole dataset, so they have to be Data Filters or point filters set up to read data bounds or @Data attributes.

outputs.label: Default
outputs.note: Datasets no branch claimed. This pin is never deactivated, so a node wired to it still runs even when nothing lands here.

outputs.label: 0 arrow-out, 1 arrow-out and so on
outputs.note: One per branch. A branch that claimed nothing this run has its pin deactivated, culling whatever hangs off it.

pins.dynamic: The input and output pin sets are rebuilt from Num Branches, and the data pins accept and mirror any type.

NumBranches.tooltip: Number of branch filter groups to evaluate.
NumBranches.semantics: Adds or removes a matching filter input and numbered output. The two label arrays behind the pins are rebuilt only when the value is changed in the details panel.
NumBranches.trap: Overriding this at execution time changes nothing about the pins, which were fixed when the graph compiled, and a value above the number the panel last built has no label to read.

AsyncChunkSize.tooltip: Number of collections to check for in parallel. Use 0 to force execution in a single go. Can be beneficial if filters are simple enough.
AsyncChunkSize.semantics: How many datasets one worker takes at a time. Zero runs the whole routing pass inline instead, which is the faster shape when the filters are cheap and there are only a handful of datasets.

hints.text: A branch whose filters cannot bind, a misspelled attribute being the usual cause, is skipped rather than failed: it silently claims nothing, and its datasets fall through to the next branch or to Default.
Branch order is precedence. Put the narrow rules first, because a broad branch placed above a narrow one takes everything the narrow one was meant to catch.

UPCGExUberFilterCascadeSettings.name: Uber Filter (Cascade)
UPCGExUberFilterCascadeSettings.purpose: Sorts elements into buckets by which condition they satisfy first. Each branch carries its own filter pin and its own output pin, and an element is offered to branch 0, then branch 1, and on down the list until one claims it; once claimed it is gone, and the branches below never see it. That ordering is what the node is for: overlapping conditions stop competing, because the branch nearer the top wins. Elements no branch claimed leave on **Outside**, or, under Write result, every element stays on one output with its branch number recorded as an attribute.
UPCGExUberFilterCascadeSettings.situation: Several conditions overlap and each element should be handled by exactly one of them.

mechanism.text: `Num Branches` decides how many filter pins the node shows, three to begin with, and under Partition points each of them is paired with an output pin. Every element is tried against the branches in pin order and stops at the first one whose filters it satisfies. A branch with nothing on its filter pin is passed over instead of counting as a match, so an unwired branch claims nothing and the element carries on down. Input order survives on every output, and no element reaches more than one of them.

off_label.claim: Because a branch only ever sees what the branches above it rejected, a set of banded conditions can be written as plain thresholds: order the branches from the highest threshold down and none of them needs an upper bound.
off_label.grounded_in: The per-element branch loop in FProcessor::ProcessPoints breaks at the first branch manager that returns true, so later branches are only reached by elements earlier ones declined.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The elements to sort. Point data and attribute sets both work; other data on this pin is skipped with a warning.

inputs.label: One filter pin per branch
inputs.note: Labelled with an arrow and the branch number, from 0 upwards. Each is optional, and an unwired one claims nothing.

outputs.label: Outside
outputs.note: Elements no branch claimed. It is the first output pin and the node's main output, so a disabled node forwards its input here.
outputs.condition: Partition points

outputs.label: One pin per branch
outputs.note: Labelled with the branch number and an arrow, carrying the elements that branch claimed. A branch that claimed nothing has its pin deactivated, and the work behind it is skipped.
outputs.condition: Partition points

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: Every element, in order and untouched, carrying the branch attribute.
outputs.condition: Write result

pins.dynamic: Both pin sets are computed. `Num Branches` sets how many filter pins and how many branch outputs there are, and `Mode` decides whether the outputs are that per-branch set or a single **Out**. The data pins accept any type and hand back what they were given.

NumBranches.tooltip: Number of filter groups (branches) to evaluate. Not overridable: branch pins are built at edit time, so a runtime override cannot change them.

Mode.tooltip: How results are output. Partition splits points into per-branch pins; Write records the matched branch index onto a single output.
Mode.semantics: Under Partition points an output pin with nothing on it is deactivated, so the work behind it is skipped, and **Outside** doubles as the node's main output. Write result replaces the whole set with one **Out** that carries every element and is never deactivated, so the branch behind it always runs.

PartitionAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the int32 attribute the matched branch index is written to.
PartitionAttributeName.semantics: The attribute is built from scratch on every run, so an attribute of this name already on the data is replaced instead of being built on.

DefaultValue.tooltip: Base value written to the attribute. Unmatched points receive this value; a point matching branch i receives DefaultValue + i + 1.
DefaultValue.semantics: The offset is what keeps unmatched elements apart from branch 0, which would otherwise both read as zero. Set it to -1 and the attribute reads as the branch index itself, with -1 for the elements nothing claimed.

bOutputDiscardedElements.tooltip: If enabled, will output unmatched points to the Outside pin, otherwise omit creating the data entirely.
bOutputDiscardedElements.semantics: The **Outside** pin stays on the node when this is off. It is deactivated instead of removed, so a wire already on it survives and carries nothing.

hints.text: An unwired branch claims nothing, and so does a branch whose filters all failed to bind. Elsewhere an empty filter stack passes everything; a cascade branch has to hold a working filter before it can claim an element, so a misspelled attribute name drops that branch's elements through to the branch below rather than letting it swallow the lot.

A spatial filter run over an attribute set reads the world origin. Attribute-set rows carry no positions, so each one reaches the filter stack as a default point at 0,0,0 with default bounds. Attribute-reading filters are unaffected; **Filter : Distance**, the Inclusion filters and **Filter : Raycast** still run, and answer for a stack of coincident points. Nothing is logged, and the uniform verdict reads as the filter having no effect.

UPCGExUberFilterCollectionsSettings.name: Uber Filter (Data)
UPCGExUberFilterCollectionsSettings.purpose: Keeps or drops whole datasets. Everything arriving on **In** leaves untouched on **Inside** or **Outside**: the elements are never split, only the datasets holding them. What makes a dataset pass is `Mode`: every element passes, at least one does, or a share of them measured as a count or a ratio. Feed it a stack made only of filters that can judge a dataset as a whole and it skips the element pass entirely, testing each dataset once against its tags, its `@Data` attributes or its bounds.
UPCGExUberFilterCollectionsSettings.situation: Several datasets arrive on one pin and only the ones meeting a condition should carry on.

mechanism.text: One execution routes whole datasets and never rebuilds one: what arrives on **In** is what leaves, on **Inside** or on **Outside**, with its elements, tags and attributes as they were. How the verdict is reached depends on what is wired to **Filters**. If every filter there can judge a dataset as a whole, each dataset is tested once and that answer is the verdict outright. If any of them needs to look at elements, the node instead tests every element, counts the passes, and hands the count to `Mode`. `Swap` exchanges the two output pins, so the datasets that passed leave on **Outside**.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The datasets to route. They are forwarded as they arrived, whatever type they are.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: The stack that judges each dataset. An empty pin is a missing-input error here, not an absent condition: the node produces nothing at all.

inputs.label: Pickers
inputs.note: Narrows the count to a selection of elements, so All means every picked element. It decides nothing when the whole stack is data-level, because that path tests no elements.

outputs.label: Inside
outputs.note: Datasets that passed. With nothing landing here the pin is deactivated, and the branch behind it is skipped.

outputs.label: Outside
outputs.note: Datasets that failed, deactivated the same way when empty. This pin is always on the node; there is no setting that removes it.

pins.dynamic: Both output pins accept any type and carry back what came in, so a dataset leaves as the kind of data it arrived as.

Mode.tooltip: How many points must pass the filters for a collection to pass: all of them, any of them, or a Partial threshold.
Mode.semantics: `Mode` reads a count of elements that passed, so it only decides anything while at least one filter on **Filters** needs to look at elements. With a stack that is entirely data-level the dataset is judged in a single test and All, Any and Partial give the same answer. Connecting the **Pickers** pin narrows the count to the selection, so All then means every picked element.
Mode.trap: One per-element filter beside a data-level one puts the node on the counting path, and the data-level filter still has a say there: it answers the same for every element of the dataset, so a dataset it rejects reaches `Mode` with a count of zero.

Measure.tooltip: How the Partial threshold is measured: Relative compares the ratio of passing points (0..1), Discrete compares their count.

Comparison.tooltip: Comparison between the measured passing ratio/count and the threshold.

DblThreshold.tooltip: Ratio of passing points (0..1) a collection is compared against.
DblThreshold.semantics: The share is taken over the elements the node counted, so with the **Pickers** pin connected it is a share of the selection rather than of the whole dataset.

IntThreshold.tooltip: Number of passing points a collection is compared against.
IntThreshold.semantics: The count is over the elements the node counted, so with the **Pickers** pin connected a dataset is judged on how many of its picked elements passed, never on how many it holds.
IntThreshold.trap: Under a greater or equal-or-greater comparison, a dataset with fewer elements than this number can never reach it and always leaves on **Outside**. With **Pickers** connected the same holds against the size of the selection, which can be far smaller than the dataset.

Tolerance.tooltip: Tolerance for nearly equal/not equal comparisons; only applies to the Relative (ratio) measure.
Tolerance.semantics: The default macro is 0.01, which on a ratio is one element in a hundred.
Tolerance.trap: Its edit condition reads `Comparison` alone, and `Comparison` keeps its stored value while it is hidden. Leaving it on a nearly-equal operator and then switching `Mode` to All or Any keeps this row on the panel with nothing to do.

bSwap.semantics: The pin labels stay where they are. With this on, the pin labelled **Inside** carries the datasets that failed and **Outside** carries the ones that passed.

hints.text: Every filter on the pin failing to bind, under the default `Initialization Failure Policy` of Error, leaves an empty stack, and an empty stack passes. Every dataset then leaves on **Inside** and the node reads as a pass-through. A misspelled attribute name on the only filter is enough to produce it.

An attribute set arriving on **In** is converted to points before any filter sees it, and those points have no positions: every row lands at 0,0,0 with default bounds. Attribute-reading filters are unaffected. A spatial filter on the counting path, and **Data Filter : Bounds** on the dataset path, both answer for a stack of coincident points at the origin. The datasets themselves are forwarded untouched, so what goes wrong is the routing.

UPCGExUberFilterSettings.name: Uber Filter
UPCGExUberFilterSettings.purpose: Turns a filter stack's verdicts into data. Partition points sends the elements that passed to **Inside** and the rest to **Outside**, two streams the graph wires on separately. Write result leaves the data as it arrived and records each verdict as an attribute, so element counts, ordering and anything downstream pairing against them survive. Either mode takes an attribute set on **In** as readily as points, splitting or annotating its rows.
UPCGExUberFilterSettings.situation: A condition decides where elements go next, and both the passes and the failures have work waiting for them.

mechanism.text: One execution handles every dataset on **In** separately, so three datasets in give up to three on each output. Within a dataset each element is tested once against the filter stack, and `Mode` decides what becomes of the verdict: a split across two pins, or an attribute written onto the data as it stands. Input order survives into every output and the elements themselves are untouched.
steps: Every element is tested against the stack, unless the **Pickers** pin excludes it.
Excluded elements take the `Unpicked Fallback` verdict without being tested.
`Swap` flips every verdict, the substituted ones included.
`Mode` disposes of the result: **Inside** and **Outside** under Partition points, an attribute under Write result.

off_label.claim: Set `Mode` to Write result and ignore the result attribute: the three tagging options then turn a per-element condition into a tag on the whole dataset, which a tag filter or **Uber Filter (Data)** can route on.
off_label.grounded_in: The Write branch of FProcessor::OnPointsProcessingComplete decides the three tags from the pass count against the element count, independently of what the result block wrote.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The data to test. Point data and attribute sets both work; other data on this pin is skipped with a warning.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: The filter stack. An empty pin is a missing-input error here, not an absent condition: the node produces nothing at all.

inputs.label: Pickers
inputs.note: Narrows the test to a selection of elements. Everything outside the selection takes the `Unpicked Fallback` verdict without being tested.

outputs.label: Inside
outputs.note: Elements that passed. With nothing landing here the pin is deactivated, and the branch behind it is skipped.
outputs.condition: Partition points

outputs.label: Outside
outputs.note: Elements that failed, deactivated the same way when empty.
outputs.condition: Partition points, and only while Output Discarded Elements is on

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The input data with its elements intact, carrying the result attribute.
outputs.condition: Write result

pins.dynamic: The output pin set belongs to `Mode`: Partition points shows **Inside** and **Outside**, Write result collapses both into a single **Out**. The data pins accept any type and hand back what they were given, so an attribute set in means attribute sets out.

Mode.tooltip: Write result to point instead of split outputs
Mode.semantics: The mode decides the pin set as well as the disposal. Partition points builds two datasets per input and lets an empty side deactivate its pin, so a branch with nothing to do is skipped. Write result keeps one dataset per input and never deactivates its output, so the branch behind **Out** always runs. `Result` exists only under Write result; the **Outside** pin and its toggle exist only under Partition points.
Mode.trap: Under Partition points the node's main output is **Inside**, so disabling the node forwards the whole input there and the **Outside** branch goes quiet.

ResultDetails.semantics: The same block appears on **Cluster : Filter Vtx** and **Cluster : Refine**, and is documented once on [filter-result-details.md](common-settings/filter-result-details.md). The part that decides how this node behaves across runs is `Action`: Boolean builds the attribute fresh and ends up holding this run's verdict alone, while Counter and Bitmask read whatever is already stored under that name and build on it. Two nodes aimed at one attribute name therefore overwrite under Boolean and accumulate under the other two.

bSwap.semantics: The flip happens after the **Pickers** pin has substituted `Unpicked Fallback` for the elements it excluded, so those are flipped along with the rest. Under Write result there are no pins to exchange, so what changes is the value the result attribute records.
bSwap.trap: Leave `Unpicked Fallback` at Fail and turn this on, and every element the pickers excluded arrives on **Inside** untested.

bOutputDiscardedElements.tooltip: If enabled, will output discarded elements, otherwise omit creating the data entirely.
bOutputDiscardedElements.semantics: Turning this off takes the **Outside** pin off the node, so a wire already on it is dropped. It stays visible under Write result, where it decides nothing: that mode discards no elements.

HasAnyPointPassedTag.tooltip: Tag to add when at least one point passes.
HasAnyPointPassedTag.semantics: The pass count is per dataset, so several datasets on **In** are each tagged on their own terms. Under Partition points the tag lands on the **Inside** data, where the elements it describes are; under Write result it lands on the single output.

AllPointsPassedTag.tooltip: Tag to add when all points pass.
AllPointsPassedTag.semantics: Placed like the any-passed tag: **Inside** under Partition points, the single output under Write result. It is measured against the dataset's own element count, so a dataset where everything passes carries this tag and the any-passed one together.

NoPointPassedTag.tooltip: Tag to add when no points pass.
NoPointPassedTag.semantics: The one tag that lands on **Outside** under Partition points, since that is where the elements ended up.
NoPointPassedTag.trap: It needs somewhere to land: with `Output Discarded Elements` off and nothing passing, no data is produced under Partition points and the tag goes nowhere.

UnpickedFallback.tooltip: How should point that aren't picked be considered?
UnpickedFallback.semantics: Live only while the **Pickers** pin carries something. With that pin empty every element is tested and this setting decides nothing. Connected, the selection is the only thing tested and everything else takes this verdict wholesale, so at the default of Fail a picker naming ten elements out of a thousand sends the other nine hundred and ninety to **Outside** without a filter ever running on them.

hints.text: A filter left on the default `Initialization Failure Policy` of Error is dropped from the stack when it cannot bind, a misspelled attribute being the usual cause. If it was the only filter on the pin, the stack is now empty, and an empty stack passes: every element arrives on **Inside** and the node reads as having done nothing. The **Filters** pin being required guards against an empty pin, not against a stack that empties itself.

**A spatial filter on an attribute set reads the world origin.** An attribute set has no positions, so each row reaches the filter stack as a default point at the world origin with default bounds. Attribute-reading filters are unaffected, but a spatial filter (Distance, the Inclusion family, Raycast) still runs and answers for a stack of coincident points at 0,0,0. Nothing is logged, and the uniform verdict reads as the filter having no effect.

UPCGExUberNoiseSettings.name: Uber Noise
UPCGExUberNoiseSettings.purpose: Turns a stack of Noise : sub-nodes into an attribute. Each point is sampled at its own position and the result is either written over the target or blended into what the target already holds. The target is an attribute or a point property, written the same way either way, which is why the shipped default aims at $Density rather than at a name of its own.
UPCGExUberNoiseSettings.situation: Points that already exist need a spatial value, whether that is a fresh mask attribute or a nudge applied to something they already carry.

mechanism.text: One dataset in, the same dataset out, same point count and same order. Every point is sampled at its own transform location, so nothing depends on where a point sits in the array and two points in the same place get the same value. The target decides the arity: a one-field target asks the stack for a scalar, a two, three or four-field target asks for that many components, and a target counting any other number of fields fails the node. Points rejected on the Filters pin are skipped entirely, so nothing at all is written for them.

off_label.claim: Point the target at a vanilla point property with a dollar prefix and the node drives that property directly, so a three-field property takes three noise components without an attribute ever existing.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExAttributeSourceToTargetDetails::GetTargetSelector feeding FProxyDescriptor::Capture, validated through ValidateNamesOrProperties

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to sample the field at.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Points that fail are skipped and nothing is written for them.

inputs.label: Noises
inputs.note: The Noise : sub-nodes making up the field.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, with the target written.

Mode.semantics: New Attribute ignores what the target held and writes the field over it. Mutate Attribute reads the target first, and what it reads is also what decides how many noise components get asked for, so the same graph hands back a scalar or a vector depending only on the attribute it was pointed at.

OutputType.semantics: Consulted only when the target does not already exist on the output. Aim New Attribute mode at something already there, a point property included, and that type wins while this setting does nothing.
OutputType.trap: Only the field count of the chosen type reaches the noise: Double and Integer both ask for a scalar, Vector and Rotator for three components, Vector4 and Quaternion for four. Transform counts nine and fails the node with a message about the noise type.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Attribute to read on input

fields.name: Target
fields.tooltip: Attribute to write on output, if different from input

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SourceValueWeight.semantics: This is the blend weight, and most blend modes never read it. Weight, Weight (Always Normalize), Weighted Add, Weighted Subtract and Lerp are the ones that do, and the shipped Add is not among them.
SourceValueWeight.trap: Under Lerp the weight runs toward the noise, not toward the source its name suggests, so the default of 1 replaces the source entirely.

hints.text: The Noises pin is required. With nothing on it the node fails during setup and produces no output at all, rather than passing its points through untouched.

UPCGExUnpackClustersSettings.name: Cluster : Unpack
UPCGExUnpackClustersSettings.purpose: Splits a packed cluster back into a Vtx dataset and an Edges dataset and pairs them again. It is the other half of **Cluster : Pack** and reads nothing but what Pack wrote: the seam comes from the edge count recorded on the dataset, so it only unpacks data that was packed.
UPCGExUnpackClustersSettings.situation: A cluster is being read back out of a PCG Data Asset and has to become two pins again.

mechanism.text: Each dataset on **Packed Clusters** is cut at the recorded edge count: the points before the seam become the Edges half, the points after it become the Vtx half, and both come out tagged as one pair. Each half then loses the other's cluster attribute, so the Vtx dataset keeps the endpoint ids and the Edges dataset keeps the pairs of ids it names. One packed dataset becomes exactly one Vtx dataset and one Edges dataset.

inputs.label: Packed Clusters
inputs.note: Datasets produced by **Cluster : Pack**. A dataset with no recorded edge count is skipped with a warning, and so is one whose recorded count does not fit the points present.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One Vtx dataset per packed dataset, holding the points after the seam.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One Edges dataset per packed dataset, holding the points before the seam.

bFlatten.tooltip: Flatten unpacked metadata  Depending on your setup this is a tradeoff between memory and speed.
bFlatten.semantics: Nothing reads it. The value never reaches the element, so the output is the same either way, whatever the tooltip's tradeoff suggests.

hints.text: What comes back is not the shape that went in. One Vtx dataset paired with four Edges datasets was packed as four datasets and comes back as four separate pairs, each with its own copy of only the vertices it uses, in cluster order rather than their original row order. Both halves come back carrying the tags the Edges dataset had, because that is what the packed dataset was built from; the Vtx dataset's own tags did not travel. An attribute name that was on both halves comes back correct on the Vtx points and at its default on the edge points. The endpoint ids do survive, so the pairing itself is sound.

UPCGExValueHashFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Contains (Hash)
UPCGExValueHashFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Asks whether the value an element carries also appears somewhere in a reference set you supply, for any attribute type at all. The reference sets arrive on the Sets pin as ordinary data, one named attribute is read off each of them, and every distinct value found becomes a lookup key. Hash is how the lookup is built rather than what you configure: values are keyed by a hash of the stored value, which is what makes the test work on strings, names, vectors and asset paths as readily as on numbers, and also what makes it refuse to match across two types holding the same number.
UPCGExValueHashFilterProviderSettings.situation: A list of allowed or forbidden values exists as data somewhere in the graph, and elements have to be kept or dropped by whether their own value is on it.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element. Each dataset on the Sets pin contributes one lookup set, built from every value of a single attribute read on that dataset; Mode then decides whether those sets are pooled into one or kept apart. The element's own value is looked up in whatever survived, and Inclusion decides whether landing in one set is enough or every set has to hold it. Values are keyed by type as well as by number, so an attribute stored as float and one stored as double never match each other however equal they read.

off_label.claim: Wire the same dataset into both a consumer and the Sets pin, with Operand A and Set Attribute Name naming two different attributes, and the filter answers whether each element's value in one attribute appears anywhere in the other. That is a cross-column membership test over a single dataset, which nothing in the family offers directly.
off_label.grounded_in: the Sets pin accepting any data and the set attribute being resolved on the set data independently of Operand A, in UPCGExValueHashFilterFactory::Prepare

inputs.label: Sets
inputs.note: The reference values. Any data type is accepted, attribute sets included, and each dataset contributes one lookup set.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so it is accepted on every filter pin, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

hints.text: Sets that arrive wired but yield no readable values count as missing data exactly as an unwired pin would, and Missing Data Policy then stands a constant filter in place of this one. Under its default of Fail that constant rejects every element and nothing reaches the log to say why; Error is what makes the node report the empty pool instead.

UPCGExVariantCollection.name: Collection | Variant
UPCGExVariantCollection.purpose: A Variant Collection themes other collections: it declares source collections and, per source, rows saying what a source entry resolves to instead. Each row carries a full replacement entry of any concrete type, so a mesh entry can be replaced by an actor entry and the pick keeps resolving. Asset Swaps do the same job in bulk, one rule retargeting every source entry that stages a given asset, across every declared source at once. Nothing spawns from a variant on its own: Staging : Swap rewrites staged picks to the replacement entries, and spawning, fitting and property loading then work off the replacement.
UPCGExVariantCollection.situation: One distributed layout has to ship in several dressed versions, and every version differs only in which assets the same picks resolve to.

mechanism.text: A Variant Collection is a first-class collection: it carries its own identity, its replacement entries get their own staging data on a rebuild, and consumers resolve them the way they resolve any other collection's entries. What it adds is a correspondence rather than a library of its own. Each row names one entry of one source by that entry's stable id and holds the entry that replaces it; each asset rule names an asset path and covers every source entry staging it. The correspondence is worked out against the live sources every time a consumer runs, so an edit to the variant or to one of its sources lands on the next execution. A row whose source entry no longer exists resolves to nothing and is reported, and the rest of its group keeps working.

off_label.claim: Point Staging : Distribute at a Variant Collection and it picks among the replacement entries alone, weights included, which is one way to see everything a theme can spawn before any swap is wired.
off_label.grounded_in: UPCGExVariantCollection::BuildCache flattens every row and rule payload into the standard entry pool, and the Distribute collection picker accepts any UPCGExAssetCollection subclass

Sources.tooltip: Source collections this variant themes; overrides are grouped per source.

fields.name: SourceCollection
fields.tooltip: The source collection whose picks this group can redirect. Hard ref (SubCollection rationale): loads with the variant, so mappings resolve live.

Sources.semantics: Any collection type is a legal source, another Variant Collection included, which is what lets two swap passes chain one behind the other; only the variant itself is excluded. The reference is hard, so a declared source loads with the variant and travels with it into a cook. Rows bind to source entries by identity, so reordering, renaming or re-weighting entries on a source leaves every swap pointing where it did, while deleting an entry orphans its row, which the grid marks and resolution skips. A group whose Source is empty contributes nothing, and a row left undeclared keeps its place in the group, so a half-authored variant applies the rows that are declared and leaves the rest inert.
Sources.trap: Entry ids live on the source, not on the variant, and they persist only when the source is saved. A source carrying none gets them minted the moment the grid draws it, which dirties that source asset. Discard it without saving and the next session mints different ids, orphaning every swap bound against the old ones.

PathOverrides.tooltip: Asset-path swap rules -- shorthand over the per-entry rows. Resolved by BuildGroupMapping against the declared sources; entries already claimed by an explicit row are untouched (specific beats general). First matching rule wins; duplicate MatchAsset values warn. Rule payloads occupy the tail of the flattened raw-index view, after all source-group rows.

fields.name: MatchAsset
fields.tooltip: Source entries whose staged asset path (Staging.Path) equals this swap to Entry.

fields.name: Entry
fields.tooltip: Replacement entry. Any concrete FPCGExAssetCollectionEntry type. Unset = rule inert.

PathOverrides.semantics: A rule matches on the asset path baked into a source entry's staging data, so one rule retargets every entry staging that asset across every declared source at once. Rules cover only entries no explicit row claimed, and they never match an entry flagged as a sub-collection. Where two rules name the same asset the first one wins and the log says so. A rule naming an asset no declared source stages covers nothing and stays in the grid as a tile, ready the moment a declared source does stage that asset. Rule payloads sit after every source group's rows, so adding a rule never disturbs a group.
PathOverrides.trap: Matching reads the staged path, not the entry's authored asset reference. A source whose staging is stale matches against yesterday's paths, so a rule that suddenly covers nothing is a reason to rebuild the source before rewriting the rule.

hints.text: When every bound row in a group fails to resolve, Staging : Swap reports it on the node and passes those points through unthemed. The source's entry ids either changed or were never saved, so re-save the source; the variant holds nothing of its own that needs re-saving.

A variant authored before sources became hard references migrates its source paths when it loads. Where the old path no longer resolves, the group comes back with an empty Source and stays inert until that asset is available again.

UPCGExVerletRelax.name: Verlet (Gravity)
UPCGExVerletRelax.purpose: The one relaxation with momentum. Each Vtx keeps the movement it made on the previous iteration, gravity is added to it, and the edges then haul the result back toward the lengths they arrived with, which is what makes a cluster hang and sag rather than being nudged into place. `Gravity` and `Friction` are read per Vtx while `Edge Scaling` and `Edge Stiffness` are read per edge, so a run can be heavy at one end and stiff at the other with no filter involved. Edge rest lengths are always the incoming lengths, scaled, so there is no target length to choose the way the fitting rules let you.
UPCGExVerletRelax.situation: A cluster that should behave like something hanging: a rope, a cable run, a net held at a few points and left to fall.

mechanism.text: Three turns per iteration. The first walks the Vtx and moves each one by the movement it made last iteration, damped, plus gravity. The second walks the edges and gathers a correction for every edge whose length has drifted from its rest length. The third walks the Vtx again and adds each one's gathered corrections. The edge turn measures the positions the first turn has just written, so the springs pull against this iteration's gravity rather than the last one's, and the rest lengths are the lengths the edges arrived with, measured once before the first iteration and multiplied by `Edge Scaling`.

off_label.claim: Gravity is read per Vtx and nothing requires it to point down. An attribute holding a direction turns the rule into a drag along that direction, with the edges deciding how far a Vtx can be hauled from its neighbours before they pull it back.
off_label.grounded_in: The gravity turn reads the gravity buffer per Vtx and adds it to the predicted position with no assumption about its direction, and the edge turn corrects whatever that leaves behind

GravityValue.tooltip: Gravity. Think of it as gravity vector.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

GravityValue.semantics: An acceleration rather than a distance: the vector enters multiplied by `Time Step` squared, and it enters again on every iteration on top of the movement already being carried, so how far a free Vtx has fallen grows with the square of the iteration count. It is read per Vtx, so an attribute can send one part of a cluster down while another rises, and a zero on a Vtx leaves that Vtx moving on momentum and edge corrections alone.

FrictionValue.tooltip: Friction. Expected to be in the [0..1] range.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

FrictionValue.semantics: Scales down the movement a Vtx carries into the next iteration, by one minus its value, alongside `Damping Scale`. At 0 a Vtx keeps all of it, which is what lets a hanging cluster swing past the shape it would come to rest in and back again. At 1 or above the Vtx is anchored outright: it takes no gravity, no carried movement and no edge correction, and it stays where it started for the whole run while its edges still pull on everything at their other ends. That makes an attribute reading 1 on a few Vtx the way to hang a cluster from those points.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

EdgeScalingValue.semantics: Multiplies each edge's incoming length to give the length that edge is corrected toward. It is read per edge from the Edges dataset rather than per Vtx, so an attribute fed to it has to live on the edges: below 1 the cluster tightens up, above 1 it slackens and hangs deeper.

EdgeStiffnessValue.tooltip: Edge Stiffness. Expected to be in the [0..1] range.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

EdgeStiffnessValue.semantics: How much of an edge's length error is taken out in one iteration. Read per edge from the Edges dataset, so one part of a cluster can behave like rope and another like cable. The value is multiplied by about a third on its way in and both ends of the edge are corrected, so even at 1 an edge closes roughly two thirds of its error over an iteration instead of snapping to length, and a long chain needs several iterations to carry a correction from one end to the other.

TimeStep.tooltip: If this was a physic simulation, represent the time advance each iteration
TimeStep.semantics: The only thing it multiplies is gravity, and it multiplies it squared, which makes it a gravity scale rather than a rate for the rule as a whole. Doubling it quadruples the distance gravity adds per iteration and leaves the edge corrections and the carried movement untouched.
TimeStep.trap: The tooltip reads as though this set the pace of a simulation. It never reaches the edge turn or the damping, so at a gravity of zero the value does nothing at all.

DampingScale.tooltip: Velocity damping multiplier applied each iteration. Lower values = more damping, smoother convergence. Higher values retain momentum for more natural sag.
DampingScale.semantics: Multiplies the movement carried into the next iteration, on top of `Friction`, and the two multiply rather than one of them winning. At 1 nothing bleeds off and a cluster keeps swinging for as long as the run lasts. At 0 there is no momentum left at all and every iteration starts from rest, which is as close as this rule comes to a plain spring solver.

hints.text: Gravity is added to the movement being carried rather than to the position, so it compounds: how far a Vtx has fallen grows with the square of the iteration count, not in step with it. An iteration count that looks right at 10 is well past it at 20, and the edges are the only thing holding that in check.

UPCGExVolumeFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Inclusion (Volume)
UPCGExVolumeFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Answers whether each element sits inside a volume placed in the level. The volumes arrive on the Volumes pin, and the test runs against each volume actor's own brush, so a shape that is not a box is respected as authored; the node produces a filter on its Filter pin, which any node carrying a filter pin runs once per element. The element reaches the test as a location and a sphere derived from its bounds, and the palette carries the four checks as separate drop-in entries, each suffixed with (Volume). Leaving `Extra Radius` and `Penetration Threshold` on constants also lets this filter serve the consumers that judge whole datasets, which pointing either of them at a per-point attribute withdraws.
UPCGExVolumeFilterProviderSettings.situation: Volumes already block out the level, and whether an element survives depends on which of them it falls in.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this filter once per element, and every volume on the pin is searched as one pool, so the first volume that satisfies the check decides a pass. The element reaches the test as two things: its location, and a sphere radius derived from its own bounds. Inside is settled by the location alone, and the intersection checks are the only ones the radius reaches. Volume data whose actor is no longer in the level is dropped before any of that, and so is anything on the pin that is not volume data. The volumes are gathered and indexed once, on this node, and every consumer wired to its Filter pin shares that work.

off_label.claim: Invert `Is Outside or Intersects` and the filter answers a question none of the four checks state on their own: the element's location is inside some volume and its sphere reaches no other volume's boundary from outside. That reads as well inside one volume and clear of its neighbours, which is a two-volume relationship the other checks cannot express.
off_label.grounded_in: the bFoundInside branch taken after the octree walk in FVolumeFilter::TestPoint, which returns the inverted verdict only when a volume contained the location and no volume was grazed from outside

inputs.label: Volumes
inputs.note: The volumes to test against. Several datasets are accepted and searched as one pool, and only volume data backed by a volume actor still present in the level counts; anything else is passed over in silence.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node produces. It carries the point-filter type, so every filter pin accepts it, Vtx and Edge pins included.

hints.text: An empty Volumes pin routes through Missing Data Policy rather than Initialization Failure Policy, and so does a pin carrying volume data whose actors have left the level: those entries are passed over in silence, and what reaches the policy is an empty result that reads exactly like an empty pin. Nothing is logged unless that policy is set to Error.
The node subtitle reads back the check, with a flag prepended when Invert is on, so a graph carrying several of these can be read without selecting them one at a time.

UPCGExVtxPropertyAmplitudeSettings.name: Vtx : Amplitude
UPCGExVtxPropertyAmplitudeSettings.purpose: Measures how far and how evenly a Vtx's neighbours are spread around it, and writes the answer on the Vtx. Three of its four rows describe the box those neighbours occupy, as its two corners and its size. The fourth is a separate reading that says how much the edges agree with one direction rather than cancelling each other out. Every row is independent, so the node stays as small as the one number you wanted.
UPCGExVtxPropertyAmplitudeSettings.situation: A cluster where the Vtx worth treating differently are the lopsided ones: a junction whose edges all leave the same way, or one whose neighbours sit far off along one axis and close along another.

mechanism.text: Two unrelated readings share one node. The first is a box: every edge contributes the offset from its neighbour to the Vtx, `Min` and `Max` are the componentwise smallest and largest of those offsets, and `Range` is `Max` minus `Min`, which makes it the size of the axis-aligned box the Vtx's neighbours occupy. The second is `Sign`: the average, across the same edges, of how closely each edge agrees with one reference direction. Each of the four rows is off until its checkbox is ticked and each names its own attribute.

off_label.claim: Under Custom Up Vector with the direction read from an attribute, the Sign row stops being about up at all: it is the mean agreement between any per-Vtx vector and that Vtx's edges, so feeding it a flow direction or a surface normal grades every Vtx by how well its connections follow that field.
off_label.grounded_in: The Custom Up Vector branch of FPCGExVtxPropertyAmplitude::ProcessNode reads the direction per Vtx and averages its dot product against each adjacency direction, without treating the vector as vertical anywhere

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: The reading this node defines, for the **Properties** pin on **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeAngleSettings.name: Vtx : Edge Angle
UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeAngleSettings.purpose: Measures how sharply a Vtx turns, from the angles between the edges meeting at it. A Vtx with two edges has one angle and the answer is that angle; a Vtx with more has an angle for every pair, and the aggregation decides which number represents it. Leaves have no pair at all and take a fallback instead.
UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeAngleSettings.situation: Cluster Vtx that should be classified by how sharp a corner they form, for filtering junctions from straights or finding kinks.

mechanism.text: Every pair of edges at a Vtx gives an angle, and `Non Binary Aggregation` folds those into the one value written. `Angle Range` decides the units and whether the result is signed, and the signed and full-turn ranges need a reference direction to say which way round a turn goes, which is what `Up Vector` supplies. A leaf has one edge and therefore no pair, so it receives `Leaves Fallback` unchanged.

outputs.label: Vtx Property
outputs.note: The property definition, read by **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

fields.name: AngleAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write the edge angle to.

fields.name: AngleRange
fields.tooltip: Unit/range to output the angle to.

fields.name: NonBinaryAggregation
fields.tooltip: How to aggregate the pairwise edge angles of complex nodes (more than two edges).

fields.name: LeavesFallback
fields.tooltip: Value written as-is for leaf nodes (single edge, no pair to measure). Never mapped to the selected range.

fields.name: UpVector
fields.tooltip: Winding reference Up vector. Only affects winding-aware ranges (signed or 0..360 outputs).

UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeMatchSettings.name: Vtx : Edge Match
UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeMatchSettings.purpose: Names the one edge at each Vtx that best lines up with a direction you give it, and writes that edge's direction, length and indices onto the Vtx. The reference can be a constant or a vector attribute read on the Vtx, and out of the box it is read in the Vtx's own frame, so it follows point rotation. `Dot Comparison Details` sets how close counts as lined up, which is what lets a Vtx with nothing close enough come back empty instead of settling for its least-bad edge.
UPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeMatchSettings.situation: A cluster where each Vtx needs to know which of its connections continues a heading: the edge along an authored flow vector, or the one carrying on in the direction the point already faces.

mechanism.text: One reference direction is settled per Vtx, from the constant or from a vector attribute on that Vtx, normalised, then optionally read in the Vtx's own frame. Every edge at the Vtx is compared against it with a dot product, `Dot Comparison Details` decides which of those readings count as a match, and among the edges that pass, the one nearest the reference wins. Which way round each edge is read for that comparison is `Origin`'s decision. When nothing passes, the output block still writes: a zero direction, a zero length, indices of -1 and a count of 0.

off_label.claim: Setting the comparison to reject everything, an operator of greater-than against a Scalar threshold of 1 being the surest way, turns the node into a per-Vtx zero: every Vtx writes the miss values, which gives a clean baseline to blend or compare a real run against.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExVtxPropertyEdgeMatch::ProcessNode keeps the best index at -1 unless some edge passes DotComparisonDetails::Test, and writes the miss values on that branch

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: The reading this node defines, for the **Properties** pin on **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

hints.text: At the shipped settings, a `Direction` of 1, 0, 0 with `Transform Direction` on picks the edge whose neighbour sits ahead of the Vtx along its forward axis. `Flip` on the `Direction` row turns the reference around and picks the edge behind it; `Origin` reaches the same two results from the other side, by changing which way the edges are read instead.

UPCGExVtxPropertyProviderSettings.name: Vtx : Abstract
UPCGExVtxPropertyProviderSettings.purpose: The base every Vtx : node inherits, and the page carrying what the whole family shares: the Property pin they all emit on, what the consumer hands them and when, and the two output blocks most of them are built from. It never appears in the palette. Their consumer is Cluster : Vtx Properties, which is the only node that reads the pin.
UPCGExVtxPropertyProviderSettings.situation: Reading any Vtx : page and needing to know what its Direction and Length rows measure, which way the direction points, or what the index rows are indices into.

mechanism.text: The consumer asks every factory on its Properties pin the same question once per Vtx: here is a Vtx, here are its edges. Each entry in that list carries the neighbour it reaches, the edge joining them, the distance between the two positions, and the direction running from that neighbour toward the Vtx. A sub-node answers from that list alone and writes its answer onto the Vtx dataset, choosing every attribute name itself; nothing any of them writes reaches the Edges. They run in the order they arrive on the pin, so two pointed at the same attribute name and type share it and the later one wins at every Vtx.

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: What every Vtx : node emits. The Properties pin on Cluster : Vtx Properties is the only place it is read.

hints.text:
## The two output blocks

Most of the family writes through one of two shared blocks, and every row in them is off until its checkbox is ticked. The simple block writes `Direction`, a unit vector, and `Length`, the distance to the neighbour. The indexed block adds `EdgeIndex`, `VtxIndex` and `Count`, which is how many edges the named neighbour has. Attribute names default to the block's own prefix, so a block labelled Shortest ships `ShortestDir`, `ShortestLen`, `ShortestEdgeIndex`, `ShortestVtxIndex` and `ShortestNeighborCount`.

The direction the consumer hands out runs from the neighbour toward the Vtx, and the ` └─ Invert` row under each Direction is what turns it around. Only **Vtx : Sorted Neighbor** ships with that box already ticked, so the same row on **Vtx : Special Edges**, **Vtx : Special Neighbors** and **Vtx : Edge Match** writes the inward direction until you tick it yourself.

`EdgeIndex` and `VtxIndex` are row numbers in the two datasets as they leave the consumer: the edge's row in the Edges dataset, and the neighbour's row in the Vtx dataset. They are positions, not the endpoint ids that hold the cluster together, so anything that reorders or removes points downstream leaves them pointing at whatever now sits in that row.

A sub-node that cannot bind what it needs, a misspelled attribute name being the usual cause, says so and takes the whole cluster down with it: that cluster is skipped for the rest of the run, so none of the sub-nodes on the pin measure anything into its Vtx. The Vtx and Edges still come out, and any attribute the stack had already declared is there holding its default.

UPCGExVtxPropertySortedNeighborSettings.name: Vtx : Sorted Neighbor
UPCGExVtxPropertySortedNeighborSettings.purpose: Ranks each Vtx's neighbours by rules you supply, keeps the single extreme, and describes the edge that reaches it. Where **Vtx : Special Edges** ranks on edge length and **Vtx : Special Neighbors** on the neighbour's edge count, this one ranks on whatever the Sorting Rule sub-nodes on its **SortRules** pin name, read either from the neighbour or from the edge between.
UPCGExVtxPropertySortedNeighborSettings.situation: A cluster where the interesting neighbour is settled by data rather than by geometry: the highest scored, the one holding a particular value, the one an upstream pass marked.

mechanism.text: Every neighbour of the Vtx is ranked by the rules on the **SortRules** pin and the single extreme is kept. `Sort Source` decides where each rule reads its value, and `Sort Direction` decides which end of the ranking counts as extreme. The winner fills the indexed block about the edge reaching it, written on the Vtx being evaluated whichever source was ranked. Every field is off until its checkbox is ticked, so an untouched node writes nothing.

off_label.claim: One rule reading a constant-valued attribute ranks nothing, which makes the node a way to capture one arbitrary but stable neighbour per Vtx: ties resolve to the first edge in the Vtx's own edge order, and that order does not move between runs on unchanged data.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExVtxPropertySortedNeighbor::ProcessNode keeps the incumbent unless the sorter strictly prefers the candidate, walking the adjacency list in order

inputs.label: SortRules
inputs.note: Sorting Rule sub-nodes ranking the neighbours. Their own priority values decide which rule breaks which tie.

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: The reading this node defines, for the **Properties** pin on **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

hints.text: When no rule survives, the node logs a warning naming itself and the cluster it was preparing is skipped for the whole run, so every Vtx : sub-node on the pin goes silent for that cluster and not just this one. The two ways to get there are an empty **SortRules** pin and a set of rules that all name attributes the chosen `Sort Source` does not carry.

UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialEdgesSettings.name: Vtx : Special Edges
UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialEdgesSettings.purpose: Ranks each Vtx's edges by length and describes the two extremes on the Vtx: the shortest edge and the longest one. A third row, Average, names no edge and instead reports what the junction looks like as a whole. Its near-sibling **Vtx : Special Neighbors** fills the same output blocks from the same list of edges, ranking them by the neighbour's own edge count instead of by length.
UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialEdgesSettings.situation: A cluster where each Vtx needs to know how far its nearest or furthest connection reaches, or how lopsided the spread of its edge lengths is.

mechanism.text: Every edge at the Vtx is measured by its length, and three rows come out of that: the shortest edge, the longest edge, and an average across all of them. Shortest and Longest each name one edge and fill the indexed block about it, so the edge's row, its neighbour's row and that neighbour's own edge count come with it. Ties keep whichever edge comes first in the Vtx's own edge order. Every field is off until its checkbox is ticked, so an untouched node writes nothing.

off_label.claim: Writing only Shortest Length and Longest Length gives each Vtx the two ends of its own length range, which is what a per-Vtx remap of edge length needs and what a single global range cannot supply.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExVtxPropertySpecialEdges::ProcessNode tracks the minimum and maximum adjacency length independently per Vtx

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: The reading this node defines, for the **Properties** pin on **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialNeighborsSetting.name: Vtx : Special Neighbors
UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialNeighborsSetting.purpose: Finds the busiest and the quietest neighbour of each Vtx and describes the edge that reaches it. Ranking is on the neighbour's own edge count, so Largest is the neighbour with the most connections and Smallest the one with the fewest, and the geometry of the edge plays no part in the choice. Its near-sibling **Vtx : Special Edges** fills the same output blocks from the same list of edges, ranking them by edge length instead.
UPCGExVtxPropertySpecialNeighborsSetting.situation: A cluster where a Vtx needs to point at the shape of the network next to it rather than at the nearest thing: growing toward hubs, or stepping away from dead ends.

mechanism.text: Every neighbour of the Vtx is compared by how many edges it has of its own, and two rows come out of that: the neighbour with the most, and the neighbour with the fewest. Each names one neighbour and fills the indexed block about the edge reaching it, so the edge's row, the neighbour's row and that neighbour's edge count come with it. Ties keep whichever neighbour comes first in the Vtx's own edge order. Every field is off until its checkbox is ticked, so an untouched node writes nothing.

off_label.claim: Writing only Largest Count and Smallest Count gives each Vtx the range of degree in its immediate surroundings, which separates a Vtx sitting between two hubs from one hanging off a single hub without any of the direction data.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExVtxPropertySpecialNeighbors::ProcessNode tracks the highest and lowest neighbour edge count and passes each into its block as the neighbour count

outputs.label: Property
outputs.note: The reading this node defines, for the **Properties** pin on **Cluster : Vtx Properties**.

UPCGExWaitForPCGDataSettings.name: Wait for PCG Data
UPCGExWaitForPCGDataSettings.purpose: Pulls the output of PCG components living on other actors into this graph, holding execution until they have produced it. Target points name the actors by attribute; the node finds the components on them that match a template graph, decides whether to let them generate, waits, and re-emits what they produced. Its output pins are copied from the template graph's own output node, so the data arrives on pins with the same labels the source graph published.
UPCGExWaitForPCGDataSettings.situation: A graph that has to consume what another actor's PCG component produced, in the same generation pass, without knowing whether that component has run yet.

mechanism.text: Each target point contributes one actor reference, and identical references collapse to a single actor. On each actor, every PCG component that passes the filters becomes a candidate; what happens next depends on the component's own generation trigger, which selects one of the three Grab settings. Once a candidate has finished generating, its output is re-staged here, entry by entry, onto the pin whose label matches the one the source graph published; anything whose label is not part of the template goes to the roaming pin. The Target points themselves are not forwarded, so this node produces the fetched data and nothing else.

off_label.claim: With Must Match Template off and a tag in Must Have Tag, the template graph stops being a filter and becomes only the source of the output pin layout, which turns the node into a tag-driven harvester across differently authored components.
off_label.grounded_in: the component filter tests the graph identity only under bMustMatchTemplate, while the output pin set is always built from the Template Graph asset

inputs.label: Targets
inputs.note: Points carrying the actor references to watch. Not forwarded to any output.

outputs.label: One pin per template graph output
outputs.note: Mirrored from the Template Graph asset's output node and cached on the node. Use the Refresh Pins button after the template's outputs change.

outputs.label: Roaming Data
outputs.note: Everything a component emitted on a label the template does not declare. Renamed by Roaming Pin.
outputs.condition: when Output Roaming is on

outputs.label: Execution Dependency
outputs.note: The standard dependency-only pin; carries no data.

ActorReferenceAttribute.tooltip: Actor reference that we will be waiting for PCG Components with the target graph.
ActorReferenceAttribute.semantics: Read per target point and deduplicated across the whole input, so ten points naming one actor watch it once. Points whose reference does not resolve contribute nothing.

TemplateInput.tooltip: Actor reference that we will be waiting for PCG Components with the target graph.
TemplateInput.semantics: Constant names the graph asset directly. Attribute reads a graph path per target dataset from the @Data domain, which lets one node watch for different graphs on different targets.
TemplateInput.trap: The output pin set is always built from the Constant Template Graph asset, whatever this is set to. In Attribute mode the pins still have to be primed by pointing Template Graph at a representative graph and pressing Refresh Pins.

TemplateGraph.tooltip: Graph instance to look for. Will wait until a PCGComponent is found with that instance set, and its output generated.
TemplateGraph.semantics: Serves two jobs at once: it is what components are matched against, and it is where the output pins are copied from. Changing it refreshes the pins; changing the graph's own outputs does not, which is what the Refresh Pins button is for.

TemplateGraphAttributeName.tooltip: Graph instance to look for. Will wait until a PCGComponent is found with that instance set, and its output generated.

bMustMatchTemplate.tooltip: If enabled, will skip components which graph instances is not the same as the specified template.
bMustMatchTemplate.semantics: Compares the candidate component's graph against the template by identity. With it off, every activated component on the actor that clears the tag and trigger filters is a candidate, whatever graph it runs.

MustHaveTag.tooltip: If not None, will only consider components with the specified tag.
MustHaveTag.semantics: Tested against the component's own tags, not the actor's. Leaving it None disables the check rather than matching untagged components.

MatchGenerationTrigger.tooltip: If enabled, only process component with the specified generation trigger.
MatchGenerationTrigger.semantics: Narrows candidates to components set to this trigger. The component executing this graph is always excluded from its own search, as are components that are not activated.

bInvertGenerationTrigger.tooltip: If enabled, only process component that do not match the specified generation trigger
bInvertGenerationTrigger.semantics: Keeps every trigger except the selected one.

bWaitForMissingActors.tooltip: If enabled, will wait for actor references to exist.
bWaitForMissingActors.semantics: Keeps retrying the actor lookup until the timeout, for actors that are spawned during the same generation. With it off, references that do not resolve immediately are dropped.

WaitForActorTimeout.tooltip: Time after which the search is considered a fail.
WaitForActorTimeout.semantics: Seconds, clamped to thirty. Its edit condition also governs the component timeout below, so hiding this one hides that one too.

bWaitForMissingComponents.tooltip: If enabled, will wait for at least a single PCG component to be found that uses the target Graph. Use carefully, and only if you know for sure it will be found at some point!
bWaitForMissingComponents.semantics: Holds the node open on an actor that resolved but carries no matching component yet. Only worth enabling when something else in the generation is known to add that component, because otherwise it converts a warning into a timeout error.

WaitForComponentTimeout.tooltip: Time after which the search is considered a fail.
WaitForComponentTimeout.semantics: Seconds, clamped to thirty, applied to the component search.
WaitForComponentTimeout.trap: Its edit condition names the actor toggle rather than the component one, so this field appears and disappears with Wait For Missing Actors while governing the component wait.

GenerateOnLoadAction.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateOnLoad'
GenerateOnLoadAction.semantics: What to do with a matching component whose trigger is Generate On Load. Ignore skips it unless it is already generating; As-is takes whatever output it currently holds without triggering anything; Generate asks it to generate and waits, leaving an already generated component alone; Generate (force) regenerates it even if it already has output.

GenerateOnDemandAction.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateOnDemand'
GenerateOnDemandAction.semantics: The same four choices for components whose trigger is Generate On Demand. These never run by themselves, so Ignore and As-is on a component that has never generated yield nothing.

GenerateAtRuntime.tooltip: How to deal with found components that have the trigger condition 'GenerateAtRuntime'
GenerateAtRuntime.semantics: Components whose trigger is Generate At Runtime get three choices rather than four: Ignore, As-is, and Refresh, which asks for a refresh and waits for it.

bTrackSourceComponents.tooltip: If enabled, registers an editor-only dependency on each fetched component's owning actor, so this node re-runs when that source component regenerates. Off by default.
bTrackSourceComponents.semantics: Editor only. Registers a dependency on each fetched component's owning actor so this graph re-runs when that component regenerates. Off by default because it couples two generations that are otherwise independent.

bIgnoreRequiredPin.tooltip: If enabled, available data will be output even if some required pins have no data.
bIgnoreRequiredPin.semantics: By default a component whose output is missing any of the template's Required pins contributes nothing at all, not even its other pins. Turning this on takes whatever it did produce.
bIgnoreRequiredPin.trap: The check is per component, so one component short of a required pin silently removes its whole contribution while its neighbours still report.

bDedupeData.tooltip: If enabled, only output component data once per unique actor. Otherwise, output data as many time as found. When enabled, TargetIndexToTag is disabled.
bDedupeData.semantics: On, an actor's component data is emitted once however many target points named it, tagged from the first of those points. Off, it is emitted once per naming point, which multiplies the output.
bDedupeData.trap: It also forces the index tag off in Target Attributes To Data Tags, since with one output per actor there is no single point index to record.

bCarryOverTargetTags.tooltip: If enabled, target collections' tags will be added to the output data.
bCarryOverTargetTags.semantics: Copies the tags of the target dataset, not of the individual point, onto every piece of fetched data.

TargetAttributesToDataTags.tooltip: Lets you tag output data with attribute values from target points input
TargetAttributesToDataTags.semantics: Reads from the target point that asked for the actor, which is what ties fetched data back to the row that requested it.

RoamingPin.tooltip: If enabled, adds an extra pin that contains all the data that isn't part of the template.
RoamingPin.semantics: With roaming off, data on labels the template does not declare is dropped rather than redirected.

bQuietActorNotFoundWarning.tooltip: Suppress warnings when referenced actors are not found.

bQuietComponentNotFoundWarning.tooltip: Suppress warnings when no matching PCG components are found on actors.

bQuietTimeoutError.tooltip: Suppress errors when waiting for components times out.

hints.text: The output pins are a snapshot of the template graph taken when Template Graph was last assigned. Edit the template's output node afterwards and this node keeps the old pins until Refresh Pins is pressed.
Generate and Generate (force) make this node drive other components' generation. Pointing it at a component whose own graph reaches back to this one is a cycle the node cannot detect.

UPCGExWithinRangeFilterProviderSettings.name: Filter : Within Range
UPCGExWithinRangeFilterProviderSettings.purpose: Tests one number against a band of values, or against a whole set of bands at once. The bounds are typed on the node, or read as `FVector2` attributes from data on the Ranges pin, where every distinct pair found becomes one more band and an element passes if it lands inside any of them. Inverted, the same node asks for the values that land in none of them. Point Operand A at a `@Data.` attribute and the filter answers once per dataset instead of once per element, which is what Uber Branch and Break require of every filter they are handed and what lets Uber Filter (Data) judge a dataset in one question.
UPCGExWithinRangeFilterProviderSettings.situation: A band of acceptable values, or several bands, where a pair of comparison filters would say the same thing twice.

mechanism.text: The consumer runs this factory once per element and decides what the answer means; the filter reads Operand A on the element and writes nothing. The bands are settled once, on this node, and every element every consumer tests is judged against that one set: the verdict is whether the value fell inside any of them, flipped by `Invert`. A band whose min sits above its max is swapped as it is built, so a pair always reads as the interval between its two values.

inputs.label: Ranges
inputs.note: Data carrying the bands as `FVector2` values, X the min and Y the max. Several datasets are accepted and read into one pool, and identical pairs collapse into a single band.
inputs.condition: when Source is Attribute Set; under Constant the pin sits among the advanced pins and nothing reads it

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: The filter this node defines. It carries the point-filter passport, so it is accepted on every filter pin, Vtx Filters and Edge Filters included.

fields.name: OperandA
fields.tooltip: Operand A for testing -- Will be translated to `double` under the hood.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Where to read ranges from

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: List of attributes to read ranges from FVector2.

fields.name: RangeMin
fields.tooltip: Range min value.

fields.name: RangeMax
fields.tooltip: Range max value

fields.name: bInclusive
fields.tooltip: Whether the max end of the range is inclusive. The min end is always included.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: If enabled, invert the result of the test and pass if value is outside the given range

hints.text: Under Attribute Set the bands are resolved before the filter is emitted, which is what puts `Missing Data Policy` in play on this node. A Ranges pin with no data on it, or with no readable `FVector2` pair on it, is a missing-data failure: Error cancels the node and emits no filter at all, while Pass and Fail emit a constant filter of that verdict in its place. The policy defaults to Fail, so an empty pin rejects every element rather than waving them through.

The node subtitle prints the operand and the two bounds, with a flag marker prepended when Invert is on. Under Attribute Set there is no single band to print, so the subtitle falls back to the plain node title.

UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings.name: Cluster : Edge Properties
UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings.purpose: Writes what an edge is onto the point that stands for it. An edge point sits in the Edges dataset carrying almost nothing about the connection it represents, and this fills that in: how long the edge is, which way it runs, what a heuristic stack scores it at, and what its two Vtx would blend to. It also carries the operation that turns edge points into geometry, replacing each one's transform and bounds with a box that lies along the edge, which is what a mesh spawner or a spline needs to build along a cluster.
UPCGExWriteEdgePropertiesSettings.situation: Something downstream has to work on the edges themselves, whether that is filtering them by length, spawning along them, or sorting them by direction.

mechanism.text: Edges in, the same Edges out, carrying whatever was enabled; the Vtx pass through untouched and no edge is added or removed. Each edge is handled once, on its own, from the positions of its two Vtx and nothing further out. Direction Settings runs first and decides which of the two Vtx that edge calls its start, and every output that has a sense of direction reads that decision: the direction vector, the order the heuristic is scored in, and which way a solidified box points.

off_label.claim: Write only the length and nothing else, and the Edges dataset becomes filterable by edge length with ordinary point filters, which is the shape Cluster : Refine's length refinements already work in but reachable by any node that takes points.
off_label.grounded_in: EdgeLength is the straight-line distance between the two Vtx positions, written on the edge point with no other output required

off_label.claim: Turn on Endpoints Blending with no other output, and the edge point inherits its two Vtx values, which gives an Edges dataset the attributes its Vtx carry and makes edge filters able to test them.
off_label.grounded_in: The blend runs on every edge regardless of which other outputs are on, taking Edge Start and Edge End as its two operands

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster. Read for positions, for blending operands and for sorting values, never written.

inputs.label: Edges
