inputs.note: The Edges half, and the only thing this node writes to.

inputs.label: Blend Ops
inputs.note: Blend operations combining the two endpoint Vtx into the edge point. Hidden among the advanced pins until Endpoints Blending is on, and read only under the Individual interface.

inputs.label: Heuristics
inputs.note: The stack whose combined score is written. Several heuristics collapse through Heuristics Score Mode.
inputs.condition: appears and is required when the Heuristics output is enabled

inputs.label: Direction Sorting
inputs.note: Sorting rules deciding which endpoint of an edge ranks first.
inputs.condition: appears and is required when Direction Settings uses the Endpoints Sort method

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged. Nothing on this node writes to the Vtx.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The same edge points, carrying the enabled attributes and, under solidification, a rewritten transform and bounds.

DirectionSettings.tooltip: Defines the direction in which points will be ordered to form the final paths.
DirectionSettings.semantics: Decides which Vtx an edge calls its start, and every direction-sensitive output on the node follows from it. Endpoints Order keeps whatever order the edge already stores, which makes the whole block a no-op unless the incoming edges were ordered on purpose; Cluster : Edge Order is the node that gives them that order once for the whole cluster instead of re-deriving it here.

EdgeLengthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write the edge length to.
EdgeLengthAttributeName.semantics: The straight-line distance between the two Vtx positions. Solidification and `Edge Position Lerp` move and resize the edge point without changing it.

EdgeDirectionAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write the edge direction to.
EdgeDirectionAttributeName.semantics: The value is a unit vector, and it points at the endpoint Direction Settings ranked first rather than away from it, which is what Direction Choice means when it says the vector points at the smallest-value endpoint.

bEndpointsBlending.semantics: Turns the edge point into a mixture of its two Vtx. Which attributes travel and how they combine is not decided here: under the Individual interface it is the blend operations on the pin, and under Monolithic it is the block below. Turning this on is also what promotes the Blend Ops pin out of the advanced set.

EndpointsWeights.tooltip: Balance between start/end point. Solidification computes its own balance and overrides this; Edge Position Lerp does not.
EndpointsWeights.semantics: The balance between the two endpoints, 0 taking one and 1 the other. Solidification derives its balance from `Solidification Lerp` instead of reading this, which is why the row leaves the panel whenever a solidification axis is set.

BlendingInterface.tooltip: How to blend data from sampled points
BlendingInterface.semantics: Individual takes only the attributes its wired operations name, one operation per attribute, and with nothing wired it blends nothing at all. Monolithic starts from everything the Vtx carry and works by exclusion instead. The two never mix: the pin is ignored under Monolithic and the block is hidden under Individual.

BlendingSettings.tooltip: Defines how fused point properties and attributes are merged together.

HeuristicsAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write heuristics to.
HeuristicsAttributeName.semantics: The value is a double: the combined score of the wired heuristic stack for this one edge. Enabling this output is what makes the Heuristics pin appear and required.

HeuristicsMode.semantics: Heuristics score a step from somewhere to somewhere, so an edge has two scores and this picks which one is written. Endpoints Order takes the score in the direction Direction Settings chose. Smallest Score and Highest Score compute both directions and keep one, which makes the result independent of the edge's order and is the choice when the ordering is arbitrary.

HeuristicScoreMode.tooltip: Scoring mode for combining multiple heuristics
HeuristicScoreMode.semantics: How several heuristics collapse into the one number written. With a single heuristic wired the mode changes nothing.

bWriteEdgePosition.tooltip: Update Edge position as a lerp between endpoints (according to the direction method selected above)
bWriteEdgePosition.semantics: Moves the edge point onto a spot between its two Vtx. On its own it changes position and nothing else, so bounds and rotation stay as they were; solidification is the setting that rebuilds the whole transform. Turning it on under solidification hands the pivot over from `Solidification Lerp` to `Edge Position Lerp`, and the box follows the pivot either way.

EdgePositionLerpValue.tooltip: Position lerp between start & end points.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

EdgePositionLerpValue.semantics: 0 puts the point on the edge's start Vtx and 1 on its end, so which Vtx each extreme means is decided by Direction Settings. Under solidification the one value both places the pivot and splits the box around it, so the box goes on spanning the edge exactly while the pivot slides through it from one endpoint to the other.

SolidificationAxis.tooltip: Align the edge point to the edge direction over the selected axis.
SolidificationAxis.semantics: Sets which local axis of the edge point is aligned along the edge, and turning it away from None is what enables the whole solidification group. The chosen axis takes the edge's length as its bounds; the other two take theirs from Radius and Slide, mapped cyclically so X hands Y and Z to Secondary and Tertiary, Y hands Z and X, and Z hands X and Y. Bounds are divided by the point's own scale, so a scaled edge point still ends up the length of its edge in the world.

SolidificationLerp.tooltip: Solidification Lerp (read from Edge when using an attribute).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SolidificationLerp.semantics: With Write Edge Position off, this places the edge point and splits the box around it, running the opposite way from `Edge Position Lerp`: 0 sits on the edge's end Vtx, 1 on its start. Turn Write Edge Position on and the placement moves to that row, leaving this two jobs it keeps in either case: the balance the endpoint blend runs at, and the mix between the two endpoint radii wherever a radius `Source` is set to Vtx.

SecondaryAxis.tooltip: Secondary axis bounds, relative to the solidification axis.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Whether to write bounds over this axis.

fields.name: Radius
fields.tooltip: Radius for this axis.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Element the radius attribute is read from. Vtx reads both endpoints, lerped by the solidification lerp.

fields.name: Slide
fields.tooltip: Slide factor that shifts the bounds along this axis while preserving their size (2*Radius). 0.5 = centered (min = -Radius, max = +Radius), 0   = shifted fully negative (min = -2*Radius, max = 0), 1   = shifted fully positive (min = 0, max = +2*Radius).

SecondaryAxis.semantics: Radius is a half-width, so the bounds it produces are twice it across. Its Source picks which element the value is read from: Edge reads the edge point itself, Vtx reads both endpoints and mixes them by the solidification lerp, so a radius attribute authored on the Vtx tapers along the edge. Slide shifts the bounds across the axis while keeping their size, which is how an edge is made to sit on one side of its own line rather than centred on it.

TertiaryAxis.tooltip: Tertiary axis bounds, relative to the solidification axis.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Whether to write bounds over this axis.

fields.name: Radius
fields.tooltip: Radius for this axis.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Element the radius attribute is read from. Vtx reads both endpoints, lerped by the solidification lerp.

fields.name: Slide
fields.tooltip: Slide factor that shifts the bounds along this axis while preserving their size (2*Radius). 0.5 = centered (min = -Radius, max = +Radius), 0   = shifted fully negative (min = -2*Radius, max = 0), 1   = shifted fully positive (min = 0, max = +2*Radius).

TertiaryAxis.semantics: The same block as Secondary, on the other cross axis. Leaving one of the two disabled leaves that axis's bounds exactly as the edge point already had them rather than collapsing them.

hints.text: A heuristic is asked about this edge alone. Where a pathfinding run would supply a seed, a goal and the route taken so far, this node supplies the edge's own two Vtx as both seed and goal and no route at all. Heuristics reading local geometry, edge length and steepness among them, answer normally. Heuristics that score progress toward a goal, or that accumulate along a route, have nothing to work from here.
Solidification rewrites the edge point's rotation, position and bounds outright. Anything already authored on those, including bounds a staging fit was going to read, is gone.

UPCGExWriteGUIDSettings.name: Write GUID
UPCGExWriteGUIDSettings.purpose: Gives every point a stable identity attribute, computed from the point rather than handed out in sequence. The value is a GUID assembled from up to four things the point already carries, so the same point in the same place gets the same identity on every regeneration, and two points that differ in any enabled respect get different ones. It leaves as a string, or as a compact integer derived from that string.
UPCGExWriteGUIDSettings.situation: Points that have to be recognised again across regenerations, or seeded independently of the order they arrived in.

mechanism.text: Points in, the same points out, carrying one extra attribute. The GUID is built from four 32-bit slots: a base value holding the unique key and, when `Grid` is on, a hash of the component's grid bounds; the point's index; the point's seed, combined with the unique key when that key is read per point; and a hash of the point's position. Each of the four uniqueness flags governs one slot and empties it when off. Nothing about neighbouring points enters the value, so a point's identity survives everything except a change to the parts that built it.

off_label.claim: Clear every uniqueness flag and the value collapses to one constant shared by every point in every dataset, which turns the node into a way to stamp a configuration-derived marker rather than an identity.
off_label.grounded_in: With all four flags off the four slots resolve to the unique key, minus one, zero and zero, none of which reads anything from the point

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to identify.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, carrying the GUID attribute.

UPCGExWriteIndexSettings.name: Write Index
UPCGExWriteIndexSettings.purpose: Writes position-in-the-data as attributes. Three independent outputs: each point's index inside its own dataset, optionally reversed or rescaled to 0-1; the dataset's index among everything on the pin; and how many entries that dataset holds, optionally as a fraction of the largest. The first lands per point, the other two ship aimed at the `@Data` domain, and either of them can be written as a tag instead. Switch the per-point index off and the node stops being a point node at all: its pins widen to any type and it will index and count attribute sets and splines the same way.
UPCGExWriteIndexSettings.situation: Anything downstream that has to know where an element sits in a sequence, or how big the sequence is, without recomputing it.

mechanism.text: One input, one matching output, nothing added or removed. The per-point index is the point's position in its own dataset, so it restarts at zero for every dataset on the pin, and it is written as a whole number unless `Normalized` is on, which makes it a double. The dataset index is that dataset's position on the input pin. Normalisation always divides by the largest value in play: the last index for a point index, the biggest dataset on the pin for an entry count.

off_label.claim: In the collection-level mode the counting rule follows the data type, so an attribute set is counted by its rows and a spline by its segments, which turns the node into a size probe for data that has no points at all.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExWriteIndexElement::Boot's collection-level branch casts each input to UPCGParamData, UPCGSplineData and UPCGBasePointData in turn and counts entries, segments or points

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The data to index. Points, unless every enabled output is collection-level, in which case any type is accepted.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same data, carrying whichever of the three values are enabled.

pins.dynamic: With `Output Point Index` off and every other enabled output aimed at a `@Data` attribute, the node has nothing per point to do: both pins widen to accept any data type, and the run works on the raw inputs instead of on point batches.

OutputAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute to write its index to.
OutputAttributeName.semantics: The attribute's type follows a checkbox rather than the name: a whole number normally, a double once `Normalized` is on. A graph that switches that toggle changes the attribute's type under everything reading it.

bOneMinus.tooltip: Invert the index (MaxIndex - Index) before writing.
bOneMinus.semantics: Counts from the far end: whole numbers run last to first, and normalised values run 1 down to 0. It carries the same divide-by-zero on a single-point dataset that `Normalized` does.

bNormalizedEntryIndex.tooltip: Whether to write the index as a normalized output value
bNormalizedEntryIndex.semantics: Divides by the last index rather than by the count, so the first point is exactly 0 and the last is exactly 1.
bNormalizedEntryIndex.trap: A dataset holding a single point has a last index of 0, and the division is by zero, so its one value comes out as not-a-number rather than as 0 or 1.

CollectionIndexAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute/tag to write the collection index to.
CollectionIndexAttributeName.semantics: Ships pointing at the `@Data` domain, so the value is stored once for the whole dataset. Strip the `@Data.` prefix and it becomes an ordinary attribute instead, with the same number on every element.

CollectionIndexOutputType.tooltip: Output data type for the collection index attribute.

bOutputCollectionIndexToTags.tooltip: If enabled, output the collection index as a tag
bOutputCollectionIndexToTags.semantics: Swaps the attribute for a tag rather than adding one: with it on, no attribute is written, and the name becomes the tag's key.

NumEntriesAttributeName.tooltip: The name of the attribute/tag to write the collection num entries to.

NumEntriesOutputType.tooltip: Output data type for the num entries attribute.

bNormalizeNumEntries.tooltip: If enabled, output the normalized collection num entries to the points
bNormalizeNumEntries.semantics: Divides by the largest count among the datasets arriving on the pin, so the biggest one is exactly 1 and the value says how this dataset compares with its siblings rather than how big it is. Remove the biggest dataset upstream and every remaining value moves.

bOutputNumEntriesToTags.tooltip: If enabled, output the collection num entries as a tag
bOutputNumEntriesToTags.semantics: Swaps the attribute for a tag rather than adding one, the same way the collection index does.

bAllowInterpolation.tooltip: Whether the created attributes allows interpolation or not.
bAllowInterpolation.semantics: Covers the per-point index attribute alone. The two collection-level values are written through a different path that always marks them interpolatable, whatever this says.

UPCGExWritePathPropertiesSettings.name: Path : Properties
UPCGExWritePathPropertiesSettings.purpose: Measures a path and writes the numbers down. Two kinds come out. Per-point values say where a point sits in the run and how sharply it turns; per-path values describe the whole path, from its length to the box around it, and land in the data domain and in an attribute set of their own. A third group needs more than one path at once: inclusion works out which paths sit inside which, which is what tells a hole from the outline enclosing it, and the node can tag, flag or route paths on that answer.
UPCGExWritePathPropertiesSettings.situation: Something downstream has to decide from the shape of the run: a filter on how sharp a corner is, a spacing that follows distance travelled, or a hole that has to be told apart from the outline around it.

mechanism.text: One execution takes paths and returns the same points in the same order, carrying new attributes. Point count, order and locations never change. What is written splits in two: per-point values, one entry per point, and per-path values, one entry per dataset, whose shipped names all carry a `@Data.` prefix and which are also emitted as rows on the **PathProperties** pin. Anything answered in a plane, area and winding among them, is answered in the projection rather than in 3D, and anything about one path sitting inside another is decided across every dataset on the input pin at once. A path of fewer than two points is dropped with a warning.

off_label.claim: `Num Inside` counts every path enclosed by this one across the whole input pin, so feeding one large boundary alongside a batch of small paths turns the node into a containment counter: the boundary comes back knowing how many of the others fall inside it, and none of them are modified.
off_label.grounded_in: FPathInclusionHelper::AddPath increments the containing path's Children for every path it contains, over the whole batch, and the count is written as a per-path value only

off_label.claim: Turn `Write Path Data To Points` off, enable only per-path values, and the node stops touching the points at all: everything it measured leaves on the **PathProperties** pin as a table with one row per path, which is a shape for reading rather than for feeding back into geometry.
off_label.grounded_in: the per-path write macro calls WriteMark only while bWritePathDataToPoints is set, and the attribute-set row is written unconditionally

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to measure. Inclusion is worked out across everything arriving here in one execution.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: Every input path, carrying whichever attributes were asked for.

outputs.label: PathProperties
outputs.note: An attribute set carrying the per-path values as rows. Sits under the node's advanced pins.
outputs.condition: when any per-path value, or the Outer, Inner or Odd Depth tag, is enabled

outputs.label: Outer
outputs.note: Paths that nothing else encloses.
outputs.condition: when Use Inclusion Pins is on

outputs.label: Inner
outputs.note: Paths that at least one other path encloses.
outputs.condition: when Use Inclusion Pins is on

outputs.label: Odd
outputs.note: Paths at an odd inclusion depth, which the even-odd rule counts as holes.
outputs.condition: when Use Inclusion Pins is on

ProjectionDetails.tooltip: Projection settings. Some path data must be computed on a 2D plane. The projection normal (static, @Data attribute, or best-fit) also serves as the up/winding reference for point normals, binormals and signed angles.
ProjectionDetails.semantics: Decides more of this node than its position in the panel suggests. Answered in the projection: area, perimeter, compactness, winding, concavity, every inclusion result, and the sign of a signed `Angle`. Answered in 3D and untouched by it: path length, centroid, the distances, point time, the oriented bounding box, and the directions to next and previous. The projection normal doubles as the up vector the point normals and binormals are built from, so changing the plane rotates those too.

fields.name: InclusionOffset
fields.tooltip: Offset applied to projected polygon for inclusion tests.

fields.name: InclusionTolerance
fields.tooltip: Percentage of points that can lie outside a path and still be considered inside it

InclusionDetails.semantics: `Inclusion Offset` grows or shrinks each projected outline before any containment test, which is what forces a decision on a path lying along another's edge; positive grows the outline, negative shrinks it. `Inclusion Tolerance` is the share of a path's points allowed to fall outside another and still count as inside, so raising it turns strict containment into rough overlap. Concavity is computed before the offset is applied and so ignores it.

bWritePathDataToPoints.tooltip: Whether to also write path attribute to the data set. Looks appealing, but can have massive memory cost -- this is legacy only.
bWritePathDataToPoints.semantics: Every per-path value reaches the **PathProperties** pin whatever this says. What it decides is whether the same value is also written onto the path data itself. The shipped names all begin `@Data.`, which puts them in the data domain as a single value per dataset, so leaving this on is cheap.
bWritePathDataToPoints.trap: The memory cost the tooltip warns about arrives only if a name is changed to one without the `@Data.` prefix. That makes it an ordinary point attribute holding one repeated value on every point of the path, which is what the legacy behaviour was.

PathLengthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write path length to.
PathLengthAttributeName.semantics: Segment lengths summed in world units, including the closing segment on a closed path. It measures the run in 3D, unlike `Perimeter`, which measures the projected outline.

PathDirectionAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write averaged direction to.
PathDirectionAttributeName.semantics: Every point's direction to its next point, averaged and normalised, so it reads as the way an open path generally runs.
PathDirectionAttributeName.trap: On a closed path those directions cancel out, and what is left after normalising is numerical noise pointing nowhere in particular.

PathCentroidAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write the path centroid to.
PathCentroidAttributeName.semantics: The mean of the point locations, so a densely pointed stretch pulls it toward that stretch. It is not the area centroid of the enclosed shape, and it is not the centre of the bounding box.

IsClockwiseAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'bool' attribute to write winding to.
IsClockwiseAttributeName.semantics: The winding of the projected outline, which flips with the projection plane as readily as with the point order. Read it alongside `Reverse Order` rather than as a fixed property of the data.

AreaAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write area to.
AreaAttributeName.semantics: The area enclosed by the projected outline, taken as an absolute value and scaled by one hundredth on the way out. An open path is still closed for this measurement, straight from its last point to its first, so a path that does not loop still reports an area.

PerimeterAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write perimeter to (differ from length because this is the 2D projected value used to infer other values).

CompactnessAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write compactness to.
CompactnessAttributeName.semantics: Four pi times the area over the perimeter squared: 1 for a circle, falling toward 0 as an outline gets longer for the area it encloses. It is computed before `Area` is scaled down, so the two rows are not in the same units and their ratio is not meaningful.

BoundingBoxCenterAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write bounding box center to.
BoundingBoxCenterAttributeName.semantics: The box is solved over the path's points in 3D, so it is free to tilt and owes nothing to the projection. The fallback is silent: nothing is logged when the solve fails.

BoundingBoxExtentAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write bounding box extent to.
BoundingBoxExtentAttributeName.semantics: Half-extents along the box's own three axes, so they mean nothing without the orientation row beside them.

BoundingBoxOrientationAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FQuat' attribute to write bounding box orientation to.

InclusionDepthAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute to write inclusion depth to.
InclusionDepthAttributeName.semantics: How many other paths enclose this one, counted at every level rather than one step: 0 for a path nothing encloses, 1 inside a single outline, 2 inside two.
InclusionDepthAttributeName.trap: The count is taken across every dataset arriving on **Paths** in one execution. Adding an unrelated path that happens to enclose this one changes the number, and splitting the same paths across two runs of the node changes it again.

NumInsideAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute to write how many paths are contained inside this one.
NumInsideAttributeName.semantics: The mirror of depth: how many paths this one encloses, again at any level, so an outline holding a hole that itself holds an island counts both.

bWriteIsHole.tooltip: Write a per-path 'Is Hole' flag attribute (true for odd inclusion-depth paths -- the standard even-odd hole rule).
bWriteIsHole.semantics: Writes a boolean in the data domain under the fixed name `IsHole`, with no row to rename it. On every path that is not a hole the node deletes any `IsHole` attribute already present rather than writing false, so the absence of the attribute is the answer.

DotAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write the prev/next dot product to.
DotAttributeName.semantics: How straight the point is: 1 along a straight run, 0 at a right angle, -1 where the path doubles back on itself.
DotAttributeName.trap: On an open path the first and last point read 1, the same as a straight run, because the missing neighbour resolves to the point itself and the two directions collapse onto one segment. An endpoint and a straight run cannot be told apart in this attribute.

AngleAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write angle to next point to.
AngleAttributeName.semantics: The corner angle at the point, between the direction it arrives on and the direction it leaves on, mapped into whatever `Range` names. A straight run is the widest value of the range and a doubling back is zero. Both endpoints of an open path are written as a straight run.

AngleRange.tooltip: Unit/range to output the angle to.
AngleRange.semantics: The signed entries take their sign from which way the corner turns against the projection normal, so they separate a left turn from a right one; the unsigned and normalized entries fold the two together. Changing the projection plane flips every sign at once.

ConcavityAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' attribute to write concavity to.

bFlagRightAngles.tooltip: If enabled, corners forming a right angle (within tolerance) write 0 instead of -1/+1.
bFlagRightAngles.semantics: The right-angle test measures the corner in 3D while the concave and convex signs come from the projected outline. A corner that is square in 3D is zeroed here even where the projection makes it look like anything but, and a corner square only in the projection is not.

RightAngleTolerance.tooltip: Tolerance, in degrees, around 90° within which a corner is considered a right angle.

DistanceToNextAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write distance to next point to.
DistanceToNextAttributeName.semantics: The length of the segment that starts at this point. The last point of an open path starts none and is written 0; on a closed path it holds the closing segment's length.

DistanceToPrevAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write distance to prev point to.
DistanceToPrevAttributeName.semantics: The length of the segment that ends at this point. The first point of an open path is written 0; on a closed path it holds the closing segment's length.

DistanceToStartAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write distance to start to.
DistanceToStartAttributeName.semantics: Distance travelled along the path from the first point to this one, summing segments rather than measuring the straight line between them.

DistanceToEndAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write distance to end to.
DistanceToEndAttributeName.semantics: The total length less the distance to start. On a closed path the total includes the closing segment, so the first point reads the whole loop rather than 0.

PointTimeAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'double' attribute to write point time to.
PointTimeAttributeName.semantics: Distance to start over total length, so it follows spacing rather than index: evenly numbered points at uneven spacings do not produce even times. An open path runs it from 0 at the first point to 1 at the last; a closed one never reaches 1, because the closing segment is still in the total.

bTimeOneMinus.tooltip: Output (1 - time) instead of time, so 0 is at end and 1 is at start.

PointNormalAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write point normal to.
PointNormalAttributeName.semantics: The normal of the segment starting at this point, the projection normal crossed with that segment's direction, so it holds steady along a segment and jumps at every corner. The last point of an open path borrows the final segment's.

PointAvgNormalAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write point averaged normal to.
PointAvgNormalAttributeName.semantics: The two segment normals meeting at the point, averaged and renormalised, which is the one that stays continuous through a corner.

PointBinormalAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write point binormal to. The binormal is sign-matched to the segment normal, so it does not flip along the path.
PointBinormalAttributeName.semantics: The corner's own bisector: the incoming and outgoing directions summed and normalised. Along a straight run the two cancel and the segment normal is written instead.

DirectionToNextAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write direction to next point to.
DirectionToNextAttributeName.semantics: The last point of an open path has no next point.
DirectionToNextAttributeName.trap: It is written the direction of the final segment rather than a zero vector, so it points off the end of the path at something that is not there.

DirectionToPrevAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute to write direction to prev point to.
DirectionToPrevAttributeName.semantics: The first point of an open path is written the reverse of the first segment, pointing off the start.

ConcaveTag.semantics: Convexity is decided by walking the whole path and asking whether every turn goes the same way, so the two tags describe the path rather than any point on it. A path whose turns never resolve to a direction, a perfectly straight run among them, is given neither tag.

OuterTag.tooltip: Outer paths are not enclosed by any other path

InnerTag.tooltip: Inner paths are enclosed by one or more paths

OddInclusionDepthTag.tooltip: Median paths are inner with a depth %2 != 0
OddInclusionDepthTag.semantics: Odd depth means enclosed by an odd number of paths, which under the even-odd rule is what makes a path a hole. The tooltip's median wording names nothing else on this node.

PairingTag.tooltip: Pairs each outer path with the holes directly inside it: an outer (even inclusion depth) and the holes it immediately encloses share a unique integer id -- the outer's collection index -- written as a "Prefix:Id" value tag. Nested odd/even stacks (outer/hole/outer/hole) split into separate groups.

bUseInclusionPins.tooltip: If enabled, will output data to additional pins. Every output still goes to the default Path pin; the extra pins carry a filtered view of the same data.
bUseInclusionPins.semantics: The pins are not a partition: a path at odd depth reaches **Inner** and **Odd** both.

bOuterIsNotOdd.tooltip: If enabled, outer path (inclusion depth of zero) will not be considered "odd" even if they technically are.
bOuterIsNotOdd.semantics: Consulted only where a path already counts as odd, and a path nothing encloses is at depth 0, which is even. Nothing it gates can change, in either the tag or the pin.

UPCGExWriteStatesSettings.name: Write States
UPCGExWriteStatesSettings.purpose: Turns a stack of named conditions into one number on every point. Each **State : Point** on the **States** pin decides per point whether its filters hold, then applies its own bit operation to a shared int64, and what comes out is a flag mask saying which conditions were true there. It is the point-level twin of **Cluster : Write States**, and the mask it writes has the same shape, so the same bitmask filters and bitmask nodes read either one.
UPCGExWriteStatesSettings.situation: A dataset whose points have to be classified once, several ways at a time, so everything downstream can select on the classification instead of recomputing it.

mechanism.text: Points in, the same points out, carrying one extra int64 attribute. Every point starts at `Initial Flags`, and every state on the pin is asked whether it holds there, in ascending `Priority` order; a state that holds applies its pass operation to that point's number, one that does not applies its fail operation. States never name an attribute and never create one. The mask belongs to this node, and mutating it is the only thing a state can do. Point count, point order and every other attribute come through untouched.

off_label.claim: Run it on a Vtx dataset before that dataset enters a cluster node and the mask it leaves is indistinguishable from one **Cluster : Write States** would have written, which is a way to classify Vtx by conditions that need no connectivity at all.
off_label.grounded_in: Both consumers take the same int64 buffer through PointDataFacade->GetWritable(FlagAttribute, InitialFlags, false, EBufferInit::Inherit) and hand it to a PCGExPointStates::FStateManager

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The points to classify.

inputs.label: States
inputs.note: The **State : Point** sub-nodes whose bit operations build the mask. Required: the node does not run without at least one.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, carrying the flag attribute.

FlagAttribute.semantics: One int64 per point, and the only thing this node writes. It is the same shape **Cluster : Write States** produces on Vtx, so the bitmask filters and the bitmask nodes read either of them without needing to know which made it.

InitialFlags.semantics: The value every point starts from before any state runs, which only applies when the named attribute is new. Point the node at an int64 attribute the points already carry and their incoming values are the starting point instead, which is what lets a second **Write States** add bits to a mask an earlier one wrote.
InitialFlags.trap: The corollary is that this row goes quiet the moment the named attribute exists upstream. A mask that will not reset is usually a Flag Attribute already carried in from an earlier pass, not a value typed here.

hints.text: A **State : Point** needs at least one filter of its own. With its **Filters** pin empty the state's factory is never built, so nothing arrives on the **States** pin here and the run stops on a missing-input error naming **States**, which reads as though the wire itself were missing.

UPCGExWriteTangentsSettings.name: Path : Write Tangents
UPCGExWriteTangentsSettings.purpose: Runs a tangent rule over a path and leaves the answer on the points, as two vector attributes named `ArriveTangent` and `LeaveTangent` by default. **Create Spline**, both Spline Mesh nodes and **Copy to Path** can run the same rules inline, so this node is for when the answer has to persist: read by more than one of them, edited on the way through, or built in more than one pass with a different rule over different stretches of the same path.
UPCGExWriteTangentsSettings.situation: One path feeds both a spline and a run of spline meshes, and the curve has to bend the same way in both.

mechanism.text: Every point comes out in the order it went in, carrying two vector attributes named by `Arrive Name` and `Leave Name`. The rule runs once per point and fills both. A path tagged closed has no first or last point as far as the rule is concerned, since the neighbour indices wrap; an open one hands its two ends to `Start Override` and `End Override`, or to the base's endpoint answer where those are empty. Paths of fewer than two points are never processed, and `Omit Invalid Paths Outputs` decides whether they are dropped or passed through untouched.

inputs.label: Paths
inputs.note: The paths to compute tangents for.

inputs.label: Point Filters
inputs.note: Decides which points the rule runs on. Points that fail are skipped rather than zeroed.

inputs.label: Overrides : Tangents
inputs.note: An attribute set whose entries are matched by name against the main rule's own properties and applied before it runs.

inputs.label: Overrides : Start Tangents
inputs.note: The same, for whatever rule sits in `Start Override`.

inputs.label: Overrides : End Tangents
inputs.note: The same, for whatever rule sits in `End Override`.

outputs.label: Paths
outputs.note: The same points in the same order, with the two tangent attributes written.

ArriveName.semantics: `ArriveTangent` and `LeaveTangent` are also what the `Source` block on **Create Spline**, both Spline Mesh nodes and **Copy to Path** reads by default, so leaving both names alone is what carries the result downstream without reconfiguring anything.

Tangents.semantics: The rule that answers for every interior point, and for the two ends of an open path when no override is set. A newly placed node starts on **Auto**.

StartTangents.tooltip: Optional module for the start point specifically
StartTangents.semantics: Applies to the first point of an open path, and to nothing at all on a closed one.
StartTangents.trap: Three of the five rules define no first-point behaviour of their own: **Auto**, **Catmull-Rom** and **From Neighbors** fall through to the same answer the base already gives, so setting this to one of them changes nothing. **From Transform** and **Zero** are the two that do something here.

EndTangents.tooltip: Optional module for the end point specifically
EndTangents.semantics: Applies to the last point of an open path, and to nothing on a closed one. The same three rules that do nothing in `Start Override` do nothing here.

ArriveScale.tooltip: Scale applied to the arrive tangent.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

ArriveScale.semantics: Starts on the constant, one on every axis, with `$Scale` already filled into the attribute slot for when it is switched over. The multiply is component by component in world axes, so an uneven value turns the tangent as well as lengthening it.

LeaveScale.tooltip: Scale applied to the leave tangent.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

hints.text: A point the **Point Filters** pin rejects is skipped, not zeroed. Where an attribute of that name already existed on the input it keeps its value at that point, and where this run created it the value is zero. Two passes with complementary filters therefore give one path two different rules.

UPCGExWriteVtxPropertiesSettings.name: Cluster : Vtx Properties
UPCGExWriteVtxPropertiesSettings.purpose: Writes what each Vtx's own edges add up to, onto that Vtx. Two readings are built in, the count of edges meeting there and a normal taken from the frame fitted to its neighbours, and every other reading arrives as a Vtx : sub-node on the Properties pin. The node also carries the one operation in this family that moves data instead of annotating it: replacing each Vtx transform with the oriented box its neighbours span.
UPCGExWriteVtxPropertiesSettings.situation: A cluster where what happens next turns on the shape of each junction, and the Vtx have to carry that shape as attributes before anything can filter, sort or blend on it.

mechanism.text: Vtx in, the same Vtx out, carrying whatever this node and its sub-nodes wrote. Every Edges dataset passes through untouched. Each Vtx is visited once and sees only the edges that meet at it, so nothing here reaches past one step, and every Vtx has at least one edge because that is what puts it in the cluster. Sub-nodes on the Properties pin write into the same Vtx dataset, under names each of them chooses, in the order they are wired.

off_label.claim: The fit ranks its axes by how far the neighbours spread along each, so setting Axis to X instead of Z hands back the direction the junction spreads most along rather than a normal, which is a per-Vtx principal direction for free.
off_label.grounded_in: PCGExMath::FBestFitPlane::ProcessBox sorts the fitted axes by extent, widest first, and GetTransform maps that ranking onto X, Y and Z through Axis Order

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster to annotate.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Every Edges dataset that finds its Vtx is one cluster and one run.

inputs.label: Properties
inputs.note: Vtx : sub-nodes, each adding its own readings. With nothing wired here the node still writes whichever of its own two rows are enabled.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, carrying every attribute this node and its sub-nodes wrote.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged. Nothing in this family writes to Edges.

bMutateVtxToOOB.tooltip: Mutate Vtx into their OOB based on neighboring connections.
bMutateVtxToOOB.semantics: The box is fitted to the positions of the Vtx's neighbours, so the transform that replaces the Vtx sits at the centre of that neighbourhood, carries the fit's axes, and has a scale of one; the bounds become the fit's extents either side of it. Every reading the node and its sub-nodes take comes from the incoming transforms, so turning this on changes nothing about the other values written on the same run.
bMutateVtxToOOB.trap: The Vtx moves. Its authored position, rotation and scale are all replaced. At a Vtx with a single edge the entire sample is that one neighbour's position, so the Vtx lands on top of its neighbour.

bUseMinBoxFit.tooltip: If enabled, use precise min box fit.
bUseMinBoxFit.semantics: On, the frame is solved as the smallest oriented box containing the sampled positions. Off, it comes from how those positions spread about their mean, which approximates the same axes without bounding anything. Only the solved path can come back empty-handed, and when it does the frame stays at the world axes with unit extents, which reads as an unrotated Vtx rather than as an error.

AxisOrder.tooltip: Which fitted axis maps onto X, Y and Z. Also decides which axis Normal reads.
AxisOrder.semantics: The fit ranks its three axes by how far the sampled positions spread along each one, widest first, and this maps that ranking onto the transform's X, Y and Z. Left at X > Y > Z the widest spread lands on X and the narrowest, which is the plane normal, on Z.

VtxEdgeCountAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'int32' vertex attribute to write the edge count to.
VtxEdgeCountAttributeName.semantics: The value is how many edges meet at the Vtx, and it is never zero: a point joins a cluster by being an edge endpoint. One edge is a leaf, two is binary, more than two is complex, and this attribute is what turns that vocabulary into a number the rest of the graph can test.

VtxNormalAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the 'normal' vertex attribute to write normal to.
VtxNormalAttributeName.semantics: The value is one axis of the frame fitted to the neighbour positions, chosen by Axis, written as a unit vector in world space. It describes the neighbourhood, so it is a normal only where those positions describe a plane.
VtxNormalAttributeName.trap: Three positions that are not in a line are the least a plane can be fitted to. A leaf Vtx offers one neighbour and a binary Vtx offers two, so unless Include Vtx In OOB adds a third and the three are not collinear, what lands there is not a normal of anything.

NormalAxis.tooltip: Which axis of the vtx OOB to use as normal.
NormalAxis.semantics: Names which axis of the fitted frame becomes the normal, after Axis Order has mapped the fit's ranked axes onto X, Y and Z. At the shipped order Z is the axis the neighbourhood spreads least along, which is the plane normal; changing either row changes what this one hands back.

bIncludeVtxInOOB.tooltip: Include the vertex position in the oriented bounding box calculation.
bIncludeVtxInOOB.semantics: The sample is the neighbour positions alone; this adds the Vtx's own position to it. One fit feeds both outputs, so this changes the written normal as well as the box, and it counts for most at low degree where one extra position is a large share of the sample.

hints.text: The Properties pin advertises a broad type and narrows when the node starts, so a sub-node from another family connects, logs an invalid-input warning and is dropped. The node then runs with whatever survived, which may be nothing, and still writes its own two rows.

UPCGExZeroTangents.name: Zero
UPCGExZeroTangents.purpose: Returns a zero vector for both tangents at every point, and ignores the scales, since zero times anything is zero. Its use is as `Start Override` or `End Override`, where it strips whatever direction the base would otherwise have put on an open path's first and last point while the interior keeps the rule you chose. As the main rule it clears the tangents on the whole path.
UPCGExZeroTangents.situation: A curve should hold its shape through the middle of a path and carry no tangent at the two ends.

mechanism.text: Both vectors come back as zero, at every point, on open and closed paths alike. Nothing is read: not the neighbours, not the point transform, not the two scales. It answers for the first and last point of an open path as well as for the interior ones, so nothing falls through to the base.

off_label.claim: Set as the main rule on **Path : Write Tangents**, it writes a zero vector into both attributes on every point the filters admit, which clears tangents an earlier pass left behind without deleting the attributes.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExTangentsZero returns FVector::ZeroVector from all three handlers, and PCGExWriteTangents writes both buffers for every point its Point Filters admit.
